title: Baker Mayfield: Cleveland's next — we have a bad taste in our mouth, want to get it out
summary: Baker Mayfield’s Sunday afternoon did not go well, with three lost fumbles directly contributing to Tampa Bay’s 33-27 loss to Cincinnati.
full_text: Baker Mayfield’s Sunday afternoon did not go well, with three lost fumbles directly contributing to Tampa Bay’s 33-27 loss to Cincinnati. After agreeing to a contract extension earlier in the week, Mayfield finished 23-of-28 for 216 yards with no touchdowns, no picks, and the three giveaways. “ This one falls on me ,” Mayfield said in his postgame press conference. “I mean, they had, I think, 17 points alone off of my turnovers. Turns out to be a one-score game — six points.” But the Bengals were just one of two AFC North opponents that the Buccaneers have to begin their 2026 slate. The next, of course, is the Browns. “I mean, obviously, there’s history there — there’s no way to go around that,” Mayfield said. You think? The Browns infamously decided to move on from Mayfield after the 2021 season and traded for Deshaun Watson as his replacement. While Mayfield has found a home with the Bucs after stints with the Panthers and Rams in 2022, the Browns are still reeling from the aftereffects of that disastrous trade. While Mayfield is 0-1 against Cleveland, having lost to the team with Carolina in 2022, he now has a unique chance to rub the Browns’ nose in it. But, at least publicly, he’s not making more of it than what it is. “It’s the next opponent,” Mayfield said. “Cleveland happens to be the next opponent — our home opener. So, yeah. Have a bad taste in our mouth, looking forward to getting it out. “It’s still the next one, and that’s the most important one,” Mayfield added. “I’ve said that to you guys over the years — it doesn’t matter who it is, the most important one is the next one. And we’ve got — I’ve got to get some stuff fixed. And we’ve got to move forward.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Sunday's loss was the latest Green Bay meltdown
summary: Late in the third quarter of Sunday's Week 1 game at U.S.
full_text: Late in the third quarter of Sunday's Week 1 game at U.S. Bank Stadium, the Packers controlled the game, with a 22-10 lead. Then came the latest melting of the cheese. The Vikings scored the final 29 points of the game, becoming the first team who trailed by 12 or more with less than 20 minutes left in a game to win by 17 or more points. It's the most recent example of a very troubling trend for the Packers. In last year's wild-card game against the Bears, the Packers led at the half, 21-3. They were then outscored 28-6 in the second half before losing 31-27. In Week 17 against the Ravens, the Packers trailed by three points after three quarters, 27-24. The Ravens outscored Green Bay in the final 15 minutes, 14-0. In Week 16 against the Bears, Green Bay led by 10 after three quarters, 13-3. The Packers were outscored in the fourth quarter and OT, 19-3. In Week 15 at Denver, the Packers led 23-14 in the second half. The Broncos outscored them the rest of the way, 20-3. Much of it relates to the absence of linebacker Micah Parsons. The offense has had a hand in it, too. As Chris Simms pointed out on Monday's PFT Live , the Packers often empty the tank with the best stuff in their game plan early, and then they don't have answers as the game continues. Whatever the reason, it has become a problem for the Packers. On Sunday, it robbed them of the opportunity to wrest a road win against the division rival who had lost its starting quarterback. Instead, the Vikings staged a dramatic turnaround that will leave the Packers searching for answers. The good news is that they play the Jets on Sunday. If the Packers blow that one, there will be nothing good about the early weeks of their season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kellen Moore stands by decision to go for two at end of overtime vs. Lions
summary: When the Saints scored a touchdown against the Lions with 1:34 remaining in overtime on Sunday, they could have kicked the extra point to tie the game, then hoped that either their defense could get the ball back so they could win, or at least hold the Lions' offense to preserve a tie.
full_text: When the Saints scored a touchdown against the Lions with 1:34 remaining in overtime on Sunday, they could have kicked the extra point to tie the game, then hoped that either their defense could get the ball back so they could win, or at least hold the Lions' offense to preserve a tie. Instead, Saints head coach Kellen Moore decided to go for two, and end the game right there, one way or the other. The way it ended was the Saints lost: Tyler Shough's two-point conversion pass was incomplete out the back of the end zone, and the Saints walked off the field 0-1. After the game, Moore said he thinks he made the right call. "There was 1:34 left. That's a really talented offense. We had a chance to go win the football game," Moore said. "I really viewed it as we're going for two there to win the game, if we have a chance." The Saints also decided to kick off at the start of overtime, thinking they'd rather get the ball second and know what they have to do. Deciding to kick at the start of overtime played into the decision to go for two at the end of overtime: Because the Saints had the second possession, Moore knew what his team had to do, and what his team had to do was score a two-point conversion. It didn't work, but Moore still thinks it was the right call.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deshaun Watson says he'll "keep smiling, regardless of who's against me or who's with me"
summary: Watson seems likely to remain Cleveland's starting quarterback for at least another week.
full_text: If you look at Deshaun Watson's final numbers from Cleveland's 34-10 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday, you might be able to talk yourself into some positives. After all, Watson was 16-of-22 for 205 yards with a touchdown and an interception — good for 9.3 yards per attempt and a 97.7 passer rating. But if you watched the game, you’d know 46 of those yards came on a garbage-time touchdown to Denzel Boston against the Jaguars’ backups. You would’ve seen Watson fire an interception to end Cleveland’s first drive, almost throw another to end the second, and then get strip-sacked on the third. You would understand that most — if not all — of Jacksonville’s five sacks on Watson happened because he was dropping so far back that the offensive line couldn’t form a cohesive pocket. You might’ve been baffled by how often he was trying to change a call at the line of scrimmage too late in the play clock. Cleveland’s first drive had gotten off to a solid start, with the team moving the ball before Watson’s interception. After that, the unit was off the rails with no sense of rhythm. But Watson said postgame that the pick didn’t rattle him. “No, I mean, bad plays are going to happen all the time,” he said in his press conference. “You look all around the league. Everyone throws interceptions, everyone makes bad plays. You've got to give the defense credit. He made a good play on that. Even though I got knocked off my platform a little bit, I thought I got it over him. He reached up and grabbed it. So you've got to move on to the next play and try to move forward and try to put something positive on the next drive. And we weren't able to do that. “So it didn't really bundle up my confidence. It's just — we didn't get back on track like we wanted to.” Will the Browns’ dalliance with Watson continue? It seems likely, for at least another week. And so, Watson will lean on his experience in dealing with adversity as the Browns ready to play the Buccaneers. “Yeah, I mean just keep moving forward, keep stepping forward, keep smiling, regardless of who's against me or who's with me,” Watson said. “I think that's more beneficial for the team in that locker room. I've had a lot of support in that locker room after the game telling me to keep my head up, keep pushing forward, keep working. They're behind me, so that's always positive to see and hear. Yeah, we just got to keep going. “The adversity is going to be there. You've got to embrace it. That's the only way — I thought it was going to be gone two years ago, but I guess not. So you just embrace it and keep pushing through until you break that wall through.” The Browns will be on the road to face Baker Mayfield and the Bucs next Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: CBS announces next two weeks of broadcasters, with no Tony Romo
summary: CBS has said nothing more about the status of No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo since CBS placed him on leave, with a one-sentence press release.
full_text: CBS has said nothing more about the status of No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo since CBS placed him on leave, with a one-sentence press release. On Monday, CBS confirmed that Romo's leave won't be ending before Week 4. CBS has announced the broadcast teams for Week 2 and Week 3. The top team continues to consist of Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt. That includes the Ravens-Cowboys game to be played in Brazil. Most believe Romo won't return this year. Many believe he'll never be back, with only a buyout to be negotiated. After Romo issued a statement on September 1 disclosing that he would be pleading no-contest to charges related to an OWI arrest in Milwaukee, CBS had nothing to say . Which said plenty. There may never be a statement in which CBS declares that its relationship with Romo is over. The message may simply come one development at a time, starting with Watt replacing him for Week 1 — and continuing with Watt keeping the spot for Week 2 and Week 3.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Falcons DL Da'Shawn Hand believed to have a torn quad
summary: The Falcons opened the 2026 season with a loss to the Steelers and they may have lost a defensive lineman for the rest of the year as well.
full_text: '' The Falcons opened the 2026 season with a loss to the Steelers and they may have lost a defensive lineman for the rest of the year as well. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand is believed to have a torn quad that would require season-ending surgery. Hand is soliciting other opinions before making a decision about a course of action. Hand signed a one-year deal with the Falcons this offseason. He played seven snaps on Sunday before leaving with his injury. The Falcons have already lost linebacker Jalon Walker for the season and James Pearce has seven games to go on his suspension, so the front seven is getting thin in Atlanta.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Anderson is now the betting favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year
summary: Rams defensive end Myles Garrett entered the season as the clear favorite to win the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year award.
full_text: Rams defensive end Myles Garrett entered the season as the clear favorite to win the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year award. That didn't last long. Garrett did nothing in Week 1, and is now out through at least Week 5 with a knee injury, and his odds to win Defensive Player of the Year have dropped to +2500. And now there's a new favorite. Texans defensive end Will Anderson is now favored to win the award, with +320 odds. Anderson and the Texans' defense did not have a great game in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills, but Anderson is one of the best pass rushers in the league, and Defensive Player of the Year usually goes to a great pass rusher. Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, who had two sacks in a Week 1 win over the Saints, is second in Defensive Player of the Year odds at +500. He's followed by Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt (+650), who had a tremendous pick-six in Sunday's win over the Falcons, and Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby (+900), who had 1.5 sacks in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Derrick Henry, Lamar Jackson star in win over Colts
summary: Henry ran for three touchdowns in a 41-23 Ravens win.
full_text: The Jesse Minter era in Baltimore got off to a winning start. One of Minter's first big moves was hiring Declan Doyle as his offensive coordinator and that decision paid off for the Ravens' biggest stars in their season-opening win over the Colts. Derrick Henry ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns, Lamar Jackson produced a pair of touchdowns and the Ravens will head into Week 2 off the back of a 41-23 win. Jackson finished 17-of-25 for 324 yards through the air and he ran four times for 43 yards in the kind of performance that the Ravens saw far too infrequently while missing the playoffs last year. He opened the scoring with a touchdown run that he set up with a 49-yard strike to wide receiver Zay Flowers and later hooked up with Flowers for a 52-yard score. Flowers had five catches for 150 yards in less than two quarters, but then missed the rest of the game with a hamstring injury. The Ravens also lost wideout Ja'Kobi Lane to a wrist injury, which gives them a pair of concerns at the position as they get set to host the Saints in Week 2. The Ravens fell down 6-0 to open the game, but quickly took the lead with a pair of touchdowns wrapped around a Roquan Smith interception of Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey forced another turnover by stripping Jonathan Taylor and the Ravens were up 28-6 at one point in the first half. The final score got more respectable as the Ravens slowed down in the wake of Flowers's injury, but the overall picture is one that will make for a lot of smiles around the team's facility this week. Jones finished 19-of-31 for 166 yards in his first game since tearing his Achilles last season. He only ran once, which is a big difference from how he was used prior to the injury and that missing dimension didn't help the Colts' cause on Sunday. Their defense's inability to stop the Ravens hurt them more, though, and they'll have to try to come up with something better on both sides of the ball to avoid an 0-2 start when they head to Kansas City next week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions choke away 21-0 lead, survive to beat Saints 31-30 in overtime
summary: In a wild Week 1 battle, the Saints nearly completed an epic comeback, but couldn't convert their two-point attempt in overtime.
full_text: The Lions and Saints played an epic Week 1 game that couldn't be decided in 60 minutes, but after each team scored an overtime touchdown, Detroit ultimately prevailed. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's two-point conversion pass was incomplete out the back of the end zone on the final play of overtime, and the Lions survived 31-30. For most of the game, it looked like the Lions would win easily: Detroit led 21-0 in the third quarter and seemed poised to cruise to an easy win. Instead, the Lions choked the lead away and easily could have lost in regulation: Saints kicker Daniel Carlson lined up for a game-winning field goal as time expired in the fourth quarter, but his 62-yard attempt missed. There were some positives for the Lions: Jahmyr Gibbs, whom the Lions made the highest-paid running back in the NFL last month, delivered in a big way, with 156 yards rushing and two touchdowns. And Aidan Hutchinson sacked Shough twice. But for the Lions, the big question coming out of the game is why they couldn't put the Saints away when they should have. For the Saints, it was a heartbreaking loss but a sign that Shough is starting to grow within Kellen Moore's offense. The heavily favored Lions won, but the Saints have to feel good about the way they fought until the end.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bengals recover four Bucs fumbles, hold on to win 33-27
summary: The Bengals had a makeover of their defense in the offseason after ranking 31st in yards and 30th in points last season.
full_text: The Bengals had a makeover of their defense in the offseason after ranking 31st in yards and 30th in points last season. They showed off their new look on Sunday. The Bengals allowed only 282 yards, forced four fumbles they recovered and had four sacks in a 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield lost three fumbles — one that Bengals linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. returned 27 yards for a touchdown and another into the end zone that safety Bryan Cook recovered. Running back Bucky Irving also lost a fumble. Still, Mayfield gave the Bucs a chance with a 9-yard touchdown run with 3:19 left. Joe Burrow, though, drove the Bengals 54 yards in eight plays, allowing the clock to expire on Tampa Bay's comeback. Burrow went 25-of-35 for 254 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Bucs rookie Josiah Trotter intercepted Burrow on a third-and-5 pass intended for Andrei Iosivas and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown. Burrow's touchdown was a 2-yard throw to tight end Mike Gesicki, who had five catches for 78 yards. Ja'Marr Chase had only two catches for 12 yards. Evan McPherson kicked field goals of 20, 55, 58 and 32 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Myles Garrett will have knee surgery, head to IR
summary: The dream team has encountered an unexpected detour.
full_text: The dream team has had an unexpected detour. After losing to the 49ers badly in Melbourne, and given Myles Garrett's candid remarks about the impact of his health on his performance, Garrett will have knee surgery and be placed on injured reserve, per multiple reports. It's a stunning development for a Rams team that became the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl after Garrett's arrival in June. His presence lured Aaron Donald out of retirement. Now, Donald will be playing for at least four games (if Donald plays in Week 2) without Garrett. And it won't be an easy road. The Rams host the Giants next Monday night. The following Sunday night, they face the Broncos in Denver. Then, the Rams head to Philly for a date with the Eagles. After that, the Rams return home for a Monday night showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears beat Panthers 59-37 in Week 1 offensive frenzy
summary: Plenty of points were scored as Chicago went to Carolina and won a fun one in Week One.
full_text: The Bears' and Panthers' offenses ran wild today in Carolina, but the Bears were wilder. Chicago had an incredible game running the ball, with a total of 39 carries for 291 yards and six rushing touchdowns, and Caleb Williams added 269 passing yards and two more touchdowns, in a 59-37 win. The Panthers' offense played well too, with Bryce Young passing for 361 yards and three touchdowns and adding a rushing touchdown. If the Panthers' defense could have stopped anyone, Young and the Panthers' offense could have been the talk of the league in Week 1. But the Panthers' defense couldn't stop the Bears, who ran the ball almost at will. (The one exception was a surprising fourth-and-1 attempt from the Bears' own 21-yard line that went nowhere.) It was a tremendous showing from coach Ben Johnson's offense. The Bears were one of the surprises of the NFL last season, winning the NFC North when few thought they could. This year they look like they're going to be a tough team to beat again.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bears-Panthers was highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history
summary: The Bears and Panthers made some history on Sunday afternoon.
full_text: The Bears and Panthers made some history on Sunday afternoon. Chicago's 59-37 road win was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The previous record was 88 points, which came in a 48-40 Buccaneers win over the Saints during the 2018 season. It was also the first time that any NFL game ended in a 59-37 score. The 96 points were also the most total points in a game for both the Bears and the Panthers and it was the highest-scoring game in the NFL since the Rams and Chiefs combined for 105 points in a 2018 game. It was not the most points that the Bears have ever scored in a game. They put up 61 points in regular season games during the 1965 and 1980 seasons and they scored 73 points in the 1940 NFL championship game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward has all the tools, but it's a long process
summary: Titans quarterback Cam Ward said he was disappointed with how he and the team played in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets and he's sure to find plenty of people willing to co-sign that assessment of their first game under head coach Robert Saleh.
full_text: Titans quarterback Cam Ward said he was disappointed with how he and the team played in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets and he's sure to find plenty of people willing to co-sign that assessment of their first game under head coach Robert Saleh. Some people might go a little further than disappointed when it comes to where the first overall pick of the 2025 draft is as he starts his second NFL season. Ward's best moments of the game came on a drive with under five minutes to play and the Titans down big, which led to Saleh being asked at a Monday press conference if the quarterback is more of a work in progress than the staff thought when they got to Tennessee. Saleh pointed out that Ward has had seven offensive coordinators in the last seven years and that they are "trying to build a foundation" for him to make the needed improvements. "His growth will happen throughout the year," Saleh said. "His growth is gonna happen next year and the year after. This young man is at the floor of what it takes to be an NFL quarterback, but he has all the tools, the mental makeup to get to where he needs to go. It’s time on task, it’s giving the kid stability, it’s giving the young man the chance to be repetitive in his day-to-day process with the right coaching to help him get better. . . . It's a long process, long process to get these kids to get them where you need to get to, quarterback especially." Saleh said he's not trying to "shield" Ward and noted both some "easy throws" that he thinks the quarterback would want to have back and improvements he's seen in Ward's pocket presence. Signs of those gains are going to have to start coming a little more often if Ward is going to continue looking like a worthwhile project in Tennessee.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jahmyr Gibbs had career-high 29 carries, and Dan Campbell says he can do even more
summary: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a career-high 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday, and he added five catches for 30 yards.
full_text: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a career-high 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday, and he added five catches for 30 yards. That's an enormous workload for any player, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game that Gibbs could do even more. "I thought it was a very promising Week 1," Campbell said. "Certainly, we know what Gibbs is, what he's capable of, and he's still not there yet. And I mean that in a good way." What more could Gibbs do? Campbell said that on a day when Gibbs' longest run was 21 yards, he's capable of breaking some much longer runs than that. "We were this close to breaking three or four more of these, breaking them wide open," Campbell said. "A shoestring away, just a little longer block at the second level. I mean, we were close, and we're going to get that cleaned up, and he's going to get better. Week 1, yeah, I like where he's at. I'm glad he's here." Campbell is not looking for Gibbs to get 29 carries a game for 17 games. That would be 493 carries for the season, which would be the second-most in NFL history. But Campbell said he's happy to keep feeding Gibbs the rock. "Do I want to set records with how many carries? No, that's not something I want to do, but when you look at a guy and you think he's in good shape, he had a really good camp, he's in the best shape I've seen since I've been here," Campbell said. Gibbs will have to be in good shape for the workload the Lions are giving him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bills score late, then stop Texans to win 36-31 in classic
summary: Josh Allen, who was 0-4 in Houston, threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Josh Palmer with 1:36 remaining.
full_text: The Bills and Texans put on a show on Sunday afternoon. There may not be many games this season that are better than the season opener in Houston. Josh Allen, who was 0-4 in Houston, threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Josh Palmer with 1:36 remaining for a 36-31 lead and then had to watch from the bench as the Bills held on. The Texans had first-and-goal at the Buffalo 9 with 25 seconds left, but Deone Walker sacked C.J. Stroud for a 9-yard loss. After an incompletion, Greg Rousseau had a strip-sack of Stroud that Terrell Bernard recovered with 9 ticks left to end it. The back-and-forth game had nine lead changes. Allen ripped apart the Texans' vaunted defense, throwing for 334 yards and two touchdowns as the Bills had 409 total yards. He nearly threw his only interception on the play before the game-winner, but Kamari Lassiter, who had a rough day, dropped the pick in the end zone. Tight end Dalton Kincaid caught five passes for 130 yards and DJ Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown in his Buffalo debut. James Cook ran for 57 yards on 13 carries. The Texans gained 381 yards, but Stroud had the only two turnovers. He also lost a fumble on a strip-sack by Rousseau in the first half. Stroud finished 26-of-38 for 274 yards and two touchdowns. The Texans showcased their free agent acquisition, David Montgomery, as he had 20 carries for 60 yards and two touchdowns and three catches for 19 yards and a touchdown. The Texans had 32 rushes and 38 passes, held the ball for 36:17 and went 2-for-2 on fourth down.
author: Charean Williams

title: Packers melt down in fourth quarter, Vikings pull off 39-22 victory
summary: Despite losing Kyler Murray in the first quarter, Minnesota pulled off a stunning win with a huge fourth quarter.
full_text: Early in the fourth quarter, armed with a 22-17 lead over Minnesota, Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur made a couple of decisions. The result of those choices proved to be disastrous and allowed the Vikings to come away with a 39-22 victory to open the 2026 season. On fourth-and-6 from Minnesota’s 22-yard line, Packers rookie Trey Smack hit a 40-yard field goal to give Green Bay an eight-point, 25-17 lead. But the Vikings were flagged for an offside penalty. That induced LaFleur’s first choice — taking the field goal off the board to go for it on fourth-and-1. The second choice was LaFleur’s play call: A QB sneak. But quarterback Jordan Love failed to convert, with a virtual measurement confirming Love was short of the sticks. Now with Green Bay holding just a five-point lead, the Vikings got down the field due to a cacophony of errors from Green Bay’s defense. It looked like the Packers would get off the field on third-and-11 with a sack of Carson Wentz, but Green Bay was flagged for illegal contact for a free first down. On the next set of downs, when Wentz just avoided a sack by getting rid of the ball on third-and-3, Chris McClellan was flagged for a questionable roughing-the-passer penalty, as he braced himself before falling on Wentz with his full body weight. Then when Wentz was intercepted by safety Evan Williams in the end zone, the Packers got flagged for defensive holding, giving the Vikings another free first down. Finally, Aaron Jones ran it in against his old team for a 3-yard touchdown. It got worse — or better, depending on your perspective — from there. Love was sacked twice in a row on the ensuing drive, with the ball coming out on the second. The Vikings started their next drive from the 1-yard line, with Jordan Mason powering it in for a touchdown on the first play. And then Love tossed the first interception of his career at U.S. Bank Stadium, with the ball getting tipped at the line before going off of Harrison Smith’s hands and into the waiting arms of James Pierre. Justin Jefferson caught his second touchdown of the game to finish that drive, giving the Vikings a stunning 17-point lead. The Packers had led 22-10 in the third quarter and were outscored 29-0 for the rest of the game, including 22-0 in the fourth quarter. It was a remarkable victory for the Vikings, who lost their starting quarterback on their third possession. Kyler Murray was hit hard in the head while sliding on a third down. The Packers were flagged for unnecessary roughness while Murray went straight to the locker room for further examination and was diagnosed with a concussion. So Wentz came in and managed the game well, finishing 12-of-19 for 133 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Two of his TD passes went to Justin Jefferson, who hadn’t caught a score at home since 2024. The wideout finished with eight catches for 92 yards with two TDs. On the other side, things were going very well for the Packers before the ill-fated QB sneak. Love finished the contest 21-of-42 for 387 yards with two touchdowns and a pick. Christian Watson had six catches for 147 yards with two TDs, but five of those receptions and 131 of those yards came in the first half. Now at 1-0, the Vikings will be on the road for another divisional game against the 1-0 Bears next week. The 0-1 Packers, who now have a disturbing trend of blowing significant leads, will again be on the road to face the 1-0 Jets.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cardinals beat Chargers in NFL's biggest upset of Week 1
summary: The Chargers were the NFL's biggest favorites, with a 9.5-point spread. Instead, the Cardinals won 26-14.
full_text: The Chargers were 9.5-point favorites against the Cardinals today in Los Angeles, the biggest betting line in the NFL for Week 1. No one thought this was a game Arizona would win. But that's why they play the games. In a major upset that may force us to reassess what we thought we knew about both teams, the Cardinals went to Los Angeles and beat the Chargers 26-14. First-year Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur deserves an enormous amount of credit for having his team ready to play, and Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh will face plenty of questions about why his team wasn't. Harbaugh had previously been 6-0 in Week 1 in his NFL coaching career. Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett played well, completing 27 of 37 passes for 277 yards, with one touchdown and no interceptions. His favorite receiver was Trey McBride, who caught nine passes for 95 yards and a touchdown. The Cardinals surprisingly made Tyler Allgeier, not rookie Jeremiyah Love, their primary ball carrier. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert turned in a highly disappointing performance, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. And the Chargers' running game never got going. Also alarming for the Chargers is that wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a chest injury late in the game and went to the locker room. The Cardinals also had a concerning injury when safety Kitan Crawford was carted off during the fourth quarter, but today was mostly great news in Arizona: This team looks better than anyone thought.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Malik Nabers knew it was time to make his return during pregame warmups
summary: Wide receiver Malik Nabers made his first appearance in the Giants' lineup in almost a year when he took the field against the Cowboys on Sunday night.
full_text: Wide receiver Malik Nabers made his first appearance in the Giants' lineup in almost a year when he took the field against the Cowboys on Sunday night. Nabers tore his ACL last September and he remained noncommittal about playing all the way through the week. After the 28-20 win, Nabers said he was up in the air all the way through pregame warmups and that he told his family not to come to the game because he didn't want to disappoint them by not playing. "The deciding factor was just when I got out there, I just felt good ," Nabers said after the game. "I felt good. I got a little chill through my body and I was like, "Yeah, it's time. It's time." Quarterback Jaxson Dart said in his press conference that head coach John Harbaugh tackled Nabers during a walkthrough earlier in the weekend to show the wideout that he was ready. It took a little longer for Nabers to be convinced, but Dart was happy that the outcome allowed him to throw the ball to his top target. "It was great, it was great. He's just a guy where, no matter what the coverage is, no matter who they put out there on him, you have all the confidence in the world that he's going to make a play," Dart said. Nabers finished the day with six catches for 69 yards and the Giants will be looking for even bigger numbers now that he's got the first game back under his belt.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sunday Night Football: Jaxson Dart throws three TDs, Giants beat Cowboys 28-20
summary: New York won its first game under new head coach John Harbaugh by controlling the ball and the clock.
full_text: The Giants certainly looked like a new squad under new head coach John Harbaugh. New York used long, punishing drives to control the game, defeating Dallas 28-20 on Sunday Night Football . After a Dak Prescott interception late in the second quarter, the Giants took a 14-7 lead into halftime with Isaiah Likely’s 15-yard touchdown catch from quarterback Jaxson Dart. Then, after receiving the second-half kickoff, Likely scored his second touchdown to cap a 12-play, 74-yard drive that took 8:01 off the clock, pushing the lead to 21-7. The Cowboys responded with a long touchdown drive of their own. But the Giants effectively put the game out of reach with another long drive featuring several swing passes — including Dart’s 9-yard TD pass to Devin Singletary. That drive took 8:11 off the clock, leaving just 7:26 in the final period. Dallas again scored, this time on a 17-yard reception from Javonte Williams. But the running back taunted as he crossed the goal line, resulting in a 15-yard penalty. Brandon Aubrey missed the extra point wide right, keeping it an eight-point game. But even with an extra point — or a potential two-point conversion — it wouldn’t have mattered, because the Cowboys defense could not get a stop. Dallas never got the ball back, as the Giants held it for the last 5:21 to win. New York ended the game with 29 first downs, 394 yards, and was 9-of-11 on third down. The club was really 9-of-10, as the final third down was a knee from Dart to run out the clock. The Giants’ second-year QB was 23-of-29 for 230 yards with three touchdowns and no picks. He also had 54 yards on the ground. Likely was his top target throughout the night, catching all eight of his targets for 78 yards with his two TDs. Malik Nabers — returning from a torn ACL — caught six passes for 69 yards. Cam Skattebo had 81 yards on 18 carries with a TD. On the other side, Prescott finished 22-of-34 for 175 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. There wasn’t much running room, as Williams finished with just 41 yards on 12 carries. CeeDee Lamb was limited to 44 yards on five catches with a touchdown. George Pickens had a bad drop down the sideline in the first half, finishing with just three catches for 28 yards. Dallas may have some more issues defensively, as the team lost a couple of key players. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown went down in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury. Malik Hooker also had to exit with a forearm injury in the second half and was not able to return. Now at 1-0, the Giants will be on the road next week to play the Rams on Monday night. The 0-1 Cowboys will have their home opener next Sunday afternoon against the Commanders.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jonathan Taylor: Loss to Ravens definitely a wakeup call
summary: The Colts picked up right where they left off in Week 1 of the 2026 season, but that was not a good thing.
full_text: The Colts picked up right where they left off in Week 1 of the 2026 season, but that was not a good thing. Indianapolis lost their final seven games last year and they are 0-1 after giving up 506 yards and turning the ball over twice in a 41-23 home loss to the Ravens on Sunday. The Colts only managed 251 yards of their own and running back Jonathan Taylor said after the game that he hopes the beating serves as a reminder that its time for the team to start taking things seriously. "Definitely an eye-opener, definitely a wakeup call ," Taylor said, via the team's website. "Like, hey, season's here. Obviously we know no one's gonna give us anything, but it's a good team over there and it's like, hey, doesn't matter what you guys did last year, you gotta prove it again this year." Taylor ran for 98 yards and two scores, but the rest of the offense was underwhelming in quarterback Daniel Jones's return from a torn Achilles. They'll have to hope that more time back on the field helps Jones get back to where he was early last season because more of the same in the weeks to come is going to make for a long season in Indianapolis.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jim Harbaugh: We were too sloppy
summary: Sunday night saw John Harbaugh win his first game as the head coach of the Giants, but it wasn't a great day for the whole Harbaugh family.
full_text: Sunday night saw John Harbaugh win his first game as the head coach of the Giants, but it wasn't a great day for the whole Harbaugh family. Jim Harbaugh's Chargers came into Week 1 as the biggest favorite in the league, but anyone who backed them at home over the Cardinals went home a little poorer. The Cardinals never trailed and shut the Chargers out in the fourth quarter of a 26-14 win that left Harbaugh to say that "quite a few things" went wrong for his team. “Some uncharacteristic things happened . Give them credit for making them happen,” Harbaugh said at his press conference. “I would call it sloppy at times. Too sloppy. That’s something we need to get fixed.” Harbaugh cited seven penalties, but there were also two turnovers, a blocked punt and the offense failing to convert multiple times on fourth downs. The offense was limited to 268 yards overall, which didn't fit with the enthusiastic praise that Harbaugh lavished on quarterback Justin Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel throughout the offseason. That duo will have more chances to get things right, but the first look at this year's Chargers looked a lot like the last glimpse of the 2025 version and that's not where anyone with the team hoped to find themselves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaxson Dart: Identity starts at the top and we bought into John Harbaugh's plan
summary: The Giants capped the first Sunday of the 2026 season with their first win under head coach John Harbaugh.
full_text: The Giants capped the first Sunday of the 2026 season with their first win under head coach John Harbaugh. Dallas was the favorite at MetLife Stadium, but the Giants drove for a touchdown the first time they had the ball and never trailed on their way to a 28-20 win that featured plenty to like in every phase of the game. Quarterback Jaxson Dart threw three touchdowns and ran for 54 yards while showing full command of the offense to kick off his second season, and said after the game that the effort was a result of putting everything Harbaugh has been preaching into action. "I just think that we have so much respect for coach Harbs, and this team will do whatever he says because we have all the faith that he's going to put us in the best situation to win," Dart said. "The identity of a team starts at the top and it starts with how he's conducted himself, with how he's created a tough team. We want to take that on our shoulders and we bought in to what his plan is week in and week out. We're definitely happy to get it for him. We were just really happy to get it — not only for the players but for the organization." It's the first time the Giants opened a season with a win since 2022, which was the last time that they ended a season with a trip to the playoffs. Sunday night's performance will have some around the team thinking about a similar destination and it will be on Harbaugh to make sure that no one gets too far ahead of themselves after a stirring debut.
author: Josh Alper

title: DeMeco Ryans: C.J. Stroud played well enough for us to win
summary: C.J.
full_text: C.J. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns. He had a 106.7 passer rating. The Texans quarterback also lost two fumbles on strip sacks by Greg Rousseau, and the Bills won 36-31 as Stroud couldn't get them in the end zone despite a first-and-goal at the 9. Coach DeMeco Ryans thought Stroud played well enough to win, pointing to the 409 yards his vaunted defense gave up. That included 334 passing yards by Josh Allen. “C.J. was very much in control the entire game," Ryans said, via texanscommenter. "Took what the defense gave him. Made great decisions with the football. Proud of the way he played today. He showed what he’s been showing all camp, that confidence, that growth. Was very calm, great demeanor, putting us in a great position to win the game. "Unfortunately, we lost the football there two times. Don’t want those plays at all, but not going to let that overshadow the game that he had. Offense put up way more points than needed for us to win this game. Could’ve definitely played much better defensively.” The Texans had first-and-goal at the Buffalo 9 with 25 seconds left, but Deone Walker sacked Stroud for a 9-yard loss. After an incompletion, Rousseau had a strip-sack of Stroud that Terrell Bernard recovered with 9 ticks left to end it. “Got down there," Stroud said. "Can’t get stalemated like that. That sack kind of made it tougher, but even then, we still had a chance. I’m trying my best to protect the ball but also to make plays. We needed seven right there, so I can’t be super conservative. I've got to be able to take shots. Sometimes it doesn’t roll your way. We’ll try to fix that and go forward.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Jalen Hurts: It's about meeting the moment when opportunity comes
summary: There were some long stretches during Sunday's game when the Eagles offense failed to click, including five three-and-outs in 11 total possessions, but they were able to beat the Commanders because of big plays that got sprinkled throughout the contest.
full_text: ' There were some long stretches during Sunday's game when the Eagles offense failed to click, including five three-and-outs in 11 total possessions, but they were able to beat the Commanders because of big plays that got sprinkled throughout the contest. Quarterback Jalen Hurts had a hand in many of them. He hit a 64-yard pass to wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks to set up tight end Dallas Goedert's first touchdown catch and then hit Wicks for another score later in the first half. After the Commanders cut the Eagles' lead to one point in the fourth quarter, Hurts scrambled for 22 yards on third-and-18 and then hit Goedert for a 43-yard score that gave them the cushion they needed to finish out a 24-22 victory. After the game, Hurts was asked about his ability to come up with big plays when his team needs them the most. “Yeah, but it's not something that's forced," Hurts said, via a transcript from the team. "It's the same focus that you have throughout the whole entire game. It's the same poise that you play with throughout the whole entire game. And so, it goes back to all 11 being on the same page and then me taking responsibility and the opportunities I have with the ball in my hand. Talking about this on a production meeting leading up to the game with [Tom] Brady. When you're playing a position, a lot of it is about making sure you're in the right play, when you're doing the right thing that takes no talent. . . . It’s just about meeting the moment when your opportunity comes. Collectively, we’ve got a lot to build on, obviously a lot to correct and I'm excited to get back into the process of becoming the team that we're supposed to become.” Putting together a steadier and more consistent offensive attack will be on the list of things to correct as the Eagles move into Week 2 and beyond, but that process will be made easier thanks to the knowledge that they can turn to Hurts and expect him to come up with something special in the biggest moments of games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Allen on late TD to beat Texans: Sometimes the ball bounces your way
summary: It's hard to come up with too many examples of how thin the line between winning and losing can be than back-to-back plays that the Bills ran late in the fourth quarter in Houston on Sunday.
full_text: It's hard to come up with too many examples of how thin the line between winning and losing can be than back-to-back plays that the Bills ran late in the fourth quarter in Houston on Sunday. On a second down from the Texans' 34-yard-line with just under two minutes to play and the Bills down one, quarterback Josh Allen chucked a pass into the end zone and Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter was the only player in position to catch it. Lassiter was unable to make the interception while stumbling backward, however, and Allen got another chance. He made good on it with a perfect strike to Josh Palmer for the game-winning touchdown. "Hey, it's football. What can I say? Sometimes the ball bounces your way," Allen said in his postgame press conference. Allen was 0-4 in previous trips to Houston and the Bills had not won there since 2006. That stretch included Allen taking eight sacks in a loss last season, but the Bills only allowed two this time and Allen had enough time to average 11.5 yards per attempt. That and a little good fortune made all the difference for the Bills on this trip to Texas.
author: Josh Alper

title: Travis Hunter played 4 snaps on offense, 29 on defense
summary: Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter was a starter on defense and a bit player on offense in Week 1 against the Browns.
full_text: Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter was a starter on defense and a bit player on offense in Week 1 against the Browns. Hunter played 29 snaps on defense, which was 57 percent of the Jaguars' defensive plays, and four snaps on offense, or 7 percent. Hunter did not play at all on special teams. The Jaguars tried to get Hunter the ball when he was on the field on offense, and he got one carry for three yards and one catch for eight yards. On defense, he had one tackle. When the Jaguars drafted Hunter last year, they thought he could be the NFL's only full-time starter on both offense and defense. So far in his NFL career, it hasn't worked out that way. As a rookie last year he had played 67 percent of offensive snaps and 36 percent of defensive snaps when an injury ended his season after seven games, and the early indications this year are that he won't be a regular contributor on offense. Hunter is contributing, but not enough to live up to the hype surrounding his status as last year's second overall pick.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Zac Taylor: We felt the presence of our defensive additions on Sunday
summary: The biggest storyline of the Bengals offseason was the moves they made to improve their defense and the new players were front and center in Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
full_text: The biggest storyline of the Bengals offseason was the moves they made to improve their defense and the new players were front and center in Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. Defensive end Boye Mafe had a sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery while safety Bryan Cook also forced and recovered a fumble. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had a sack and the defense forced four turnovers while sacking Baker Mayfield four times overall. After the game, head coach Zac Taylor said the team "felt their presence" when asked about the new faces but holdover linebacker Barrett Carter shrugged off any suggestion that the performance validated anything to the team as a whole. "We haven't answered any questions," Carter said, via a transcript from the team. "Like I said, this what we expected. We haven't answered any questions. The Bengals are 1-0, we had four turnovers — that's great — but we should have won by much more. I don't mean that against the Buccaneers, but we need to dominate teams, so there's a lot more plays to be made. This defensive team, we have not done anything. We have not even scratched the surface. There's a lot more plays to be made." The key for the Bengals will now be to use Sunday's effort as a foundation for the continued defensive growth they will need to end their playoff drought. The next test of that will come in Houston in Week 2.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ashton Jeanty: We're building a new culture that's going to win games
summary: When the Raiders took running back Ashton Jeanty at the top of the first round in 2025, they had performances like Sunday's in mind.
full_text: When the Raiders took running back Ashton Jeanty at the top of the first round in 2025, they had performances like Sunday's in mind. Jeanty ran 23 times for 102 yards and caught a pair of touchdowns in a 27-13 win over the Dolphins. That came after Jeanty missed extended time this summer with an ankle injury, but he showed no signs of it on Sunday and the Raiders showed no signs of being the overmatched team that went 3-14 last season. “The past is the past,” Jeanty said in a postgame press conference. “We’re moving forward, and we’re not worried about what happened last year. This is a new team, new staff, and we’re building a new culture here. And that’s a culture that’s going to win football games.” There was a lot of talk about the Raiders turning the corner when they beat the Patriots in Week 1 under Pete Carroll last year, but they promptly went on a four-game losing streak that was much more indicative of how the year would play out. Klint Kubiak's charge will be making sure that the positives against Miami remain in place and riding Jeanty like they did on Sunday will likely be part of that plan.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys' new defense flops vs. Giants: Why Christian Parker, other additions have work cut out for them
summary: Dallas had the worst defensive success rate of any team Sunday
full_text:
By all accounts, this was one of the more normal offseasons for the Dallas Cowboys . George Pickens didn't get an extension, but the contract drama stopped there. Jerry Jones hinted at big moves but didn't stir up his usual distracting storylines, and he pledged he was all in on winning now.
The Cowboys' moves reflected that: a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker, two first-round defenders in Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence and a plethora of other veterans -- Jalen Thompson , Cobie Durant, Dee Winters and Rashan Gary -- brought in. Add an extension for Quinnen Williams , and even if it didn't have the makings of a dominant defense, it had the makings of a much-improved one.
And it still might. But it sure didn't in Week 1, as the Giants trounced the Cowboys 28-20 , a result that indicates how far Parker and his unit have to go and raises questions of whether they can get there.
"I thought overall we were really, as a football team, we were pretty poor," Brian Schottenheimer said. "... They were the more physical team tonight. That's certainly not our standard. That's certainly not how we see our identity playing. ... Situationally, they were outstanding. They did a really good job of keeping the ball away from us in the second half. I think they had the ball for 36 minutes and 40 seconds. So, this is a humbling business. We got humbled tonight, and that's what I told the guys."
It was indeed humbling, and a reminder that problems don't go away overnight or, in this case, in one week. Some issues actually were mitigated. The Cowboys didn't allow a single play of 25+ yards; last year, they allowed an NFL-high 54.
Rather than bleeding out from huge gashes, though, the Cowboys' defense died by a thousand paper cuts. Dallas allowed 29 plays of between 5 and 15 yards; only the Saints and Rams have allowed more in Week 1. And too many of these were easy, easy gains.
No sequence was more damning than the Giants stamping their 13-play, 65-yard touchdown drive late in the game with three Devin Singletary dump offs in four plays. These are essentially give-up plays from the offense: hope for a few yards and move on. Instead, they gained 13 yards (on a third and 9, no less), 7 yards and, finally 9 yards, untouched, for a touchdown.
Hard watch from the Cowboys defensive film: three straight (pretty straightforward) dump offs with blown assignments to finish a 13-play, 65-yard touchdown drive. pic.twitter.com/B48ZNrWmJL
This is Day 1 install stuff, and it caused Schottenheimer's blood to boil.
"We don't push three different times to the f---ing flat route, excuse my language," Schottenheimer steamed.
Scottenheimer also mentioned the breakdowns being a product of youth, and that's one area that's indisputable. Downs and Jaishawn Barham are rookies. There are other youngsters. Parker is a young coordinator, and everyone is "young" in his new system. But opponents don't take any pity on that. In fact, the Giants targeted it, and others will, too. On under-center play action plays, Dart was 5-for-7 for 34 yards and a touchdown and ran three times for 26 yards. He had a 0.34 EPA per play on these plays; for reference, that would have been the third-highest mark in the NFL last year.
These are not only the plays Dart feasted on, but the plays that are increasingly popular in the NFL -- the ones that stress linebackers. And Dallas' top linebacker, DeMarvion Overshown , left with a hamstring injury.
"We have to coach the young players better," Schottenheimer said. "But when you play young players, it's part of the deal, and they need to learn quickly."
The pass rush, which has plenty of veterans, proved a similar disappointing reality check. No player had more than two pressures. And the secondary, which has plenty of veterans, had too many issues, too. Here's fourth-year pro Winters and fifth-year pro DaRon Bland completely bungling coverage on a Likely touchdown.
Isaiah Likely hauls in his first TD as a Giant! DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FVcsGIrPsG
Dallas upgraded its defense, but it's worth considering that upgrading to try to get to the middle while also acclimating to a new coordinator can lead to uninspiring results. For example, Winters and Gary were trade acquisitions this offseason. Winters started all 17 games last year for the 49ers , but San Francisco finished dead last in defensive success rate. Gary might simply be a "bigger name than game" player at this point; he had one pressure on 20 pass-rush snaps.
Dallas needs pass rush juice to make everything else easier defensively. It's unclear where it will come from consistently, especially if no edge presence emerges to complement Williams. Parker can't create better players, like the players he had in Philadelphia. But he can teach his current players better and put them in more situations to succeed.
"You're going to get humbled at times," Schottenheimer said of the message after Parker's debut. "It happens. He'll learn from it. We'll learn from it."
It should be noted that youth can be a crutch, but it also leaves room for improvement. The Cowboys had some flashes. They forced four fumbles and only recovered one. Downs had a sack. Donovan Ezeiruaku had half a sack and two quarterback hits.
The bad news it's only one game, and it looked really bad. The good news is it's only one game, and there are 16 more to go. The youth will get older, the new scheme more familiar. There's no guarantee either will be enough if the requisite talent or exceedingly good scheme -- two things the Cowboys thought they had this offseason -- isn't there.
"The defense that we saw in practice was not what we saw tonight," Schottenheimer said. "But the offense wasn't the offense that we saw in practice. We just didn't perform very well. ... I'm not going to push the panic button. I know we're better than that."
They had better be, and soon, because Week 1 was a startling yet all-too-familiar disappointment.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: How John Harbaugh helped Malik Nabers get over mental hurdle in return from knee injury
summary: The first-year Giants coach took an unorthodox approach in preparing his star receiver for Week 1
full_text:
Malik Nabers ' status for Week 1 was a true game-time decision. The New York Giants wide receiver entered Sunday unsure about whether he would suit up for the season opener against the Dallas Cowboys , and it took until pregame warmups for him to decide that he was ready to make his return from a torn ACL and meniscus.
The decision may have had more to do with Nabers' mental hurdle than the strength of his knee.
Anyone who has recovered from a serious injury understands the physical element is just half the battle. Convincing yourself that you can do what you were once capable of — without the fear of reinjury — is the other element. It is part of the reason why Nabers did not even invite his family to the NFC East showdown.
"It's a one-on-one battle that you gotta go through," Nabers said postgame . "You gotta do it for yourself. I didn't want my family here and to feel like I let them down by not playing. I had to do it for myself first. I had to go out there, feel it out, feel what I could do, and I felt good."
It was not until Nabers got onto the field at MetLife Stadium and felt the adrenaline of game day that he got past the uncertainty. The Giants' first pass of the game, a nine-yarder to Nabers, had to have helped him settle his nerves in the first quarter. But what John Harbaugh did to his star receiver in the hours before kickoff did not hurt, either. He shook off Nabers' nerves by tackling him.
"It was right before we were supposed to start our walkthrough," quarterback Jaxson Dart said. "Things were just up in the air. We didn't know exactly what was going to happen. Me and Coach Harbs had some conversations, and he was like, 'I think once he gets hit for the first time and realizes that he's OK, that he's gonna feel confident.' I think in his mind that triggered, 'Maybe I should tackle him right then and there.'
"We were all just standing there, and then all of the sudden, 'Lik goes down on the ground. Our team is super protective of him, so we all turned to look. And it's Coach Harbs tackling 'Lik. And then he pops up and he goes, 'See, you're all good.'"
Nothing like a pregame tackle from your head coach to settle the nerves.
That is the Harbaugh effect. Not only did the first-year Giants coach help Nabers realize that he was, in fact, ready to play for the first time since October 2025, but he also guided his team to a 28-20 win over a division rival.
Nabers caught six passes on nine targets in the win, and he tallied 69 yards to finish second on the team in production through the air. He took a back seat to tight end Isaiah Likely , who paced the squad and scored two touchdowns, but the first game back from knee surgery was never going to be about filling the stat sheet. The top priority was for Nabers to prove that he can play. And he did just that.
"I put in great work," Nabers said. "Everyone had seen it. I was here early, late. I felt like my team needed to see me out. It brings out another focus when your teammates can see what you've overcome and that you're out there, giving it your all for the team. I think they needed to see that, and I'm happy they got to see that. I'm happy that I was able to come out there and feel good and give it my all."
author: Carter Bahns

title: Saints' Chris Olave explains why he wears a Guardian Cap, what it means for his family
summary: After suffering four concussions in his first 39 games, Olave chose the protective helmet cover to 'live regular life after football'
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints fell to the Detroit Lions in overtime of their season opener, 31-30, but there were some positive takeaways. Wide receiver Chris Olave , for example, caught a whopping 10 passes for 182 yards. It marked the second-most receiving yards ever recorded by a Saint in a season opener, and he currently leads the NFL in receiving.
It was hard to miss Olave on the field Sunday, one because he was lighting up the stat sheet and two because he was sporting a new Guardian Cap. The former No. 11 overall pick has a documented history with head injuries, suffering four concussions in his first 39 NFL games . After Sunday's game, Olave got honest with reporters about his decision to choose the Guardian Cap, saying he wants to "live regular life after football."
After dealing with head injuries over the years, Chris Olave says it was his decision to wear a guardian cap. He says he is thinking about his life after football and the kids he has now. #Saints pic.twitter.com/d82633uR1D
"You all know the head injuries I've had in my career," Olave said. "So it was just a decision I've made. Shoot, I got kids now. I want to be able to live the long game, it's not all about football. I want to live regular life after football. I love my kids to death. I don't really care how it looks no more I just got to throw it on, and shoot, it did me good today."
TYLER SHOUGH FINDS CHRIS OLAVE FOR 43 YARDS LATE IN THE 4TH 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/cs39B0lI1r
The connection between football and head injuries is tough to ignore. A study published this summer by The BMJ found that at least 25% of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had chronic traumatic encephalopathy , the brain disease known as CTE. The disease is thought to be caused by repeated hits to the head or head injuries like concussions.
The Guardian Cap, created in 2010, is a soft-shell cover for the helmet designed to reduce impacts during play.
The NFL began requiring certain positions to wear Guardian Caps during preseason practices in 2022 and made them available to players to wear in the regular season if they chose. More and more players are opting for the extra protection, such as New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs , Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson and Houston Texans safety Jalen Pitre . Pitre actually became the first-ever Guardian Cap Signature Athlete just this offseason.
"Regardless of the level you play at, protection is the most important thing," Pitre said in a statement. "Be proactive. Don't wait until after you get a concussion. This is about continuing to push the game forward. Think about your safety now because that's what you'll have when you leave the game."
According to the Guardian Cap's official website , studies have shown a 54% to 62% reduction in practice concussions among players required to wear Guardian Caps. Laboratory testing claims protection doubles when both players involved in a collision wear Guardian Caps.
Sure, the puffy helmets aren't exactly a fashion statement, but more and more players are caring less about that. They want to protect their long-term health and still have a life to enjoy after football.

title: 2027 NFL Draft: Dante Moore's early struggles and why history tells us to watch Drew Mestemaker
summary: Our model was higher on Mestemaker, more cautious on Moore, and their Week 2 matchup gave us our first real test
full_text:
Two weeks of college football aren't enough to make sweeping declarations about the 2027 quarterback class, but they can give us a glimpse of what the future might hold, both for the next few months and maybe even the next few years.
It's why we all made a mental note to see how Drew Mestemaker and Oklahoma State stacked up against Dante Moore and Oregon in Week 2. One quarterback dominated at North Texas before transferring; the other could have parlayed a strong 2025 season into the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 draft. On paper, the Ducks should have won. In reality, they slept through their second straight game, and this listless performance ended with a well-deserved upset loss, 39-31.
Mestemaker threw for 317 yards and two touchdowns, ran for another 109 yards and a score and, on first viewing, outplayed Moore.  I should reiterate, Moore entered the season as my QB1 and the No. 1 player on my big board. Moore rallied after a rough start and made some impressive throws — much like he did against Boise State last week — but this was Mestemaker's statement game.
What does this mean in the scheme of things? Not a whole helluva lot, honestly. Mestemaker looked overwhelmed against Tulsa in his debut and then bounced back to be the best player on the field against the Ducks. Moore, meanwhile, has a season's worth of really good tape, but so far through two games in 2026, he's been far less consistent than he was a year ago.
Instead of making some grand declaration, the better exercise is going back to what I saw last season, what former Titans GM Ran Carthon — my co-host on With the First Pick — and I saw during summer scouting, and what I wrote back in August before the season.
Essentially: identifying exactly what both quarterbacks needed to show us in '26 and then asking whether anything we've seen so far has changed our minds.
Moore entered the season as QB1 because he's as good as anyone in the class (it's also why he would've been the No. 2 overall pick back in April). His ability to push the ball downfield stood out on tape (his big-time-throw rate on deep balls ranked in the 99th percentile in '25), but so did the drop-off when he had to get beyond his first read or when the pocket became compressed. His 2025 second-read passing grade was 63.5, according to PFF, while his passing grade fell from 92.6 in a clean pocket to 51.0 under pressure.
Mestemaker's evaluation heading into the season looked very different. He was my QB9 after a huge season at North Texas, and the tape showed a calm pocket passer who would get through reads, keep his eyes downfield and throw with touch on intermediate routes. The questions centered on arm strength, sometimes being late downfield and whether some of those limitations would become pronounced with the step up in competition.
There was another wrinkle, too. Over the summer, I wanted another way to pressure-test what I was seeing on tape, so I came up with the First-Round Readiness Score, or FRED . It looks at where a quarterback is in his development at a given point in his college career and compares it with quarterbacks who eventually became first-round picks. It's not a draft grade, and it's not meant to replace the tape.
But it can tell you when history sees a player differently than the prevailing narrative does, whether that comes from league evaluators, fans or the media. And entering the season, it liked Mestemaker a lot more than Moore.
Mestemaker's FRED score was 40.4, third in the class. Moore was at 19.2 (A score of 50 has been the historical first-round threshold). That didn't mean Mestemaker was the better prospect heading into the season, but it did give us another reason to pay attention to the gap between their evaluations. Two weeks on, that appears to be a worthwhile question to keep asking.
My preseason big board rank
Can the elite flashes survive beyond the first read?
Does the historical case hold up against better competition?
Still really good on deep throws, progression concern persists
Passed the Oregon test; need to see him continue to improve his processing
Given how Oregon has stumbled out of the gate, it may be easy to overlook that the thing that made Moore QB1 is still a big part of his game. In Week 1, he was 2-of-5 for 72 yards on throws of 20-plus yards, then went 3-of-4 for 94 yards and two touchdowns against Oklahoma State.
But getting beyond his first read remains problematic. Moore was 2-of-5 for 11 yards in those situations in Week 1, then 1-of-5 for six yards on Saturday, including a sack and not a single first down. That's two more weeks where Moore has been much better throwing deep than working past his first read. That's not the end of the world — pushing the ball downfield is a critical part of playing quarterback in the NFL. But so is getting through your progressions against increasingly complex defenses.
Rewatching the tape, it was better than it looked live. Moore still had some of the same issues we've been tracking — he faced some drop-8 looks that seemed to frustrate him, and he forced a few turnover-worthy throws into tight windows. He also missed some throws he usually hits, but his receivers weren't creating much separation. There were several drops that could've turned into big gains, and Moore still showed glimpses of what made him QB1: smooth footwork, anticipation on deep comebacks, touch on intermediate in-breakers and the ability to extend plays and throw accurately on the move.
Like Week 1, he got better as the game went on. He converted a third-and-17 out of structure, ripped a seam throw and later dropped a 36-yard touchdown in the bucket.
And now Dante Moore is the one heating up for @oregonfootball as he tosses a 36 yard TD to make it 27-23. pic.twitter.com/U7rYAA4eKf
This game was just more confirmation of the good and not-so-good versions of Moore we've seen. He can indeed get off his first read on time and he clearly knows where he wants to go based on the pre-snap look. The issue is doing it consistently enough once the defense changes the picture after the snap.
Mestemaker's Week 1 wasn't especially revealing. He went 1-of-5 for 27 yards on throws of 20-plus yards and 4-of-8 for 55 yards after his first read in his first start for the Cowboys. It wasn't particularly impressive, and that's fine. He's just 20 years old, and the prevailing wisdom was that he'd likely stay in school beyond this season anyway.
The Tulsa game allowed Mestemaker to get his feet wet ahead of his first real test. And his Oregon performance gave us our first real answer. He was responsible for 426 total yards, created explosive plays with both his arm and legs and helped Oklahoma State answer every Oregon rally.
Oh my, Mestemaker! pic.twitter.com/Qx5Sv7Zpjx
What a touchdown run from Drew Mestemaker. Shades of Fernando Mendoza. He’s showing why he is on so many 1st round draft boards today pic.twitter.com/hjMlklFC5q
More importantly for our FRED-related purposes here, the moment never looked too big for a quarterback who had faced exactly zero Power 4 schools last season for North Texas.
There's plenty to clean up, for sure. He can still panic when the first read isn't there. He'll get locked onto his primary target and force throws into traffic. There were a few examples where he didn't see underneath defenders dropping into zones he was trying to attack. Oregon also didn't create much pressure, which isn't Mestemaker's fault, but playing from clean pockets while throwing the ball 43 times won't be a weekly thing.
But there was a lot to like. Mestemaker looked much more comfortable when protected, worked from Read 1 to 2 to 3 with good footwork, played on time over the middle and showed excellent touch on intermediate and deep balls. His arm also looked stronger than it did last season. Add in his prowess as a runner and the larger takeaway is hard to miss: Mestemaker needed to show he could produce when the competition got better, and against Oregon, he looked…

full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
Remember when the White Sox held a 5½-game lead in the AL Central? That was fun while it lasted. A month later, they've let go of the rope all the way down to half a game, and in turn, the South Siders slipped in our MLB Power Rankings . Matt Snyder explained why Chicago is down to No. 13 this week.
As a matter of fact, there is a ton of movement around the postseason bubble in this week's rankings. The 12 best teams might not necessarily be the 12 that clinch spots in the playoffs -- in fact, they almost certainly will not be, because of how putrid the American League is this year -- but here is how things look around that mark in the updated power rankings:
10. Diamondbacks (↓1) 11. Guardians (↑3) 12. Pirates (↑5) 13. White Sox (↓1) 14. Blue Jays (↓1)
The early window alone provided more entertainment than anyone could have expected. Shocking results in the evening made Week 1 even more mind-blowing. The first week of NFL games in 2026 is nearly complete, and what a ride it has been thus far. Here's a full breakdown of the opening week's takeaways.
At least the Big Ten has Michigan . The Wolverines helped salvage what was an otherwise rough day for the conference with their upset of No. 11 Oklahoma in a 17-10 slugfest . Outside of that bounce-back effort for Michigan -- wherein Bryce Underwood did just enough to help the offense get off the mat -- the Big Ten was among the biggest losers of college football's Week 2 .
The most concerning result for the conference came in the form of No. 6 Oregon 's unfathomable loss at Oklahoma State . Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker had his way with the vaunted Ducks defense in a game that defied all logic. Among the most mind-blowing stats : Oklahoma State became the first team to snap a 12-game losing streak with a win over a top-10 team. So where does Oregon go from here? The CFP is not out of reach , but if the Ducks lose another game or two, this will be a disastrously disappointing season.
Our John Talty went so far as to say that Dante Moore should have gone pro instead of returning to Eugene.
Another team that underwhelmed: No. 8 LSU . Now, it wasn't nearly to the same extent, because the Tigers beat Louisiana Tech by 31. But four turnovers in the second quarter alone and the surrendering of 11 tackles for loss was a wake-up call just in time for the highly anticipated battle against No. 9 Ole Miss . That's why we gave the Tigers a "C-" on this week's college football report card .
Rounding out the results that matter the most in the CFP picture, our Tom Fornelli is a little worried about No. 13 Texas Tech . The Red Raiders trailed in the fourth quarter at Oregon State for their second less-than-convincing win in as many weeks.
