title: Vikings rule out QB Kyler Murray with a concussion in Minnesota debut vs. Packers
summary: Murray's debut ends early with him being ruled out after a late hit in the first quarter
full_text:
Two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Kyler Murray's Minnesota Vikings debut in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers went from bad to ugly in a hurry.
He threw an interception into double coverage after facing a Green Bay blitz on his first pass of the game, and then his day ended because of an injury in the first quarter. Murray scrambled on a third-and-6, and he appeared to start his slide after gaining just a yard. However, Packers safety Javon Bullard hit him from the side late as he was sliding down. Murray landed awkwardly and grabbed his knee, and Bullard earned a penalty for unnecessary roughness that moved the chains for the Vikings with 6:16 left in the first quarter with Green Bay leading 9-0.
Murray went straight to the locker room, and shortly after, Minnesota announced Murray is officially ruled out with a concussion. He finished the afternoon with 18 yards passing on three of five attempts and an interception. He also had nine yards rushing on two carries.
QB Kyler Murray has been ruled out with a concussion. https://t.co/RQOUPuQ0iT
Eleven-year veteran Carson Wentz is filling in for the injured Murray.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bills vs. Texans takeaways: Josh Allen overcomes Houston defense in potential AFC championship preview
summary: Buffalo earned a dramatic 36-31 victory as Allen finally overcame his struggles in Houston and the Bills' defense delivered when it mattered most
full_text:
It is only Week 1, but the NFL might have already seen a preview of the AFC Championship Game. The season-opening duel between the Buffalo Bills and Houston Texans could very well go down as one of the campaign's most entertaining showdowns, too. The Bills' 36-31 triumph at Reliant Stadium had the feel of a postseason game, and it is only September.
The quarterbacks and defenses entered the game as the focal points, and while the defenses flipped pregame notions on their heads, the signal-callers lived up to expectations -- one for better, the other for worse.
Houston's defense and its past dominance over Josh Allen vanished entirely in the clutch. Cornerback Kamari Lassiter had a chance to haul in a potential game-sealing interception in the end zone but dropped it, opening the door for Allen to pull off his typical heroics and deliver the decisive touchdown.
Just over a minute later, a leaky Bills defense that capped the team's upside in 2025 delivered when it needed to the most. Third-round rookie Deone Walker and veteran edge rusher Greg Rousseau sacked C.J. Stroud on the final series, and the latter resulted in a fumble that put the game on ice and sealed Buffalo's five-point advantage. It was another collapse by Stroud and a positive sign for a Bills defensive front that, too often in the past, came up short in big moments.
Below are four more takeaways from the Bills' thrilling Week 1 victory.
Containing Josh Allen might be the single most difficult task for NFL defenses. The Texans had been masters at that craft heading into 2026 , though, with four wins in as many home matchups with the former MVP. The last two meetings featured two of Allen's worst performances against any opponent, as he completed a career-low 30% of his passes in 2024 and took a career-high eight sacks last year.
It was a completely different experience on Sunday.
Allen completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns, and he added 24 yards and two additional scores on the ground. It was vintage Josh Allen. What's more, he was clean in the turnover department and took a modest two sacks against the most fearsome edge rushing tandem in the league. Will Anderson Jr . got home on him once, but for the most part, Allen was in total command.
As he is wont to do, Allen delivered in the game's most tense moments, too. Down 31-30 with 3:24 to play, he orchestrated a 96-yard drive with a couple of chunk plays through the air, including what proved to be the game-winner: A 24-yard strike to Josh Palmer .
Allen is on the board. In games played in Houston, make it Texans 4, Allen 1.
There were signs that the Texans might have fixed their offense. C.J. Stroud threw for a pair of touchdowns on 26-of-38 passing and helped put 31 points on the board against a perennial Super Bowl hopeful. Perhaps he was turning the corner against elite competition.
But then the final drive happened, reminding everyone why the outlook for the former No. 2 overall pick's career is so tepid.
Within striking distance of a go-ahead touchdown, Stroud crumbled under pressure. He took two sacks in three plays on goal-to-go situations and coughed up the ball on the second. It was his second lost fumble of the day and sealed the Texans' fate.
Look back at the 2025 postseason, and the story is eerily similar. Stroud completed 51.9% of his throws during the playoffs and served up five interceptions while taking six sacks and fumbling five times. When the lights are brightest and the opponent is at their best, Stroud continues to lack what it takes to win games.
In March, the Texans traded Juice Scruggs and two draft picks to the Detroit Lions in exchange for David Montgomery . Six months later, that deal paid major dividends, even if it did not result in a win.
Montgomery was not the problem for Houston on Sunday. In fact, he was the primary reason why the home team even had a chance to win in the closing seconds. Montgomery ran for 60 yards and two touchdowns and caught three passes, including a touchdown reception. He was the best player on the Texans' offense all day.
Everything lines up for this to be a breakout year for Montgomery. He is already taking advantage of being the featured back -- a role that would have never been available to him on a full-time basis if he had stuck around in Detroit and served as the No. 2 option behind Jahmyr Gibbs . He also stands behind a retooled Houston offensive line that could help elevate a run game that suffered in 2025.
If Montgomery keeps this up, he will reduce some of the pressure on Stroud. That was not enough in Week 1, but it could be against most of the teams on the Texans' schedule.
Allen has a go-to receiver again. To be clear, DJ Moore was not the most productive target on the Bills' roster on Sunday. Instead, that was tight end Dalton Kincaid , who led all players with 130 receiving yards. But he commanded the largest target share on the squad and turned in a 100-yard game in his Buffalo debut. Moore also found the end zone.
Four different players hauled in catches of at least 19 yards, so it remains clear that this offense will thrive regardless of how many capable weapons Allen has by his side. He is that elite of a quarterback that he will put anyone in a position to find success. Moore gives him more upside out wide than he had in 2025, though, and that is a difference maker.
While Moore regressed in his final two years with the Chicago Bears and bottomed out in 2025 with career lows in receptions (50) and yards (682), he is already on pace to shatter those numbers. Such a promising first game in a new uniform is all the more impressive considering the caliber of defensive backs that lined up across from him.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Steelers offense struggles vs. Falcons: Who's to blame, what needs fixing
summary: Aaron Rodgers and Pittsburgh gained just 264 yards in a 20-13 win
full_text:
Mike McCarthy's debut as the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach will go down in the books as a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons . However, the win was somewhat overshadowed by a highly disappointing performance from Pittsburgh's offense.
All told, Pittsburgh's offense gained just 264 yards, going 3 for 13 on third down and 0 of 2 on fourth down. The Steelers had just two trips inside Atlanta's 20-yard-line and set up the Falcons' only touchdown when running back Jaylen Warren fumbled the ball inside Pittsburgh's 30-yard-line late in the first quarter.
Fortunately, the Steelers' defense made up for their offensive struggles. Facing third-string quarterback Cooper Rush , Pittsburgh's defense allowed just 238 yards and held Atlanta to 2 of 12 on third down. The unit forced two turnovers, including T.J. Watt's incredible pick-six that proved to be the game-winning score.
Pittsburgh's struggles against Atlanta were a collective failure. Aaron Rodgers (24 of 40 passing for 221 yards and a touchdown) wasn't his usual accurate self, and running backs Warren and Rico Dowdle didn't produce much splash while combining to run for just 61 yards on 18 carries.
The biggest issues, however, were Pittsburgh's offensive line woes and a DK Metcalf's performance that was nothing short of horrific.
Despite their promise, the Steelers' offensive line left something to be desired during training camp, and that continued to be the case on Sunday. The unit failed to open up consistent holes for Warren and Dowdle, and it often put Rodgers in harm's way. Rodgers was "only" sacked twice, but it would have been a considerably higher total against a better defense.
Metcalf, the Steelers' highest-paid offensive player, continues to not live up to his monstrous contract. Of his 10 targets, he caught just four passes for 40 yards. He failed to come up with multiple 50/50 balls and had one inexcusable drop over the middle that — had he caught the ball — would have been a big play.
This is why DK Metcalf is overpaid and needs to stop making fun of people online. Catch the ball bro. pic.twitter.com/vxLBlekQWc
As he has done throughout his career, Metcalf showed flashes of his brilliance during training camp, but only in spurts. His lack of consistency remains an issue.
Fortunately for the Steelers, there are tangible things they can do to improve their offensive output. And it starts with Metcalf.
As noted above, Metcalf was unable to come down with several combat catches, but some of the incompletions between him and Rodgers were the byproduct of Rodgers' accuracy issues. Metcalf was also the victim of a missed pass interference call on a deep sideline pass. He should — and needs to — improve.
Two positives from Sunday were the performances of Michael Pittman and Pat Freiermuth . Pittman, an offseason acquisition who missed practice time this summer with an injury, caught each of his three targets for 58 yards, including a 28-yard reception. Freiermuth, who was underutilized by former offensive coordinator Arthur Smith in 2025, caught each of his five targets for 46 yards, including Pittsburgh's only offensive touchdown.
FIRST TD OF THE SZN! 📲 Stream on NFL+: https://t.co/vqIDzYZB2x pic.twitter.com/n79eqeWNJN
One can assume that rookie Germie Bernard's role in the offense must increase in the coming weeks. Bernard, a second-round pick who had an impressive training camp and preseason, didn't receive a single target on Sunday while playing behind Roman Wilson , who caught half of his six targets for 26 yards. Wilson's so-so performance on Sunday may give Bernard a chance to have a bigger role sooner rather than later.
An improved passing game should open things up for Warren and Dowdle. That should, in turn, increase the Steelers' third-down success rate. On Sunday, Warren showed his resolve after his early fumble by averaging 4.6 yards-per-carry and accumulating 73 total yards on 15 touches. He also helped in pass protection .
As far as the offensive line, time should help the young but promising unit. Pittsburgh's offensive line includes two semi-experienced starters (right tackle Dylan Cook and right guard Spencer Anderson ) and a new left tackle in Troy Fautanu , who moved over from right tackle. There was a period on Sunday when Rodgers' blind side was being protected by rookie Max Iheanachor , who made his NFL debut when Fautanu was temporarily sidelined after suffering an injury scare.
Sunday wasn't a banner day for Pittsburgh's offense. But when you consider all of its new pieces — plus a new coaching staff — it wasn't the worst of starts for Rodgers and Co. Fortunately for them, they were the beneficiaries of a defense that showed it is capable of winning games when the offense isn't at its best.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Bears' wild win over Panthers ends with final score that's never happened before in NFL history
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, we have a scorigami!
full_text:
Before the season started, Ben Johnson said his goal was for the Chicago Bears to make some NFL history and they did exactly that in Week 1 -- just not the way Johnson was planning to do it. The Bears pulled off a wild 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, marking the first time in league history that a game has ended with that exact final score.
Yup, we got a scorigami in Week 1.
With just under four minutes left to play, the Bears were leading 52-37, and if that had been the final score, it wouldn't have been a scorigami. At that point in the game, Chicago was essentially trying to run out the clock, but was still able to get another touchdown after D'Andre Swift scored on a 28-yard run with just 3:40 left to play. That made it 59-37, which officially gave us the 1,096th unique final score in NFL history.
CHI 59 - CAR 37 🚨 SCORIGAMI 🚨 That is the 1096th unique score in NFL history, and the 1st of the 2026 season. pic.twitter.com/AXQo4c8nTy
Swift was a big reason why the Bears were able to put up nearly 60 points. The veteran led a rushing attack that totaled 291 yards with 124 coming from Swift and 100 coming from Kyle Monangai .
And let's not forget about Caleb Williams , who had a performance that will instantly put him in any the MVP conversation if anyone decides to have that conversation after Week 1. Not only did the Bears quarterback rush for 65 yards and two touchdowns, but he also threw for 269 yards and two more touchdowns.
Before the season started, Johnson said that one of his goals was to break the NFL record for most points scored per game (37.9) and although some people snickered at that, the Bears are now firmly on track to make it happen after one week.
"You've got 31 other teams coming to training camp saying, 'Our goal is to win the Super Bowl ,'" Johnson said. "I want more than that. I want to have the highest-scoring offense ever, which happens to be the 2013 Denver Broncos . I know how many points per game they scored (37.9), and I want to surpass them. I want shutouts. I want blowouts."
For the Bears, this is the first scorigami they've had in more than a decade. The last one they were involved in came all the way back in 2013 in a 54-11 loss to the Eagles . Before Sunday they hadn't won a game that ended with a scorigami since 2012.
As for the Panthers, this is the first time they've been involved in a scorigami since a 46-23 loss to the Buccaneers back in November 2020.
This actually marks the THIRD straight season that we've gotten a scorigami in Week 1. Last season, there were only four scorigamis all year and one of them came in the opening week when the Bills beat the Ravens 41-40.
author: John Breech

title: Deshaun Watson struggles in return as Browns leave Week 2 starting QB under evaluation
summary: Monken defended Watson following Cleveland's 34-10 loss but said the Browns will "evaluate everything" before facing Tampa Bay
full_text:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson made his first game appearance since October of 2024, and it certainly looked like he hadn't played in nearly two years. Watson struggled from the start, with ball security issues and a lack of offensive control. The 34-10 loss to the Jaguars saw Watson complete 73% of his passes for 205 yards, but he also threw a pick, fumbled and took five sacks.
Watson beat out Shedeur Sanders this offseason, and ultimately, the $230 million player earned the starting job. The decision fell under heavy scrutiny before the regular season started. While Monken came to Watson's defense after the loss, it was not the strongest endorsement for Week 2 or beyond.
"It wasn't all him, it really wasn't all him, I mean, that's unfair," Monken said after his head-coaching debut. "Certainly could've called it better, certainly could've played better around him. Certainly there's plays I'm sure he wish he had back ... we're not where we want to be ... It's not good enough, but it's just one and we got the right guys to fix it."
When asked whether Watson would be the starter for next week's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Monken said he needed to watch the tape and would "evaluate everything."
"It's unfair for me to comment on any one given player because it's never as bad as you think and it's usually never as good as you think," he said. "It's hard to say that right now, because we didn't play very well, we really didn't."
Monken kept repeating that the team as a whole needs to improve and that they will all come back tomorrow to address the film and move forward to the Buccaneers.
"I'm disappointed, but I'm fired up to get back to work," he said.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: LOOK: Derrick Henry makes NFL history during Ravens' Week 1 showdown vs. Colts
summary: Henry reached a major milestone after two first-half scores in Week 1
full_text:
Derrick Henry made NFL history during the first half of the Baltimore Ravens ' season opener against the Indianapolis Colts , moving to No. 3 on the NFL's list of career rushing touchdowns.
Baltimore's future Hall of Fame running back entered the season ranked fourth all-time in rushing TDs, but with 4:05 left in the opening quarter, Henry found paydirt from four yards out to give the Ravens a 14-7 lead. The score marked Henry's 123rd career rushing touchdown and tied him with Hall of Famer Marcus Allen for third all-time.
WALK IN TOUCHDOWN FOR DERRICK HENRY 3RD ALL TIME IN RUSHING TOUCHDOWNS #NFL #Ravens #RavensFlock #Colts #ForTheShoe pic.twitter.com/pB0CVqhNGT
In the second quarter, Henry passed Allen when he galloped 32 yards for his second touchdown of the half. The score showcased Henry's unique and vast skillset that includes his impressive vision, strength and closing speed.
THE KING!!!! 32-YARD TOUCHDOWN FROM @KingHenry_2 FOR HIS SECOND TD OF THE DAY!!! Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @ParamountPlus . pic.twitter.com/TDSbqCwka3
Henry wasn't done yet. In the fourth quarter, he tallied a "hat trick" when he reached the end zone again, this time from three yards out to give the Ravens a 38-16 lead. On the play, Henry quickly took Lamar Jackson's handoff before outrunning the entire defense to the left corner.
The score was Henry's 125th career rushing touchdown.
HAT TRICK FOR @KingHenry_2 👑 👑 👑 Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @ParamountPlus . pic.twitter.com/atdcMYowND
Allen, whom Henry passed on Sunday, retired after the 1997 season as the NFL's career leader in touchdown runs. Allen's career accomplishments also included being the MVP of Super Bowl XVIII, the 1985 NFL MVP, the 1993 NFL Comeback Player of the Year and the first player in history to have at least 10,000 rushing and 5,000 receiving yards.
Allen also held the record for the longest run in Super Bowl history (74 yards in Super Bowl XVIII) for 22 years, until then-Steelers running back Willie Parker broke it in Super Bowl XL.
Marcus Allen reversed the field...and left defenders in the dust. Rewatch the @Raiders Super Bowl XVIII victory for FREE with NFL GamePass: https://t.co/3yQtk4LcnE pic.twitter.com/W8YomtRy0V
Fellow Hall of Famers Emmitt Smith and LaDainian Tomlin are the only players who have more career touchdown runs than Henry. Smith, the NFL's career rushing leader, ran for 164 touchdowns during his 15-year career with the Cowboys and Cardinals . Tomlinson ran for 145 touchdowns over an 11-year career with the Chargers and Jets .
Henry entered Sunday's game 10th all-time in career rushing yards. He is less than 1,000 rushing yards away from becoming only the seventh player with at least 14,000 rushing yards.

title: 49ers rookie De'Zhaun Stribling to miss at least a month with ankle injury
summary: The No. 33 overall pick built considerable preseason momentum, but an extended absence could derail his Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers must chart a path forward without wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling , at least for a sizable part of the season. The exciting rookie sustained a deltoid strain in his ankle during the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, according to ESPN , and will miss at least a month.
There are no plans at present for Stribling to undergo surgery, but the wideout continues to seek opinions on the ankle issue, and the possibility of a procedure is still on the table. The 49ers reportedly plan to be cautious with their young asset.
This is a considerable blow to Stribling's Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign, which built momentum across his exhilarating preseason performances. Despite entering the league less heralded than his first-round counterparts, the Mississippi State product emerged as a candidate to contend for NFL honors. With one quiet game under his belt and a looming extended absence further reducing his 2026 sample size, he faces an uphill battle in making enough of an impact to command such recognition.
In the second quarter of the season opener, Stribling pulled up in the middle of a route after cutting toward the middle of the field. He brushed off Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie and appeared to tweak his left leg upon breaking away from the defender. He hobbled forward on one leg and went to the ground, holding his left leg in pain.
Trainers assisted Stribling into the medical tent, and he appeared unable to put any weight on the injured leg as he moved along the sideline. Following his examination, team personnel carted him into the locker room.
49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling headed to the medical tent with an apparent injury. 49ers vs. Rams is LIVE now on Netflix pic.twitter.com/m1JWw2pNiv
Stribling had not been healthy for most of the first half. He missed time earlier in the game with an ankle issue, which also required a trip to the medical tent. The 49ers initially listed him as questionable to return, but minutes later, he headed back onto the field and resumed play. The second injury occurred shortly thereafter.
During his curtailed regular-season debut, Stribling did not record any offensive statistics. Quarterback Brock Purdy did not target him at all in the passing game.
The unfortunate start to Stribling's career halts the momentum he built during a stellar preseason. The No. 33 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft was a training camp standout who earned playing time with the first-team offense in San Francisco's preseason games, and in those exhibition contests, he looked the part of an immediate difference-maker. Stribling turned 13 targets into 11 catches and 109 receiving yards and displayed a strong connection with Purdy. In a remarkable effort against the Tennessee Titans in August, Stribling became just the second receiver in the last decade to record seven receptions in the first 20 minutes of a preseason game .

title: Browns vs. Jags game to see temperatures up to 105 degrees: Will extreme heat play a factor in Jacksonville?
summary: It's a hot one as Cleveland and Jacksonville kick off their season in Florida
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns and Jacksonville Jaguars will need to drink plenty of water during today's game at EverBank Stadium , as feels-like temperatures are expected to reach 105 degrees. At kickoff, the temperature was 92 degrees at 1 p.m., with a real-feel temperature of 103 degrees.
The conditions can be dangerous for anyone at the game, from players to fans, and could cause issues for both teams during the Week 1 matchup. Expect players and staff to stay vigilant, hydrate, and stay cool as heat and humidity rise.
The Browns acknowledged the high temps, posting a video of the on-field thermometer at the game.
gonna be a hot one! 🌡️ pic.twitter.com/7k6ODAKnbL
Turf surface temperatures can be much hotter than air temperatures, but grass stays much cooler. Thankfully, the Jaguars have natural grass, which will help with these extreme temperatures.
Artificial turf traps the heat, getting 30-80 degrees hotter than natural grass. Hot temperatures on turf can increase the chances of heatstroke, dehydration and blisters.
The hottest NFL game on record was the 2000 Week 1 matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys at 109 degrees. The on-field temperature got as high as 130 degrees.
The game was called the "Pickle Juice Game" because the Eagles drank pickle juice to prevent cramping. Philly won the divisional matchup 41-14 under head coach Andy Reid. In 2008, Brigham Young University did a study confirming pickle juice can help stop muscle cramps.

Nobody in Vegas is expecting much from Arizona this year. In fact, they are underdogs in every contest on the calendar. RELATED: CARDINALS FANS ARE CONFIDENT IN DIRECTION OF FRANCHISE The biggest news is this new offense that LaFleur has installed. The concern going into this game was whether their shiny new toy, Jeremiyah Love, would play, and how the makeshift offensive line would perform. In the end, the Cardinals won 26-14. That first time on the field during a regular season game as a head coach feeling 🙂‍↕️ 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/xf5EVS13hQ — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 13, 2026 So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS Play of the day – With the Cardinals up 23-14, the Chargers took over on their own 20 with 4:44 left in the game. Los Angeles has a very potent offense and can drive the field and score. Penalties killed the Chargers and had a third-and-30. 12-yards to TE David Njoku made it fourth-and-18 from their own 23. They had to go for it. Herbert found Njoku open, who assumed he could make 20 yards out of the catch since, annually, his YAC numbers are exceptional. Instead, CB Will Johnson hauled him down after a gain of 15 and a turnover on downs. Head coach Mike LaFleur – Congrats, coach, on your first win in your first game as a head coach in the NFL. K Chad Ryland – As the Cardinals’ offense had numerous good drives, they just couldn’t convert that last pass or get a good run for another first down in order to get a new set of downs. Ryland came through again and again. He did miss that 54-yarder on Arizona’s second drive, but one more inch the other way and it wouldn’t have smacked the right upright. Very nice kickoff placement as well. Went 4 for 5 on field goals, 2-2 on PATs, and scored 14 points. Awesome day. Trey McBride + the end zone = Perfection 🤌 pic.twitter.com/yoZ9mHD15t — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 13, 2026 TE Trey McBride – This guy should just be on a template for every game. When does he have a bad game, or when does the opposing defense have a plan to thwart him? Right out of the gate 27-yards. Two possessions later, a nice 17-yard grab followed by a 10-yard reception. When the offense gets inside the 20-yard line, on any passing play, it should be coming his way. Led all receivers with 13 targets, nine catches for 95 yards, a 10.6 average per catch, and one TD grab. Opening drive – Wow. Is this going to be a weekly thing? Whoever called the game’s first play is a mastermind. 27-yards to TE Trey McBride was an eye-opener to everyone in the NFL. Arizona used a good mix of pass and running plays, including an 11-yard scramble by QB Jacoby Brissett and the 11-yard catch by WR Kendrick Bourne. Suddenly, the Cardinals were sitting on the eight-yard line with a first-and-goal. A three-yard run by RB Jeremiyah Love got them to the five. Then Love took it outside for the game’s first score. We request that every game this year have a similar opening drive, please. Dante Stills WE SEE YOU 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/XswhNMDnET — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 13, 2026 DE Dante Stills – All the defensive line talk was about whether DT Walter Nolen could remain healthy, the sacks of DE Josh Sweat, and how DT Roy Lopez was going to change the run-support game. Someone forgot to tell Dante Stills that he was still a good pass rusher and took away the job from DE Darius Robinson. The Chargers had started on their own 21 and had driven to Arizona’s seven. A loss by S Andrew Wingard, an incompletion, and a seven-year run now had Los Angeles with a fourth-and-goal at the three. The score was 10-7 Cardinals, so why not take the three? Ah, that Harbaugh bloodline. QB Justin Herbert dropped back to pass as LT Trey Pipkins was now playing left guard. Stills used his right hand and stunned Pipkins, then moved to the inside until he found Herbert for the sack. The Chargers had spent 10 plays and 4:56 of clock and ended up with nothing. LB Jack Gibbens – Not much has been said about the seasoned veteran, but he led all tacklers with seven and had a half sack as the game was winding down. Nice job. GEEKS Finishing by the offense – Making good drives by this new offense wasn’t an issue all game. Finishing was another matter. The Cardinals’ second possession at their own 30. Several good plays were 10 yards to Bourne, then 17-yard and 10-yard completions to McBride. Next, gains of only six yards plus an incompletion forced the offense to attempt a 54-yard field goal. On the next possession, Arizona spent 12 plays with 6:31 of clock only to die at the Chargers’ nine-yard line. This drive had touchdown written all over it. The Cards ended up with three instead of seven. The following two drives? At the LA 26 and a 44-yard field goal. A 15-yard facemask penalty on Marv Harrison pushed the offense back. The next drive: on the 15, and yet another field goal. Last three plays on this drive? Minus one rush, incompletion, incompletion. In the fourth quarter, after the blocked punt and TD by McBride, the defense provided an interception. Arizona was leading 23-14. This was the time to put a nail in that coffin, but instead, the offense sputtered, and after a sack by LB Troy Dye, it was time to punt. Watch for the Jacoby pass and stay for the Marv catch 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/cgJGVlO1aW — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 13, 2026 Limited usage of receivers – This offense plugged along and drove the field all game. But the big dogs in the receiver room hardly got any attention. Marv Harrison had just three targets, with one sensational catch for 33 yards. Michael Wilson had seven targets, but only five catches for 56 yards. Bourne had a decent game with eight targets, eight catches for 75 yards. If this offense is going to fly, these three need the ball more. Defensive pass rushers – Josh Sweat, two tackles, Darius Robinson one tackle, Walter Nolen one tackle, and L.J. Collier one tackle. Needless to say, this Cardinals’ defense is going to need more from these guys going forward. Bird Seed – Football is not a contact sport; it is a collision sport. Dancing is a contact sport LB Jordan Burke – Had a good position on most coverage situations and had an important sack. He did have that costly 24-yard pass interference call in the second quarter that got the Chargers out of a deep hole. Finished with three tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one QB hit. SIMI FEHOKO THE MAN YOU ARE 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/ysT2sORxwW — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 13, 2026 ST Simi Fehoko – Yes, the Cardinals’ receiver room is very deep. And players must find other jobs to get them on the field. Fehoko has been a really good special teams player as a sure tackler, but now? He can add kick blocking to his resume. The play was a designed stunt. LB Eku Leota pushed the left guard into the tackle as the long snapper blocked down as well. The upback, SS Kendall Williamson, also helped out to the left side, which opened a huge hole up the center. Fehoko came free up the middle. Williamson could have prevented the block, but tried to block another player, not seeing Fehoko loop. The result was a blocked punt and a Cardinals first down on the two-yard line. Two plays later, Brissett found McBride for six. Offensive line – Held up for most of the game and only allowed one sack. 116 yards on the ground isn’t anything special, but this group did give Brissett ample time to survey the field as he passed for 277…

summary: For the first time in a long time the Arizona Cardinals new head coach won his first game. While it wasn’t pretty, the results are all that matters for the Arizona Cardinals and they are 1-0 on the season. Jacoby Brissett was fine, Jeremiyah Love did enough but to everyone’s surprise the defense of the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: Head coach Mike LaFleur of the Arizona Cardinals takes the field before a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time in a long time the Arizona Cardinals new head coach won his first game. While it wasn’t pretty, the results are all that matters for the Arizona Cardinals and they are 1-0 on the season. Jacoby Brissett was fine, Jeremiyah Love did enough but to everyone’s surprise the defense of the Arizona Cardinals won the day. Mike LaFleur is the first head coach in decades to win his first game, but his defense under Nick Rallis won the day. The Arizona Cardinals defense had three sacks, the offense was able to do enough despite an impotent running game and the Cardinals sit at 1-0 on the season. Jacoby Brissett did enough to win a game, going 27/37 for 277 yards and one touchdown, but the defense was ready for no offense. The special teams was good! This team may be ready to win games! At least in week one.

title: Arizona Cardinals fans are confident in direction of franchise heading into 2026
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cardinals fans and fans across the country. We are back and we are… well mostly confident. That is what the results of the first confidence poll of the 2026 season tell us at […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cardinals fans and fans across the country. We are back and we are… well mostly confident. That is what the results of the first confidence poll of the 2026 season tell us at least. Which says something since our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook have no confidence in the Arizona Cardinals. Their win total sits at 4.5 heading into today, and they have the longest odds of any team to make the playoffs (+1600) in the NFL. They can change some of that today. The Cardinals open the season with a trip to Hollywood (Inglewood technically) to take on the Los Angeles Chargers and 67% of fans are confident the Cardinals are heading in the right direction. For me, I live in the world of cautious optimism. The Cardinals as an organization are more worrisome to me than who is the head coach, but there are things that both excite and worry heading into the season. The biggest excitement, the growth of LaFleur as a play caller, the biggest worry… Nick Rallis (really Michael Bidwill but that is out of my control). The more interesting take was how fans voted for the “X-Factor” for the season, and the majority think it is Walter Nolen. The breakdown is reverse how I would rank them for the top three. I think Brissett has to be the X-Factor and find a way to win close games. 0-6 and made no plays when he had the ball in his hands last year. Marv has to help that, he needs to be a threat at any point on the field. For Nolen, for me it is simply the fact that I don’t see enough talent around him for him to make a big enough impact. If the Cardinals defense had shown anything the last several seasons, then he would be the X-Factor because I think he could be a top 7 defensive tackle in the NFL if he can stay on the field this year. I just don’t know if he has the help necessary.

title: Falcons may lose DL Da’Shawn Hand for the season
summary: The Atlanta Falcons have lost Jalon Walker for the season, seen James Pearce Jr. suspended for eight games, started their third-string quarterback, and lost a road game featuring awful turnovers, tons of penalties, and missed field goals. We are only one week into the season and struggling to keep the vibes positive, and today’s news […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Da'shawn Hand #91 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action during the AFC Wild Card Playoff game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons have lost Jalon Walker for the season, seen James Pearce Jr. suspended for eight games, started their third-string quarterback, and lost a road game featuring awful turnovers, tons of penalties, and missed field goals. We are only one week into the season and struggling to keep the vibes positive, and today’s news is not going to help. Defensive lineman Da’Shawn Hand, who only played seven snaps in Week 1 before exiting with a knee injury, may miss the rest of the 2026 season with a torn quad. Hand was expected be a key piece of this run defense up front, and his loss would be a major blow to a promising defensive line. The #Falcons have lost Jalon Walker to a torn ACL, James Pearce Jr to a suspension and now Da'Shawn Hand. Another loss to the defensive front. https://t.co/btUORBC4Gs — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 14, 2026 Hand was one of the bigger (pun intended) signings of the offseason, and was added with an eye on improving an often shaky 2025 run defense. While the Falcons did a nice job in Week 1 with Brandon Dorlus, LaCale London, Gervon Dexter, and Maason Smith all playing well, that’s a four man rotation and none of them have the track record against the run that Hand does. Atlanta will almost certainly add either Zach Harrison or Zacch Pickens to the active roster and may scour free agency for more additions, simply because any attrition at all will leave this team perilously thin up front. We’ll have to hope for some miraculous good news, but given the way the season has gone already, I’m not expecting it. Devastated for Da’Shawn Hand.
author: Dave Choate

title: Falcons – Steelers recap: New faces, an all-too-familiar result
summary: Atlanta was dealt a tough hand going against the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road with a limited Cooper Rush under center. They looked at their cards, arched an eyebrow, and proceeded to play that lousy hand…well, let’s say not as well as you’d like. Rush was as abjectly bad, as you’d expect for a guy […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Cooper Rush #13 of the Atlanta Falcons hands the ball off to Bijan Robinson #7 during the second quarter of a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Atlanta was dealt a tough hand going against the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road with a limited Cooper Rush under center. They looked at their cards, arched an eyebrow, and proceeded to play that lousy hand…well, let’s say not as well as you’d like. Rush was as abjectly bad , as you’d expect for a guy who has been a career backup who didn’t have a job until training camp and had extremely limited first team reps and reportedly dealt with back spasms on Saturday. The Falcons were unwilling to expose Jack Strand to Week 1 game action as they look to develop him and ran one of the most conservative gameplans you’ll ever see for Rush, who had one sharp screen pass leading to a touchdown and a nice intermediate throw to Jahan Dotson sprinkled in between a lot of misses, near misses, and a hideous interception followed later by a pick six. I don’t think the team could have or would have asked for much more from Rush aside from a couple of decisions back, and the limits on the quarterback put limits on this offense that were very obviously difficult to overcome. That wasn’t all, of course. The offense and defense were both undone by penalties, with two defensive pass interference calls on A.J. Terrell and five holding calls (three accepted) on Atlanta’s offensive linemen outside of Ryan Neuzil. Special teams were a mixed bag after a summer that looked encouraging, with Nick Folk missing a pair of kicks, Jake Bailey missing the landing zone on a kickoff, and another penalty hurting Atlanta. It was the kind of effort that earns you a loss against a misfit Steelers squad, and the fact that Pittsburgh could only muster a touchdown win over this version of the 2026 Falcons does not bode well for them. That was largely because the defense, a question mark again heading into this game, held Pittsburgh to 20 points and just 264 yards, with both of Pittsburgh’s touchdowns coming off Rush turnovers. I’m upset primarily because this game was winnable in the right set of circumstances, but with a little distance from the effort I can only be so down about it. Rush starting was the kind of circumstance the Falcons exposed themselves two by having their top two quarterbacks being guys who have extensive injury histories, but needing him out there as the starter in Week 1 is absurd and unlikely enough as to simply be unlucky. It’s not hard to imagine more competent quarterback play making a huge difference, even if Chris Lindstrom needs to miss a little time with his concussion, and at least daydream of a decent season ahead. If they can get Michael Penix Jr. out there in Week 2, the passing game goes from an active liability to something approaching a danger. For all that, the penalties, the uncertainty around quarterback, and this team’s clearly future-looking ethos combine to make you think 2026 may once again be a year where flashes of hope and spells of frustration mellow into mediocrity. Perhaps that’s a bit harsh after one week. Though the coaching staff and front office do not bear the sins of those that came before them, these are still the Atlanta Falcons, and the Atlanta Falcons have been struggling so mightily and for so long that it’s difficult not to assume the first sign of another tough year is the sign. This team still has the talent and ability to right the ship, but it goes without saying that they’ll need to do so quickly to earn the fanbase’s trust and stay competitive, even with the NFC South once again looking like a mud pit. I hope we can look back at this as the day the Falcons fell prey to an inevitable tough road matchup with their third-string quarterback, rather than the start of something miserable and mediocre. On to the full recap. The Good Bijan Robinson is, of course, one of the very best players in football. He turned an errant Cooper Rush pass into seven yards early in this one, another errant Rush pass into a positive gain, and then a Rush screen and a couple of nice blocks by Charlie Woerner and Chris Blair into a touchdown just in the first quarter. He would finish with 21 carries for 83 yards and 8 catches for 90 yards and a touchdown, accounting for about two-thirds of Atlanta’s yardage. The Falcons need to be less one-dimensional, but Bijan gives you a fighting chance every week even if he’s your only dimension. Brian Robinson Jr. also ran reasonably well and was effective as a kick returner, which was nice to see. He averaged 32 yards on kick returns and had a couple nice runs, though he average just 3.4 yards per carry, and looks like the complement the Falcons were hoping to get when they scooped him out of free agency. The mar on his day was hesitation on his initial kick return, but everybody gets a Week 1 freebie. Drake London didn’t get much work, but made the most of it, with a six yard gain on a jet sweep and two grabs for 29 yards. He will have better weeks when he gets more chances, but he looked like the same top-tier player he’s always been when we saw him. I thought Jahan Dotson made a great first impression, which might seem like an odd thing to say about a player with one catch for 19 yards. You have to remember that Rush overshot him badly on his first interception for what should’ve been a quality gain in traffic, and that Dotson was the heads-up player who recovered Bijan’s screen pass fumble. I thought he showed the kind of awareness and ability to get open that should make him a legitimate factor with more competent quarterback play. The blocks from Chris Blair and Charlie Woerner on Bijan’s touchdown catch were fantastic. It beggars belief that Blair couldn’t get on the field for last year’s decimated offense when he’s a sure-handed target who can do that . Aside from one missed interception that went just beyond his hands, Divine Deablo looked really good in this one with a credited forced fumble and seven tackles. The fact that rookie linebackers Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. also showed up and delivered some big plays gives you real hope for this inside linebacker group as they try to navigate life post-Kaden Elliss. Atlanta put a lot of effort into stacking up their defensive interior, and I will say it looked like it paid off. Brandon Dorlus was really good in this one, and if he missed a sack, he still came up with multiple big stops and was aggressive and effective rushing from the interior. Maason Smith’s leaping effort on the second Steelers drive ensured they had to settle for three points, and it was both an impressive display of athleticism and extremely well-timed tip. He also had a coverage sack on Aaron Rodgers in the first quarter that was erased by an A.J. Terrell holding call. I thought LaCale London looked really good in this one, with a couple of big run stops and a non-stop motor that allowed him to keep impacting the game throughout. He’s slowly climbed the ladder with the Falcons and is now one of their essential interior defenders. Za’Darius Smith rocks. After retiring and un-retiring, dealing with awful loss, and working himself back into game shape, Smith came up with two sacks in this one to key a Falcons pass rush that was inconsistent but got home just enough to impact this game. What an effort from a player the Falcons are going to have to count on. The NFC South went winless in Week 1, so the damage here was not as bad as it could’ve been. The Panthers putting up 30-plus points, the Saints almost beating the Lions, and the Buccaneers hanging in against the Bengals may impact how good this one feels to you, though. The Ugly Cooper Rush looked like a third-string quarterback who hadn’t had enough time with this team, this offense, and also just was having…
author: Dave Choate

title: Falcons news: Week 1 is not the time to panic, despite Steelers loss
summary: Good morning Falcoholics. I was hoping to be able to kick off today’s post with a “happy victory Monday,” but after learning of Cooper Rush’s back spasms late last night (after Arthur Smith gave me flashbacks to his Falcons offense in Ohio State-Texas), I was pretty sure I wouldn’t have the opportunity. Sadly, I was […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey (5) talks to Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) after a game at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Good morning Falcoholics. I was hoping to be able to kick off today’s post with a “happy victory Monday,” but after learning of Cooper Rush’s back spasms late last night (after Arthur Smith gave me flashbacks to his Falcons offense in Ohio State-Texas), I was pretty sure I wouldn’t have the opportunity. Sadly, I was right, and the Falcons lost to the Steelers, 20-13. Yes, it’s not an ideal way to start of the season. But Week 1 is always a little weird, and we did see some reasons for optimism. Below, I’ll go through three reasons we shouldn’t overreact to this loss , and I’ll also give you one valid reason people still might overreact to this loss . As always, we’ll take a trip around the beat to learn more about what Kevin Stefanski and Falcons players had to say after the loss and what this loss means for the Falcons , and don’t miss our question of the day: What’s your good, bad, and the ugly from the Steelers game? Falcons Opening Drive: Week 1 is not the time for panic Week 1 of the NFL season is always full of surprises, and in many cases, disappointments. The Falcons’ loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers fits into the latter category. It wasn’t surprising that the Falcons lost given the pure chaos of its quarterback situation. Cooper Rush isn’t just third on the quarterback depth chart; he became the third injured guy in the quarterbacks room during the team’s Saturday walk-through before flying to Pittsburgh. Still, he got the start, and it wasn’t great. Rush finished the day completing 12 of 22 attempts for 143 yards, one TD, and two picks. The Falcons finished with 9 penalties for 96 yards, which is just abysmal, but at least some of that can likely be attributed to normal Week 1 sloppiness, and sloppiness can be corrected. I’m hoping that also explains Nick Folk’s bad day. Bijan Robinson was basically the entire offense, and that’s not sustainable — but Rush won’t be the long-term starter. Either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. should be healthy enough to start soon — and we should all cross our fingers that’s the case. Setting all those things aside, there are definitely reasons to take this loss in stride. It’s Week 1 And Week 1 is generally weird. I’d argue it’s been weirder for the Falcons this season than it is for most teams, which is even more reason to not put too much stock into it. Even if starters did get some preseason action, they’re often on a stricter pitch count than players down the depth chart. Teams don’t want to risk injury to their top players for a scrimmage, which I do get. But it means that many starters are still knocking off some rust in Week 1. And for players who did get plenty of run in the preseason, the overall caliber of competition is different once roster cuts are finalized. It’s just different. Jeff Ulbrich’s defense This game shouldn’t have been as close as it was given how poorly Rush played, but credit definitely goes to Jeff Ulbrich’s defense. The Falcons have a lot of last year’s sacks sitting on IR or the Commissioner’s Exempt List, plus several key players left this past offseason. But newcomer Za’Darius Smith had two sacks of Aaron Rodgers on Sunday, and he added two of the Falcons’ six quarterback hits. Mike Hughes had two pass breakups, while AJ Terrell, CJ Henderson, and Maason Smith each added one. The Falcons had a beautiful forced fumble by Cameron Thomas that was recovered by Divine Deablo, and Atlanta limited Aaron Rodgers to 24 completions out of 40 attempts, 221 yards, and one touchdown. Michael Penix Jr. will be ready to play soon He’s been physically cleared, and according to the Falcons’ media calendar for the upcoming week, the unnamed “starting QB” is on the Wednesday schedule, just like it was last week. Here’s hoping it’s this week that Penix Jr. feels ready to start. Maybe that will be the boost the team needs. But … we’re talking about the Atlanta Falcons So if you’re doubting them after Sunday’s loss in Pittsburgh, I don’t blame you. Now let’s get to the Falcons coverage you absolutely must read, watch, or listen to today. From our own Tre’Shon Diaz: Snap Reactions from Sunday’s loss to the Steelers . Special teams struggled, as did the offense, unsurprisingly. But the defense was a bright point. From Daniel Flick at the AJC: The Falcons were still in this game until TJ Watt snagged that pick-six . Instead of sneaking out a win, they took home a Week 1 loss for the ninth time in 11 years. (gift link) ESPN’s Marc Raimondi breaks down why a Week 1 loss to the Steelers isn’t the end of the world for the 2026 Falcons . Josh Kendall at The Athletic explains why the Falcons won’t have real hope for the 2026 season until they have a starting quarterback . (gift link) D. Orlando Ledbetter of Bowtie Sports shares what Steelers players had to say about Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson . AtlantaFalcons.com’s Will McFadden covers Kevin Stefanski’s postgame comments , including, “Hard to win on the road when you do those things.“ From the Falcoholic Community I understand why the Falcons didn’t want to put Strand out there — he’s a rookie UDFA who had taken zero practice snaps with the starters, he’s an UDFA out of a small program, and that Steelers defense was bringing it. Atlanta doesn’t need FOUR banged-up QBs. But I can’t argue with the fact that he couldn’t have been worse than Rush. From Falcon’66 : The Falcoholic’s Question of the Day The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly from the Steelers game: Let’s share ‘em. I’ll get us started: The Good: Bijan Robinson and the Falcons defense The Bad: Special teams The Ugly: Cooper Rush and the overall QB depth chart. Share your Good, Bad, and the Ugly from the Steelers loss in the comments.

title: NFC South Week 1 Standings: Everyone’s a Loser
summary: There’s nothing like NFC South football. It is reserved for only the most tormented fans. Trying to predict who comes out on top this year? You’ve got better luck predicting the Powerball numbers. Here’s the Week 1 NFC South Review: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1) Week 1 Result: Buccaneers 27 – Bengals 33 Week 2 Opponent: […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts in the secound half against the Chicago Bears at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s nothing like NFC South football. It is reserved for only the most tormented fans. Trying to predict who comes out on top this year? You’ve got better luck predicting the Powerball numbers. Here’s the Week 1 NFC South Review: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1) Week 1 Result: Buccaneers 27 – Bengals 33 Week 2 Opponent: Cleveland Browns The Buccaneers signed Baker Mayfield to a hefty extension that ties him to the team for four years earlier in the week. He did not reward them for it. Mayfield had a costly fumble that was returned for a touchdown and ended the game with no passing touchdowns and an ADoT (average depth of target) of 4.7. His rushing touchdown kept it close, but the offense’s sloppy day (4 lost fumbles) cost them the game. BENGALS WITH THE SCOOP AND SCORE!!! TBvsCIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XV5FjYppBP — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Todd Bowles’ defense managed to get a pick-six but was otherwise ineffective. That includes 1st-round pick Ruben Bain, who finished the game with 41 snaps but zero sacks or pressures. Tampa Bay will host the Browns in their home opener next week, who are coming off a tough loss of their own. New Orleans Saints (0-1) Week 1 Result: Saints 30 – Lions 31 Week 2 Opponent: Baltimore Ravens THE SAINTS CAN'T CONVERT THE TWO-POINT TRY AND THE LIONS WIN IT IN OVERTIME! WHAT A FINISH IN DETROIT! pic.twitter.com/u7OYvAgUHI — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 13, 2026 The Saints lost a nail-biter in overtime after they failed to convert their 2-point attempt. Tyler Shough and the offense looked completely discombobulated up until midway through the 3rd quarter. Once they started firing on all cylinders, the touchdowns came in bunches. It was at this point that the Saints defense started to malfunction and, after a strong start, couldn’t keep the Lions out of the end zone. The Saints have the potential to be a good team if they clean up their act; if not, their volatility will be their undoing. They’ll travel to Baltimore to take on the Ravens , who had a commanding win over the Colts. Carolina Panthers (0-1) Week 1 Result: Panthers 37 – Bears 59 Week 2 Opponent: Atlanta Falcons The Panthers offense put up 37, most in the division. They also gave up 59, which was the most in the division. The Panthers defense was no match for Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson’s high-powered offense. Bryce Young put up a fight, but costly offensive turnovers spoiled too many opportunities. Caleb Williams DOT to Cole Kmet for the TD 😮‍💨 Absolute seed in double coverage 🔥 (via @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/hUC5ka3bYn — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) September 13, 2026 Carolina invested heavily in its defense this offseason, including extending Ejiro Evero , a decision many questioned. Those investments failed to impact the game, and that extension looks even more questionable. Carolina will drive down I-85 to take on the Falcons, and look to extend their 3-game winning streak. Atlanta Falcons (0-1) Week 1 Result: Falcons 13 – Steelers 20 Week 2 Opponent: Carolina Panthers The Falcons quarterback room is a chiropractic marketing scam. Cooper Rush experienced back spasms the day before the game and did his best to play through it. The Falcons tried to run their offense exclusively through Bijan Robinson, but they couldn’t hide Rush forever. Two ugly interceptions, one of which was a pick-six, and the inability to push the ball more than five yards led to an upended offense. Nick Folk missing twice as many field goals in this game as he did in all of 2025 was the cherry on top. GIMME THAT 📲 Stream on NFL+: https://t.co/vqIDzYZB2x pic.twitter.com/KXo1i7gWZ6 — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) September 13, 2026 The defense played well and stifled the Steelers offense for most of the game. The Falcons defense will need to carry over that performance against a hot Carolina offense. Hopefully by then one of the Falcons’ preferred quarterback options has a working back. It feels good to be back in the trash heap known as the NFC South. No other division is quite like it. The 2026 division crown is anyone’s for the taking, and I have a gut feeling we won’t know the winner until the final week of the season.

title: Falcons vs Steelers Week 1 Snap Reactions
summary: Atlanta Falcons football is back (derogatory). The Dirty Birds’ offense and special teams were a mess and wasted a good defensive performance—a far too familiar story. Here are the Week 1 Snap Reactions: Special Teams comes out cold Nick Folk missed one kick in 2025, he doubled that in his Falcons debut. While the offense was […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers and Za'Darius Smith #55 of the Atlanta Falcons shake hands after the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Atlanta Falcons football is back (derogatory). The Dirty Birds’ offense and special teams were a mess and wasted a good defensive performance—a far too familiar story. Here are the Week 1 Snap Reactions: Special Teams comes out cold Nick Folk missed one kick in 2025, he doubled that in his Falcons debut. While the offense was a massive disappointment, the special teams left six points on the board. In a slugfest, those points are more critical than ever. Folk was able to go 2/4 on the day but fans wil once again worry about their kicker when he comes on the field for the next few games. It wasn’t just the field goal unit that struggled. The Falcons kickoff and kickoff return unit was sloppy. The Steelers opened with a nice return, which led to points on the drive. Later, Brian Robinson looked confused about whether to kneel or return the ball, which led to poor field position for the offense. The decision to keep Goodson on the practice squad and go with only two backs, despite his return experience, is puzzling. Craig Aukerman and Chase Blackburn have a lot to clean up Playing Cooper Rush was unwise Look, I understand wanting to protect Jack Strand, but the decision to go with Rush cut the Falcons offense off at the knees. The intermediate and deep areas of the field were inaccessible all afternoon, and outside of Bijan, none of the Falcons pricey investments could get going. The offense’s passing game became so repetitive that TJ Watt timed up a screen play and took it to the house for six. From ESPN Research: Cooper Rush's longest completion in terms of air yards today is 5 yards. On throws more than 5 air yards, Rush is 0-for-5 with an interception. #Falcons — Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) September 13, 2026 Bijan did his best to put the team on his back, but the workload led to some uncharacteristic mental mistakes. Ultimately, the death by a thousand cuts strategy didn’t work. Credit to Rees for at least putting together a game plan that moved the ball; unfortunately, they couldn’t overcome the quarterback play. Defense picked up where they left off Don’t let the score fool you; the defense did their job today. Turnovers put them in a bad spot, but when the Steelers were forced to drive the ball down the field, they struggled. The defense held the Steelers to 3/13 on 3rd down and 0/2 on 4th down. Maason Smith was a force from the first snap. He pushed the pocket and was a nuisance in the run game. The other Smith addition (Za’darius) also had a hell of a debut, coming away with two sacks. It wasn’t the best day from stars like Divine Deablo and AJ Terrell, but the defense showed they have enough talent to pick each other up when everyone isn’t firing on all cylinders. Za'Darius Smith with the SACK 😤 ATLvsPIT on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hPAMVvbmIy — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Looking ahead The Falcons played not to lose instead of playing to win. No, the team couldn’t foresee Cooper Rush’s back giving out the night before the game, but refusing to adjust to that information is what cost them. Heading into Week 2, the hope is that either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. will be ready to go but if that’s not the case, then it should be Jack Strand’s first start. After a summer of anticipation, fans are left feeling no better about the state of the team than they did in the final week of the 2025 season. The Carolina Panthers are on deck, and their offense was rolling against the Bears.

title: Falcons at Steelers instant recap: A new season features a familiar sort of falling short
summary: The Atlanta Falcons came into this game with a third string quarterback, which increased the degree of difficulty significantly. They looked like a team starting their third string quarterback. Because the Steelers are shaky themselves and because the defense largely was game, Atlanta hung around in this one until very late. But the team looked […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers throws a pass against the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons came into this game with a third string quarterback, which increased the degree of difficulty significantly. They looked like a team starting their third string quarterback. Because the Steelers are shaky themselves and because the defense largely was game, Atlanta hung around in this one until very late. But the team looked like a squad clinging to experience instead of upside and hoping for the best, and they got what they asked for, with Rush assuredly throwing them out of the game throughout this one and Bijan Robinson and the D battling valiantly to make up for that. The whole game felt like that. The Falcons would get a key stop and the offense would set up a field goal try that didn’t convert or turn the ball over, with special teams and the offense falling short again and again in this one. It was once again an example of this team having one phase hold up their end of the bargain and the other two fall short, and for what seems like the hundreth time in the past few seasons, it led to a tough loss against a team that would’ve been beatable if all cylinders were firing. It’s difficult to say much more about a game that felt tough going in and was tough to watch throughout. Rush looked every bit like a limited quarterback injury-wise and a limited quarterback skill-wise, and Nick Folk missing two kicks with some other miscues on special teams and penalties hurting the Falcons on defense sounded the death kneel for Atlanta. They never beat Pittsburgh, basically, and they ruined any shot they had at winning this one. Where the Falcons go from here is anyone’s guess, but they have to figure out a quarterback solution and settle into something better to avoid 2026 being something other than another 2o25, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, 20219, and 2018. For those of us who are beyond weary of watching this team lose, hopefully this proves to be an uncharacteristic, ugly Week 1 for the next era of Falcons football, rather than more of the same. Here’s the drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter Nick Folk kicked things off by…kicking things off, with the Steelers returning it to about the 33. Aaron Rodgers was immediately pressured and threw it away. Jaylen Warren took it about four yards going left. Rodgers badly overthrew DK Metcalf on third down. Punt, and the Falcons got it after it bounced out at the 16. Cooper Rush handed off to Bijan Robinson for a yard going left. A screen to Bijan got about three yards. On third down, Rush took a look, pumped the ball, and was swarmed by the Steelers pass rush for a sack. Punt, and Jake Bailey got the Steelers back around their own 30. Rico Dowdle plunged ahead for six yards. Rodgers threw a short pass to Pat Freirmuth on second down and he bullied through contact for 10 yards and a first down. A quick slant to Metcalf picked up six yards. Rodgers had an eternity in the pocket and found Michael Pittman for 21 yards. One yard gain on the ground followed. On second down, the Falcons blitzed and tipped Rodgers’ pass into the air, after which it fell incomplete. Rodgers was under a ton of pressure on third down and Maason Smith tipped the pass into the air, where it once again fell incomplete. The Chris Boswell field goal was good to make it 3-0 Steelers. Brian Robinson Jr. hesitated taking the ball out of the end zone and ended up getting it back to about the 22 yard line. Bijan took a poorly throw ball from Cooper Rush and made a one-handed grab, turning it into about a seven yard gain. Bijan then took it about four yards on second down for a first down. Rush then threw another very quick one to Bijan for six more yards. Brian Robinson then did a nice job plunging ahead for six yards and a first down. The bobbled snap turned into a handoff to BRJ for a yard. Bijan then took it a yard or so, but Matthew Bergeron was called for holding. Rush then took a deep shot to Kyle Pitts and it was broken up by Rayshawn Jenkins, as it was thrown a bit short. Rush then missed Jahan Dotson on a sideline ball. Punt, and a fair catch at the 13. Rodgers hit DK Metcalf against Mike Hughes for nine yards. Warren then plunged ahead for two yards and a first down. Warren was stopped by Kendal Daniels for a minimal gain. A swing pass to Warren went nowhere, was fumbled, and the Falcons recovered after Mike Hughes and Cameron Thomas knocked it out and Divine Deablo recovered. The Falcons got a couple yards on first down, but the toss to Brian Robinson went nowhere after Kyle Pitts missed a block. A screen pass to Bijan Robinson went for a touchdown after a couple of nice blocks from Charlie Woerner and Chris Blair and Bijan got loose. Falcons 7, Steelers 3. The kickoff got to about the 30 yard line. Rodgers had zero chance on the next one, with Maason Smith coming in for the sack, but a defensive holding call on A.J. Terrell erased that good work. Dowdle was then tackled after three yards. 2nd Quarter Brandon Dorlus ate Dowdle for lunch on second down. A.J. Terrell was called for pass interference on a Rodgers deep shot to Roman Wilson. Rodgers then went for a touchdown shot to Metcalf, but Hughes did a nice job in coverage to prevent it. Metcalf then had a first down catch that popped out, but was ruled a fumble that he recovered. Dowdle then got four yards. A quick pass to Freirmuth went for a yard, but Daniels crushed him. Rodgers had to throw it away under pressure from LaCale London. The field goal try was good to make it 7-6 Falcons. The Falcons had a killer return by Zachariah Branch erased by a Josh Woods holding call, and it looked pretty borderline. Rush then threw an ugly interception to Jaquan Brisker, missing badly over Jahan Dotson’s head. A trick play with multiple handoffs and a toss back to Rodgers resulted in a quick route to Warren for a first down. Seven yards followed. Rodgers was then low on his second down pass. On third down, Rodgers found Freiermuth for a touchdown. 13-7 Steelers. Bijan took it five yards, and then spun out of contact for a first down. Rush then tried to escape and was sacked on first down, but a holding call on the Falcons superseded it. On second down, Rush hit Bijan for about nine yards. Bijan was hit as he rushed, fumbled, and fell on it for a loss of six. Punt. Warren got maybe a yard, with Dorlus on the tackle. Rodgers scrambled on the play for a close to a first down, but a holding call on the Steelers backed it up to 2nd and 16. Rodgers threw a ball low and it was incomplete. A delay of game then made it 3rd and 20. On third down, Rodgers got away from pressure and threw it away, but Metcalf shoved Terrell on the play as well. Punt. A goose through the air to Drake London went for eight yards. Bijan then took it for three yards and a first down. On first down, Bijan was hit quickly and picked up a yard. A quick pass from Rush to London went for close to a first down, but Chris Lindstrom got hit with holding. Rush was had his pass tipped and it fell incomplete. A quick screen to Robinson got about six yards. The Falcons ran out the clock on fourth down to set up a long field goal try by Nick Folk, but he just missed it. A quick pass to Warren was taken down for no gain by Deablo. A quick shot to Wilson then got five yards. A third down pass to Metcalf went for a first down, but he was called for an offensive pass interference again. On 3rd and 15, Roman Wilson sat down in the middle of the zone and got the first down on a pass from Rodgers. Rodgers then spiked it into the ground with the pressure coming. Warren then lost multiple yards. Rodgers then took a touchdown shot to Wilson working against Hughes, but Hughes did a nice job and managed to keep it from…

title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Steelers
summary: The Atlanta Falcons kick off the 2026 NFL season against a formidable foe in the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Falcons have never won a game in Pittsburgh, and the last two times they opened the season against the Steelers, they couldn’t beat a pair of backup quarterbacks: Justin Fields (2024) and Dennis Dixon (2010). If the […]
full_text: The Atlanta Falcons kick off the 2026 NFL season against a formidable foe in the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Falcons have never won a game in Pittsburgh , and the last two times they opened the season against the Steelers, they couldn’t beat a pair of backup quarterbacks: Justin Fields (2024) and Dennis Dixon (2010). If the Falcons are going to swing a historic road win on Sunday, they’ll have to do it with a backup of their own. Here are five Falcons to watch in this potential history-making opener. Cooper Rush It starts with the backup quarterback, Cooper Rush, who will be under center this Sunday. With starter Tua Tagovailoa nursing an oblique strain, and Michael Penix not ready to return as he works his way back from an ACL tear, Rush becomes the next man up. The Falcons’ game plan for Rush is unlikely to shift dramatically from their strategy for Tua . Still, it remains an open question of how well Rush can execute a quick-rhythm, low-risk passing script. Rush executed a similar mandate in Dallas behind strong run games featuring Ezekiel Elliott and Tony Pollard while force-feeding CeeDee Lamb. The Falcons have the requisite firepower in Bijan Robinson and Drake London to shoulder that same workload. However, during his brief 2025 stint in Baltimore, even Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers couldn’t mask Rush’s limitations as an injury fill-in. Rush needs to prove he remains a dependable option as he could be playing for his job. Atlanta is currently carrying four quarterbacks, which looks prescient today, but once other injuries spring up elsewhere on the roster, carrying four signal-callers will quickly become a luxury. If Rush fails to spearhead an efficient, competitive offense vs. Pittsburgh, then he’ll become very expendable once Tua and Penix return. Bijan Robinson Rush’s presence in the lineup means Robinson will have to shoulder the burden of the offense. The Falcons need to feature Robinson as much as possible in a run-heavy attack. Robinson had an up-and-down day in his first and only battle with the Steelers back in 2024. A fast start and a strong third quarter of production, however, were not enough to prevail over the Steelers that Sunday. This weekend, the Falcons will need Robinson to put together four good quarters of play as both a runner and a pass-catcher. There’s no doubt that until the Falcons’ quarterback situation gets settled, Robinson will be the focus of the team’s offense, and also opposing defenses. This puts tremendous pressure on the Falcons’ offensive line to control the line of scrimmage to get Robinson going. Jawaan Taylor The lineman who is facing the most pressure, literally, will be right tackle Jawaan Taylor, who will spend most of the afternoon lined up across from future Hall of Famer T.J. Watt. This game marks Taylor’s official debut in Atlanta, replacing retired right tackle Kaleb McGary. McGary’s 2024 outing against Pittsburgh was a disaster, largely due to a questionable scheme from former offensive coordinator Zac Robinson that left him stranded on an island against Watt. New head coach Kevin Stefanski cannot repeat that mistake with Taylor, especially given the latter’s tendency for procedural penalties. He was flagged for false starts in both preseason series he played, in his incessant attempts to get a jump on the snap count. That problem will only get exacerbated against a speed rusher of Watt’s caliber in a hostile road environment. Any pre-snap penalties will easily derail Atlanta’s run-heavy, quick-game approach before it even gets off the ground. Cameron Thomas The Falcons hope their own defensive line can help decide the battle in the trenches, and defensive end Cameron Thomas figures to be a big part of that campaign. Thomas flew under the radar as a free-agent addition, but is now a starter and a potential major factor in why the Falcons saw a player like Zach Harrison as expendable . Thomas spent 95 percent of his pass-rush snaps on the left side facing the right side of opposing offensive lines in the preseason, according to PFF . With the Steelers breaking in a pair of new starters in right guard Spencer Anderson and right tackle Dylan Cook, left-sided players like Thomas have a great opportunity to take advantage. A strong day from Thomas and the rest of the Falcons defensive line to stymie the Aaron Rodgers-led Steelers offense. A.J. Terrell Cornerback A.J. Terrell will also be essential to containing Rodgers and Pittsburgh’s passing attack as he draws the primary assignment on D.K. Metcalf. Sunday marks their fourth career matchup, though the previous three came during Metcalf’s tenure in Seattle. Keeping Metcalf in check was critical to stopping the Steelers’ passing attack last year. In games where Metcalf hit at least 60 yards receiving, Pittsburgh sported a 4-0 record. In games where Metcalf was held under 60 yards, they were 5-6. That Metcalf-centric focus explains why Pittsburgh bolstered its receiving corps with Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, giving the Steelers viable options if Metcalf is neutralized. But Atlanta’s defensive strategy still begins and ends with containing Metcalf, because if he breaks loose, keeping a lid on this offense becomes nearly impossible. If that happens, chances are the Falcons will have to wait another eight years for another shot at a win in Pittsburgh. However, a road win in Pittsburgh with a backup quarterback would mark an incredible debut for the Stefanski Era. Are these the five Falcons that will lead the team to a history-making upset, or is more heartbreak on the horizon? Can you name any more Falcons that intrigue you in this season-opening matchup?
