title: Browns vs. Jaguars: 4 winners, lots of losers as Cleveland gets destroyed
summary: The 2026 NFL season has finally arrived. The Cleveland Browns are entering the year with high hopes, with a new head coach and a new offensive and defensive coordinator, and plenty of new players dotted among the roster. Their first game of the year is against a very good team, the Jacksonville Jaguars, who went […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 13: Mason Graham #94 of the Cleveland Browns reacts after a play during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cleveland Browns on September 13, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2026 NFL season has finally arrived. The Cleveland Browns are entering the year with high hopes, with a new head coach and a new offensive and defensive coordinator, and plenty of new players dotted among the roster. Their first game of the year is against a very good team, the Jacksonville Jaguars, who went 13-4-0 last season and took home the AFC South Division crown. Going into the playoffs, they had the #3 seed and were one victory away from getting the #1 seed and a bye in the first round of the postseason. RELATED: BROWNS-JAGUARS NEED TO KNOW The Browns were on the other side of the spectrum. Winning just five games was all they mustered, and two of those wins were the final games of the season. The Jaguars had the league’s #1 run defense during that great season, but lost a 27-24 heartbreaker to the Buffalo Bills. gonna be a hot one! 🌡️ pic.twitter.com/7k6ODAKnbL — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 That meant the Browns faced an uphill battle against Jacksonville. Plus, it was on the road. In the end, Cleveland got taken to the woodshed in a 34-10 loss that was never close and was all Jaguars. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES (Winners) KR Raheim Sanders – Because Jacksonville scored so many touchdowns, that allowed a ton of returns. Have to hand it to the Rocket; he impressed on every kickoff return. Three kickoff returns for 130 yards with 43.3 yards per return. big time return for Rocket #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/tDwhSBehu6 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 The 74-yarder in the third quarter was electric and had one man to beat. In the second quarter, he scampered for 31 yards, plus the 37-yarder in the fourth quarter. Keep in mind, Sanders was not the starting kickoff man. That was Dylan Sampson, who became injured early in the game. LB Carson Schwesinger – No matter what the scoreboard shows, Schwesinger still gets behind the ball carrier to drag him down. He did have loose coverage in the second quarter on tight end Brenton Strange for the touchdown. Led the team in tackles with 10, one QB hit, and one tackle for loss. Denzel Boston with his first NFL TD #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/2EzcBkQMF5 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 WR Denzel Boston – Okay, somebody has to have had a great play, and that was the rookie Boston, who waited all game to show his talent. Excellent catch on the deep ball for the touchdown. Four targets, two catches for 59 yards, a 29.5-yard average per reception for the rookie. More to this kid, please. K Andre Szmyt – He did everything you wanted your kick to accomplish: 1 for 1 in field goal attempts, 1 for 1 on PATs, scored the game’s first points for Cleveland to avoid the shutout, and the few kickoffs he had were placed well. FROWNIES (Losers) Third-down efficiency – One for eight isn’t going to get any offensive unit anywhere. QB Deshaun Watson – Dreadful for most of the game, and it began early. In the Browns’ first possession, they were doing really well on offense: a 14-yard pass completion, a 4-yard run, a 9-yard pass completion, a 5-yard run to the Jags’ 33-yard line. Then Boom! Watson threw it right to LB Foyesade Oluokun, who wasn’t even covering a man and just grabbed the pass intended for WR Jerry Jeudy. Eight plays later, touchdown Jacksonville. On the Browns’ next possession on a third-and-six, Watson was almost picked off again while trying to hit TE Harold Fannin. Later, Watson fumbled, but he recovered it and killed a third-and-10. What exactly was that lame duck throw in the second quarter that went deep to WR KC Concepcion? The TD pass to Boston with 1:52 left in the game was vintage Watson. Fantasy managers rejoice 📈 @CPW11_ | #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/RNEqOzhhm4 — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 CB Myles Harden – Still can’t find a play where Harden was in position to bat a ball away. The Jaguars completed passes all day on him. Jacksonville’s first touchdown was a great ball thrown to WR Parker Washington, who beat Harden to the corner. Yes, it was a great throw, and yes, it was an acrobatic catch. But the receiver had five steps on Harden because he fooled him off the initial break and then was wide open. Struggled all game and had just two tackles. Penalties – This goes right into the “You’ve got to be kidding” file folder. How is this for a sequence of events? Cleveland has the ball right before the half. First down on their own 30, Watson hit Jeudy for 20 yards, then an 11-yard pass to the Rocket. Now, first down at Jacksonville’s 39 with 51 seconds remaining. Incomplete pass to WR Isaiah Bond, with a holding call on LG Zion Johnson. Now, first-and-20. False start by RT Tytus Howard. First-and-25. Short pass to Jeudy. Next play: holding on Johnson after Watson scrambled for nine. Second-and-34, now at the Cleveland 37-yard line. Nine-yard pass completion followed by an incomplete pass to end the half and no chance of a field goal. Game total: 11 penalties for 75 yards. If this team’s target practice is aimed down, you will hit your foot every time. Pass defense – Or should we say lack of? This defense ranked #3 in pass defense last year. Today, they will begin the season at or near the bottom. Jags QB Trevor Lawrence completed passes almost at will. Look at how many intermediate to long passes were completed: 32 yards, 30, 22, 18, 16, and 14. A total of 10 Jacksonville receivers caught a pass. Nine completions were converted for a first down, including a second-and-18 for 22 yards, a third-and-six for 14 yards, and a second-and-19 for a 32-yard TD. Several missed tackles by CB Tyson Campbell, Harden giving way too much cushion, and S Ronnie Hickman taking his time to get over and help out guys like Harden, then overran the coverage on WR Jacobi Meyers in the third quarter for the TD. Meeting in the middle > #CLEvsJAX on CBS + @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/XTofpkfl7U — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 Offense – Absolutely a horror show. The offensive line gave up five sacks as Jag defenders were in Watson’s face for the majority of the game. Watson didn’t help his line by dropping back five to eight yards after a shotgun snap. One interception, a dropped interception, two fumbles (one lost), 0-2 in the Red Zone, 87 total yards rushing, disgusting on third downs and 1-2 on fourth, only 14 first downs, all of these projected weapons which ended up with minimal yards: Fannin two catches, Denzel Boston two catches, Jeudy two catches, Bond zero catches, and Concepcion four receptions. Milk Bones – Any last requests before football season begins? DT Mason Graham – Was decent up the middle and kept his gap responsibility. Put decent pressure on passing downs, but had two really good runs go right past him. Mason ties him up 💪 #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/HJHB8O0DyG — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 His run defense was really good, considering. Had the game’s only sack in the second quarter when he got the inside on C Robert Hainsey and was the first to Lawrence on a third-and-one that forced a punt. In the third quarter, he got to RB Bhayshul Tuten in the backfield for a four-yard loss with 13:19 left. Finished with five tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one QB hit. DE Jared Verse – The TV announcers didn’t call his name much unless they were discussing the Myles Garrett trade. Didn’t see the huge pass rush from Verse, but keep in mind he was going against LT Anton Harrison, who kept him in check. Finished with four tackles, zero sacks, zero QB hits, and one tackle for loss. Who were your winners and losers from Week 1’s…
author: Barry Shuck

title: Browns vs. Jaguars: 10 takeaways from Week 1 blowout
summary: The Cleveland Browns were destroyed by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. It was so bad that the Jags pulled most of their starters early in the second half of the game. RB Dylan Sampson left the game and didn’t return, while OL Zion Johnson was hurt but returned quickly. […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13: (L-R) Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns and Deshaun Watson #4 take the the field for warmups prior to the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns were destroyed by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. It was so bad that the Jags pulled most of their starters early in the second half of the game. RB Dylan Sampson left the game and didn’t return, while OL Zion Johnson was hurt but returned quickly . The rest of the takeaways from the game are all negative toward the Cleveland side of things in a game where it seemed far worse than the 34-10 final score. Big offseason moves = Tanking? All offseason, the Browns seemed to make moves that indicated that they didn’t want to fully tank. Even the trade of Myles Garrett only happened because they got Jared Verse back in the deal. GM Andrew Berry extended the contracts of Denzel Ward and Grant Delpit instead of trading away talented players, and hired a veteran coach (even if it is his first NFL head coaching job) instead of a youngster. However, the biggest moves may have actually indicated some level of tanking plans in Cleveland. First, hiring an unproven head coach, Todd Monken, after no other team had given him that shot despite a few decades of quality offensive coordinator jobs. Second, not only keeping Deshaun Watson but allowing him to compete for the starting quarterback job. Cutting Watson was unreasonable, but they could have just said he’d be the veteran backup in his final year with the Browns. Third, not bringing in an actual veteran quarterback with recent success in the NFL. Finally, not keeping Jim Schwartz as the defensive coordinator and/or giving him the top job. Those four big moves look Mike Rutenberg’s defense lacking… identity Couldn’t stop the run, couldn’t defend the pass, couldn’t get pressure. Add to that a couple of blown assignments and wide-open receivers all day long, and people are going to have questions about the new Cleveland defensive coordinator. Trevor Lawrence had a 150.6 QB rating against Rutenberg’s defense, with DT Mason Graham getting the only sack of the day. Jaguars bringing blitzes or extra men in the box versus Deshaun Watson One of the things about not having quality QB play is that defenses can just load up the box and bring run blitzes on the way to the quarterback. Trailing early didn’t help, but the poor quarterback play didn’t help RB Quinshon Judkins either. With 12 carries for 33 yards, Judkins’ return from injury was far from positive. System or talent? A question that we won’t have an answer for, unless you believe it is already “both,” for a few weeks is whether this poor performance is because of Monken and the coaching staff or because of the talent Berry did or didn’t bring in. Instead, right now it was all bad. Mason Graham doubles his rookie sack total After a half sack last year, Graham was one of the few decent spots on the defense and his one sack now doubles last year’s total. 3 straight penalties late in 1st half – Wow This will go into the next takeaway, but the late first half, when the drive got going and they were close to field goal position, was impressively frustrating. Then they added another hold shortly thereafter. From field goal position to throwing a Hail Mary that didn’t have much of a shot, a very bad series of events. The Todd Monken hire is gonna be under the microscope When the Browns decided to hire Monken, many fans were excited that the team went from a young, analytics guy to a gruff, no-BS old-school coach who wouldn’t let the team fail on the details. In Game 1, the team failed in pretty much every way that they could. On top of that, whether it was the halftime question or after the game, Monken’s responses were basically the same as what Cleveland fans have heard from their former head coach, Kevin Stefanski. ‘We’ve got to call it better. We’ve got to play better.‘ Monken also defended Watson’s play in a way that didn’t seem to fit what the fans and media saw on the field. Operations were crap – double-digit penalties The one thing that Monken focused on all offseason was the “operations.” Whether it was the 11 penalties for 75 yards or the need to use timeouts because plays weren’t getting going quick enough, the “operations” were far from good enough. “Got to coach better. Got to scheme better. Got to play better.” That has been the focus all offseason, and the Browns were still terrible at it. One big play to Denzel Boston probably keeps Deshaun Watson as the starter – No sarcasm While many were calling for Shedeur Sanders to replace Watson throughout Week 1, this play is likely to keep Watson as the starter: Denzel Boston with his first NFL TD #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/2EzcBkQMF5 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 That felt true when the play happened; then, listening to Monken after the game, where he wouldn’t say anything that would indicate he was blaming Watson for the performance versus the Jaguars, I’d assume Watson is the starter until he is physically unable to play or his teammates turn on him. This play is one that Monken will likely use as a reason for that decision. So tough for fans (I know, I am one) We have the greatest fan base in the world, but the Browns have tried to kill it. While the score wasn’t as bad as it could have been, Week 1 felt like one of the worst performances from a Cleveland team. Not once against Jacksonville did the team look like they had a shot at making their opponent concerned at all about the outcome of the game. Feels like one of the quickest “This season is going to be terrible” experiences in Browns history. I hate it for you; I hate it for me. What are your takeaways from Week 1 for the Browns? title: Cleveland Browns vs. Jacksonville Jaguars recap: An embarrassing display
summary: The Cleveland Browns were losing 31-0 early in the third quarter. That tells you all you need to know about the Browns’ first game of the season, as they ultimately ended up losing 34-10. Once again, we experienced another empty half of points from QB Deshaun Watson, who set the tone early by throwing an […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 13: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars throws a pass during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cleveland Browns on September 13, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns were losing 31-0 early in the third quarter. That tells you all you need to know about the Browns’ first game of the season, as they ultimately ended up losing 34-10. Once again, we experienced another empty half of points from QB Deshaun Watson , who set the tone early by throwing an interception on the team’s first drive. The defense, including newcomer DE Jared Verse , was a complete no-show, aside from maybe DT Mason Graham . Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Jaguars Cleveland received the opening kickoff, with RB Dylan Sampson taking it out to the 40 yard line. On the first play, QB Deshaun Watson tossed it to TE Blake Whiteheart for a simple, open throw that went for 14 yards past midfield. After a short run, WR KC Concepcion got his first NFL touch with a 9-yard completion off of a quick hitter. After a run by RB Quinshon Judkins went for 5 yards, Cleveland faced a 2nd-and-5 at the 28 yard line. Watson went playaction and tried to zip a pass in to WR Jerry Jeudy , but it was picked off by LB Foyesade Oluokun , who returned it 22 yards to the Jaguars’ 41 yard line. It looked like the same pick he threw in training camp multiple times, not seeing the underneath linebacker. Now that's a start! @foyelicious | #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/SjAhtWZBqL — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 After a couple runs by the Jaguars to move the chains, QB Trevor Lawrence found himself in the same position as Watson did. Instead of throwing an interception, on 3rd-and-7, and waited and found WR Parker Washington open for a diving 30-yard touchdown grab along the right side to give Jacksonville a 7-0 lead. Fantasy managers rejoice 📈 @CPW11_ | #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/RNEqOzhhm4 — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 The Browns didn’t have as good of starting field position on their second drive, as a holding penalty on the return unit started them at the 17 yard line. After two run plays only netted four yards, on 3rd-and-6, Watson had time, then bailed to his left and was nearly intercepted by Oluokun again. Cleveland punted, and the Jaguars were set to start their next drive at the 26 yard line. The Jaguars got nice grabs along the perimeter by WR Brian Thomas and Washington to get near midfield. Even when Jacksonville had bad plays — a 2nd-and-20 due to a false start and an illegal forward pass — Lawrence just casually found Washington open for 22 yards. Then, after hurrying up to the line, Lawrence hit Thomas for 18 more yards to set up 1st-and-goal at the 9 yard line. A few plays later, off of a quick playaction, Lawrence gunned it through defenders to WR Josh Cameron for a 5-yard touchdown to make it a 14-0 lead with two minutes left in the opening quarter. Cleveland’s next drive didn’t go any better. They immediately faced a 3rd-and-10, and Watson let the pressure get to him as he was sacked by DE Josh Hines-Allen and also fumbled, for a loss of 8 yards to end the quarter. Jaguars defense is COOKIN' 👨‍🍳 CLEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/nAZFaaUoHJ — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Jaguars The Jaguars’ smooth operation continued in the second quarter, using a mix of jet sweeps and quick outs to receivers to get to midfield. Jacksonville continued driving forward, but ended up facing a 4th-and-short at the 29 yard line. They could have gone for it and probably would’ve gotten it, but instead they sent K Cam Little out for a 47-yard field goal to give the Jaguars a three-possession lead at 17-0. On the first play of the Browns’ next drive, a run by Judkins accomplished nothing except seeing LG Zion Johnson , who is known to be a durable player, taken off the field with an injury. After the injury timeout, a quick play to Concepcion saw him getting stripped of the ball as he tried to dodge defenders in traffic. Jacksonville took over at the Browns’ 44 yard line. The Browns’ defense got the Jaguars into a 3rd-and-6, but Lawrence still gunned it along the left sideline to Washington for 14 yards. On the next play, Lawrence didn’t find his first couple targets, but then spotted TE Brenton Strange over the middle for 14-yard touchdown to make it a 24-0 blowout mid-way through the second quarter. Cooking with gasoline ⛽️ @BrentonStrange | #CLEvsJAX on CBS & @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/OlWnYfpsa1 — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 The Browns’ next drive started with a sweep to Concepcion for 8 yards, and then Watson ran for the first down. Watson tried to launch one deep off of playaction on the next play, but it was a wobbling duck that fell short of everyone as his arm was hit on the release. His next pass led WR Jerry Jeudy too far out of bounds for an incompletion, and then on 3rd-and-10, Watson scrambled for a few yards before Cleveland punted again. The Jaguars faced a 3rd-and-1 heading into the two-minute warning. Jacksonville tried to remain aggressive, but DT Mason Graham was in hot pursuit and sacked Lawrence for a loss of 13 yards, forcing the Jaguars into their first punt of the game. Mason ties him up 💪 #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/HJHB8O0DyG — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 Concepcion returned the punt to the 30 yard line, where Watson had 1:32 and one timeout to work with to try to get on the board. He started with a quick 20-yard pass to Jeudy, followed by a first-down pass to RB Raheim Sanders . A hold on Johnson pushed Cleveland back to a 1st-and-20, though, at midfield with 0:44 left. They were pushed five yards further back after a false start on RT Tytus Howard . And then, a delay of game made it 1st-and-30. Another hold on Johnson later made it 2nd-and-34. The clock management was bad on top of that too, and Watson’s launch to WR Denzel Boston down the left sideline was incomplete to end the half. 3rd Quarter – Browns vs. Jaguars The Jaguars took the second half kickoff out to the 40 yard line, and then a 10-yard run got them to midfield. A quick screen out to RB Bhayshul Tuten went for 22 yards, as Jacksonville can do no wrong in this game. As I say that, though, Graham helped blow up a run by Tuten on the next play for a loss of 4 yard yards. A false start made it 2nd-and-19, but then after facing pressure, WR Jakobi Meyers leaked open to the end zone and Lawrence found him for a 32-yard touchdown to go up 31-0. Lawd have mercy 🙃 #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/ZCzjHYUMsl — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) September 13, 2026 Sanders then had a breakaway 78-yard kickoff return to the Browns’ 24 yard line, the furthest they’ve been on offense all day. big time return for Rocket #CLEvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/tDwhSBehu6 — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 13, 2026 After a couple plays, Watson faced a 3rd-and-7 and dodged a defender as he rolled to the left and picked up the first down with his legs to the 11 yard line. Watson kept it again on the next play to gain 6 yards. On 2nd-and-4 from the 5 yard line, Watson gave it to Judkins for 2 yards to make it 3rd-and-2 at the 3 yard line. Watson tried adjusting the play and call for the ball, but it came too late for a delay of game, making it 3rd-and-7 at the 8 yard line. His out throw to Boston wasn’t close. Despite being down big, K Andre Szmyt was sent on to kick a 26-yard field goal to get on the board at 31-3. On Jacksonville’s next drive, they were marching until a couple run stops by the Browns’ defense. They were content to get their three points back as Little hit from 40 yards out to make it a 34-3 game. TE Harold Fannin finally caught his first pass near the end of the third quarter with a 9 yard…

Johnson was a big free-agent addition for Cleveland, hoping to build off an up-and-down early career with the Los Angeles Chargers . The Browns believed in Johnson enough to give him a three-year, $49.5 million contract. With Cleveland struggling in all aspects versus the Jaguars, they added injury to insult when Johnson went down with an apparent knee injury. Jacksonville scored on their ensuing drive, pushing their lead to 24-0 with six minutes left in the second quarter. Johnson returned on the next possession. The Browns lost RB Dylan Sampson to a knee injury earlier in the game, ruled out shortly after.

title: 5 key plays that spelled disaster for the Cowboys vs. Giants
summary: After all the hype and build-up of what was a terrific, drama-free offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, the team came out flat against the New York Giants. The offense sleepwalked through much of the game, looking like a shell of the potent offense we saw last year. Dallas’ receivers weren’t productive for much of the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - SEPTEMBER 13: Javonte Williams #33 of the Dallas Cowboys runs after the catch during the third quarter during the game against the New York Giants on September 13, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After all the hype and build-up of what was a terrific, drama-free offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, the team came out flat against the New York Giants. The offense sleepwalked through much of the game, looking like a shell of the potent offense we saw last year. Dallas’ receivers weren’t productive for much of the contest, and when they did wake up, it was far too little, too late. The defense looks different but produced eerily similar results as last year. Jaxson Dart toyed with them. On an emotional night at MetLife Stadium, the Giants beat the Cowboys more convincingly than the 28-20 score would suggest. Cowboys fans should be stunned at how we even got here. Here are the five key plays that decided Dallas disappointing loss. Not going for it on 4th and 1 The Giants were fired up going into this game. The atmosphere was electric. With the introduction of John Harbaugh, the Giants have renewed excitement, and that was felt from the coin toss. On the opening drive for the Cowboys, Dak Prescott completed a slant to George Pickens. Although initially it was ruled a first down, replay review overturned it. Dallas lined up on offense to give the impression they were going to try to pick up the first down. A hard count was unsuccessful in drawing the Giants offsides, and with a chance to sustain their drive to take some of the wind out of the Giants’ sails, head coach Brian Schottenheimer opted to punt the ball. The Giants capitalized on their drive led by a big run by Jaxson Dart. With the Cowboys’ offensive line, their quarterback, running back, and tight end, they elected to play it safe, and it cost them. The Giants took the early lead and never looked back. The Giants owned the time-of-possession battle, and you can point back to this moment as a starting point for New York’s control over the clock. Pickens Big Drop The Cowboys simply could not execute against the Giants’ secondary. Even though Prescott was under pressure, they had their opportunities. Following a terrific play by Quinnen Williams to force a fumble against Tyrone Tracy, the Cowboys had been able to stop the bleeding and manage to get off the field. At that point, the game was tied, and the Cowboys were in position to take the lead before the half . Prescott made a terrific throw to Pickens, who had beaten the Giants deep, but Pickens allowed the ball to slip right through his fingers. Pickens had multiple drops against the Giants, but that one especially stung. The Cowboys’ aerial assault was grounded Sunday night as all the explosiveness of their offense fizzled out. The Cowboys were unable to create any significant plays in the Giants’ secondary, and that play was the epitome of their passing futility in the loss. Dak’s interception Dak Prescott’s interception happened soon after Pickens’ drop, but the two plays are so directly correlated that they must be mentioned. Prescott makes the right play by eluding the pass rush to get out of harm’s way, that is until an ill-advised pass lands in the arms of Jevon Holland. Prescott claimed he was trying to throw the ball away, but upon looking at the replay, it doesn’t look that way. From that point, it killed whatever progress the Cowboys had made defensively. The Giants regained possession, and after several coverage breakdowns on the ensuing drive, scored to take a 14-7 lead. Prescott’s interception nullified the Giants turnover and set up the Giants’ chance of taking a two score lead after halftime, which in fact they did. Skattebo’s fumble takes an unfortunate bounce Despite their challenges, there were multiple times when the Dallas defense made a turnover-worthy play but couldn’t come away with the football. Having one turnover Sunday is very disappointing. DeMarvion Overshown and Caleb Downs forced fumbles that wouldn’t go the Cowboys’ way. Later in the game, Cam Skattebo almost gave the Cowboys’ defense a gift as they were sucking wind and panting for air. Early in the fourth quarter, Skattebo slipped a tackle on one of his many tough runs through the Cowboys’ defense. Cobie Durant forced a fumble, but the ball made its way back to Skattebo before Dallas could even get a chance to recover it, signifying it wasn’t going to be their night defensively. On the same drive, the Giants overcame a 2nd-and-17, a 3rd-and-9, and a 2nd-and-12 to find the end zone for the game-deciding score. Luck wasn’t on the Cowboys’ side Sunday, even when it presented itself repeatedly. Javonte Williams taunting penalty Dallas’ composure was compromised early. Overshown’s penalty early in the game was the precursor to what we would later see. In total, Dallas committed nine penalties, and awareness of the situations they were in was questionable. However, none more questionable than Javonte Williams’ penalty. Dallas had managed to answer New York’s early fourth-quarter drive and position themselves to be within one score. Yet Javonte Williams took it upon himself to taunt the Giants secondary even though the Cowboys were still trailing. His penalty was only magnified by Brandon Aubrey missing the extra point after Williams’ penalty had pushed the Cowboys back 15 yards. Although the Giants ran out the remainder of the clock after that point, Williams’ actions fully encapsulates how the Cowboys lacked disciplined in all facets, which proved to be their undoing.
author: LP Cruz

title: Javonte Williams really hurt the Cowboys on this play
summary: It appeared that the Dallas Cowboys were about to be down by seven points. As Javonte Williams was walking into the endzone after catching a pass from Dak Prescott, this was the collective thought. Unfortunately, that thought was replaced by one of “what are you doing!?” as Williams was getting called for taunting in the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Javonte Williams #33 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates a touchdown during the third quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images It appeared that the Dallas Cowboys were about to be down by seven points. As Javonte Williams was walking into the endzone after catching a pass from Dak Prescott, this was the collective thought. Unfortunately, that thought was replaced by one of “what are you doing!?” as Williams was getting called for taunting in the process. . @javontewill33 takes it in ❗️ 📺: #DALvsNYG on NBC 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/9VcBSMJUHo — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) September 14, 2026 This was at a moment where the Cowboys were trying to rally. The score was leaving them only down by one possession. Ultimately the Cowboys were unable (shocker) to get a defensive stop so this wound up a moot point, but the player in question is a veteran, one who the Cowboys gave a second contract to, and had a completely avoidable mistake. What’s more is that this happened on a team where the head coach, Brian Schottenheimer, preaches so much about culture. What kind of culture is it to make this kind of mistake? Why are you even taunting when you are still down by a touchdown? Mistakes happen and people, hopefully, learn from them. This was a rough one for Javonte Williams.

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys 28-20 Sunday night loss to the Giants
summary: Football is back. It’s always good to say that, and very few things match the excitement of kicking things off on Sunday Night Football. The Dallas Cowboys started off the 2026 season by traveling to Jersey to play the New York Giants. Usually, a Week 1 date with the Giants has meant a good start […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Skattebo #44 of the New York Giants runs with the ball during the fourth quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is back. It’s always good to say that, and very few things match the excitement of kicking things off on Sunday Night Football . The Dallas Cowboys started off the 2026 season by traveling to Jersey to play the New York Giants. Usually, a Week 1 date with the Giants has meant a good start for the Cowboys. But not this time. The Giants brought more of the fight and came away with a 28-20 victory. Cue the sad music. Here are 10 thoughts on the Cowboys’ Sunday night defeat. 1. Terrible start to the game The new season couldn’t have started any worse. The offense went three-and-out on their opening drive, including a scaredy-cat decision not to QB-sneak it when they came up inches short after the third-down catch from George Pickens. Then, the defense let the Giants offense waltz down the field on their opening drive, allowing 6.3 yards per play, and ending it with a touchdown. The defense also committed two quick penalties, including a bonehead late hit out of bounds by DeMarvion Overshown. Just like that, it was 7-0 Giants. The Cowboys looked unprepared. 2. Pass Interference After punting on their first two drives, the Cowboys finally got on the board with six minutes left in the first half, but it wasn’t easy. They put together a 10-play, 85-yard drive to tie the game up 7-7, but they got some help on third down. Twice the Giants’ defense was called for pass interference, once against Pickens and once against Jake Ferguson. Both plays were obvious calls and helped keep the drive going, setting up the Cowboys’ first score of the new season. 3. Lucky Skattabounces The Cowboys’ defense came out aggressive and hitting hard. Four times in this game, the Cowboys forced a fumble, but only once did they come away with the ball. Donovan Ezeiruaku stripped Isaiah Likely, and Caleb Downs knocked the ball out of Jaxson Dart’s hands, but both times a Giants offensive lineman was in the right place at the right time. In the second half, Giants’ running back Cam Skatteboo lost control of the ball, but it bounced right back into his arms. The only takeaway the Cowboys got was when Quinnen Williams punched the ball away from Tyrone Tracy Jr., and the ball went right into the arms of Shavon Revel Jr. 4. A costly miscue With just under two minutes left in the first half, the Cowboys’ offense was poised to strike and go into halftime with the lead. Sadly, it wasn’t meant to be. After being the recipient of the game’s first turnover, Dak Prescott gave the ball right back when he tried to throw the ball away on third down and heaved it downfield. Unfortunately, Giants safety Jevon Holland flew over and hauled in the catch before sliding out of bounds. Just like that, the Giants were now poised to strike before the end of the half. 5. Being a softy The Dak interception hurt because the Giants proceeded to march 55 yards on six plays in only 29 seconds to score a touchdown and take a 14-7 lead into halftime. It was frustrating to see the Giants move so easily as three times Jaxson Dart found wide-open receivers in space in soft coverage. The Cowboys’ defense wasn’t anywhere close to the Giants’ pass catchers, making fans have flashbacks of last year’s red-carpet defense. It was a terrible way to end the half. 6. Terrible start to the second half If the end of the first half didn’t sting enough, the Cowboys made sure the pain would linger into the second half. On their opening possession of the second half, the Giants went 74 yards on 12 plays in just over eight minutes to go up 21-7. It was tough to watch. The defense couldn’t make stops. To make matters even worse, the Cowboys burned a second-half timeout because they were discombobulated on the Giants’ opening drive. 7. Pass Interference If you feel like you’ve read this already, you have. Bad start to the half. Giants commit pass interference penalties. Cowboys strike back. Yes, it happened again. While the New York defenders were guilty most of the time, it wasn’t always the case. The last one in the end zone against CeeDee Lamb looked a little suspect. The Cowboys probably score anyway there, so it’s probably moot, but the Cowboys kept benefiting from the grabby defenders and the flag-ready refs. A promising drive cut the lead to 21-14 late in the third quarter. The suspense was building. 8. Couldn’t make stops The Cowboys’ offense started slow, but eventually, they moved the ball. However, it didn’t matter because they never had enough opportunities. They scored every time they touched the ball in the second half, but unfortunately, they only touched it twice. Two second-half possessions! That’s because the Cowboys’ defense couldn’t get off the field. The Giants’ offense kept churning out long, time-consuming drives, holding the ball for over 21 minutes in the second half. Dallas was never going to get back into the game if they couldn’t make stops, and they couldn’t. The Giants punted once in the game. 9. A Likely hero The Giants’ offense was sharp. Dart was impressive, making good decisions all night. Skattaboo was running over people, flexing, and doing backflips. Even Malik Nabers made some nice catches, which showed his resiliency after returning from his injury a year ago. But on this day, the Giants’ biggest offensive hero was tight end Isaiah Likely, who had an impressive debut with his new team. He finished the game with eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns, including several key third-down catches. The Cowboys had no answer for him. 10. Sloppy play This game was a physical battle with both teams bringing a lot of tenacity, but sometimes that fire got them burned. Both teams were committing penalties left and right. The Cowboys finished with nine penalties for 90 yards while the Giants were even worse with 10 penalties for 114 yards. The Giants struggled with pass interference while the Cowboys kept committing super lame personal foul penalties. Late hits, facemasks, and even taunting penalties from nice-guy Javonte Williams. That’s when you know it’s bad. Both teams just looked very undisciplined and were out there running amok at times.
author: Dan Rogers

In the passing game, Dak Prescott, under regular pressure, completed 64.7% of his attempts for 175 passing yards with two touchdowns and an interception, his passer rating coming in at 84.8. Overall, the Giants were simply more physical, outgaining the Cowboys in total yards, 394 to 244, and dominating the time of possession, 36:40 to 23:20. Download the SB Nation app today! Jerry Jones was ‘nervous’ before Cowboys played Giants – he was right to be – USA Today The Cowboys owner had a feeling, but it wasn’t quite right. Before his Dallas Cowboys fell to the New York Giants 28-20 to open the 2026 regular season , Jerry Jones admitted to being “nervous” and “anxious” during an appearance on Dallas radio. The Cowboys owner and CEO told 105.3 The Fan “my biggest concern is: Can we block them up?” That distinction belonged to the Giants’ offensive line, which bullied the Cowboys’ new-look unit under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Cowboys did the talking, but Giants looked like the most improved team in decisive Week 1 win, 28-20 – Yahoo Sports The optimism was real, but seemingly misplaced. title: The sequence that cost the Cowboys the game in New York
summary: Before getting into anything else, it should be said that the Dallas Cowboys got thoroughly worked by the New York Giants on Sunday night. They deserved the 28-20 win as they outplayed the Cowboys in almost every way. The trio of Jaxson Dart, Cam Skattebo and Isiah Likely tortured Dallas all night. John Harbaugh has […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys reacts during the first quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before getting into anything else, it should be said that the Dallas Cowboys got thoroughly worked by the New York Giants on Sunday night. They deserved the 28-20 win as they outplayed the Cowboys in almost every way. The trio of Jaxson Dart, Cam Skattebo and Isiah Likely tortured Dallas all night. John Harbaugh has the G-men playing ball again. The NFC should take note. But the game didn’t really have to go that way. There was a moment in time when the Cowboys could have seized control. Right around the two-minute warning to end the first half, the Cowboys recovered a fumble at their own 16-yard line, preventing a score and giving themselves a chance to break a 7-7 tie. The Giants had controlled the early part of the game, but Dallas was back in it with a chance to take the lead heading into halftime. Then the mistakes started to happen. First, Dak Prescott dropped a dime on George Pickens deep into the Giants secondary, but Pickens dropped it. Then, facing a third down, Dak made a huge error. He decided to launch a desperation heave to save a sack, but instead of getting it out of bounds, he threw an interception. New York took over with 58 seconds left before the half at the 45-yard line. Then the defense just fell apart. It took the Giants 29 seconds to cover 55 yards and score a touchdown. 29 seconds. The Giants went into halftime leading 14-7. They got the second half kickoff, drove that for a touchdown and it Dallas was in catch up mode the rest of the way. They never caught up.

title: Cowboys mistakes and missed opportunities doom them in opener
summary: In the immediate aftermath of the loss, one thing is exceptionally clear: the Dallas Cowboys left far too many plays on the field. From penalties to missed opportunities, Dallas was outplayed by both the New York Giants and themselves. Dallas had seven penalties for 60 yards in just the first half alone. They would end […]
full_text: In the immediate aftermath of the loss, one thing is exceptionally clear: the Dallas Cowboys left far too many plays on the field. From penalties to missed opportunities, Dallas was outplayed by both the New York Giants and themselves. Dallas had seven penalties for 60 yards in just the first half alone. They would end up finishing the game with nine penalties for 90 yards. This included a taunting call from Javonte Williams late into the fourth quarter en route to a touchdown, leading to a missed PAT. Paired with that, the Cowboys defense finished with five turnover-worthy plays but only walked away with a single takeaway. From forced fumbles that just bounced the wrong way to dropped interceptions, the Cowboys defense just couldn’t take advantage. On a night where the Giants moved the ball slowly yet methodically down the field, chewing up clock on the way to the endzone, this defense needed to finish when the ball was up for grabs. They just didn’t do that. As mentioned earlier in the week , one of the ways that Dallas could lose this game was due to lack of defensive scheme experience and familiarity. This lack of experience certainly factored into the large voids left on the field by Cowboys defenders leading to multiple New York Giants touchdowns. These mistakes allowed the Giants offense to convert on third downs at a rate of 81%. This kept the Cowboys offense off the field for much of the second half. And let’s not give the offense a pass. Against the Giants, George Pickens was not the same player that we saw throughout training camp. Two untimely drops resulted in a punt and an eventual turnover – an interception thrown by Dak just before the half on a ball he seemingly meant to throw away. The Giants would go and score back-to-back touchdowns after that mistake and never look back. The dropped deep ball from Pickens was a turning point in this game. The expectation for the Cowboys was to come into their division rivals house and knock them down. But Dallas found out the hard way that when you play an underdog like the Giants in their own stadium, the quickest way to lose is to commit untimely penalties, turn the ball over, and miss your opportunities at big plays. The Cowboys did just that, and now they will start the season 0-1.

title: Christian Parker failed his entry exam with the Dallas Cowboys
summary: As things wore on for the Dallas Cowboys throughout training camp, new defensive coordinator stuck within a theme of academia. He referred to the earlier part of the offseason, things like OTAs, as the undergraduate program for the defense, from a learning perspective obviously. He followed that up by saying that training camp was akin […]
full_text: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely (9) catches a pass during a week one opening game between the New York Giants and Dallas Cowboys at Metlife Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026, in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As things wore on for the Dallas Cowboys throughout training camp, new defensive coordinator stuck within a theme of academia. He referred to the earlier part of the offseason, things like OTAs, as the undergraduate program for the defense, from a learning perspective obviously. He followed that up by saying that training camp was akin to a master’s program. Philosophically, the analogy made sense. In the lead up to Week 1 and the first formal work for the group, Parker was asked what that worked out to within his analogy. He said that Sunday night against the New York Giants was walking the graduation stage. I’m not so sure that the Cowboys received any kind of diplomas at MetLife Stadium in their 28-20 loss. Consider that the Giants scored a touchdown to start the game, and then followed it up with a punt and fumble. To be fair that fumble came after they picked up 65 yards. But then the Giants scored three touchdowns in a row that just about put the game on ice. One came to end the first half, another to start the second, and then the third to ice things midway through the fourth quarter. It felt like the Cowboys found out while waiting in line to walk that they actually didn’t have the grades to graduate. Christian Parker was afforded an enormous amount of optimism and trust over the offseason. To be clear, he could still wind up being the answer. One game does not make anything. But the first outing for this new-look defense felt a lot like all of them for the group that they are trying to replace, one of the worst defenses in franchise history. Unfortunately it felt like more of the same, the same failing grades where the bare minimum of passing felt so far out of reach. Maybe Parker and company will turn things around over their version of summer school? The analogy is difficult to build on at this point because nobody expected this. Nobody expected more of the same. How did this possibly happen?
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys lose to Giants 28-20: Christian Parker defense no stop for Jaxson Dart
summary: It was supposed to be different. Last season saw the Dallas Cowboys field one of the worst defenses in franchise history. The organization spent the entire offseason hiring people and bringing in players to make sure that such a thing never happened again. We are only one game in… but it looked a lot like […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Tyrone Tracy Jr. #29 of the New York Giants runs the ball during the second quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was supposed to be different. Last season saw the Dallas Cowboys field one of the worst defenses in franchise history. The organization spent the entire offseason hiring people and bringing in players to make sure that such a thing never happened again. We are only one game in… but it looked a lot like last year. The Cowboys lost a game of significant to the New York Giants and did so with Dak Prescott under center. This sort of thing has not happened often in the last decade, but maybe it will more in the future. Prescott and the offense took some time to find their form, but they certainly contributed to the problem by stalling out early. The defense never really did much, outside of a fumble that they forced and recovered, and let the Giants completely handle them in the second half. Below you will find our recap of it all. You will surely have questions as you re-live the performance to get down to the comments. The Cowboys are now 0-1 to start the season. First Quarter The Giants won the toss and deferred. GOTI, the Cowboys’ appointed nickname for their offense (Greatest Offense There Is) was on the field first. Unfortunately the first possession of the GOTI era did not go well. Dallas went three and out, but sort of surprisingly so. It appeared that George Pickens converted on third down, but as the Cowboys took to line up on what they thought was first down, officials referenced replay assist to note they did not make it which led to a punt. The Giants capped off their 10-play, 6-minute drive in style… Cam Skattebo punched it in for the score. Cam Skattebo is back to scoring TDs and hitting backflips 🙌 DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZoMoPaWGmh — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 While the next Cowboys drive actually moved the ball a little bit… it also ended in a punt. The quarter ended with New York holding the ball and a 7-0 lead. Second Quarter The Giants were approaching midfield as the quarter began, and Kenny Clark made sure that Skattebo moved backwards in that endeavor. Thankfully the Cowboys forced their first stop of the season and took over on offense once more. The Cowboys began moving the ball, albeit thanks to some pass interference penalties. They were correctly called to be clear, but they were certainly a part of the drive. All told they were part of the first scoring drive of the season. After Javonte Williams initially scored and had it overturned due to being short… Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb left no doubt to even the game up. CEEDEE TD!!! pic.twitter.com/cZW8OwdAZE — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 14, 2026 New York took over on offense and the Cowboys couldn’t seem to fully stop them. In what felt like no time they were beyond midfield and threatening to score. Caleb Downs jarred the ball loose as he picked up the first sack of his career, but even then it landed in the hands of a Giants lineman. Caleb Downs tho pic.twitter.com/Cx1BeRXxEB — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 14, 2026 While the Cowboys were not able to get on that ball… they got on the one that Jalen Thompson (and Quinnen Williams) popped loose right after! Shout out Shavon Revel for the quick reflexes. COWBOYS FORCED FUMBLE! pic.twitter.com/ODo7paePQD — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 14, 2026 The Cowboys took over at their own 16-yard line with almost two minutes remaining before halftime. Given that they received the ball to start the game and that the Giants were set to receive after halftime… the possession was important. Unfortunately it went pretty poorly. George Pickens dropped what would have been a huge gain early on, and a few plays later Dak Prescott threw off of his back foot in a serious manner of tempting fate, and the Giants made him pay by picking him off at their own 45-yard line. What an INT from Jevon Holland! DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E8xJcAU6ji — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 It turns out the team to more fully understand the importance of end-of-first-half possessions was the Giants, unfortunately. Jaxson Dart moved with extreme ease, so much so that the NBC broadcast was baffled at how the Cowboys were letting it happen. After what felt like no time, the Giants found the endzone. Isaiah Likely hauls in his first TD as a Giant! DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FVcsGIrPsG — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 The home team went into the locker with a 14-7 lead. Third Quarter It would stand to reason that the Cowboys spent halftime talking about how things did not go the way they wanted in the first half. They likely pledged to make changes in the name of turning things around. Assuming that happened… things did not exactly go according to plan. The Giants came out of halftime and just about had their way with their rivals. In a drive that totaled 12 plays, 74 yards, and a staggering 8:01 of game clock… they scored yet again for the double-dip that every team so badly seeks. Likely TD No. ✌️ DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0dgzfS3uCX — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 Dallas took over on offense for the first time in the second half, and trailing by 14 points with pressure starting to really mount. To their credit, the Cowboys seemed to embrace that pressure. They responded with their own 12-play drive, this one only traveling 63 yards and consuming just over six minutes of game clock, for a touchdown to respond. JAVONTE TD! pic.twitter.com/HpLLg33rcd — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 14, 2026 With return serve being met on the day of the U.S. Open final in New York, it was suddenly time for the G-Men to take center stage once more. Such action would require the fourth quarter to unfold. Fourth Quarter At this point the Giants were on their second possession of the second half, one of those games where time just worked out that way. This was the case because New York was stringing together long and methodical possessions, bleeding the clock and the Cowboys’ will simultaneously. They did it once again and punched in their third touchdown in a row, dating back to the end of the first half, to basically put the game on ice as it gave them a 28-14 lead. Jaxson Dart swings it out to Devin Singletary for another Giants TD! DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Z1q4jAeBkY — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2026 Give the Cowboys credit, at least give the offense credit, for not quitting. Facing a herculean task… they delivered. They marched right down the field and scored a touchdown to keep the faint heartbeat of this game still going for them. Unfortunately it did not come without a cost. . @javontewill33 takes it in ❗️ 📺: #DALvsNYG on NBC 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/9VcBSMJUHo — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) September 14, 2026 You will see that Javonte Williams, who scored the touchdown, got called for taunting while strolling into the endzone. That penalty moved Brandon Aubrey back a ways for the extra point and he missed it as a result. This left the Cowboys down by a touchdown and a 2-point conversion. It didn’t matter, ultimately. The Giants were able to run the ball out and end the game in victory formation. The Dallas Cowboys are 0-1.

title: Broncos get huge injury news ahead of Week 3 showdown with Rams
summary: The Los Angeles had a ton of hype entering the 2026 season. They acquired star pass rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns, traded for star cornerback Trent McDuffie from the Chiefs, and coaxed star pass rusher Aaron Donald out of retirement to join their defense. They had a loaded roster on paper and were […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles had a ton of hype entering the 2026 season. They acquired star pass rusher Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns, traded for star cornerback Trent McDuffie from the Chiefs, and coaxed star pass rusher Aaron Donald out of retirement to join their defense. They had a loaded roster on paper and were ready to dominate their already banged-up divisional rivals the San Francisco 49ers in Australia on primetime with the game being aired on Netflix. Well, that did not happen. Not only did the Rams lose, they were dominated, jet lagged, and blown out by their divisional rivals. The news did not get better for them this weekend. On Sunday, it was reported by NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport that star pass rusher Myles Garrett is set to undergo knee surgery and is headed to the injured reserve. This means that Garrett will miss a minimum of 4 games which includes a primetime matchup vs. the Denver Broncos in Week 3. Rams DE Myles Garrett to undergo knee surgery, headed to injured reserve. (via @RapSheet ) pic.twitter.com/PTwFKccgiB — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 This is a huge loss for the Rams and a big break for the Broncos and the rest of the teams playing the Rams while Garrett is sidelined. Now, the Rams will be getting back Aaron Donald, but the 35-year old who has sat out the past two seasons will likely still be on a snap count and shaking off some rust during their Week 3 matchup vs. the Broncos. The Broncos have one of the best offensive lines in the NFL (If not the best), and this was set to be a fun strength vs. strength matchup. However, with Garrett sidelined, the Broncos will now have the edge against a still talented Rams front 7. Before we worry about Week 3, the Broncos have to take care of business tonight vs. their Divisional Rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs. They will be playing on the road in loud Arrowhead and will be dealing with the return of quarterback Patrick Mahomes who is returning from a major knee injury. Then, in Week 2, they will be hosting the Jacksonville Jaguars, who were the only team last season to really beat the Broncos. The rest of their losses were one-score games with penalities, missed opportunities, and injuries being a big reason why they lost. That wasn’t the case vs. the Jaguars. They dominated the Broncos late last season, and now Bo Nix and the Broncos will seek revenge against their small market rivals. Injuries happen and reshape the landscape of the NFL and the Broncos schedule each and every week, and the loss of Myles Garrett is a big one for the Rams. The Broncos will catch a break there but first, will need to take care of business against the Chiefs and Jaguars before they can focus on the Garrett-less Rams squad.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Chargers fall to the Cardinals in the season opener
summary: The AFC West watch is on. Looking at the Week 1 schedule, many expected the Los Angeles Chargers to defeat the Arizona Cardinals. On paper, the Chargers are the more talented team, they have quarterback Justin Herbert, and Mike McDaniels running their offense. This should have been a layup Week 1 win for the offseason […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Burch #52 of the Arizona Cardinals sacks Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the fourth quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The AFC West watch is on. Looking at the Week 1 schedule, many expected the Los Angeles Chargers to defeat the Arizona Cardinals. On paper, the Chargers are the more talented team, they have quarterback Justin Herbert, and Mike McDaniels running their offense. This should have been a layup Week 1 win for the offseason favorites. But that’s not what happened. Not only did the Chargers lose to the Cardinals at home, but they were also thoroughly outplayed by first-time head coach Mike LaFleur’s squad. The worst part for the Chargers is that this was supposed to be the easy part of their schedule. A lot is made about the Broncos schedule, especially their start, but the Chargers have a tough stretch coming up. Especially coming off a loss @ home to the Cardinals 😬😬. pic.twitter.com/2h28G4odRo — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 13, 2026 The Chargers have a home date vs. their AFC West rivals, the Las Vegas Raiders, next week in a game they will be favored to win. However, if they had issues with the Cardinals, they could struggle with the Raiders, who looked pretty decent against a bad Miami Dolphins team on Sunday. After the Raiders game is when the Chargers go through a brutal stretch of games that will frankly define their 2026 season. They start this stretch of games with back-to-back road games in Buffalo at New Highmark Stadium vs. Josh Allen and the explosive Bills offense. Then, they head to Seattle, where the 12s will be loud to take on the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks. They will then head home to take on the reigning AFC West Champion Denver Broncos before going on the road again to take on the Chiefs and Rams. It doesn’t stop there, they will then host the Houston Texans and their elite defense, followed by a road date vs. Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens. A lot has been made about the Broncos start of the season, and it is a tough one on paper, but the Chargers schedule is equally, if not more difficult. An upset loss to the lowly Cardinals who many have penciled in for a top 5 pick in next April’s NFL Draft is not the start they wanted. The Broncos have to handle their own business starting tonight in Arrowhead vs. the returning Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. If they can do that, they can put a game between them and the Chiefs and Chargers and be competing with….the Las Vegas Raiders…for control of the AFC West early on in the 2026 NFL season.

title: Broncos gameday is finally here!
summary: The last time the Denver Broncos played football was 17-days ago when the Minnesota Vikings visited Denver in the preseason finale. The last meaningful game, the AFC Championship Game, was played 232-days ago. To find a meaningful game featuring Bo Nix, a win, you’d have to go back 240-days the divisional round of the playoffs. […]
full_text: Nov 3, 2019; Denver, CO, USA; General view of a sunset over Empower Field at Mile High during the fourth quarter of the game between the Cleveland Browns against the Denver Broncos. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-USA TODAY Sports The last time the Denver Broncos played football was 17-days ago when the Minnesota Vikings visited Denver in the preseason finale. The last meaningful game, the AFC Championship Game, was played 232-days ago. To find a meaningful game featuring Bo Nix, a win, you’d have to go back 240-days the divisional round of the playoffs. Today, finally, is gameday in Broncos Country. It was a special kind of torture, having week 1 kick off on a Wednesday and having to wait 5 whole days before the Denver Broncos get to join in the fun. Football so close y0u could touch it, but no. No, there is a price that must be paid in order to be the Monday night marquee matchup to close out week one. Your patience. The mysteries that have carried storylines all offseason will soon give way to the wins and losses of the 2026 season. How will Bo respond coming back from his ankle injury? How will Davis Webb fare taking over the play calling duties? Is Jonathan Cooper’s absence going to affect the defense? What about Jonathon Franklin-Myers departure via free agency? You’ve been reading those beat storylines for the last 33-weeks with a knot in your stomach. It was a gut punch, watching an inferior Patriots team advance to the Super Bowl. It was obvious to just about everyone outside the northeast that a Bo Nix-led Broncos squad would have offered much more than the whimper turned in by New England. But that was last season… This offseason has been one of tremendous patience for Broncos Country and, today, all that waiting pays off. The days, weeks, and months of thumb-twiddling have FINALLY given way to gameday in Broncos Country. All that non-nutritive talk of what could have happened, what should have happened, last season are over. It’s time to welcome new triumphs, new hopes, and new history into the 2026 season. …and Broncos Country couldn’t be more ready.

title: Ultimate Fan: Win in the trenches and Broncos can win in Arrowhead
summary: WOOOO HOOOO! The football season is here, the Broncos are playing on prime time, the week 1 matchup is a major rivalry game on the road, and our Ultimate Fan Guide is debuting the 2026 season with a post as electric as a Monday Night Football game between the Broncos and Chiefs. Mad Horses is […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 10: Mike McGlinchey #69 of the Denver Broncos blocks Mike Danna #51 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the first quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on November 10, 2024 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images WOOOO HOOOO! The football season is here, the Broncos are playing on prime time, the week 1 matchup is a major rivalry game on the road, and our Ultimate Fan Guide is debuting the 2026 season with a post as electric as a Monday Night Football game between the Broncos and Chiefs. Mad Horses is kicking off the season predicting a win, and I could not be happier. The prediction is for a little closer of a game than most of Broncos Country voted earlier this week, but I don’t care how the W happens as long as it happens. And I doubt any ultimate fan cares either. So here’s to the start of a great season for the Broncos and an even better one for the UFG! GO BRONCOS! When the @Broncos found a way to make it happen for @BoNix10 🫴⁰ DENvsKC – Monday 8:15pm ET on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ig3OidxtPq — NFL (@NFL) September 11, 2026 Week 1: Broncos at Chiefs on MNF MHR: Let’s get the obvious question out of the way…after reaching the AFC Championship Game last season, what are your expectations for the Broncos in 2026? Is anything less than the AFCCG again still a success? mad horses: The very first UFG question posed in this new season, so here we go! When we think about expectations after last season (and it was a phenomenal season) the Broncos record of 14-3 comes with an asterisk. Out of those 14 wins, 11 were one-score games, and five of those games were won with fourth quarter comebacks (including that amazing 33-point fourth quarter game against the Giants). Can the Broncos replicate this? I am a bit skeptical. This is not to say that they won’t be just as good, and perhaps even better. My expectations are that our Broncos will have an excellent season and win the AFC West. I also see them going to the AFCCG again. But I am not so sure that they will wrap up the No.1 seed and land a bye, and I don’t believe that they can match their 14-3 record as there are likely to be fewer wins in these one-score games. Is anything less than the AFCCG still a success? No, not really. MHR: The Broncos have won three straight against Kansas City and four of the last six matchups, but this one is at Arrowhead on Monday Night Football. Does it seem like the balance of power in this rivalry has genuinely shifted, or does it still feel like the Broncos have to “prove” their dominance over the Chiefs? mad horses: Clearly things have shifted. The Broncos swept the Chefs last year, and have won four of the past five. I think what is more telling is that KC went from a powerhouse with seven AFCCG appearances and three Super Bowl victories (going back to Mahome’s first starting season) to a 6-8 record (if you include the game in which he was injured, which I am). A rather abrupt shift. But there remains something for the Broncos to prove, and the numbers reveal why. Over the past 10 seasons, the Broncos have won just four out of 20 games against KC. It gets worse if we consider that KC had a 16-game winning streak against Denver when we throw in the last game of the 2015 season, which was a notable game in Denver’s Super Bowl run as PFM was benched after four picks for backup Brock Osweiler. But I digress. The point is it has been a very long run for KC. It is unrealistic to think that all that is now behind us. Denver most certainly has something to prove, and it will take more than a single season to check that box. It pains me to state this, but we must respect what KC has accomplished here. And their record at home remains atop the NFL over the past decade. A shift, yes. More to prove, absolutely! MHR: Both Bo Nix and Patrick Mahomes are returning from significant injuries. Which quarterback’s mobility will have the greater affect on Monday night’s outcome? mad horses: If both injuries were equal, that would be tough to answer. But Mahomes suffered a significant ligament injury (ACL and LCL) requiring considerable recovery time. Bo Nix’s injury was a clean bone fracture with little soft-tissue damage. He was ready to go at training camp and had some snaps in preseason. By all accounts, Nix is 100%. We do not know that about Patrick Mahomes. The last snap he took was the one that did not end well. His mobility, nine months later, remains in question. This will no doubt be the subject of much scrutiny come Monday night. I have to believe that Bo’s running ability will have the greater impact. MHR: What does Bo Nix need to do Monday night to show that he has taken another step forward in Year 3? mad horses: Continued patience in the pocket and better pre-snap reads. In year one, Bo often displayed “happy feet” and rushed through his reads. He bailed out of the pocket routinely. Last season he seemed more comfortable in the pocket and relied on his quick release to get him out of trouble. His release is quite fast. Not PFM fast, but up there. What we will want to see in Year 3, now with Davis Webb calling the plays, will be less time in the huddle, more time at the line for pre-snap reads, and continued patience both under center and in the gun. This, coupled with his ability to run when needed, will keep defenses guessing. MHR: Hype and expectations are off the charts for Jaylen Waddle already this season. How would you like to see Sean Payton use him in his Broncos debut, and what could his speed unlock for the rest of the offense? mad horses: Jaylen Waddle’s strength is getting open with speed and excellent route running. He is a weapon on the outside and across the middle. I would love to see SP play into those strengths. We don’t need a lot of gadget plays for Waddle … just let him do what he does best. Successfully integrating Waddle into the game plan should have real consequence in changing defensive strategies. It would be good get a taste of this in the opener. Spagnuolo throws a lot of disguises pre-snap, and will mix in schemes when not expected, like throwing in a Cover 0 blitz on a medium-yardage second down. A receiver like Waddle, with his big play ability, can level things out and force the defense to take fewer risks. I believe that this might be Waddle’s biggest impact — keeping defenses honest. MHR: So much has been said about Jaylen Waddle joining the offense that any talk of Courtland Sutton has been an afterthought. But the guy has been clutch every year. Does Waddle’s addition actually allow Sutton to be an easier target for Nix now that he’s not the only WR1? What are your expectations for Marvin Mims, Pat Bryant and Troy Franklin this season? mad horses: The topic of Denver’s wide receivers has garnered a lot of discussion in this forum, especially with Jaylen Waddle’s arrival and the amazing preseason that Bryant had. I enjoy all the perspectives and predictions. There is so much talent in Denver’s WR corps … it’s deep, man. My expectations: Sutton will indeed have more opportunities on his side of the field. And his numbers will show for it. Mims will be your gadget guy with running and deep ball threat, much like we have seen. His return abilities will continue to be his signature contribution. Pat Bryant has his breakout season and his snap count will increase significantly. He should see a lot of time in the slot. Troy Franklin will get his snaps. While there has been much speculation that Franklin sees some reduced play time, I think differently. He was Bo’s No. 2 last year with over 700 yards and six scores. They played together in college (Go Ducks!), and there is a tight bond. I think he will be a solid inclusion in the rotation, and I am not confident that LJH will compete for a lot of those snaps. Humphries is a Payton guy with solid run blocking skills and ST utility. We have seen his ceiling as a WR, and I don’t see him taking snaps from the…

title: Broncos Country highly confident heading into Monday Night Football
summary: The Broncos open their 2026 season in prime time at Arrowhead Stadium, and a vast majority of Broncos Country believes the visiting team will walk away the victors. A whopping 89% of fans voting in this week’s Reacts Poll believe the Broncos will march into one of the toughest stadiums to play on the road […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos attempts a pass under pressure from Charles Omenihu #90 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Eric Thomas/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Broncos open their 2026 season in prime time at Arrowhead Stadium, and a vast majority of Broncos Country believes the visiting team will walk away the victors. A whopping 89% of fans voting in this week’s Reacts Poll believe the Broncos will march into one of the toughest stadiums to play on the road and beat the home team. Love that confidence. The only real debate is over how big the margin of victory will be, with 58% predicting a win of seven points or more and another 31% choosing a much closer contest. Still love that confidence…even if I can’t quite bring myself to believe in a 7+ point win. Hopefully the Broncos players are not as overly confident since they will face a healthy Patrick Mahomes who cannot wait to step on his home field. Broncos’ defensive coordinator Vance Joseph is ready for that. “I think Patrick is going to be Patrick. In my opinion, he wouldn’t play if he couldn’t be himself. He’s had a good summer and spring to kind of rehab and from what I hear and from what I read, he’s feeling great,” Joseph said. “So we expect Patrick to be Patrick, and he is obviously the guy in the league who wins an awful lot. He’s obviously motivated, and it’s a big game for them, it’s a big game for us obviously. It’s Week 1 so everyone’s healthy and excited to play, so we’ll get his best shot.” “You get put on Monday Night Football in Week 1, it means you have something to go out there and prove. …It’s going to be a really big challenge, but one that we are going to respond well to.“ BO NIX No matter how ready the Chiefs are, Sean Payton is also confident in his 2026 Broncos to get the job done, especially with a little more experience from many in the locker room. “I think it’s a smart team. I think there is … still that hunger for coming up short,” Payton said of carry over from the 2025 season. “So I would also say leadership, the culture, those types of things. Ultimately any good team begins to get taken over by the leaders within the locker room. I feel like that experience can serve this team well.” It’s also at Arrowhead, which is no walk in the park. Thankfully it’s Arrowhead in September — and not November as the Broncos seem to usually draw — but prime time should have both fan bases in prime form, and that will make for an electric atmosphere. Bo Nix is 100% ready for that. “Absolutely it doesn’t get old [playing on Monday night]. It’s very exciting. It means that you are in a really good spot as an organization, but it’s also a great responsibility,” Nix said. “You get put on Monday Night Football in Week 1, it means you have something to go out there and prove. We’re excited as a team. It’s going to be a really big challenge, but one that we are going to respond well to. We just have to go out there and play really hard.”

title: Chiefs rule out LT Josh Simmons and will start undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at LT vs. the Broncos
summary: The Broncos will kick off their 2026 regular season on Monday Night vs. their division rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs, in Arrowhead. This game will feature the return of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who is returning from a major knee injury last season, but he will be down his blindside protector. It was trending this […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 21: Nik Bonitto (15) of the Denver Broncos stands on the field before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 21, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Broncos will kick off their 2026 regular season on Monday Night vs. their division rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs, in Arrowhead. This game will feature the return of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who is returning from a major knee injury last season, but he will be down his blindside protector. It was trending this way all week, but on Saturday, it was confirmed that starting left tackle Josh Simmons would be ruled out, and undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will get the start at left tackle vs. the Denver Broncos. With Chiefs LT Josh Simmons out and former CU Buff right guard Kahlil Benson, an undrafted rookie, presumably in for the Chiefs at LT, the matchup of Monday night is Bonitto vs. Benson. Chiefs' superstar QB Patrick Mahomes is coming back 9 months from ACL injury. Seems scary for… — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) September 12, 2026 Benson is an undrafted free agent out of Indiana who has played primarily right tackle and some guard throughout his college career. His first snaps at left tackle came during the preseason with the Chiefs. So, the undrafted rookie will be making his NFL debut and his first career start at left tackle vs. the Broncos on Monday Night. Obviously, the Broncos NEED to take advantage of this. I would expect the Chiefs to be very run-heavy with Mahomes coming back from injury, the addition of Kenneth Walker, and being down at left tackle vs. a strong pass rush. The Broncos defense needs to control the line of scrimmage, stop their run game, and force the Chiefs into some uncomfortable situations. As we know, the Broncos will be down starting edge rusher Jonathon Cooper, who is currently on the exempt list. However, they still have All-Pro pass rusher Nik Bonitto and promising young players Jonah Elliss and Que Robinson, so they still have plenty of pass rush off the edge. The Broncos have led the NFL in sacks in back-to-back seasons and look primed to do that again this season. If they want to achieve that goal and break the team sack record this season, they will need to have a big night on Monday Night. The Chiefs will run the ball and throw a lot of quick passes, but the Broncos’ pass rushers have an opportunity to pin their ears back; they need to take advantage of this weakness.
