title: Jaguars Defense Sets the Tone in 34-10 Win Over Browns
summary: If there was any question about what the Jacksonville Jaguars wanted to look like entering 2026, they answered it emphatically Sunday. In front of a fired-up EverBank Stadium crowd, the Jaguars dominated the Cleveland Browns from start to finish, turning their home opener into exactly the kind of statement performance the fanbase had been waiting […]
full_text: If there was any question about what the Jacksonville Jaguars wanted to look like entering 2026, they answered it emphatically Sunday. In front of a fired-up EverBank Stadium crowd, the Jaguars dominated the Cleveland Browns from start to finish, turning their home opener into exactly the kind of statement performance the fanbase had been waiting for. Jacksonville’s defense was relentless by virtually every measure, making life miserable for Cleveland while the Jaguars steadily pulled away on the scoreboard. By the middle of the third quarter, multiple Jacksonville starters were already on the sideline in baseball caps, watching the rest of the afternoon unfold. For a team entering the season with legitimate expectations, this was about as ideal a Week 1 performance as Liam Coen, his coaching staff, and the Jaguars could have drawn up. The defense set the tone, the starters did their damage, and Jacksonville never gave Cleveland much of a chance to make this interesting. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 1 home opener, a 34-10 domination of the Cleveland Browns Live blog: Catch up on all the big plays and best moments from tonight’s game in our live blog ! Game Recap Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence on Sunday put together a career day with another quarter still remaining in the game. Just 3 minutes into the third quarter, Lawrence already had four passing touchdowns, a near-perfect passing rating, and no turnovers while nursing a blowout lead. The Jaguars’ defense kicked off where they left things in 2025, with the defense initially bending, giving up 32-yards on the opening drive, before linebacker Foye Oluokun said enough. The veteran linebacker shut the door on the series with an aerobic Devin Lloyd-esque interception, and Anthony Campanile’s unit never looked back. 3 drives for Deshaun Watson Drive 1: INT Drive 2: 3 and out where on 3rd down, the Jags dropped an interception Drive 3: 3 and out where on 3rd down, Watson got strip sacked He’s doing great https://t.co/x8kBrBoQQy — JaguarGator9 (@JaguarGator9NFL) September 13, 2026 The Jacksonville offense, similar to 2025, made Cleveland pay, continuing their 2025 hot streak after four opening-drive runs. The rushes came courtesy of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, with two Parker Washington catches sprinkled in on the drive – none more impressive than Parker’s 30-yard, play-action, diving touchdown reception. Parker Washington cooked him right off the line and what a catch. (also note that little RB motion) pic.twitter.com/qrL0OUy8CU — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 13, 2026 Following a quick three-and-out, the Jaguars offense continued to press the Browns defense. Trevor Lawrence, smelling blood in the water, proceeded to throw on six of the nine plays towards a nine-play, 74-yard, 4:42 drive that featured the offense, somehow overcoming three penalties and a recovered fumble. The drive was capped by a four-yard Trevor Lawrence dagger to rookie Josh Cameron. even a simple RZ play action like this was a fun use of personnel. put Jakobi Meyers and rookie WR Josh Cameron in (screaming RUN RUN RUN!) and then pull the bait & switch. pic.twitter.com/QaSZK41sxL https://t.co/diajEqDKlr — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 13, 2026 Following another three-and-out with a Hines-Allen, Walker shared sack, the Jaguars took the points instead of attempting a fourth-and-one from the 29 to extend the lead. The players confirmed that decision as a wise one, with the linebacker Ventrell Miller forcing a KC Conception fumble just two offensive plays later. – Travon Walker pressure. – Ventrell Miller forced fumble. – Josh Hines-Allen recovery. pic.twitter.com/4Qdw2rAhYP — Daniel Griffis (@DanDGriffis) September 13, 2026 Lawrence then completed the 44-yard drive with a 14-yard Brenton Strange touchdown just five plays later. With punts by both teams on the following drives, Logan Cook’s first punt of the day came with 1:45 remaining in the half. To show the clear dominance in this one, QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half 13/18 for 166 yards and three touchdowns, while Parker Washington had five catches on six targets for 83 yards and a touchdown. Jacksonville punted just twice on the day. Halftime Stats: Score: 24-0 First downs: 16 to 5 for Jacksonville Time of possession: Jacksonville 18:51 to 11:09 for Cleveland Defensive Sacks: Jacksonville 2 to 1 for Cleveland Turnovers forced: Jacksonville 2 to 0 for Cleveland Rushing yards: Jacksonville 79 to 29 for Cleveland Passing yards: Jacksonville 155 to 66 for Cleveland Redzone: Jacksonville 2-2 (100%), Cleveland 0/0 Penalties: Jacksonville 2 for 10 yards, Cleveland 6 for 45 yards Points off turnovers: Jacksonville 10, Cleveland 0 The Jacksonville offense continued to push the envelope following the half, with Trevor Lawrence leading the team on a four-play, 60-yard touchdown drive to open the second quarter, extending the lead to 31 and effectively ending the day for Lawrence. Best highlight: Jakobi Meyers standing still in the end zone, with little semblance of defense by Cleveland, may not have heavily impacted the final outcome, but it eliminated any thought of a Browns comeback. if you see 16 rolling left it's over pic.twitter.com/9sFsqs7NTm — Gus Logue (@gus_logue) September 13, 2026 Biggest play(s) of the game: According to rbsdm.com, the biggest play of the game by Expected Points Added (EPA) and win probability (-11%) was Foye Oluokun’s first-quarter interception (-6.4 EPA). Key stats (traditional): QB Trevor Lawrence: 18/23 for 245 yards, 4 touchdowns, 0 turnovers, 150.6 passer rating WR Parker Washington: 5 catches on 6 targets for 83 yards (16.6 YPR), and a touchdown RB Bhayshul Tuten: 15 carries, 66 yards (4.4 YPC), 1 reception for 22 yards DE Josh Hines-Allen: 5 tackles, 2 solo, 1.5 sacks, 1 TFL DE Travon Walker: 2 tackles, 1 solo, 1.5 sacks, 1 TFL, 1 pass defensed LB Ventrell Miller: 10 tackles, 7 solo, 1 sack, 2 TFL LB Foye Oluokun: 4 tackles, 3 solo, 1 interception Notable statistical gaps: Score: 34-10 First downs: Jacksonville 23 to 14 for Cleveland Time of possession: Jacksonville 33:51 to 26:09 for Cleveland Defensive Sacks: Jacksonville 5 to 1 for Cleveland Turnovers forced: Jacksonville 2 to 0 for Cleveland Rushing yards: Jacksonville 126 to 87 for Cleveland Passing yards: Jacksonville 234 to 185 for Cleveland Redzone: Jacksonville 2-2 (100%), Cleveland 0/2 (0%) Third Down: Jacksonville 5/10 (50%), Cleveland 1/8 (12.5%) Penalties: Jacksonville 4 for 25 yards, Cleveland 11 for 75 yards Points off turnovers: Jacksonville 10, Cleveland 0 View the full box score here Game balls: Special Teams: Cam Little: 2/2 with a long of 47 yards and 4/4 on extra points Defense: Ventrell Miller: 10 tackles, 7 solo, 1 sack, 2 TFL Offense: QB Trevor Lawrence: 18/23 for 245 yards, 4 touchdowns, 0 turnovers, 150.6 passer rating Post-game notables: 1. Parker’s Clearly the No. 1 WR A consistent question throughout the fantasy football community and the Jacksonville Jaguars fan base this off-season has been: What will Parker Washington be for the 2026 season? That question was emphatically answered in the opening half of the game, with Washington leading the Jaguars in targets, with six by halftime before the game was out of hand. He ended the day with his halftime stat line of 5 catches on 6 targets for 83 yards (16.6 YPR), and a touchdown. 2. Dominance on defense Anthony Campanile’s defense played with their hair on fire in front of the home crowd on Sunday with 5 sacks, 6 tackles for loss, 8 quarterback hits, two turnovers, 0/2 in the red zone (0%), and 1/8 on third down (12.5%). Pure dominance by the Jacksonville defense. 3. Jaguars avoid serious injury With wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. heading into the locker room at the half, for a brief moment there was concern in the Duval fan base. Thomas headed to the locker room in the middle of the second quarter after injuring his shoulder attempting to recover a fumble from the offense.…

title: Chiefs-Broncos Week 1 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos for “Monday Night Football” in Week 1, our writers predicted the final score and result. The Chiefs enter the AFC West battle as 2.5-point favorites according to FanDuel Sportsbook. In the old […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - NOVEMBER 10: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) looks to pass around Kansas City Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones (95) on November 10th, 2024 at GEHA Field Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos for “Monday Night Football” in Week 1, our writers predicted the final score and result. The Chiefs enter the AFC West battle as 2.5-point favorites according to FanDuel Sportsbook . In the old school, with home-field advantage, this points to the game basically being a toss-up. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I am not as down on the Chiefs as this will make it sound. I expect them to make the playoffs and challenge for the AFC West title. However, this offense has not appeared together in the preseason. I think Denver’s defense will show the most readiness of the units that take the field on Monday. I expect the Broncos to come out on top in an ugly affair. Broncos 19, Chiefs 13 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) Both teams will be missing key pieces heading into Monday Night, especially along the offensive and defensive lines. Broncos star pass rusher Jonathan Cooper is on the NFL Commissioner Exempt List, while Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons is not likely to play due to a back injury. This will leave the Chiefs starting rookie Khalil Benson at right tackle, while the Broncos will likely go rusher by committee to make up for Cooper. This isn’t great news for the Chiefs, but they can focus on proving Benson helps with chips and extra slides to the left, especially when he ends up going against Nik Bonitto. Overall, this game will likely come down to which offense builds momentum early and sustains drives late, especially with both quarterbacks coming off serious injury. Kenneth Walker will make his home debut, and the Chiefs should look to pound the rock with him early and often to let Mahomes ease into the game. Chiefs 21, Broncos 17 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I’ve got the Chiefs beating the Broncos because I think Patrick Mahomes is playing with a chip on his shoulder with so many people counting him and Kansas City out. Adding Kenneth Walker should give this offense the balance it’s been missing and take some pressure off Mahomes. I also really like the upside of this young, improved Chiefs defense. I think KC reminds everybody why you don’t bet against Mahomes. Chiefs 24, Broncos 23 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) I expect this game to remain tight throughout. Neither team’s starters played many preseason snaps together, so I anticipate some early rust—particularly from both offenses. The defenses could control the first half before the quarterbacks and play-callers begin settling into the game. Ultimately, I believe the opener will be decided late in the fourth quarter. Mahomes leads one final drive, Kansas City kicks the winning field goal, and the Chiefs open the season with a three-point victory. Chiefs 20 Broncos 17 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) My heart says Chiefs, my head says otherwise. An undrafted rookie left tackle protecting Mahomes’ blindside in his first game back from injury doesn’t inspire confidence. Nor does Chris Jones showing up on the injury report late in the week. I just feel like there’s too much on paper against the Chiefs in this one. But it’s just game 1, and it doesn’t mean I’m down on them for the entire season. Broncos 24, Chiefs 20 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) I understand the trepidation over the Chiefs entering this game without a proven left tackle. Especially since this is Mahomes’ first game back since injury. But I also expect Kansas City to run the rock a lot. I don’t think this is going to be a high-scoring affair. Despite public opinion on social media, I think Bo Nix is still just an average young quarterback. And if the Patriots vs. Seahawks game taught us anything, it’s that when a mediocre young QB meets a really good defense, the defense usually wins. Now I do think Denver has better pass catchers than New England, but I also think the Chiefs’ secondary matches up really well against Denver. I think both teams keep this one close, and Denver has a shot to win at the end of the game, and just like Seattle’s defense, the Chiefs break their little Donkey hearts and walk away with the win at home to start the season. Chiefs 16, Broncos 13 Nate Christensen Denver has been a tough matchup for the Chiefs these past few years due to their ability to play man coverage against our wide receivers and their explosive pass rush. Those things still remain, and the Chiefs are dealing with their best tackle, Josh Simmons, being unavailable for this game. I worry about the Chiefs’ ability to throw the ball in this game. I do think the Chiefs’ defense keeps this game close, but Denver pulls ahead late to win. Denver 19, Chiefs 13 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) As unideal as it is to begin the season with two starters down, especially when your reigning-division-champion opponent has no injuries (Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper is on the Commissioner’s Exempt List), this game is as make-or-break as a season opener can be. I believe a win can set Kansas City up for the comeback season optimists are expecting, while a loss could spiral into a similarly frustrating season as 2025. There is that much riding on this game, and I think you will see it from the players, coaching staff and fans in the best way possible. We may only have five years left of the Arrowhead advantage, but it will still be alive and well until then, especially on a beautiful Monday evening in September. Chiefs Kingdom makes a difference on defense, energized by the all-time aura moment when Patrick Mahomes runs out of the tunnel 274 days after tearing his ACL and LCL. I expect to be fired up about the pass rush after this one. Chiefs 20, Broncos 17

title: Chiefs-Broncos: 5 things to watch in Week 1 matchup
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will kick off the 2026 season at home against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football.” The game will kick off at 7:15 Arrowhead time and air on ABC and ESPN. This offseason, the Chiefs tried to reload after a disappointing 6-11 season in 2025, the first time Kansas City missed the playoffs […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Alex Forsyth #54 of the Denver Broncos lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will kick off the 2026 season at home against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football.” The game will kick off at 7:15 Arrowhead time and air on ABC and ESPN . This offseason, the Chiefs tried to reload after a disappointing 6-11 season in 2025, the first time Kansas City missed the playoffs since 2014. Multiple players will make regular-season debuts at Arrowhead on Monday Night. Denver just had its best season in a decade, winning the AFC West and hosting the AFC Championship Game. After a decade of Kansas City dominance, the Broncos switched the script under head coach Sean Payton and finished 14-3, sweeping the Chiefs in the process. Both teams have a lot to prove in 2026; one of football’s best stages will host the first AFC West battle of the season. Here are five things to watch: 1. The return of Patrick Mahomes As improbable as it may seem, Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes will return to start his first game since December 14th of last season, when he tore his ACL in a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers . For months, it has been widely speculated that Mahomes could miss time at the start of the 2026 season, but over the past couple of weeks, he and the Chiefs have made it clear he will suit up and start on Monday Night against Denver. #Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes walking off the podium today: “Hopefully I’m done with the questions about the leg.” 😅 ( 📽️ @KSHB41 ) pic.twitter.com/sZWOgsD47Y — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 10, 2026 As a reminder, Mahomes did not play in any preseason games. It will be interesting to see how head coach Andy Reid and the offensive brain trust handle Mahomes early, especially against a fierce Denver defense. It would be in the team’s best interest to give Mahomes as many layups as possible early in the game, allowing him to get into a flow as he readjusts to the speed of the game. I expect to see a few deep shots throughout the game. 2. How the Chiefs work around a hampered tackle position The Josh Simmons saga continued and once again has taken a strange path with no clear answers. The only thing certain is that he will not play on Monday Night, as the Chiefs made clear. I asked Andy Reid what goes into deciding that an undrafted rookie free agent like Kahlil Benson is ready to start Week 1 at left tackle. pic.twitter.com/rLaJ8uXaCe — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) September 10, 2026 Undrafted rookie Khalil Benson— who played mostly right tackle in camp— will make his first-ever NFL start in his first regular-season game. From starting in the National Championship for Indiana last season to making his NFL debut at left tackle, Benson has a tall task ahead of him. Denver’s pass rush might not have the name power it did last season, but outside linebacker Nik Bonitto, 14 sacks in 2025, will still be screaming off the edge, and it would seem likely that they will line him up directly over Benson. The Chiefs coaching staff should be prepared for this and able to provide slide protection to the left, as well as chips from tight ends and running backs. While the move has some fans scratching their heads, having Benson start on the left side is an effort to keep Jaylon Moore on the right side of the line where he has appeared to be more comfortable, and where he will line up when Simmons returns from injury. Moore needs to have a big game as the Chiefs will be giving help to Benson. I expect Reid to make the game plan very offensive-line friendly, with run-action looks as well as rollout plays. 3. New-look secondary The Chiefs’ secondary looks much different than it did this time last year, but that is not necessarily a bad thing. With Alohi Gilman and Jaden Hicks set to line up as the safeties — Chamarri Conner (Knee) will miss Week 1 — Nohl Williams, L’Jarius Sneed, and rookie Mansoor Delane will line up as the corners, with rookie Jadon Canady rotating in. While the unit may take time to gel, it has the potential to become solid, especially under the tutelage of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo and defensive backs Dave Merrit. L’Jarius Sneed on who called him to return to the Chiefs 🤣 In Spags we trust. pic.twitter.com/KzbMLpDLNp — SleeperChiefs (@SleeperChiefsKC) September 2, 2026 The unit will have its work cut out for it in Week 1 against a reloaded Broncos receiver unit featuring wide receivers Courtland Sutton, Jaylen Waddle, Marvin Mims and tight end Evan Engram. As the unit gels, there could be some early issues, but the potential of the young corners, Delane and Williams, should help propel the unit into one of the stronger units in the NFL by the season’s end. 4. Rookie defensive linemen Two of the Chiefs’ top 50 picks in the draft this past spring were defensive tackle Peter Woods and edge rusher R Mason Thomas. It's the preseason. These are backup-caliber players, but this movement and explosion from Thomas is absolutely transferable. The OT tries to jump set and force him up the field, but Thomas is too quick. Bends the arc and a strip sack. pic.twitter.com/yXsmldXFvh — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 29, 2026 Both flashed in training camp and the preseason, with Thomas drawing the most attention, displaying a combination of speed and bend that the Chiefs have not had off the edge in a while. This is where Woods will make an impact as a rookie. Penetrating and creating disruption, whether it is blowing up cutback lanes in zone or quick pressure looks. A supremely athletic, moldable player. pic.twitter.com/kkQZJZowIA — Caleb James (@CJScoobs) August 29, 2026 Woods was less disruptive in the preseason, but his impact should be more seen when he shares the field with star defensive tackle Chris Jones on Monday. While both players excel in pass rushing situations, they will have to earn the right to get after Bo Nix. The Broncos have a powerful offensive line and good backs, which means the front seven, including both Thomas and Woods, will need to stand up against the run. 5. Kenneth Walker It has been many years since the Chiefs have had a truly elite running back, but on Monday night, Kenneth Walker will make his debut with such a title. The Chiefs didn’t use Walker much in the preseason, but with offensive line issues and Mahomes coming into his first game post-surgery, I would expect a heavy dose of the fifth-year running back. Walker’s skill set to hit cutback lanes and explode out of the backfield in the passing game makes him a perfect fit for the Chiefs. He is in for a big season. Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid tells Doug Pederson that he cannot wait to cut new running back Kenneth Walker loose this season 👀🏈 Watch the full interview now! https://t.co/viaQJvCy1h pic.twitter.com/cH61UlrUXw — Westwood One Sports (@westwood1sports) September 11, 2026

title: Kingdom Keys: 3 keys to a Chiefs victory over the Broncos in Week 1
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs will begin a season unlike any other in the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes when the team welcomes the Denver Broncos to Arrowhead Stadium on Monday night. The Chiefs will have a chance to put last season in the franchise’s rearview mirror, but beating the Broncos will require them to win […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Running back Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs watches game action from the sidelines of an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will begin a season unlike any other in the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes when the team welcomes the Denver Broncos to Arrowhead Stadium on Monday night. The Chiefs will have a chance to put last season in the franchise’s rearview mirror, but beating the Broncos will require them to win in three critical areas: Offensive key: Reach 125 rushing yards Kansas City cannot allow Denver’s pass rush to turn Monday night into a four-quarter assault on Mahomes. The Broncos recorded an NFL-leading 68 sacks last season and can consistently generate pressure without sending additional defenders. That makes establishing the running game essential — especially with Mahomes playing his first regular-season game since tearing his ACL. The Chiefs need to finish with at least 125 rushing yards. That does not mean the ball should be taken out of Mahomes’ hands, but the offense must run it effectively enough to keep Denver’s defensive front honest. A productive running game would create manageable third downs, slow down the Broncos’ edge rushers and give Kansas City more opportunities to use play-action. It would also prevent Mahomes from having to drop back 40 or more times against one of the league’s most dangerous defensive fronts. Denver allowed only 3.9 yards per rushing attempt last season, so reaching the 100-yard mark will not be easy. But if the Chiefs become one-dimensional, the Broncos can attack Mahomes without hesitation. Defensive key: Make Bo Nix uncomfortable Defensively, the Chiefs must first put Denver in situations where it has to throw the football, then make Bo Nix uncomfortable when it does. That begins with limiting the Broncos’ rushing attack and winning on early downs. If Kansas City can force Denver into second-and-long and third-and-long situations, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo can open up his pressure package and force Nix to make quick decisions. The Chiefs cannot allow him to settle into a rhythm with easy completions and extended drives. Pressure does not always have to result in a sack. Moving Nix off his spot, forcing him to reset his feet and speeding up his internal clock can be just as important. Kansas City’s defensive front must collapse the pocket, while the secondary holds up long enough for that pressure to arrive. If the Chiefs can make Denver’s offense one-dimensional and consistently force Nix to operate under pressure, they will create opportunities for sacks, turnovers and short possessions. X-Factor: Win the field-position battle The x-factor is making sure Kansas City’s offense is not repeatedly asked to drive 80 yards to score. When the Broncos punt, the Chiefs’ return unit must secure the football, get upfield, and take advantage of every available yard. Even when a return does not produce a highlight, an additional 10 or 15 yards can completely change the approach of an offensive possession. The same responsibility falls on Kansas City’s punt and coverage units. When the Chiefs are forced to give the ball away, they need to pin Denver deep and make the Broncos earn every yard. Field position could be especially important in an opening-week divisional game in which both offenses may need time to find their rhythm. Giving Mahomes shorter fields while forcing Nix to consistently start drives near his own goal line would give Kansas City a significant advantage. The bottom line The Chiefs do not need Mahomes to carry the entire offense in his first game back. Kansas City needs to support him by reaching 125 rushing yards, controlling Denver’s pass rush and avoiding obvious passing situations. Defensively, the group must stop the run and make Nix uncomfortable. On special teams, the Chiefs must consistently create shorter fields for their offense and longer ones for Denver. If Kansas City can accomplish those three things, it will have an excellent opportunity to open its new season — and its attempt to reclaim the AFC West — with a statement victory on Monday night.

title: Chiefs News: Chiefs’ comeback campaign named top NFL storyline
summary: NFL’s Week 1 only has one game left on the schedule: the “Monday Night Football” matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium. There has been plenty to take away from the first Sunday of the season: Buffalo Bills’ quarterback Josh Allen looks as unstoppable (and fortunate) as ever, the […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 27: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders at Arrowhead Stadium on October 27, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images NFL’s Week 1 only has one game left on the schedule: the “Monday Night Football” matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium. There has been plenty to take away from the first Sunday of the season: Buffalo Bills ’ quarterback Josh Allen looks as unstoppable (and fortunate) as ever, the Cincinnati Bengals may have a defense for once and the Los Angeles Chargers lost to the Arizona Cardinals at home by multiple scores. Take away from that what you will. Yet, the biggest storyline of the NFL season surrounds the team that will host the last game of the week, according to NFL Hall of Famer and FOX Sports analyst Charles Woodson. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Why Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs’ Response To Disappointing 2025 Is Top Storyline In 2026 | FOX Sports “Last year, we were deprived in the playoffs of seeing the best of the best,” Woodson said. “Patrick Mahomes has been Superman. Over the last 10 years, this Kansas City Chiefs team has been to five Super Bowls, and they won three of them. This past year, he had his first major injury where he had to miss significant time. “So, I want to know how that affects him mentally, because he’s had to carry this team rushing the football over this 10-year span. Over this 10-year span, they’ve only had one 1,000-yard rusher, and that was back in 2017.” Chiefs vs. Broncos: 9 things to watch in Monday night season opener | KMBC 9 2. Bo Nix is back, too Mahomes isn’t the only quarterback returning from injury. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is also returning from a serious injury. Nix broke his ankle during Denver’s 2025 playoff run and missed the AFC Championship Game. He had an impressive season before the injury and delivered in key moments, including leading Denver to a late victory over Mahomes and the Chiefs last November. Five Things to Watch on Monday, Broncos vs. Chiefs | The Mothership 2. Kansas City will aim to flip the script on its one-possession struggles from a season ago. The Chiefs and Broncos experienced the two polar opposite ends of the spectrum when it came to one-possession games in 2025. Denver was a record-matching 11-2 in those contests last year, tying the 2022 Vikings and the 2024 Chiefs for the most one-score wins in a single season in NFL history. Kansas City, meanwhile, went just 1-9 in one-possession games after winning a league-record 17 consecutive one-score games prior to last season. In other words, both the Chiefs and Broncos were in virtually every game each team played last season. The difference truly game down to the fact that Denver made the handful of plays necessary to come out on top in nearly every close game that it played while Kansas City consistently came up just short. Broncos vs. Chiefs Monday Night Football betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props | Yahoo! Sports Player props RB Brashard Smith over 12.5 rushing + receiving yards Through thick-and-thin last season, Brashard Smith was a pet props project of ours over at THE WINDOW, as a quasi-gadget player out of the Chiefs’ backfield, capable of turning a few touches into big plays. Before Mahomes’ injury, Smith had at least three touches in a six-of-seven game stretch. In this second season, more should be on Smith’s plate for an offense that he was added to late in the 2025 draft because it has lacked explosiveness. Chiefs Confidence Meter: How I Feel About the Team Against Broncos in Week 1 | Sports Illustrated The X-factor to monitor in Week 1 is wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. An offseason trade pickup from the Miami Dolphins, the speedy wideout is a constant threat to stretch the field and might be precisely what the Broncos were missing. The 2025 Broncos sat 22nd leaguewide with a 7.5-yard average depth of target. In a sport that revolves around generating explosive plays — particularly in the passing game — Waddle entering the fold is a noteworthy development. First-round corner Mansoor Delane and company need to be on the lookout. ‘Everybody’s fired up’: Chiefs fans gather ahead of season opener against Broncos | KCTV 5 Joy said Monday’s game will be his 250th consecutive Chiefs home game. Joy said the streak started as a personal goal. “It was just a goal. One day I said I wonder how many games I’ve been to. And I was at 173 so I said I’m gonna go for 200. Then I hit 200, so I said let’s do 250. But you know I’m getting tired. I don’t know if I’m gonna make 300, but I’ll try. But, that counts Germany, that counts London. Those were all home games. All the COVID games, I mean I never called in sick,” Joy said. Around the NFL Bears’ offense makes statement with ‘amazing’ 59-point opener | ESPN The Bears walked away from their opener with a historic 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers, one that saw them score the fourth-most points in a game in franchise history (Chicago began its 107th season Sunday) and saw the teams combine for 96 points, most ever in a season opener. Following the win, Johnson doubled down on his aspirations for the offense. “That will always be the goal,” he said. “We want to be the highest scoring, we want to have the most wins, we want to win Super Bowls. That’s what we do. We didn’t get into this profession trying to be mediocre or average.” NFL teams on pace for highest scoring Week 1 since 1970 merger | The Athletic But even though Bears-Panthers might go down as Week 1’s most memorable shootout, scoreboards were lighting up around the country. In total, 10 teams scored 30-plus points, tied for the third-most such teams in Week 1, behind only 1986 (12 teams) and 2002 (11). Ravens RB Derrick Henry passes Marcus Allen for third on all-time rushing TD list | NFL.com “Love Marcus Allen,” Henry said after the game. “He’s a great dude, and for my name to be mentioned over his is an honor. I’m very grateful.” Henry now has 125 career scores on the ground — two ahead of Hall of Famer Marcus Allen (123). His record-breaking score came in vintage Henry fashion as he rumbled through the Colts defense for an explosive 32-yard TD to contribute to a 31-point first half for first-year coach Jesse Minter. Saints-Lions included controversial reversal of strip-sack-score | Pro Football Talk “If the defender contacts the passer prior to the passer starting the throwing motion, then it can be ruled as a backward pass. Because Goff already started his throwing motion and then the defender contacted him, it is therefore a forward pass.” Butterworth explained that the “determining factor” is whether the passer begins his throwing motion before contact from the defender. “The throwing motion starts as he begins to bring the ball up as a part of his windup and then the defender’s contact made the pass go backwards,” Butterworth said. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs-Broncos Week 1 final injury report: Chris Jones has clear status Defensive tackle Chris Jones (Calf) did not participate in Saturday’s practice after a limited practice on Friday, but will be good to go with no game status. title: Chiefs Market Movers: The team’s Bulls and Bears ahead of Week 1
summary: The sentiment around your Kansas City Chiefs has been quite volatile. We went from peak optimism when training camp broke to widespread panic as the team made roster cuts and started preparation for the Denver Broncos. The market doesn’t trust the health or depth of the Chiefs offense, or that the defense will be improved […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Emmett Johnson #10 of the Kansas City Chiefs finds running room in the first quarter of an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The sentiment around your Kansas City Chiefs has been quite volatile. We went from peak optimism when training camp broke to widespread panic as the team made roster cuts and started preparation for the Denver Broncos . The market doesn’t trust the health or depth of the Chiefs offense, or that the defense will be improved enough. Expect the volatility to continue late into Monday night’s opener against a tough division opponent. We’ll finally have some concrete evidence on film to review, instead of just speculation. Here are a few Chiefs who look to be trending heading into Week 1: Bulls Running back Emmett Johnson : Not only did the rookie impress all summer, but he literally took a grown man’s job. When it came time for roster cuts, the Chiefs were confident enough in Johnson’s ability to let veteran Emari Demercado hit the waiver wire. As the season wears on, NFL teams need to be able to rely on a number of running backs — injuries happen, gameplans vary, roles evolve. It’s no longer a stretch to say that the former Cornhusker is likely to get the bulk of the carries if Kenneth Walker were to get injured. What we’ll be watching for on Monday night and going forward: is there a significant role for the rookie (and can he capitalize) even when Walker is healthy and productive? Sack Nation: If there were ever a time in recent years to be optimistic about the Chiefs being able to field a competent pass rush, it’s right now. Defensive tackle Chris Jones and defnensive ends George Karlaftis and R Mason Thomas might be a formidable trio, combining the unique traits of Jones on the inside with some actual speed rush from Thomas on the outside. Even more encouraging is the prospect of some actual depth with defensive tackle Peter Woods and defensive ends Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Ashton Gillotte, and maybe Jack Pyburn. To win in the NFL, you need to throw waves of pass rushers at opposing offenses, and the Chiefs finally have the chance to do just that. Defensive back L’Jarius Sneed: The coaches have spoken glowingly about the reclamation project, and he seems confident in his return to Arrowhead and the Nickel (slot cornerback) position. All signs point to a significant role for No. 38, who showed a wide range of skills in his previous stint in KC. He’s a pesky, physical playmaker who was once able to matchup on a team’s best wide receiver. It’s no sure thing that he’s still playing at a high level— but if he is even 70% of his former self, he can help lead this young defense in 2026. Others trending in the right direction this week: Tight end Jake Briningstool, Wide receiver Rashee Rice, Wide receiver Xavier Worthy , Cornerback Nohl Williams, Cornerback Mansoor Delane Bears Offensive lineman Kahlil Benson: It’s a big deal when an undrafted tryout player makes the 53-man roster of a contending team. So, we shouldn’t be too hard on the big guy — he’s accomplished a rare feat just being here. The fact that he may be the starter at left tackle in the opener is insane. But, the Broncos are a very difficult matchup for an experienced left tackle. Denver will throw one of the NFL’s best speed rushers, Nik Bonitto, at the rookie— which is a little terrifying. If it goes poorly, it could shake a young player’s confidence. Let’s hope for Mahomes’s sake that Benson gets plenty of help on Monday night. Left tackle Josh Simmons: We shouldn’t speculate about a player’s character or their love of the game; we simply don’t have enough reliable information to draw a conclusion. But, there is always plenty of speculation about player injuries, especially when the team is vague with public comments. Back injuries can be very tricky for offensive linemen, and we just don’t know where he is in his recovery. Stack that on top of the mysteriously extended absence last season, and it’s easy to see why many people are doubting the talented tackle. The team needs him to be available on a consistent basis this season, but neither the Chiefs nor Simmons are publicly projecting confidence that the investment is going to pay off. Kicker Harrison Butker: It must be a brutal job to be an NFL kicker. Maybe not as physically brutal as other positions, but certainly more stressful and requires more mental toughness than most. Miss a handful of kicks over a 17-game season, and you go from being the best, most clutch kicker in the league to the most overpaid and frustrating players on the field. If the Chiefs are going to run the ball more this season, they might rely more heavily on their kicker to win close games. Every miss is going to matter this season, and Butker just doesn’t feel as automatic as he did a couple of years ago. Others trending in the wrong direction this week: Returner Nikko Remigio, Quarterback Justin Fields, Tight end Noah Gray Value (Sleeper) Picks Running back/ returner Brashard Smith: What if the release of Demercado was in part because Brashard Smith has improved enough to be the third-down back? Dave Toub also called Smith the most improved player on the team over the past year; what if he’s able to overtake Remigio on kick and punt returns? I’d buy stock in Brashard, on returns, third downs, screens, and maybe even some gadget plays. Wide receiver Cyrus Allen: Was he just a camp sensation, or does he have staying power? Based on what we saw in the draft and offseason process, he’s got the traits: strong hands, great route running ability, enough speed, body control, and aggression to be a starter in this league for a long time. The preseason game production wasn’t good, but there were moments that gave us hope that Allen could be great. It may take a while for him to get opportunities in the regular season, but if he’s on the field Monday night and makes a couple of plays, we’ll know he’s ahead of schedule.

title: Madden Simulation Week 1: Monday Night Football! We are so back!
summary: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs are home under the lights at Arrowhead Stadium, taking on the Denver Broncos. Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 27. First quarter The Chiefs’ defense held strong on the Broncos’ opening drive as Denver went three-and-out. Chris Jones made it look easy, getting through the […]
full_text: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs are home under the lights at Arrowhead Stadium , taking on the Denver Broncos . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here. First quarter The Chiefs’ defense held strong on the Broncos’ opening drive as Denver went three-and-out. Chris Jones made it look easy, getting through the Broncos’ offensive line for a tackle for loss to help force the punt. The absence of Josh Simmons paid dividends as Nik Bonitto was able to sack Mahomes, forcing the Chiefs to punt. Kenneth Walker’s first carry in a Chiefs uniform went for two yards. End of first quarter: Broncos 0, Chiefs 0 Second quarter J.K. Dobbins was able to pick up a first down on the first play of the quarter, getting the Broncos inside the Chiefs’ 10-yard line. One play later, Bo Nix connected with Troy Franklin on a hard flat route for a nine-yard touchdown to give the Broncos the lead. Brashard Smith picked up 21 yards on a second-down run, putting the Chiefs inside Broncos territory for the first time of the game at the Broncos’ 38-yard line. Three plays later, the Chiefs faced a third-and-eight, and Broncos defensive tackle D.J. Jones sacked Mahomes, pushing the Chiefs outside of field-goal range and forcing them to punt on a promising drive. Following the Chiefs’ punt, Nix threw three straight incompletions before Denver punted the ball back to Kansas City. Bonitto sacked Mahomes for the second time of the game on third-and-six in Broncos territory, once again pushing the Chiefs out of field-goal range. The battle of field position continued. The Broncos would punt it back to the Chiefs, and on the ensuing drive, Mahomes dotted up Xavier Worthy twice. The first reception got the Chiefs across midfield, while another with 16 seconds left got them to the Broncos’ 25-yard line. Mahomes would end up being sacked by Zach Allen as time ran out in the half. End of second quarter: Broncos 7, Chiefs 0 Third quarter Andy Reid dialed up more chances for Mahomes to throw the football, as two first-down passes to Worthy and one to Tyquan Thornton helped the Chiefs get across midfield. Then it was the Kenneth Walker show, as he ripped off a 15-yard run before breaking loose for a 29-yard touchdown to tie the game. Felix Anudike-Uzomah’s name was called in the rotation, and he made the most of it, sacking Nix to force the Broncos to punt on their opening drive of the second half. The Chiefs went three-and-out. The Broncos went three-and-out. On third-and-six from the Chiefs’ own 46-yard line, Mahomes rifled a pass down the middle of the field to Thornton, who took it to the 22-yard line. One play later, a handoff to Walker got the Chiefs to the one-yard line. End of third quarter: Broncos 7, Chiefs 7 Fourth quarter On second-and-goal, Mahomes found his favorite target, Travis Kelce, for the touchdown to give the Chiefs the lead. The Broncos punted back to the Chiefs. The Chiefs once again punted back to the Broncos. The Broncos punted. Mahomes was sacked for the fifth time of the game on third down, forcing the Chiefs to punt. Nix, from the Broncos’ own 46-yard line, found a streaking Evan Engram, who somehow burned three Chiefs defenders before dropping a catch in the end zone. End of the fourth quarter: Broncos 14, Chiefs 14 Overtime The Chiefs’ defense forced the Broncos’ offense to go three-and-out and punt the ball back to Kansas City. The Chiefs marched downfield, and the Mahomes-to-Worthy connection resulted in two first downs. Walker rushed to the Broncos ‘ 12-yard line. Tyquan Thornton was left wide open in the end zone, and Mahomes found him on a post route for the game-winning touchdown. Final score: Chiefs 20, Broncos 14 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 18 for 23, 204 passing yards, 2 touchdowns Box Nix: 15 for 25, 157 passing yards, 2 touchdowns Kenneth Walker: 15 rushing attempts, 102 rushing yards, 1 touchdown J.K Dobbins: 11 rushing attempts, 24 rushing yards R.J. Harvey: 5 rushing attempts, 6 rushing yards. Xavier Worthy: 7 receptions, 105 yards Tyquan Thornton: 4 receptions, 70 yards Travis Kelce: 3 receptions, 20 yards, 1 touchdown Troy Franklin: 5 receptions, 65 yards, 1 touchdown Evan Engram: 4 receptions, 44 yards Courtland Sutton: 2 receptions, 13 yards Nik Bonitto: 3 sacks, 4 tackles for loss Zach Allen: 2 sacks, 3 tackles for loss Felix Anduike-Uzomah: 1 sack Chris Jones: 6 tackles, 2 tackles for loss Next week, will once again be under the lights, but this time for Sunday Night Football vs. the Indianapolis Colts . Until then, we will see how it is played out inside the EA Universe!

title: Chargers vs. Cardinals Game Recap: New-look Bolts implode in 26-14 loss
summary: The only way I could feasibly describe the Chargers in their 26-14 loss to the Cardinals in the season opener is…”worst-case scenario.” The worst-case scenario for the Chargers in what was arguably their easiest game of the year was going to be if the Mike McDaniel offense floundered, the Chris O’Leary defense looked abysmal, and […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Burch #52 of the Arizona Cardinals sacks Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers in the fourth quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The only way I could feasibly describe the Chargers in their 26-14 loss to the Cardinals in the season opener is…”worst-case scenario.” The worst-case scenario for the Chargers in what was arguably their easiest game of the year was going to be if the Mike McDaniel offense floundered, the Chris O’Leary defense looked abysmal, and Justin Herbert looked like he did in the team’s last two playoff games. All of that happened in this single game in what was also Jim Harbaugh’s first loss in a season opener as a head coach. Herbert began the game hot with smart, precision passing. However, he barely had the ball thanks to a Bolts defense that couldn’t find a way off the field. Arizona essentially doubled the time of possession battle in the first half and it did not get better in the final 30 minutes. Herbert finished with 209 passing yards and a score with an interception that looked way out of left field by his standards…but maybe it is now given his 2025 season. Omarion Hampton score the team’s first touchdown of the season on a blood-pumping run from nine yards out, but otherwise found little room on the ground and finished with 43 yards on 12 carries. Ladd McConkey caught three passes for 60 yards on the opening drive but only caught two more for 22 yards and the aforementioned score through the remainder of the game. David Njoku caught five passes for 58 yards while Oronde Gadsden II caught two for 32 yards. Defensively, Derwin James led the team with 10 tackles and a pass breakup. Khalil Mack recorded the team’s only tackle for loss and *should have had a sack but Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett managed to wiggle out and get a pass of to avoid it. The Bolts were bad, bad, bad on both sides of the ball. The only silver lining was McConkey, but he ended up leaving the game when the team needed him the most. What added a bit of insult to injury, however, was just how bad the offense looked without McConkey. It was night and day. That cannot be the case moving forward. The Chargers will be back at home in Week Two to host the Raiders (1-0). Kickoff is scheduled for 1:25 p.m. PST. First Quarter The Cardinals came out hot on offense to start the game after receiving the opening kickoff. On the first play from scrimmage, quarterback Jacobby Brissett found tight end Trey McBride for a 27-yard gain. They converted on multiple third downs as well, including a Brissett scramble on third-and-eight. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love capped the drive off with a five-yard touchdown run in which he bounced outside to the left and beat Cam Hart to the pylon. Justin Herbert and the Chargers offense retaliated with their own explosive drive led by Ladd McConkey’s three receptions for 60 yards. Once in the red zone, Omarion Hampton bowled over a trio of Cardinals defenders and left tackle Rashawn Slater helped push him into the end zone from nine yards out to tie the game at 7-7 with 4:22 remaining in the period. Omarion Hampton breaking tackle after tackle on his way to the end zone 😤 AZvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RyNMegHb5o — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Second Quarter The Chargers defense finally held the Cardinals on a third down when Cam Hart broke up a deep pass intended for Michael Wilson. Kicker Chad Ryland then pushed a 54-yard field goal wide right to give the ball right back to the Bolts. On the other side, Hampton started the drive with a 14-yard run followed up by another first down catch-and-run by tight end David Njoku. Unfortunately Hampton ran into the back of wideout Tre’ Harris which popped the ball loose which was recovered by Arizona at their own 34-yard line. Arizona went 12 plays following the turnover to bring the ball down to the Chargers’ nine-yard line. Facing third-and-three, Brissett found McBride at the sticks but safety Tony Jefferson jarred ball loose to force another field goal which was good by Ryland. That brought the Cardinals back in front 10-7. The Chargers continued to churn and churn on offense, reaching all the way to the three-yard line of Arizona after moving 66 yards in 10 plays. After a third-down run by Herbert on third down, Harbaugh chose to roll the dice and go for it on fourth down. Herbert set up in the shotgun with five wide. He took the snap, and surveyed the field, but Trey Pipkins (who was in at left guard for Awosika) was beat inside to give up a fast pressure on Herbert who did not get rid of the ball before being sacked for 10 yards. Brissett led the Cardinals offense swiftly down the field with little time on the clock and a defensive pass interference call on cornerback Donte Jackson helped turbo their field position into field goal range. Ryland was good from 44 yards out to give Arizona a six-point lead heading into the locker room. Third Quarter The Chargers began the half with the ball but could manage just five plays and 19 yards before punting it away. Arizona took the ball and went on another long drive, this one going 10 plays and 75 yards before kicking another field goal to raise their lead to 16-7 halfway through the quarter. Herbert and the Chargers began their next drive with a huge 48-yard DPI penalty they drew when Tre’ Harris was tackled far up the left sideline. After a pair of two-yard runs, Herbert found McConkey on an out route near the front right pylon for his first touchdown of the game. Dicker converted the PAT and the Bolts had shrunk the Arizona lead down to 16-14. The Chargers finally forced the Cardinals to punt for the first time late in the third quarter. However, their ensuing offensive drive started with a quick moving of the chains but floundered just as fast following a false start penalty by tight end Charlie Kolar. That play was followed by an incompletion, a run for a loss of one yard, and another incompletion where McConkey was hit hard and stayed down holding his back. JK Scott’s punt of 51 yards at least helped swap field position afterwards. Fourth Quarter The Chargers forced another punt from Arizona to begin the quarter which was exactly what they needed to possibly start a comeback. Well, without McConkey, the Chargers went three-and-out before JK Scott had his punt blocked. Alec Ingold recovered the ball but it unfortunately came at the Bolts’ three-yard line. Brissett immediately found McBride for a score to push their lead to 23-14 with 11:44 left in the game. With the ball now down nine, the Chargers needed points in a bad way. The drive started well enough with two movings of the chains thanks to plays from Hampton and Njoku. On first-and-10 from the 40-yard line, Herbert was flushed from the pocket to his right before lofting a deep pass down the field to receiver Derius Davis. Davis was double-covered and the questionable pass was picked off. The Chargers got the ball back with 4:44 remaining and once again looked for points. After an 11-yard run by Herbert, the Chargers had a sequence of four plays that went: Incompletion, false start, false start, and holding. It set up an insurmountable second-and-30 which the Bolts could not get out of before throwing a fourth down pass that came up short. The Cardinals added a field goal to push their lead to 26-14 and that would end up being the final score after the Bolts turned it over on downs once again. Mickens Chargers-Cardinals injury report: Deane Leonard OUT, Tuli Tuipulotu questionable Predicting the Chargers 2026 win record: Recent history says Bolts will be fine Chargers-Cardinals Game Preview: 3 things to watch in Week 1

title: The Giants stole 49ers’ playbook and that is bad news for Rams
summary: The San Francisco 49ers know the recipe for a win over the Los Angeles Rams—and that was on full display again in a stunning Week 1 upset in Australia. The bad news for the Rams is that their next opponent, the New York Giants, seem to have found San Francisco’s cookbook in the back of […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants celebrates a 28-20 win against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers know the recipe for a win over the Los Angeles Rams—and that was on full display again in a stunning Week 1 upset in Australia. The bad news for the Rams is that their next opponent, the New York Giants, seem to have found San Francisco’s cookbook in the back of the cabinet in their win against the Dallas Cowboys. LA enters Week 2 as 8.5-point home favorites over the Giants. A repeat performance by the Giants and Jaxson Dart could cook up a major upset and send the Rams to 0-2 on the young season. There are plenty of parallels between the Giants and 49ers that should make the Rams nervous: NY won time of possession with 36:40 and limited Dallas’ possessions. Despite fewer opportunities with the ball, Dak Prescott threw an interception just before halftime. New York took advantage and scored. That was ultimately the difference in this sped up contest. Make hay in the short passing game Dart gave his best Brock Purdy impression. He was decisive and accurate in the short area of the field, allowing his receivers room to run thereafter. Dart’s longest throw was 19 yards. Read how Purdy got the job done in Week 1 here. Totals by route type: Flat: 3/3 for 29 yards Slant: 2/2 for 18 yards Hitch: 6/8 for 46 yards Crossing: 4/4 for 60 yards Short out: 4/6 for 51 yards Stay committed to the run game New York rushed 37 times for 165 yards and manufactured 84 yards after contact. They remained committed to the ground attack with a 4.45-yard average and an EPA per play of -0.05. Their best work came out of 12 personnel, which is another similarity to San Francisco. Smart situational football San Francisco forced LA into long and unfavorable late downs and distances. The Giants won the early downs and finished 9/11 on third down to extend possessions and keep the ball away from Dallas. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are one of the most formidable duos in the NFL. They can’t impact the game without the football. Find hidden yardage The 49ers stuffed a Matthew Stafford sneak at the half-yard line and then drove 99.5 yards for a score. Fred Warner also forced a late fumble on Tyler Higbee. The Giants capitalized on a late first half interception and then manufactured three long second half drives to suffocate the Cowboys. What this all means for Monday night Despite Dart resembling Purdy in Week 1, he’s been more of an inefficient gunslinging playmaker so far in his career. Barring a stark shift in his style of play, this seems like an isolated storm of events that produced a limited game plan. I’ll need to see Dart do it again before I fully believe. Even without Myles Garrett , the Rams still enter Week 2 with the more talented roster. Winning on the margins in terms of late downs, time of possession, turnovers, etc. are the great equalizer. This is how the 49ers consistently surprise LA and the same recipe for how the Giants can secure their second primetime win in a row.

title: Sean McVay Meter: Fans’ confidence in coach after Week 1
summary: One game does not define a season, but Rams fans have every right to feel frustrated after what unfolded in Melbourne. The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 1 with high expectations, only to deliver a disappointing performance against the San Francisco 49ers. When a team struggles in multiple areas, the head coach is naturally going […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 26: Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams gathers the team during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 26, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images One game does not define a season, but Rams fans have every right to feel frustrated after what unfolded in Melbourne. The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 1 with high expectations, only to deliver a disappointing performance against the San Francisco 49ers. When a team struggles in multiple areas, the head coach is naturally going to face questions, and Sean McVay is no exception. McVay has earned the benefit of the doubt throughout his tenure in Los Angeles. His track record includes a Super Bowl championship, multiple playoff appearances and a reputation as one of the NFL’s best offensive minds. However, expectations have changed. Rams fans are no longer simply hoping for playoff football —they expect this team to win a championship come February. Sean McVay Fan Confidence Meter 9-10 — Unshakable 7-8 — Strong 5-6 — Cautiously Optimistic 3-4 — Frustrated 1-2 — Crisis The Week 1 performance could test the patience of a fan base that believes the Rams have enough talent to make a deep postseason run. Questions about game planning, execution and adjustments will inevitably lead back to McVay. There also could also be lingering frustration surrounding how the team handled Myles Garrett’s knee situation. If Garrett’s knee issues were already a concern in July, some fans may question why the situation wasn’t addressed more aggressively before the regular season. Seeing an important player deal with the consequences now can make those earlier decisions easier to scrutinize. The season is far from over, but the Sean McVay Meter has already moved. Whether it is a temporary reaction to one bad performance or the beginning of deeper concerns will depend heavily on how McVay and the Rams respond in Week 2 .

title: Rams had amazing offseason, dud Week 1
summary: The Los Angeles Rams had one of the best on paper off-season’s in modern sports, then followed that up with a horrible Week 1. Things can always be worse, but the Week 1 that L.A. just has proven again why picking a Super Bowl winner in August is nearly an impossible task. Starting with the […]
full_text: Westchester, - July 26: Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams speaks head coach Sean McVay along with owner Stan Kronke after the first day of the Los Angeles Rams Rams training camp on the campus of Loyola Marymount University in Westchester on Sunday, July 26, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams had one of the best on paper off-season’s in modern sports, then followed that up with a horrible Week 1. Things can always be worse, but the Week 1 that L.A. just has proven again why picking a Super Bowl winner in August is nearly an impossible task. Starting with the offseason, some would say the Rams received too much coverage the last few months, and that’s fair, but the Rams received so much coverage because they were constantly generating news. Trading for Trent Mcduffie, adding Jaylen Watson, trying to figure out their special teams, trading for Myles Garrett, keeping the offense in tact including Matthew Stafford, and Aaron Donald’s future with the team dominated NFL talk for months leading up to the 2026 season. Then, Week 1 actually happened. The Super Bowl favorite Rams got slapped in the face by the San Francisco 49ers. The Seattle Seahawks showed they can win with a backup quarterback and can still ride their defense. The Arizona Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Chargers in a major early season upset. Now, the Rams are looking up in the NFC West, and as of one week into the season, they look a bit lost. Myles Garrett is going to IR. AD must be wondering what he is coming back to? Sean McVay needs to figure it out. It’s been an interesting Week 1 for the Rams. They have more than a few games left. We’ll see what happens. A Whole Lot Changed In One Week For The Rams (defector) “How best to react to the latest news on the Los Angeles Rams? Easy: with complete abandon and logical recklessness. That’s how the veterans do it. Said latest news: that massive offseason acquisition Myles Garrett has fouled his knee, failed to will it healthy again, and now will have surgery that will take out all of September and a chunk of October as well. Garrett was the big swing of the summer , but the fact that it was the Rams that took it is no surprise. General manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay love acquisitional bat speed more than nearly any team not named Real Madrid or Barcelona, and between Garrett and veteran ace in the hole Aaron Donald, they surely constructed the most unsettling defensive front since their own Fearsome Foursome six decades ago.“ Myles Garrett Goes On IR After Knee Surgery: What Does It Mean For Rams? (foxsports) “Star edge rusher Myles Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his knee and will be placed on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least four games, The Ringer first reported . FOX Sports NFL insider Jay Glazer later confirmed the news. “Myles Garrett didn’t do a lot of practice in this training camp,” Glazer said on “FOX NFL Kickoff.” “He had a knee injury. You saw him there the other night against [San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle] Trent Williams; he just wasn’t right. So the team decided they’re going to have him undergo arthroscopic knee surgery.” Maxx Crosby reportedly turned down Rams interest after Ravens trade collapsed (sports.yah00) “League interest remained significant. Reports indicate that multiple teams contacted the Raiders after the Ravens trade collapsed. The Philadelphia Eagles , Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers were among clubs reported to have monitored the situation. Despite that interest, no offer matched what Las Vegas believed Crosby was worth, making a second trade unlikely. With Crosby remaining off the market , the Rams eventually shifted their attention elsewhere and later completed their blockbuster acquisition of Garrett. The move helped reshape Los Angeles’ defense, but the latest report suggests the organization may have initially preferred a different path.“ 3 things Rams can learn from Giants’ win ahead of Week 2 matchup (ramswire) “With the Rams looking to avoid a 0-2 start, here are three major lessons they must learn this week after New York dazzled in head coach John Harbaugh’s debut. Isaiah Likely will be a matchup problem Giants tight end Isaiah Likely impressed during his first few seasons with the Baltimore Ravens , even proving he was more productive than incumbent starter Mark Andrews when given an extended run of play. That chance never materialized, but in his debut with New York, he was ungardable. Rams gave Aaron Donald’s contract incentives creative nicknames (sports.yahoo) “The Los Angeles Rams do things their way, and one of the most defining elements of the team’s independent ideas is how they go about their roster. Their beliefs behind roster construction are often subjected to media attention, as the franchise leverages its top draft picks for star players, using its scouting and developmental departments to fill out the roster. However, that’s not the only aspect of their construction that is unique to Los Angeles . ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams give nicknames to incentive packages in their contracts, with Aaron Donald having monikers that define his return perfectly. He has one incentive named “I’m Back” and another called “I Got 99 Problems.” Rams’ Sean McVay reveals wife’s reality check after mulling media jump following losing season in 2022 (foxnews) “The Rams were 5-12 in 2022 – one year after beating the Cincinnati Bengals to win Super Bowl LVI. He said in an interview on “60 Minutes,” which aired Sunday night, that he was in a “dark” place and had to come to grips with the fact that a few losses weren’t a reflection on himself. He said his wife, Veronika Khomyn, hit him with a reality check. “I was ready to run away from coaching and hide behind a convenient narrative of some media opportunities,” he explained. “I’ll never forget, I was explaining to my wife, Veronika, it was a daunting task ahead for the ’23 season and I remember telling her, ‘Maybe I’ll take a year off,’ and she said, ‘That never sounded like the kind of leader you wanted to be.’” Rams coach Sean McVay “tormented,” even with the team as Super Bowl favorite (cbssports) “”You’re either in a storm, you’re coming out of one or you’re getting ready to go back into it,” McVay said. “And it’s one of those three things. But how you handle that is the separator.” How McVay’s handled winning and losing McVay’s Super Bowl win came after acquiring quarterback Matthew Stafford . But the coach’s joy over the win was fleeting. “The lies I told myself were, ‘I won’t be happy until I — until we win one.’ Or, ‘I win one,'” McVay said. “It was a lot more selfish. And, you know, you’re embarrassed to kind of look back on how you got to where you did.” The Rams’ 2022 Super Bowl win was followed by a losing season. “It revealed a lot of insecurities that I had. My identity was so tied up in winning and losing games, and that was where I felt like my self-worth lied,” McVay said. “It was very revealing of how fragile I was and all the insecurities that I did have.” NFL Week 1 winners, losers: Deshaun Watson disastrous in Browns offense, Bears light up scoreboard (cbssports) “While the small sample size of one game can cloud reality, there are some cases where Week 1 tells the football world all it needs to know about a particular team or individual player. In Watson’s case, a poor season debut might be all it takes to write the book on his run as the Browns’ starting quarterback. For the Bears, a 59-point onslaught is compelling evidence that they are in for a monster year. In an 18-week season, there is still ample time to right wrongs and for strengths to devolve into weaknesses. But for now, some are off to hot starts while others could not have opened the year in a worse fashion. Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday’s Week 1 action.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 1:…

title: Rams have mixed results rebounding from Week 1 losses
summary: The Los Angeles Rams lost their season opener for the third time under Sean McVay on Thursday against the 49ers. Los Angeles has a mixed track record in the McVay era when rebounding from a Week 1 loss. Under McVay, the Rams are 7-3 in season openers since the start of the 2017 campaign. The […]
full_text: LA Rams' head coach Sean McVay speaks to the media at Marvel Stadium in Melbourne on September 10, 2026. The first-ever regular-season NFL game in Australia takes place at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026, featuring the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / - IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE - | AFP via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams lost their season opener for the third time under Sean McVay on Thursday against the 49ers. Los Angeles has a mixed track record in the McVay era when rebounding from a Week 1 loss. Under McVay, the Rams are 7-3 in season openers since the start of the 2017 campaign. The 20-point loss to San Francisco was their worst opening-game loss since the 2022 NFL season opener, when they lost by 21 points to the Bills. Overall, LA has lost back-to-back games to begin a season only once since McVay became coach. That is promising enough as the team looks past its Australian adventure to its upcoming primetime matchup against the Giants. Here is how the Rams have fared in the game after their past two season-opening losses. 2024 Week 2 – Lost 41-10 to Cardinals Week 1 Result: Lost 26-20 to Lions in overtime This one stunk to high heavens all around. The Rams came into this one with injuries at wide receiver and offensive line. Regardless, no one expected Arizona to run them out of the stadium. Yeah, the same Cardinals team that would fall apart down the stretch and miss the playoffs. The Redbirds started the game with a 21-0 lead and later 34-3 in the third quarter, so the outcome was never in doubt. They also amassed nearly 500 yards of offense to the Rams’ 245. LA truly never stood a chance. Looking back, it’s amazing the Rams eventually recovered after such a poor start to win the NFC West and nearly advance to the NFC Championship. 2022 Week 2 – Won 31-27 over Falcons Week 1 Result: Lost 31-10 to Bills Following a humbling season-opening loss to Buffalo, the defending Super Bowl champions were making quick work of the Falcons. LA jumped out to a 28-3 lead, which, against Atlanta, should’ve been the sign that the game would go haywire at some point. Still, the Rams led 31-10 early in the fourth quarter, a complete reversal from the week before. Then, things began to go south. The Falcons scored touchdowns on two straight drives, narrowing the lead to six points. They drove all the way to LA’s 24-yard line before Jalen Ramsey saved the day with a jaw-dropping interception to seal the game. JALEN RAMSEY IS HIM 😤 📺: #ATLvsLAR on FOX 📱: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/bM69Jy3G4O pic.twitter.com/gBrFyR9NUa — NFL (@NFL) September 18, 2022 Los Angeles was certainly fortunate not to fall to 0-2 after the near-collapse. A win is a win, and it was a highlight for them in a season that didn’t have many. Rams facing pressure to rebound quickly If the Rams cannot get past the Giants in Week 2, they could be in some serious trouble. The schedule gets BRUTAL after New York, so they must get things figured out quickly. After the Giants come to town, LA will have road games at the Broncos and Eagles before returning home to face the Bills. Following the Buffalo game, the Cardinals will travel to Hollywood. Coming into the season, Arizona was expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL. That could still be true, yet they kicked off the Mike LaFleur era in style with an upset win over the Chargers. It’s early, but they could be a tough out this season. Needless to say, the pressure is on for a team expected to be a Super Bowl contender. It will be tough with Myles Garrett now on IR. However, LA advanced to the NFC Championship without Garrett last season, so hope is not lost whatsoever. Several players could step up, including the returning Aaron Donald and Garrett’s backup Josaiah Stewart . They should be able to hold down the fort with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year out for a few games. The Rams have been very successful under McVay, especially within the first two weeks of the season. McVay’s track record largely speaks for itself, and his team will need every bit of it if they hope to rebound against the Giants this week.

title: Myles Garrett’s injury is a big opportunity for Josaiah Stewart
summary: The Los Angeles Rams placed star pass rusher Myles Garrett on injured reserve Sunday, ruling him out for at least the next four games. While, of course, this is mostly unfortunate news for the team, if we apply the “never waste a good crisis” logic we can find some silver linings. One of the developments […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 16: Josaiah Stewart #10 of the Los Angeles Rams stands on the field during the second half of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at SoFi Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams placed star pass rusher Myles Garrett on injured reserve Sunday , ruling him out for at least the next four games. While, of course, this is mostly unfortunate news for the team, if we apply the “never waste a good crisis” logic we can find some silver linings. One of the developments to monitor will be how second-year EDGE rusher Josaiah Stewart fares in a larger role. The Rams stand to benefit from more information on Stewart. Garrett’s co-starter, Byron Young, is in a contract year and it could be tough to retain him given the number of young players on LA’s roster looking for second deals. If Stewart earns the Rams’ confidence, it would make the decision surrounding Young more straight forward. Stewart’s newfound opportunity is much bigger than the next four games. It’s about setting himself up for a starting job in 2027 and replacing Young longer term. Get to know Josaiah Stewart I wrote the following about the 2025 third-round pick back in June: What if I told you Stewart was as effective as a pass rusher as last year’s third overall selection in Abdul Carter? They both led all rookie EDGE rushers in pass rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus (PFF), at 14.7%. This would rank around 22nd among all players at the same position with at least 318 pass rushing snaps. It makes sense that Stewart’s role would increase in 2026 despite Myles Garrett joining the team. You can never have too many quality EDGE rushers, and Stewart does bring a physical presence whereas Byron Young is a straight speedster. The Rams did not shy away from using Stewart in all facets a year ago: his run versus pass rushing snaps were evenly divided and he also dropped into coverage nearly a quarter of the time. There is no stronger endorsement of a rookie than asking him to do it all. In Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, Stewart played 28 of 64 total defensive snaps. Garrett and Young were on the field for 40 and 47, respectively. Fourth-string EDGE rusher Desjuan Johnson played 15 snaps. In a small sample size, Stewart finished with the third-highest Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade on defense at 75.9. He finished ahead of Garrett, Young, and Johnson. There is one important distinction between Stewart and Garrett: the Rams view Stewart as a true 3-4 outside linebacker and ask him to drop in coverage often. Despite Garrett significantly outsnapping Stewart against San Francisco, Garrett did not drop into coverage while Stewart did so on three plays. At the same position, only Young had more with four coverage snaps. Stewart earned a PFF coverage grade of 80.6. Stewart impressed as a rookie. He continued that momentum into the first game of 2026. Now he needs to maintain his efficiency into a larger role opposite Young while Garrett is on injured reserve. Josaiah Stewart just became a very important member of the Rams.

Malik Nabers is officially ACTIVE for SNF pic.twitter.com/Arlwm4DDQ0 — New York Giants (@Giants) September 13, 2026 Nabers, the sixth overall pick of the 2024 draft, has the potential to be one of the very best receivers and players in the NFL.
