title: Aaron Donald is no longer just a luxury for the Rams’ defense
summary: The Los Angeles Rams suddenly need Aaron Donald more than they could have imagined this offseason. It’s been a common refrain for fans around the league, pundits, analysts, that the Rams don’t even need Donald, one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, because of how good the rest of the defensive line and […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams suddenly need Aaron Donald more than they could have imagined this offseason. It’s been a common refrain for fans around the league, pundits, analysts, that the Rams don’t even need Donald, one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, because of how good the rest of the defensive line and defense as whole are. But, to have him would be a bonus and a luxury for the Super Bowl favorites. Now that Myles Garrett is headed to injured reserve , that doesn’t feel like the case anymore. Garrett is out for at least four weeks, which means the Rams will have to find a way to replace his nearly incomparable presence on the edge. He wasn’t great in the season opener, in fact he wasn’t even remotely close to good, but he admitted after the game against the San Francisco 49ers that he didn’t feel like himself and didn’t put the best version of himself on the field. There’s still talent on that Rams front, without question. Byron Young and Kobie Turner are high-quality young players, and Poona Ford is one of the best individual run stoppers in the league, but this front seven was built around No. 95 and his unique game-wrecking ability. He was going to absorb double and triple teams constantly, setting up favorable matchups for the rest of that group. Myles Garrett is now set to miss games against the Giants, Broncos, Eagles and Bills. L.A. hosts the Cardinals in Week 6. https://t.co/U5nLut5Hv3 — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 13, 2026 That sure sounds a lot like what Aaron Donald used to do. In all likelihood, Donald isn’t going to return from two years out of football and play at a first-team All-Pro level, even if interior lineman typically age fairly well . Still, this isn’t your average player, this is an inner-circle Pro Football Hall of Famer in waiting. So even if he’s not the Donald we remember from his peak, he’s going to play a crucial role for the defensive line. Alleviating stress on the rest of that group would help mitigate the loss of Garrett significantly. Can he do that? For now, it’s impossible to know. We didn’t see him take the field in Melbourne for the opener as he works his way back into game shape. And, of course, there isn’t exactly a precedent for a return like this. But uncharacteristic or not, this is a big stretch for the Rams and a big stretch for Donald. His individual legacy in untouchable, but keeping this defensive line afloat while the current best defensive player in the league is out is a major responsibility for the NFL’s biggest offseason story.

title: Myles Garrett knee injury lands Rams’ edge rusher on IR
summary: Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic surgery on the knee injury that has recently limited him, so the Los Angeles Rams plan to place their star edge rusher on injured reserve. This means that Garrett will miss at least the next four games, and the earliest he could return is October 18 against the Cardinals. Garrett […]
full_text: Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic surgery on the knee injury that has recently limited him, so the Los Angeles Rams plan to place their star edge rusher on injured reserve. This means that Garrett will miss at least the next four games, and the earliest he could return is October 18 against the Cardinals. Garrett played 40 of 65 total defensive snaps in the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers. His availability was clearly limited by the injury and his performance wasn’t up to the level expected for last year’s Defensive Player of the Year winner. The Rams have a challenging next four games ahead of them without Garrett: Week 2 vs New York Giants Week 3 at Denver Broncos Week 4 at Philadelphia Eagles Week 5 vs Buffalo Bills Fortunately for LA, they can offset the loss of Garrett by the potential return of Aaron Donald. It’s rare to have the opportunity to swap one Hall of Fame talent for another, although the Rams cannot rush Donald back into action too quickly. It may take time before Donald is able to return to the field. No Garrett also means more of second-year EDGE Josaiah Stewart, who earned the third-highest Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade on the defense in Week 1 against the 49ers behind Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake. The two biggest trades of the offseason were Myles Garrett to the Rams and AJ Brown to the Patriots. Both players have been placed on IR after just one game played. Tough starts. https://t.co/dHdzoFzIv8 — Field Yates (@FieldYates) September 13, 2026 There is one long-term silver lining that we can find in Garrett’s absence. Byron Young is in a contract year and a free agent at the conclusion of the season. The Rams may not be interested in a long-term commitment to young given his price tag and the fact they are also slated to pay Garrett. An extended look at Stewart could provide insight into how it may look with him as a full-time starter and a potential replacement option for Young. On a macro level, we know that Week 1 can bring misleading results . Some surprises from the opening week can be real, as Garrett’s injury and upcoming absence proves. The Rams are battling sky-high expectations this season. They already finished in the losing column and now must right the ship without Garrett. It is also of the upmost importance that Matthew Stafford finds a way to bounce back, as regression from the MVP may be the final straw that proves insurmountable for a turnaround. Myles Garrett’s absence isn’t only about missing the next four games. It could be symbolic of how this season flew off the rails quickly.
author: JB Scott

title: The Rams have to get more from Davante Adams
summary: Davante Adams is not the reason the Los Angeles Rams lost their season opener to the San Francisco 49ers. To boil it down to that would be insane. That being said, if the Rams want to hit their offensive peak this season, they will need more out of the former All-Pro. It’s completely fair to […]
full_text: Davante Adams is not the reason the Los Angeles Rams lost their season opener to the San Francisco 49ers. To boil it down to that would be insane. That being said, if the Rams want to hit their offensive peak this season, they will need more out of the former All-Pro. It’s completely fair to assume Adams will produce at a relatively high level again. He has a game that should age well (and already has). Barely anyone on the entire roster played well at The MCG this week, so it’s not like he stuck out for his lackluster performance. And, as Kyle Brandt of Good Morning Football says, Week 1 is a liar . We get bizarre results and head-turning performances, for both good and bad reasons, every year during Week 1. Given the unique circumstances of this particular game, it’s understandable if you want to flush it, chalk it up to a weird situation and move on. But, speaking in generalities, the version of Adams we saw on Thursday isn’t conducive to the Rams’ offense being the best version of itself. Counting stats and advanced metrics alike will tell you how disappointing his season opener was. Three catches, 26 yards, no touchdowns, -1.7 total EPA generated (per RBSDM), -9.9% catch rate over expected (per NFL Pro). Simply put, that’s brutal. people are concerned about Davante Adams (me, im concerned). last night the Rams ran 9 plays in the Red Zone: 7 run plays only 2 pass plays (Adams played 1/2) of those 9 plays, 6 were in 13 personnel: 5 run plays only 1 pass play Davante Adams 2025 13 personnel usage on pass… — Domain Fantasy Football (@domainfantasy) September 11, 2026 This isn’t intended to be some kind of hit piece on Adams. This is coming from the same blogger who advocated for his Hall of Fame credentials this offseason. And there are at least some surface-level reasons to be concerned about what he can produce in 2026 , given his age, an increase in injuries in recent seasons, etc. It’s a combination of factors that make this scenario a bit hairy for the Rams. If Adams declines year over year at a steeper rate than most people expected, is there enough talent among the other pass catchers to overcome his drop in production? Are you at all concerned about Matthew Stafford? If you are, it probably won’t assuage your feelings if his No. 2 target isn’t just as dangerous as he was in his first year with the club. If Adams drops off and Stafford is a bigger question mark, suddenly the Los Angeles offense is stuck in a far more tenuous position than the NFL world could have imagined. Hence, the overall point. You don’t have to believe the Week 1, 2026 version of Davante Adams is the one the Rams will have to work with all season. The odds of that being the case are still quite low. But that performance does shine a blindingly bright spotlight on how important it is for him to play at a higher level as this season continues. As has been discussed ad nauseum all summer, the Rams have built a receiver corps around Puka Nacua, Adams and a slew of role players, if that. That room’s success hinges, largely, on what No. 17 can do this year. If that mirrors what he did in Week 1, there’s reason to be concerned about this passing attack.

That sets up a big Week 2 matchup between the Raiders and Chargers, as the Silver and Black can really push one of their rivals down the division standings with a win. title: Las Vegas Raiders’ offensive line dominates in Week 1 win over Miami Dolphins
summary: One of the Las Vegas Raiders’ biggest questions heading into the 2026 season was how much the offensive line could improve after being the worst unit in the NFL a year ago. If the Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins is any indication, the Raiders will be a night-and-day difference in the trenches compared […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the Las Vegas Raiders’ biggest questions heading into the 2026 season was how much the offensive line could improve after being the worst unit in the NFL a year ago. If the Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins is any indication, the Raiders will be a night-and-day difference in the trenches compared to last season. A dominant win is typically paired with a dominant performance from the offensive line, and Las Vegas’ 27-13 victory was no different. Quarterback Kirk Cousins wasn’t sacked and was only hit twice on his 30 pass attempts. Gameballs are in order for new o-line coach Rick Dennison, Kolton Miller, Spencer Burford, Tyler Linderbaum , Jackson Powers-Johnson and DJ Glaze, as they played a big part in giving Raider Nation something to cheer about in the season opener. title: Raiders start Klint Kubiak era with complete team victory
summary: Like last year, the Las Vegas Raiders began the season with a victory. But this seems different. This doesn’t seem flukey. Yes, the Miami Dolphins aren’t good and yes, Week 1 can be a misnomer and perhaps the Raiders won’t be true contenders this season But they certainly look like an improved roster and have […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Like last year, the Las Vegas Raiders began the season with a victory. But this seems different. This doesn’t seem flukey. Yes, the Miami Dolphins aren’t good and yes, Week 1 can be a misnomer and perhaps the Raiders won’t be true contenders this season But they certainly look like an improved roster and have better coaching as the began the Klint Kubiak era with a complete team victory over the Dolphins in a 27-13 home win. The Raiders dominated in all three phases. The offense, under the guidance of veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins, was efficient, the offensive line was strong, the running attack was led by Ashton Jeanty and helped rookie Mike Washington and the defense looked fast as it had five sacks, an interception and a forced fumble. And the Raiders didn’t even punt until the fourth quarter. The 2025 Raiders never dominated. This version did in Week 1. Will it last? Time will tell, but it was a hell of a start. Oh, and with the Chargers being stunned at home by Arizona and the Broncos and Chiefs playing Monday night, the Raiders are alone in first place in the AFC West West. Here are some key aspects about the game: Cousins has his moments: In his first game with the Raiders, Cousins, 38, connected on his first nine passes. He was mostly hitting short passes and didn’t throw down field much. When he didn’t, it was always pretty. Cousins threw two interceptions. So, if the Raiders are forced from their game plan, it could be trouble with Cousins. Jeanty has a day: Three weeks ago Sunday, there was concern that Jeanty suffered a major injury. Sunday, coming off an ankle injury, Jeanty had a huge game. He had 102 yards rushing on 23 carries and had 45 yards and two touchdowns on six catches out of the backfield. He looks primed for a big season. Washington added 41 yards on seven carries, including an 18-yard run. This will be a fun 1-2 punch. Crosby pitch count There were some plays, including six straight, where star defensive end Maxx Crosby wasn’t on the field. Crosby is famous for playing 100 percent of the snaps. But this was his first game since last December as he recovered from a knee surgery. Kubiak said that was his call. The coaching staff is being smart with him to start a long season. He finished with two tackles and a sack and a half and seven pressures. Yes, he’s back. Need more from receivers: Las Vegas receivers Jalen Nailor, Tre Tucker, Jack Bech and Malik Benson combined for nine catches for 83 yards and a touchdown. That production must improve. Mayer doesn’t make huge impact: Fresh off of a three-year, $45 million contract extension, tight end Michael Mayer had six catches for 32 yards. It was a solid, but not great day for Mayer as he started for the injured Brock Bowers, who might be out another week or so with a knee injury. Paye delivers: Free-agent addition, pass-rusher Kwity Paye made his presence felt. He had six tackles, two sacks and four quarterback hits. If he can keep that up, he and Crosby will be a nasty pass-rush tandem. Offensive line much improved: The poster children for the Raiders’ 2025 woes was an awful offensive line. Led by the addiition of free-agent center Tyler Linderbaum, that unit looks much improved. The group opened big holes for the running backs and Cousins wasn’t sack. That’s a big step forward and will keep this offense competitive if they can keep it up. Fatukasi shows up: Defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi was signed during training camp to help a weak group there. The veteran instantly made his presence felt. He had four tackles and a half sack and was excellent in the ground game. He can be an impact player. Cole makes impact: Raiders’ standout punter A.J. Cole didn’t punt until the fourth quarter, but, man, did he have an impact. He averaged 62.7 yards a punt with a long of 72 yards. He’s silly good. Nice trend continued: The Raiders forced an NFL high 11 punts on their opponent’s first drive of the game last season. They started this season the same way. Rookie responds: Starting cornerback Darien Porter limped off the field late in the game. Fifth-round pick, Zeke Masses, took over and the Dolphins went after him on the first play. The Cal product responded by breaking up a pass. Nice start, kid. Perhaps we will see more of him next week against the Chargers. Getting tricky: On fourth and short, Kubiak had fullback Connor Hayward play quarterback and take a tush-push play with Cousins at halfback. After a review, the first down was converted. Kubiak has a bag full of plays. Nice return game: The Raiders’ special teams was dreadful last season, but the return game was on point Sunday. Dylan Laube had kick returns of 45 and 50 yards and Benson had a 23-yard punt return he almost broke for a touchdown. What a refreshing change. Big home crowd: We all know Allegiant Stadium, now in its sixth season to with fans in attendance, has been a haven for visiting teams. That wasn’t the case to open this season. The Dolphins are bad and don’t travel well. This was a very loud, pro Raiders’ crowd. That’s the way it should be. Of course, there will be future visitor takrovers this season, but the season started the right way. Got the breaks: The Raiders outplayed the woeful Dolphins all game and deserved the win. But Las Vegas did get some breaks. They had a fourth-down stop and a fumble reversed on review and received a questionable taunting penalty in their favor to extend an eventual scoring drive. It was a good day. Backup offensiveline tinkering: The Raiders offensive line seems very versatile and there are some interchangeable parts, which can help if injuries occur. Case in point was the pre-game warmup alignment with backup quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Rookie Trey Zuhn was at left tackle, Caleb Rogers was at left guard and Charles Grant wat right tackle. None of these players worked at those positions in training camp. Again, versatility is a good thing. Lindenberg inactive: The only mild surprise of the Raiders’ game day inactives was that second-year linebacker Cody Lindenberg was inactive as a healthy scratch he was a core special teamer last season and the Raiders’ don’t have much depth at linebacker. We’ll see if this becomes a trend.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders
summary: Well, folks… get ready for a long season of Miami Dolphins football. With a 27-13 defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Raiders in Week One, the Jeff Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan era in Miami got off to a rocky start. While fans of the team expected some growing pains, a win against the […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the Las Vegas Raiders in the fourth quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, folks… get ready for a long season of Miami Dolphins football. With a 27-13 defeat at the hands of the Las Vegas Raiders in Week One, the Jeff Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan era in Miami got off to a rocky start. While fans of the team expected some growing pains, a win against the team that earned the number one overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft didn’t seem to be an outlandish ask. Whoops! Before anyone panics, just remember that the Dolphins aren’t playing with a full deck right now. With a record-setting amount of dead cap holding this roster back, the team is beginning their latest rebuild with one hand tied behind their backs. It’s going to look ugly at times this season, but hey, we’re Dolphins fans. We’re used to this. GOOD Caleb Douglas has record setting performance for rookie receiver in Miami While it wasn’t a good day for the Miami Dolphins’ offense as a whole, rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas had himself an historic day. In fact, Douglas’ performance was a record setting one. His 94 receiving yards were the most for a Dolphins rookie in his first game as a professional in team history. Caleb Douglas has the most receiving yards (94 and counting) by a Dolphins player in their NFL debut. — NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) September 13, 2026 When Douglas was selected in the third-round of the 2026 NFL Draft, plenty of people scoffed at the pick. The Texas Tech product was overdrafted according to many national pundits. Well, it doesn’t matter where you’re selected once you hit the field on Sundays — and on this Sunday, Douglas proved that he belongs in the National Football League by nabbing five passes. Here’s hoping he continues to stack good games en route to a successful rookie season. BAD Dolphins offensive line gives up 5 sacks in loss With his first pick as Miami’s general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan invested in the team’s offensive line, taking Kadyn Proctor out of Alabama to start at left guard. His message was clear — the team needed to be better up front if they wanted to find success on offense. Unfortunately, on Sunday against the Raiders, despite the mobility of quarterback Malik Willis, the Dolphins still gave up five sacks. It’s early, and there will be plenty of time to work on things from a pass protection standpoint, but if offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik wants to push the ball downfield — which seemed to be the second-half gameplan — Miami’s offensive line will need to be better moving forward. Or maybe Slowik needs to adjust his plan of attack… UGLY Dolphins defense couldn’t stop the run If you take old man Kirk Cousins’ five carries out of the equation, the Dolphins defense gave up 136 yards rushing on 32 attempts — 4.25 yards per carry — to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Second-year running back Ashton Jeanty had 102 yards rushing on 23 carries himself. Time and time again, the Raiders found themselves in short yardage situations on second and third downs because Miami’s defensive line couldn’t handle the Las Vegas rushing attack. That is not a recipe for success for a defense that is filled with young, unproven talent across the board. It won’t get any easier for the Dolphins next weekend. They’ll travel to San Francisco to face Christian McCaffrey and the 49ers — a team that just ran for 174 yards on 30 carries against the Los Angeles Rams in Week One. ___ The Dolphins came out swinging against the Raiders, unfortunately they didn’t seem to land any blows. The team starts off the Jeff Hafley era with an 0-1 record and the schedule only gets harder from here. Do you think Miami will improve in Week Two against the 49ers or are we in for more of the same — if not worse — against San Francisco? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

title: Dolphins vs. Raiders final score, immediate reactions in Week 1
summary: The Miami Dolphins started their 2026 season with a visit to the Las Vegas Raiders. The good thing for traveling fans was the trip to Las Vegas. The bad thing was the show the Dolphins put on in the game. This is a rebuilding year for the Dolphins, and the expectations are about as low […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Nailor #9 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs after a catch against Chris Johnson #3 of the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins started their 2026 season with a visit to the Las Vegas Raiders. The good thing for traveling fans was the trip to Las Vegas. The bad thing was the show the Dolphins put on in the game. This is a rebuilding year for the Dolphins, and the expectations are about as low as they can be, but seeing a competitive performance on the field is still desirable. Miami had moments when they started to put things together, but it was not enough and important aspects never showed up. Here are some immediate reactions as Miami got trounced by Las Vegas. Final score Dolphins 13 – 27 Raiders Recap and immediate reactions The first half was all Raiders. Miami’s defense had no answers to the two-pronged attack of quarterback Kirk Cousins and running back Ashton Jeanty. Even when the Dolphins were in position to make a stop, the Raiders would find a way to escape and turn a loss into a big gain. According to the first yard net yardage, the game should have been close at the break. Miami gained 151 yards on 25 plays for an average of 6.0 yards per play. The Raiders had 170 yards on 31 plays, for a 5.5 yard average. The score at halftime was 17-6 and it felt like Miami was no where to be found in the game. I need that ball. Get me that ball! Taaffe with his first career pick! pic.twitter.com/B6C1Ignwb8 — The Phinsider (@thephinsider) September 13, 2026 The second half started with a bang for Miami. Rookie safety Michael Taaffe picked off Cousins on the opening drive of the half and gave Miami great field position. Four plays later, quarterback Malik Willis turned a scramble into a 14-yard touchdown run to cap a 52-yard drive. Suddenly, Miami was back in the game. On the ensuing kickoff, the Dolphins allowed a 50-yard return and, five plays later, the Raiders scored a touchdown. Two plays into Miami’s next drive, the Raiders picked off a Willis pass and, largely behind running back Ashton Jeanty’s ground attack, Pass rush no show The Raiders’ offensive line last year was ugly. In the first week of the 2026 season, you would think they had the top line in the league. Miami’s pass rush simply did not show up. Chop Robinson was a non-factor, something that cannot happen this year. The edge rushers never got close to quarterback Kirk Cousins, and the veteran was able to carve apart Miami’s young secondary – particularly targeting rookie cornerback Chris Johnson. Miami needs their pass rush to take over games so they can take some of the pressure off the secondary. On Sunday, the pass rush may not have gotten on the plane. Special teams anything but special Miami gave up a 23-yard return on a punt to start the second quarter, then allowed a 45-yard return on a kickoff late in the quarter. After Miami scored their first touchdown in the third quarter, a 50-yard kick return set the Raiders up at midfield. Special teams coverage was anything by special in the game. Mark Schlereth on the broadcast explained that you cannot experience special teams work at full speed in training camp or practice, but the Dolphins have to figure something out because giving up huge chunks of yards on returns is not going to cut it. The 23-yard punt return turned a 59-yard punt into a 36-yard net kick – these are free yards Miami cannot afford to be giving to opposing teams. When your kicker has two special teams tackles, it is a bad special teams day. Physical Dolphins still need to tackle The Dolphins focused on becoming more physical this year, moving on from a finesse team built around speed and misdirection to become a team not afraid of contact. Miami was supposed to be physical, they were supposed to like being physical, and they were supposed to make their opponents feel them. On Sunday, the Dolphins showed some of that physicality, but not nearly enough. And not in their tackling. The Dolphins’ defense had way too many missed tackles. The Raiders could just swipe Miami’s arms away from them and continue upfield. Tackling was an issue throughout the game, and for a team that talked about being physical, missinga basic aspect of the game is worrisome. A running team that cannot run Malik Willis’ first Dolphins touchdown comes on a 14 yard scramble. Finishes with his shoulder for the score! pic.twitter.com/AHCFYRAj04 — The Phinsider (@thephinsider) September 13, 2026 This ties into the physicality discussion above, but Miami struggled to run the ball, which is supposed to be the strength of their offense. Counting Willis’s scrambles, Miami ran the ball 17 times for just 65 yards. That is a 3.8 yards per attempt. De’Von Achane picked up 36 yards on 11 carries. That is just a 3.3 yards-per-rush average – not good enough for a Pro Bowl running back. Add in four receptions, and the Dolphins’ top offensive weapon was relegated to an afterthought for much of the game. So much for Hafley’s idea of getting Achane 40 touches a game. Yes, the Raiders stacked the box and dared Willis to beat them. It was the right defensive gameplan against Miami, but the Dolphins had to know that was coming, and they have to have a way to beat it. The offensive line has to open up holes better. The play calling needs to scheme ways to keep defenses from focusing only on Achane. Willis needs to do a better job of reading the defense on run-options and getting Achane into favorable runs. This is not all on Achane, but he has to be better. Safeties hightlight the day The biggest concern on the Dolphins roster coming into the game was the defensive secondary. Miami is relying on young, unproven players in the secondary, especially at cornerback. Cousins attacked them, especially rookie Chris Johnson. He did not have a huge day – throwing for just 160 yards on 21-for-30 passing, but he did rack up three touchdown passes and do everything that was needed to put this game away. The safeties, though, came away with perhaps the two highlight plays of the game for Miami. Taaffe started the second half with an interception, and Dante Trader, Jr., picked off a second pass to try to spark a Dolphins comeback. It was not to be, but it cannot be because of the safeties.

(Photo by Reginald Mathalone/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins released their inactive players list for their Week 1 game against the Las Vegas Raiders and a veteran name headlined the group. Wide receiver Jalen Tolbert will not play in Sunday’s game. The team’s rookie wide receivers, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, Jr., along with veteran Malik Washington, will carry the position group. The Dolphins are a young team this year and, along with the three rookie wide receivers, eight other rookies are active for the game. Starting left guard Kadyn Proctor, starting middle linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, starting cornerback Chris Johnson, starting safety Michael Taaffe, tight end Will Kacmarek, fullback DJ Herman, safety/linebacker Kyle Louis, and tight end Seydou Traore are all active. Quarterback Brady Cook rounds out Miami’s inactive players list. title: Dolphins vs. Raiders preview: What to watch for Miami in Week 1
summary: The Miami Dolphins open their 2026 NFL schedule with a Week 1 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders. The game features two teams with new head coaches hoping to spark a quick rebuild and head toward being competitive this year, even with predictions of a less-than-ideal season. Can Miami surprise the NFL this year, putting […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - DECEMBER 07: Chop Robinson #44 of the Miami Dolphins during the game against the New York Jets on December 7, 2025 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins open their 2026 NFL schedule with a Week 1 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders. The game features two teams with new head coaches hoping to spark a quick rebuild and head toward being competitive this year, even with predictions of a less-than-ideal season. Can Miami surprise the NFL this year, putting together more wins than anyone expects? To do that, they likely need to start off with a strong performance this afternoon against the Raiders. For the Dolphins, we take a look at five things to watch for today’s game. Jeff Hafley game management The first game for a brand-new head coach is always a stressful one. Hafley has head-coaching experience at Boston College, but he has never held this role at the NFL level. He will want to make sure his vision for the Dolphins is evident, but he will have to remember this is an 18-week marathon, not a one-game sprint. How does he manage the game? Timeouts. Challenges. Play calling. Offensive adjustments when calling plays for the defense. What is Hafley’s style when the games matter? He will face his first challenge today, and he will set the tone for the rest of the season. Rookie wide receivers Miami heads into the season with two third-round picks, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell, and a fifth-round selection, Kevin Coleman, Jr., set to have major playing time at wide receiver. The speed of the game is about to crank up; how will the receivers respond? The learning curve is steep, and there will be rookie mistakes. Can the Dolphins limit those mistakes and learn from them immediately? With three rookies, they also have to learn from each other – one makes the mistake, all three immediately make a change to their game. It is a lot to ask of young players, but the receivers cannot make excuses. Against the Raiders, they need to step up and make their presence felt. Douglas should be the primary option of the three, at least until Bell is up to full speed in his recovery from an ACL tear last year. Coleman will factor into the rotation and could be a day-three steal for Miami. Will we notice them today, and, more importantly, will we notice them for good reasons? Make sure you check out the new SB Nation app – it works so well, especially for the game chats. If you have not downloaded it yet, you can check it out here: Apple store Android store You will just log in to the app with the same account you use on the full version of the site. Chop Robinson bouncing back The Dolphins’ pass rush is headlined by Robinson, but he has not had massive success during his first two years in the league. He has 10 total sacks in his first two years, a number Robinson should have as a goal for this year. The third year is usually a breakout season if a player is going to become a force in the NFL, and this is the year for Robinson to step up. But it is not just pass rush that Robinson needs to show this year. He also has to prove he can be an every-down player, setting the edge against the run just as much as he gets after opposing quarterbacks. The Raiders should attack the Dolphins on the ground, making Miami prove they can stop running back Ashton Jeanty. Robinson will have a major part the Dolphins’ response. Against the Raiders, Robinson is going to have his opportunities, especially when matched up against Las Vegas right tackle DJ Glaze. Glaze allowed 10 sacks last season and is a big question mark heading into this season. The Raiders not starting first-overall pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza, instead turning to veteran Kirk Cousins, is in part because of their offensive line struggles and not wanting to subject the rookie to constant pressure while learning the speed of the game. Robinson could jumps start a big year with a huge day on Sunday. Offensive line establishing itself The Dolphins’ starting offensive line looks like a good unit on paper. Left tackle Patrick Paul is entering his prime; first-round pick Kadyn Proctor is next to him at left guard; and center Aaron Brewer is coming off an All-Pro season and looking to get even better. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea has a season to forget last year at left guard, but should improve because of that experience and by moving back to his natural position on the right side. Right tackle Austin Jackson has the potential to be a great lineman, but his career so far has been defined by injuries; if he stays healthy, Miami shouldn’t have to worry about either tackle position. The offensive line has questions to answer, but it should be better. Sunday will tell us whether that is a fair assumption. Can they protect quarterback Malik Willis? Will they be able to open lanes for running back De’Von Achane? Any success Miami’s offense will have this year will start with the offensive line. They have to step up early, and a test against the Raiders’ edge rusher Maxx Crosby will give us a good idea of who the line might be this season. Secondary needs to step up The biggest area of concern for the Dolphins’ defense is the secondary. Miami is relying on young, unproven players for much of their cornerbacks and safety group. Even the veterans, for the most part, are journeymen who need to prove themselves. They will get their first test against a veteran quarterback who knows how to make them pay. The good news is, the Raiders do not have a great set of receivers. This could ease Miami’s secondary into the season, giving them the experience they desperately need. Robinson and the pass rush should help out, but the secondary has to step up today and instill some confidence in the group.

title: Dolphins 2026 Week 1 mailbag: Defensive identity, offensive aggression, and running back depth
summary: The Miami Dolphins host the Las Vegas Raiders later today, kicking off the 2026 season for both teams. This season marks a massive change for the Dolphins, who have completely reshaped the team from the president down to the roster. They have taken a massive hit against their salary cap to shed ballooned contracts in […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: De'Von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins looks on after the NFL 2025 game against the New York Jetsat MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey."" (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins host the Las Vegas Raiders later today, kicking off the 2026 season for both teams. This season marks a massive change for the Dolphins, who have completely reshaped the team from the president down to the roster. They have taken a massive hit against their salary cap to shed ballooned contracts in an effort to become fiscally responsible again and build a team that will be able to consistently compete in the postseason. This morning, we open The Phinsider Mailbag and answer your questions about the Dolphins. You primarily wanted to look at the team as a whole, rather than specifically focus on this week’s game against the Raiders. Unfortunately, we could not get the roundtable-style discussion scheduled for this week, so you will have to settle for my answers to your questions. Defense, roster changes, and 2026 expectations Phoenix sliding three questions into one. Given my five questions with Silver and Black Pride this week included 11 questions, I like it. I can answer the first question pretty succinctly – if Hafley cannot establish a defensive identity, he should not be a head coach. Other than his four years as the head coach at Boston College, Hafley has been coaching on the defensive side of the ball for almost 25 years. The defense is what he knows and it is what we should see become the strength of the team. That said, I do not know that it shows itself immediately. The secondary is the team’s biggest concern heading into the season because they are relying on younger or unproven players to man the group. Maybe they step up and magic happens. Maybe they struggle as they get used to the new coach and scheme. I think the defense eventually steps up, but it might take some time to grow into its potential. I do think we will see a big change immediately. The Dolphins have transitioned to a 4-3 base defense, with four defensive linemen and three linebackers, rather than the 3-4 system they used under the last couple of coaching staffs. That is not even the extent of the change, though. I think the Dolphins will actually use a 4-2-5 look more often than not, taking out a linebacker and adding a third safety to give them flexibility in what they do – using a safety in coverage or in run support without having to make defensive substitutions. The “big nickel” look may become Miami’s base defensive system. As for moving on from players like quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and wide receivers Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, yes, it was the right decision. The Dolphins have finally decided it is time to stop putting band aids on the team and hoping to win. They will probably suffer through a year of growth, but the other option was to keep trying the same thing and hoping for a different result. As much as I am not looking forward to yet another rebuild, it had to happen. Owner Stephen Ross finally decided to do a complete rebuild, changing everything about the franchise, because the changing of pieces over the past several years had failed. Yes, it means the Dolphins have to rely on younger players this year, but were they going anywhere different this year with Tagovailoa, Hill, and Waddle than they did last year with Tagovailoa, Hill, and Waddle? Or the year before that? Finally, I think the idea of not judging this year on wins and losses is an appropriate one. I am hopeful that they can pull off some wins and surprise some people, but realistically, if this team lands the first overall pick and are the worst team in the league or if they pull off several wins and are in the middle of the pack, it does not matter. What matters is that the team is improving and looks better and more competitive late in the season than it did early this year. Another multiple question question. I like it. I assume by conservative, you mean that the team will rely on the run and short passing to get the ball out of quarterback Malik Willis’ hands quickly. Wow, that sounds like a Tagovailoa-based offense. I do not think that will be the case, but I do think they will use the running game a lot. Willis can push the ball downfield, and he is mobile, so I expect him to look deep and then use his legs if it is not there. But this offense is not going to be built around Willis’ arm, but rather around running back De’Von Achane’s legs. Achane is the best player on the Dolphins’ offense and getting him the ball early, often, and repeatedly will be what makes Miami’s offense work in 2026. That can include using him as a receiving threat. Whatever the case, expect Achane to get the ball much more than anyone else. Again, I do not think that is being conservative rather than attacking with your best weapon. There will be deeper throws, especially as the season goes along and Miami’s rookie receivers, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, Jr., become more comfortable with the speed of the NFL. But, this will be a run-first team that then looks to use play-action to create space in the passing game. As for tackle Patrick Paul and Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby, what I like the most bout that is Paul feeling comfortable enough in himself and his game to start talking. He is growing into the left tackle role, including being named a captain of the team this season, and if he starts to have a little swagger about his game, that is a good thing. Paul said of facing Crosby, “I think with him, he’s a dynamic player. So with him, just beating him to a spot, getting your hands on him, getting him off his game. He likes to play with a lot of swagger. So just getting him displaced off his game, getting him off his spots, putting your hands on him, being aggressive and just getting him out of his game.” He then added when added if trash talk falls into getting Crosby off his game, “I feel like he’s a hothead, so a lot of those things you could get into his game with that but he’s a great player. You just got to stay on it all four quarters really with him.” Do I think that means getting Crosby to do something that leads to a penalty? Not necessarily. I think Paul is trying to frustrate Crosby, making him press and take chances that open things up for Miami’s defense. Crosby just does not have a history of getting penalized or taking cheap shots. I do not see that changing today. Make sure you check out the new SB Nation app – it works so well, especially for the game chats. If you have not downloaded it yet, you can check it out here: Apple store Android store You will just log in to the app with the same account you use on the full version of the site. I think you will see plenty of running backs Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon II this week and during the year. Achane will still be the dominant back, but I think the coaching staff knows they have to keep him fresh all season. If, like I said earlier, the goal is to be better at the end of the season than at the start of the year, you need to have your best players still available late in the season. Achane has to still be effective in Week 18 and the only way to do that is to let Wright and Gordon take some of the snaps and touches. Wright is closer to a true replacement for Achane, while Gordon is the power back who can create a different challenge for defenses. I do not think there are major concerns about either – they just are not Achane, and expecting them to come in and have the same success as Achane is probably unfair to them. I do think we will see times where Gordon or Wright are in the backfield, and Achane is out wide as a receiver. That gives defenses different looks and complexities to consider. You have a talent who can do multiple things, so let him do those things. Finally, I do not think a “tank” season will ever be on the table for…

title: 2026 NFL Week 2: Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears
summary: The Minnesota Vikings will continue their tour of the NFC North, taking to the road for the first time in 2026 to face their rivals from the Windy City, the Chicago Bears. Both of these teams took home victories in Week 1. The Vikings, despite losing Kyler Murray early in the contest, rallied from twelve […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings will continue their tour of the NFC North, taking to the road for the first time in 2026 to face their rivals from the Windy City, the Chicago Bears. Both of these teams took home victories in Week 1. The Vikings, despite losing Kyler Murray early in the contest, rallied from twelve points down late in the third quarter to take home a 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium. Meanwhile, the Bears had an offensive explosion against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte, as they ran for nearly 300 yards and had six rushing touchdowns in a 59-37 win. These two teams split their two matchups in 2025. The Vikings opened last season at Soldier Field on Monday Night Football, and got a dramatic come-from-behind victory, as J.J. McCarthy rallied the team from a fourth-quarter deficit to defeating the Bears, 27-24. It looked like the Vikings might get a second dramatic win over the Bears, but Chicago won with some dramatics of their own. A big kick return by the Bears after the Vikings scored the go-ahead touchdown put Cairo Santos in position for a game-winning 48-yard field goal as time expired to give the Bears a 19-17 win and a split of the season series. The Vikings already have questions at quarterback, as Murray’s status in the concussion protocol will be something to monitor throughout the course of the week. If he is unable to go, Carson Wentz will step in as the starter again with McCarthy backing him up. Kickoff for this one is slated for noon Central Time, with coverage being provided by the FOX family of networks. We’ll be putting all of our stories for this week’s game in this stream so you can easily find them. title: Vikes Views: Sunday King – Packers at Vikings
summary: Man I love when they beat the Packers. The Minnesota Vikings gave us a scare with the slow start to the game. That sinking feeling was helped along with the nasty hit that knocked out Kyler Murray for the game, and likely the next one. However, the team showed resilience and climbed back into the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after scoring a two point conversion during the fourth quarter the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Man I love when they beat the Packers. The Minnesota Vikings gave us a scare with the slow start to the game. That sinking feeling was helped along with the nasty hit that knocked out Kyler Murray for the game, and likely the next one. However, the team showed resilience and climbed back into the game. The closing quarter was a defensive masterpiece from Brian Flores. This team has some gumption. Kevin O’Connell This team could’ve easily fallen apart to boos at home. KOC has shown his system can work with just about anyone at QB. He once again maintained his composure after losing his starting QB. The offense ended the game with four straight touchdowns, granted only one drive was more than 30 yards. Finishing in the Red Zone and winning the turnover battle decided the game. KOC’s offense was efficient when opportunities presented themselves. The Vikings consistently finished drives with touchdowns instead of settling for field goals. Brian Flores You can’t mention the coaching staff without talking about Brian Flores. It was a rough start with the Packers starting the game with three straight scoring drives and a touchdown to end the first half. The Vikings defense settled down and only allowed three points in the 2 nd half. The 4 th quarter drive list for the Packers was Turnover on Downs, Fumble, Interception, Turnover on Downs. The defense handed the offense possessions at the Packers’ 1-yard line and 14-yard line. The inventive pressures were too much for the Packers’ OL and Jordan Love. It was as dominant as you’ll ever see a defense play a quarter. Carson Wentz It’s not easy to maintain focus around the constant attention JJ McCarthy and Kyler Murray received this offseason. Wentz put in the work and got ready to play, despite the distractions. He didn’t put up a ton of yards, mainly because he didn’t have to. Wentz wisely leaned on veterans Justin Jefferson and TJ Hockenson. Quick, efficient and professional game from Carson Wentz. Justin Jefferson It’s painfully obvious Jefferson was the only real weapon the Vikings had on Sunday. He caught just about everything that was thrown his way. Jefferson comes to play every Sunday and doesn’t complain about the constant QB carousel. He’s on this list almost every week and it’d be hard to justify leaving him off this week. Myles Price Price looked dangerous every time he returned a kick. There were a couple of shoe-string tackles that saved the Packers earlier in the game. His 61-yard return in the 3 rd quarter started the comeback. It was a huge momentum swing, and the offense was able to take advantage. You never know where the spark might come from, and price took advantage of the little bit of opportunity he was given. Honorable Mentions: Will Reichard – perfect as usual, is he already the GOAT Vikings kicker? Andrew Van Ginkel – a lot of the defensive guys could be listed, but he had the fumble recovery on Love in the 4 th quarter. Harrison Smith – just glad he’s playing again.

title: Vikings Week 1 Stock Market Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings produced a dramatic 39-22 comeback victory over the Green Bay Packers that included one of the more memorable late game meltdowns by a Vikings opponent in franchise history. It was a roller coaster ride from beginning to end. Apparently it was the first time a team was down 12+ points with 20 […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings produced a dramatic 39-22 comeback victory over the Green Bay Packers that included one of the more memorable late game meltdowns by a Vikings opponent in franchise history. It was a roller coaster ride from beginning to end. Apparently it was the first time a team was down 12+ points with 20 minutes remaining and ended up winning by 17+ points in NFL history. Let’s break down the stock market report. Stock Down and Up The Vikings Coaching Staff . One thing that makes early season games more unpredictable is that teams have not shown the new wrinkles to their scheme and don’t have much beyond preseason and whatever videos of practice were leaked on tape for opponents to dissect. The Packers game plan in that respect was better than the Vikings game plan initially because the Vikings had to deal with more surprises, particularly from the Packers defense which is under a new coordinator in Jonathan Gannon. Gannon was able to bring more pressures than he has been known for in the past that made it difficult for the Vikings offense to function well. They also had a pretty good idea about what the Vikings’ offensive game plan included. The Packers also seemed to have a pretty good read on what the Vikings were doing defensively as well and had a plan for how to attack it. All that, and poor execution by the Vikings, led to a poor start to the game in all three phases. And in the midst of all that, Kyler Murray went down with a concussion on a slide that was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the Packers for hitting Murray in the head on the slide- knocking him out of the game after only a handful of plays. The Vikings clearly didn’t have as good a game plan as the Packers, nor did they execute well what they did have. That is a failure of the Vikings coaching staff to a large degree. The Packers were likely helped by signing former Vikings safety Kahlef Hailessie to their practice squad a week ago, which likely informed their game plan. But they were able to mitigate the poor start and disadvantages in game plan, keeping the game within two scores while they adapted. And after halftime things slowly began to improve for the Vikings, and go south for the Packers, as the Vikings made adjustments and the Packers didn’t as much, which had a snowballing effect as the game wore on into the fourth quarter. The Vikings began to execute better while the Packers melted down in dramatic fashion. Clearly the Vikings were aided by penalties called on the Packers, but with maybe the exception of the roughing the passer call, the calls were correct. And they also missed a couple facemask penalties on the Packers against Wentz and Justin Jefferson. The point here is not only were the Vikings’ coaching staff able to make adjustments, they also created a culture where players believe they can overcome adversity and have often done so- including this game which started about as bad as it can get. Kevin O’Connell is often judged on his ability as the offensive coordinator and play caller, but he should also be judged on the head coach’s job of creating a positive culture which he has been at the center in creating and maintaining since he arrived in Minnesota. The Vikings have won six games in a row going back to last season, at a time when they were 4-8 and effectively out of the playoffs and suffering from basically the worst quarterbacking in the league and multiple quarterback injuries. At the same time, the Packers have lost every game since their star defensive player- Micah Parsons- went down with an injured knee last season. The focus of the Packers offseason was on ‘finishing’ as they had lost both games to the Bears last season, including their playoff game, after having a double digit lead in the fourth quarter. So also credit the Vikings coaching staff with having the ability to make adjustments and maintain a belief and focus on doing what is necessary to win the game despite adversity. Stock Up Myles Price. Price had a couple good returns but his 69-yard return in the second half was just what the doctor ordered to help a struggling offense score points. Deejay Dallas . Most fans may not know Dallas is on the team as he was a recent practice squad addition who was called up for week one. He had the key block on Price’s big kickoff return. Dallas Turner. The hype about Turner’s improvement this offseason was real as Turner was credited with nine total QB pressures according to preliminary PFF charting including a sack and a forced fumble. He looked the part of a top edge rusher despite having just one sack against Jordan Love, who is among the best in sack avoidance. Blake Cashman. It didn’t come until the second half for the most part, but Cashman was credited with five pressures on 18 pass rush attempts and was in Jordan Love’s face frequently in the fourth quarter, blasting through the center and creating quick pressure. He also had a tipped pass that led to James Pierre’s interception. Carson Wentz. Wentz showed his limitations, and as he said after the game it’s better to be lucky than good when it came to penalties erasing a redzone interception, but he also showed he could move the offense under difficult circumstances with few reps in practice. He finished 12/19 for 133 yards and 3 TDs and a 123.5 passer rating. Justin Jefferson. He had most of the biggest catches of the game for the Vikings and equalled his touchdowns for all of last season in just the first game this season. T.J. Hockenson. He had four catches for just 36 yards, but they were mostly key first downs or a touchdown and so were high leverage plays and mostly difficult catches too. His passer rating when targeted was 143.8, just behind Jefferson’s 148.8. Andrew Van Ginkel. He was credited with the forced fumble against Jordan Love that gave the Vikings the ball on the Packers one-yard line, allowing the Vikings to score a touchdown and put the game out of reach. He was also credited with two sacks and an elite coverage grade in preliminary PFF grading. Levi Drake Rodriquez. He was having a good game before his sack of Love, and with a young defensive tackle group, the Vikings need LDR to step up. Domonique Orange. It was Orange who prevented Jordan Love from converting the 4th and 1, which was a key turning point in the game. He was average otherwise, but credit the rookie in his first game for rising to the challenge at a key moment. Stock Down Kyler Murray. He looked shaky in the 11 plays he had, throwing a bad interception before suffering a concussion on an unnecessary roughness call when sliding. Those two key plays hit on the key worries about his career at this point. Josh Metellus. It appeared that Metellus was responsible for a couple of the coverage mistakes that allowed the Packers to generate explosives in the passing game. Theo Jackson. It appeared that Jackson was responsible for the long Christian Watson touchdown by being out of position and missing the tackle on Watson after the reception. Buy Vikings ability to come back from adversity and poor play. Sell Vikings overall execution to start the season. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

(Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off of their victory over the Green Bay Packers to start the 2026 regular season, the Minnesota Vikings will turn around and take on another NFC North divisional rival when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears in Week 2 at Soldier Field. This time, they find themselves as a significant underdog to a team that put on one of the more impressive performances of the season’s opening week. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have released the early lines for Week 2 action around the league, and they have installed the Vikings as a 5.5-point underdog to the Bears for their game in Chicago. The early over/under has been established at 48.5 points. The quarterback situation for the Vikings. . .and stop me if you’ve heard this one. . .may already be in flux. Kyler Murray took just eleven snaps for the Vikings in the first quarter of the opener before having to leave the game with a concussion after taking a nasty late hit from Packers defensive lineman Javon Bullard. It’s the first documented concussion of Murray’s career, so nobody knows exactly how he will react to it, but it’s a situation that everyone will be monitoring as the week goes on. In Murray’s place, Carson Wentz stepped in and played efficiently enough, completing 12-of-19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns. He was largely aided by a Vikings defense that came alive in the fourth quarter, generating a pair of late turnovers and helping the Vikings come back from down 22-10 late in the third quarter to emerge with a 39-22 victory at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Bears had some defensive struggles in Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte, allowing 37 points as Bryce Young threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns. Of course, that didn’t matter very much as the Bears scored. . .59 points. Yes, fifty-nine. That included almost three hundred rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns to go along with Caleb Williams’ 269 yards passing and two passing scores. The 59 points were the fourth-most points the Bears have scored in their history. The Vikings are going to need a much better all-around performance than they got against the Packers if they want to harbor hopes of a victory against the Bears. They were outgained by the Packers by 180 yards (419-239), and the offense was largely dormant for the majority of the afternoon. That isn’t going to work against a team that just put up almost 60 points on the road to start its season. The @Vikings are the first team in NFL history to be down by 12+ points with under 20 minutes left in regulation and end up winning by 17+ points. pic.twitter.com/PnwBsd86T8 — OptaSTATS (@OptaSTATS) September 14, 2026 According to OptaStats, the Vikings are the first team in NFL history to be trailing in a game by twelve or more points with less than 20 minutes remaining in regulation and end up winning that same game by at least seventeen points. They scored the game’s final 29 points, including 22 points in the fourth quarter of play, to put together an improbable comeback win over their division rivals. So, if you sat watching Sunday afternoon’s game thinking that you had never seen anything like that before, well. . .you’re right. You had never seen anything like that before. And neither had anybody else. It’s always nice to see the Vikings on the right end of one of these statistics, isn’t it?

title: Introducing Minnesota Vikings Scorigami
summary: In our quest to make you, our readers, the most informed fans of the Minnesota Vikings that we can, we have crafted a resource that will help you to track down the results of any Vikings game from any point in their history. Ladies and gentlemen, we bring you Minnesota Vikings Scorigami. For those of […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CA - FEBRUARY 08: Detail view of the Minnesota Vikings logo seen at the Super Bowl Experience on February 08, 2022, at the Los Angeles Convention Center in Los Angeles, CA. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In our quest to make you, our readers, the most informed fans of the Minnesota Vikings that we can, we have crafted a resource that will help you to track down the results of any Vikings game from any point in their history. Ladies and gentlemen, we bring you Minnesota Vikings Scorigami. For those of you who are unfamiliar with the concept of Scorigami , it is a term coined by SB Nation’s own Jon Bois a number of years ago. It is defined as the art of building a final score that has never been achieved before in the history of the National Football League. The last league-wide Scorigami that the Vikings were involved in was not a positive one for them, as it was their 52-33 loss to the New Orleans Saints on Christmas Day in 2020. That was the first time in league history there had ever been a 52-33 final score, hence making it a Scorigami. The above chart, rather than accounting for the entire league, shows just the 1,056 games in Minnesota Vikings history. All 567 victories, all 478 losses, and all 11 ties, including playoffs. You can mouse over any of the squares on the grid and you’ll see a pop up with how many times that score occurred and in what years. Playoff games are annotated with a separate icon. If a square is blacked out, it means that score combination has not occurred at any point in franchise history. This page is also available on its own in its own Github repository . Going forward, it will update after every Vikings game. It might take a day or two, but it will self-update. We will also find a way to pin it onto the main page so that it is always available. The idea of Scorigami is kind of cool, and now we have our own version just for our favorite team. I hope that you find this useful or entertaining in some way. UPDATE : As our friend Matt Warren kindly pointed out , the Vikings’ Week 1 victory over the Packers was not only a Scorigami in Minnesota Vikings’ history, but also a Scorigami in NFL history. Our handy chart here has already updated to reflect that, and it will update with the results of each game each week to ensure that every game in Minnesota Vikings history is charted on our Scorigami chart.

title: Vikings and Packers Scorigami is second of NFL Week 1 2026
summary: On Sunday, there were two NFL scores that had never happened in the history of the league and both were accomplished by NFC North squads. After the Chicago Bears dropped 59 points on the Carolina Panthers, the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers finished a 39-22 game, the first in NFL history. The Minnesota/Green Bay […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Mason #27 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball for a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, there were two NFL scores that had never happened in the history of the league and both were accomplished by NFC North squads. After the Chicago Bears dropped 59 points on the Carolina Panthers, the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers finished a 39-22 game, the first in NFL history. The Minnesota/Green Bay final is the 1097th unique score in NFL history. When we get a new final score in the NFL, it’s called Scorigami . Normally when we get a Scorigami it’s because a team scores an absolute boatload of points or something weird happens with two-point conversions and gamesmanship. We got the latter here in the Vikings/Packers game. The Packers missed an extra point in the first quarter, but that didn’t trigger a whole lot of unique scores on its own. Everything stayed pretty normal until the fourth quarter when Minnesota scored to take the lead. They converted a 2-point conversion to go up 25-22. Scoring 25 points in an NFL game is weird. Then Minnesota added two more 7-point touchdowns on top of it. A 39-point day is pretty rare. (A 32-22 score has also never happened.) During the 2025 season we saw four Scorigamis including one in Week 1: Bills beat Ravens 41-40 Cowboys and Packers tie 40-40 Texans beat Jaguars 36-29 Bills beat Buccaneers 44-32 The NFL averages around four of these per season and we already are halfway there in Week 1. As a reminder, we have not only this score, but every other score for all 1,057 games in Minnesota Vikings history on our Minnesota Vikings Scorigami board, which you can see right here .

title: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22: Vikings Ride Huge Fourth Quarter to Wild Win
summary: The old adage is that it isn’t how you start, it’s how you finish. In Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, there’s nowhere that was on greater display than at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. After Kyler Murray went out early in the game with a concussion and after stumbling through an ugly first […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Justin Jefferson #18, Brian O'Neill #75, Jordan Addison #3, and Jordan Mason #27 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrate after Mason's rushing touchdown against the Green Bay Packers in the fourth quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The old adage is that it isn’t how you start, it’s how you finish. In Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, there’s nowhere that was on greater display than at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. After Kyler Murray went out early in the game with a concussion and after stumbling through an ugly first half, the Minnesota Vikings scored the final 29 points of Sunday’s season opener, getting three touchdown passes from Carson Wentz and getting themselves a fairly improbable 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers to start their 2026 season. The Packers won the coin toss and deferred to the second half, giving the Vikings the football first. Kyler Murray led the Vikings’ offense onto the field, and his first pass as a Viking was an interception by Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon as Murray lofted a pretty awful pass off his back foot under pressure. The Vikings’ defense was able to limit the damage, as they forced Jordan Love into three straight incompletions. The Packers then brought on their rookie kicker, Trey Smack, to attempt a 59-yard field goal, and he put it through the uprights with room to spare to give the visiting team an early 3-0 lead less than three minutes into the contest. The second drive for the Vikings didn’t go that much better, as a couple of false start penalties caused the drive to stall out near midfield after one first down and rookie Brett Thorson punted the ball away. The Packers quickly. . .very quickly. . .got back on the scoreboard again, as Love found Christian Watson on a short crossing pass, and Watson did the rest to turn the reception into an 81-yard catch-and-run for a touchdown. There was a flag on the play, but the referees picked it up and the touchdown stood. Smack missed the extra point, but the Packers still led 9-0 midway through the first quarter. On the Vikings’ next drive, Murray attempted to scramble for a first down and slid to the turf, where he was hit late by Packers’ lineman Javon Bullard. Bullard was flagged for unnecessary roughness, which gave the Vikings a first down, but Murray was taken off the field to the blue medical tent and evaluated for a head injury . Carson Wentz checked into the game at quarterback. Wentz moved the Vikings into field goal range, and Will Reichard got the Vikings their first points of the season courtesy of a 38-yard field goal to make it 9-3 with time winding down in the first quarter of play. The Packers returned the ensuing kickoff into Vikings territory, setting up shop at the Minnesota 40-yard line. The short field led to more points for the Packers, as they got another field goal from Smack, this one a 43-yarder to put the lead back to nine points as 12-3. The teams then went back and forth exchanging punts until near the two-minute warning. Wentz drove the Vikings down to the Green Bay 39-yard line, and when it looked like the Vikings would let the clock tick down to the two-minute warning, a member of the Packers jumped offsides and the Vikings snapped it to give themselves a free play, and Wentz lofted it up for the best wide receiver in the game. Carson Wentz completes a DEEP one to Justin Jefferson, and this is a 2-point game 🫡 pic.twitter.com/ppnw4VvOOT — Zone Coverage (@ZoneCoverageMN) September 13, 2026 It was a 39-yard touchdown for Jefferson, and with just under two minutes left in the half, the Vikings managed to make it a two-point game at 12-10. But, the Vikings left the Packers too much time, as they marched straight down the field with just about no resistance. Love hit big passes to Tucker Kraft and Christian Watson to put the Packers into scoring position, and concluded the drive with a 2-yard pass to Watson for his second touchdown of the afternoon to send the Packers into the locker room with a nine-point lead at 19-10. The third quarter was largely quiet until there were about five minutes remaining. Love drove the Packers to midfield and then found Jonnu Smith for a big gain into Minnesota territory at the 6-yard line to set up a goal-to-go situation, but the offense stalled out and they had to settle for another field goal from Smack, this one a 26-yarder to make it 22-10 with just over five minutes left in the third quarter. Myles Price then tried to put a spark into the Vikings, as he took the ensuing kickoff and returned it 69 yards to the Green Bay 28-yard line to give the Vikings great field position for their next possession. MUCH NEEDED from Myles Price. pic.twitter.com/iyg7V7pQJ5 — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) September 13, 2026 The Vikings took advantage of the outstanding field position, as Wentz threw his second touchdown pass of the afternoon, finding T.J. Hockenson over the middle for a 16-yard score to cut the Green Bay lead to 22-17 with just over two minutes remaining in the third quarter. Wentz finds Hockenson and the Vikings are hanging around pic.twitter.com/KOWPqL3zEJ — Sean Borman (@SeanBormanNFL) September 13, 2026 On the Packers’ next possession early in the fourth quarter, they got a 40-yard field goal from Smack that made the score 25-17 on a 4th-and-6 play, but the Vikings were called for offsides. The Packers elected to take the points off the board and go for it on 4th-and-1. Love went for a quarterback sneak, and the spot went to a virtual measurement that ultimately ruled Love short of the line to gain, giving the Vikings the ball on a turnover on downs. That would mark the true turning point of this football game. The Vikings cashed in on the ensuing possession, at least in part because the Green Bay defense couldn’t stop committing penalties. There were three third-down stops by the Green Bay defense that were negated by defensive penalties, including an interception in the end zone by Evan Williams that was negated by a defensive holding penalty on Xavier McKinney. In the end, the drive concluded with the former Packer, Aaron Jones, finding his way into the end zone on a 3-yard run around the left end that gave the Vikings a 23-22 lead. The Vikings followed that up with a pass from Wentz to Jefferson for the two-point conversion to make it 25-22 with six and a half minutes left in regulation. AARON JONES GIVES US THE LEAD! pic.twitter.com/J2FjF5vqGe — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) September 13, 2026 On the Packers’ next possession, the Vikings’ defense went absolutely berserk. Dallas Turner got a sack of Jordan Love on second down, and then Andrew Van Ginkel and Blake Cashman sacked him on third down, with Love fumbling the ball and Van Ginkel recovering the loose ball at the Green Bay 1-yard line. Vikings bring the house AND recover the fumble 😤 GBvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qd1SgYGcIY — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Just one play later, Jordan Mason took a handoff from Wentz and took it into the end zone from a yard out for a touchdown, and just like that the Vikings found themselves up by ten points at 32-22. Jordan Mason is IN! GBvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r4wirOIjUJ — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Then, it just continued to get worse for the Packers, as Love dropped back to pass and had a throw deflected by Harrison Smith into the hands of James Pierre for an interception that he returned to the Green Bay 14-yard line. James Pierre gives the @Vikings defense another takeaway GBvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jrGQSsA1BV — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 After that, Justin Jefferson got his second touchdown of the afternoon. . .matching his total from all of the 2025 season. . .by getting into the end zone on a 9-yard pass from Wentz to make it 39-22 and…

Midway through […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball during the first quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images UPDATE : Murray has officially been downgraded to OUT for the remainder of today’s game with a concussion. The 2026 season opener didn’t get off to a great start for the Minnesota Vikings, and it didn’t get much better midway through the first quarter with a very scary moment involving the Vikings’ starting quarterback. Midway through the first quarter, Kyler Murray was attempting to scramble for a first down, and when he slid to the turf he took a vicious shot to the head from Green Bay Packers defensive lineman Javon Bullard. Bullard was called for an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, but Murray was taken off the field and straight to the locker room for an evaluation for a head injury. Murray, who was signed to a 1-year deal this offseason as a free agent, was named as the team’s starter early in training camp, got off to a rough start to the game as his first pass as a Viking was intercepted by Keisean Nixon. After the injury, he was replaced by Carson Wentz, who was listed as the team’s backup. J.J. McCarthy is the team’s emergency quarterback, but he can’t enter today’s game unless Wentz also gets injured. Once again, Kyler Murray took a shot to the head midway through the first quarter of today’s regular season opener against the Green Bay Packers and is being evaluated for a head injury. When we have further word on any sort of injury he may have suffered, we will bring it to you here.
