title: Survey results: Giants fans brimming with confidence ahead of Cowboys game
summary: The off-season is the time for hope among sports fans. Every possible future is still open before them, and we never know what Schrödinger’s season has in store for us until the games are played. But right now, most New York Giants fans are a very hopeful lot as Week 1 gets under way. And […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The off-season is the time for hope among sports fans. Every possible future is still open before them, and we never know what Schrödinger’s season has in store for us until the games are played. But right now, most New York Giants fans are a very hopeful lot as Week 1 gets under way. And as it always seems to happen, the Giants are preparing to play the Dallas Cowboys to open the season. We’ll find out if the Cowboys can live up to their pre-season hype, and whether the Giants are being unfairly dismissed, soon enough. But for now, we had just one simple question for Giants fans ahead of Sunday night’s matchup: Will the Giants beat the Cowboys? The majority — and a significant majority at that — of Giants fans are expecting a win to start the season. The Giants are 3-point underdogs at home coming into the game ( per FanDuel ), up from 2.5-point underdogs after the preseason and meaning they would be considered 6-point underdogs on a neutral field. Still, most Giants fans believe their team is being dismissed and is primed to shock the NFL world. The sentiment seems to be that the Giants earned their wins over the Chargers and Eagles a year ago, and their near-victories over the Broncos, Lions, and Bears weren’t flukes. In short, they believe new head coach John Harbaugh that the Giants have the talent to compete right now . There are, of course, plenty of pessimists around who don’t believe a rapid turnaround is possible. They instead seem to buy into the belief that the Giants are fundamentally flawed and need a complete teardown and rebuild before they can compete with the best in the NFL — or the Cowboys, for that matter. (Yes, that was a not-so-subtle dig at Dallas, who have plenty to prove themselves.) We’ll find out who’s right over the coming days and weeks. For right now, however, Giants fans are confident. All but the most pessimistic fans seem to believe that the Giants are heading in the right direction as we enter 2026. John Harbaugh and Joe Schoen seem to have coalesced around a shared vision of the team, and are building towards it with a purpose and conviction we haven’t seen in a long time. A full 95 percent of Giants fans are confident that the team is headed in the right direction as we enter Week 1. That puts Giants fans in the same realm of confidence as Patriots, Seahawks, Chargers, and Broncos’ fans. The other fanbases know that they have playoff caliber teams who expect to be in championship contention. Giants’ fans, meanwhile, are by far the most confident of the teams with poor records in 2025. Giants fans are even more confident than the fans of the “good but not great” teams. Is it overconfidence? Last year fan confidence was at 92 percent after a phenomenal preseason performance. Again, we’ll find out over the coming weeks. For now, however, vibes are good among Giants’ fans.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Jets Week 1 Stock Up, Stock Down
summary: The season is finally here. And for a change, the Jets get a rare Week 1 win! The caveat, of course, is that the Titans are the Titans. But still, it’s nice to take the wins where you can get them. Who helped their stock, and who hurt it? Let’s start with the stock ups. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets reacts against the Tennessee Titans during the first quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The season is finally here. And for a change, the Jets get a rare Week 1 win! The caveat, of course, is that the Titans are the Titans. But still, it’s nice to take the wins where you can get them. Who helped their stock, and who hurt it? Let’s start with the stock ups. Stock Up Olu Fashanu Now, I could mention the whole offensive line here, because I thought they were fantastic today. But I’ll mention Fashanu solely because, to me, he was the biggest X-factor for this team both this year and long-term. Fashanu has proven to be an average NFL left tackle in his career thus far. But entering Year 3 at just 23 years old, the hope and expectation is that the former first-round pick will develop into an impact LT for years to come. Today was a good start. Against the Titans, Fashanu allowed just two pressures, no sacks, and graded out above 74.0 as both a pass blocker and run blocker. The whole offensive line played well, but Fashanu was extremely efficient against a talented Titans front. This is exactly the type of performance the Jets need to see from him if he’s going to become the long-term answer at left tackle. Azareye’h Thomas I’ve recently said I’m kind of shocked about how little discussion Thomas has gotten surrounding the Jets this year. Cornerback is arguably the position where the Jets had the most question marks entering the season. Last year’s third-round pick quietly won the starting job opposite Brandon Stephens during training camp, and his first impression was quite good. You didn’t hear his name too often, which is a good thing for a corner. But when you did, it was normally because of a positive play. Thomas led the Jets in run stops with three, making a few terrific tackles on the perimeter, which was a huge weakness for this defense last year. The competition wasn’t extremely good, but outside of a garbage-time touchdown he gave up, Thomas was excellent for the majority of the game. On a big third down, Ward challenged him down the field, and Thomas played fantastic coverage, using the sideline to his advantage to force an incompletion on Elic Ayomanor. PFF agreed too with how Thomas performed, as he finished with an 80.3 overall grade and an 81.8 coverage grade. At only 22 years old, Thomas turning into a sufficient starting boundary corner would be an excellent development for the Jets this year. Once again, the competition wasn’t great, but it’s a good start. Kenyon Sadiq Listen, Sadiq didn’t do anything incredible. But considering the injuries and all the negative vibes we heard about him this offseason, the fact that he was even a contributor at all is a positive to me for the rookie tight end in Week 1. Sadiq only had three targets, but the fact that the Jets utilized more multi-tight end sets, something Frank Reich famously hasn’t done at his last two stops, makes me think there was at least some semblance of a plan for him. There will be a lot more to watch for with Sadiq, but it’s very clear that he’s extremely athletic on the field. This isn’t just a guy who tested well athletically but doesn’t look the part in pads. The touchdown wasn’t anything incredible, but it was a shrewd play call that used one of the Jets’ freak athletes to their advantage: Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq reached a top speed of 20.09 mph on his 3-yard TD run, the fastest play by a Jets tight end as a ball carrier in the NGS era (since 2016). #NYJvsTEN | #JetUp pic.twitter.com/sx5voebKac — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) September 13, 2026 That’s exactly the type of thing I want to see from this offense. Find your good players and find creative ways to get them involved. Geno Smith The last person I’ll mention is Geno. I don’t think it was all positive for Geno. In the first half, I saw some questionable clock management decisions, including a boneheaded checkdown that ended the Jets’ chances of getting points before halftime. He also seemed a bit too slow with his decision-making to start the game. In the second half, though, I thought he was much, much better. I don’t think he had to do anything crazy considering the game script, but he was fairly accurate and efficient and was able to push the ball downfield. He ended with an 84.7 Total QBR, 0.26 EPA/play, and a 12.8 CPOE, all of which were elite numbers. Now, I think the game script helped him heavily. And I’ve said all offseason that the main way to get competent play from Geno is to protect him. The Jets showed a glimpse of what he can do when they do. Stock Down Now that we got the good out of the way, let’s get to the bad. Fortunately, there wasn’t much of it. Mason Taylor Let’s just say this was a brutal game for Taylor. And to be honest, he’s extremely fortunate it wasn’t worse. Taylor was targeted three times and had an inexcusable drop that arguably could have been a fumble. It happened in a spot on the field where it could have been completely game-changing. The other two targets resulted in catches, but one was a play that was doomed from the start, a tight end screen that went for negative yards and ultimately cost the Jets points. I can’t hate on him too much for making that catch. That was more on Geno. But if you wanted to see some progress from the second-year tight end, this wasn’t a good start. Arian Smith Sticking with the theme of 2025 draft picks, my other big loser of the game was Arian Smith. Again, I’ve long criticized the Smith pick. I don’t want to blame him for getting overdrafted. It was a boneheaded selection at the time. But for a guy entering his second season, one where I thought he was lucky to make the roster in the first place, you cannot drop a routine catch on your only offensive snap of the game. To me, it’s very clear where Smith will need to shift his focus if he wants to last in this league: special teams. With his straight-line speed, he very much could end up being a positive contributor in that facet of the game. We’ll see. Overall Overall, though, there were more highs than lows. The Jets haven’t been over .500 in nearly two years. Let’s take the wins where we can get them. The Titans might be really bad this year, but to be honest I don’t care. I’ll take it.

title: The Jets’ plan worked perfectly in Week 1 win vs. Titans
summary: All 32 NFL teams enter the season with a plan. Change is something every team has to deal with. For those at the top of the league like the Seattle Seahawks, the change is replacing key coaches and players who had departed for greener pastures. For a team that was 3-14 like the Jets, the […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets reacts after the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images All 32 NFL teams enter the season with a plan. Change is something every team has to deal with. For those at the top of the league like the Seattle Seahawks, the change is replacing key coaches and players who had departed for greener pastures. For a team that was 3-14 like the Jets, the changes focus on upgrades. Of course all of these plans clash. The Tennessee Titans, the Jets’ Week 1 opponent, made plans to improve this offseason. They wanted new coach Robert Saleh to provide the team with fresh leadership and second year quarterback Cam Ward to take a major step forward. Everybody’s plan cannot possibly work. The teams making these plans compete directly against each other. That is something the Jets know all too well. This is a team with the longest Playoff drought in the league. It has been a decade and a half since the Jets saw the postseason. It has now been over a decade since the Jets so much ended a season with a winning record. Plan after plan has failed. A year ago Justin Fields was supposed to resurrect his career. Before that, Aaron Rodgers and a cast of big name veterans were supposed to take the Jets to the Super Bowl. Before that, the Robert Saleh-Zach Wilson combination was supposed to make the Jets a permanent fixture as an AFC contender. Before that, Adam Gase and Sam Darnold were supposed to do the same. We can hope the Jets’ plan will work before each season. Based on what the team did in the 2026 offseason, it was logical to believe it was likely the team would be improved. But we didn’t know for sure until they actually took the field. We couldn’t. I think this is what made this 23-10 dominating Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans so enjoyable. Everything went according to plan. If you had ask Jets fans how this team would find success in 2026 after a busy offseason, most probably would have laid out a blueprint similar to what we saw in this game. On the offensive side of the ball, a line anchored by two talented tackles would control the trenches. The Jets could run the ball effectively with Breece Hall and when he needed a rest Braelon Allen. The pressure would be off Geno Smith, who wouldn’t need to carry the offense. The veteran quarterback would just need to distribute the ball effectively to his pass catchers. Of course Garrett Wilson would be the go to guy, but Adonai Mitchell would emerge as viable second option. Still, rookies Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper would chip in. On the defensive side of the ball, Aaron Glenn and Brian Duker would oversee a defense that looked far more prepared than what we saw from Steve Wilks a year ago. A new look edge group led by David Bailey would relentlessly get after the quarterback. In the middle of the field, Demario Davis would be stout and erase any problems. And so it was at least for this week. Look, the season in the NFL is a long one. The successful teams in this league perform at a high level consistently. It’s one thing to look great for one game. The season lasts four and a half months. This sort of effort has to be repeated over and over. The Jets drew an easy opponent in Week 1. The Titans figure to be one of the league’s worst teams. This was one of the few times the Jets will take the field in a regular season game with a pronounced talent advantage over their opponent. Beating other opponents like this won’t be as easy. Taking it a step further, a win doesn’t necessarily guarantee a great Jets season, but losing this game would have been a catastrophe. With that said, I haven’t known the Jets to avoid catastrophe too often in recent years. They also didn’t have the chance to play 17 games of consistent football this week, and they couldn’t choose their opponent. They could play one game against the team they were scheduled against. And they played that game against that opponent extremely well. There will be plenty of time to worry about future games and a tougher upcoming schedule. For now I’m just going to enjoy a truly outstanding Jets win and savor one season that has gone according to plan at least for the first week.

title: Jets open as Week 2 underdogs vs Packers
summary: The New York Jets opened their 2026 campaign with a thorough 23 – 10 thrashing of the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Beginning with a sparkling opening drive for a touchdown in which everything went just as Jets fans hoped all offseason, the Jets left no doubt as to which was the better team, dominating the […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 09: Isaiah Davis #32 of the New York Jets is pushed out of bounds by Micah Robinson #26 of the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter during the NFL Preseason 2025 game between New York Jets and Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on August 09, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets opened their 2026 campaign with a thorough 23 – 10 thrashing of the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Beginning with a sparkling opening drive for a touchdown in which everything went just as Jets fans hoped all offseason, the Jets left no doubt as to which was the better team, dominating the Titans early, late, and everything in between. The Jets ran the ball effectively and shut down the Titans’ running game. When Titans quarterback Cam Ward was forced to pass the Jets kept him under pressure all day. At halftime the Jets had built a 10 – 3 lead, which they extended to 23 -3 in the fourth quarter before the Titans scored a meaningless late touchdown in garbage time. Jets quarterback Geno Smith was efficient and effective in his triumphant return to a Jets team that gave up on him more than a decade ago. The Jets three 2026 first round picks all got in on the fun. 2nd overall pick David Baily contributed a sack of Cam Ward, 16th overall pick Kenyon Sadiq ran the ball in for the Jets’ first touchdown of the season, and 30th overall pick Omar Cooper gave the Jets an impressive 30 yard catch and run on the opening drive, pinballing off multiple defenders before exiting the game with an ankle injury. The win gave the Jets a 1-0 record to start the season. It was nice to see after the dreadful uncompetitive 3-14 Jets season of 2025. Now the Jets head home to take on the Green Bay Packers in their home opener next Sunday. A home victory would give the Jets a 2-0 record out of the gate for the first time since 2015 and would give a Jets fanbase starved for something positive hope that the Jets might finally be building something solid. The Packers present a significantly tougher challenge for the Jets than the Titans did. They have been a playoff team six of the last seven years and 14 of the last 17. The Packers opened the 2026 season with a 39 – 22 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Jordan Love was sacked four times and turned the ball over twice. The Vikings shut down a Packers running game sorely missing starting running back Josh Jacobs and harassed Love all day. The Packers will be looking to rebound against this young Jets team and avoid the dreaded 0-2 start for the season. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 4.5 points. The game has an over/under of 44.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +176 while the Packers are -210. Let’s see if some home cooking can propel the Jets to a 2-0 start for the first time in more than a decade.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Jets vs. Titans: Starting 2026 with a win!
summary: In the New York Jets’ 2026 season opener, on a stifling hot day in Nashville, Tennessee, the Jets defeated the Tennessee Titans, 23 – 10. The game opened on a positive note for the Jets, as the Titans kicked off out of bounds. That gave the Jets the ball on the 40 yard line with […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Kenyon Sadiq #16 of the New York Jets scores a rushing touchdown against James Williams Sr. #52 of the Tennessee Titans Tennessee Titans during the first quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ 2026 season opener, on a stifling hot day in Nashville, Tennessee, the Jets defeated the Tennessee Titans, 23 – 10. The game opened on a positive note for the Jets, as the Titans kicked off out of bounds. That gave the Jets the ball on the 40 yard line with a short field for the offense to open the 2026 season. The Jets took advantage. The rookies led the way, as Omar Cooper Jr had a big 30 yard catch and run and Kenyon Sadiq ran the ball in for a three yard touchdown as the Jets took an early 7 – 0 lead. It’s just one drive, but this was how Jets fans envisioned the offense looking this year. The Titans took over on offense and put together a nice drive of their own as the Jets defense struggled to get off the field on third down. In an ominous development Minkah Fitzpatrick went down with an apparent groin injury. The Titans eventually had to settle for a Joey Slye field goal to make the score Jets 7, Titans 3 late in the first quarter. On the Jets next possession they went on a long, grinding drive dominated by the ground game. The drive took up a large chunk of the second quarter before it bogged down and the Jets settled for a short field goal. That made it Jets 10, Titans 3 late in the second quarter. On the ensuing kickoff the Jets forced a fumble and Qwan’tez Stiggers recovered the ball to give the Jets great field position inside Titans territory. The Jets unfortunately squandered the golden opportunity as their drive went nowhere and Jason Sanders missed a long field goal attempt. The Jets had a chance to tack on points in the last minute of the first half, but they ran a really ugly sequence of plays with multiple penalties as the clock an out. The quarter and the half ended with the score still Jets 10, Titans 3. The Jets opened the third quarter on defense. After giving up a couple of first downs through the air the Jets forced a Titans punt. The Jets offense took over and promptly went on a long drive highlighted by a 40 yard bomb from Geno Smith to Adonai Mitchell. Breece Hall ran the ball in from the four yard line as the Jets took a 17 – 3 lead early in the third quarter. The next time the Jets got the football they again went on a long drive as the Geno Smith to Garrett Wilson heated up. Braelon Allen scored an apparent touchdown on a long run, but a holding call negated the touchdown and the Jets settled for a 51 yard Jason Sanders field goal to take a commanding 20 – 3 lead late in the third quarter. The quarter ended with the score still 20 – 3 in favor of the Jets. Early in the fourth quarter Will McDonald broke through with a sack of Cam Ward on the one yard line. The Titans were forced to punt shortly thereafter and the Jets got the ball in prime scoring position in Titans territory. A score here would all but end the game. Alas, it wasn’t in the cards. The Jets went nowhere and were forced to punt. Qwan’tez Stiggers continued his outstanding special teams play by downing the punt inside the two yard line, putting the Titans 98 yards away from a much needed touchdown. Barring a miracle, the game appeared to be all but over with less than 10 minutes to go and the Titans needing three scores. The Jets tacked on a 52 yard field goal with a little over five minutes to play to make the score Jets 23, Titans 3. The Titans put together a meaningless touchdown drive in garbage time to get them within 13 points at Jets 23, Titans 10. Final score: Jets 23, Titans 10. For one game at least the Jets performed just like they drew it up in the offseason. Geno Smith was efficient and protected the ball. The offensive line dominated. The running game kept the ball away from the Titans. The pass rush kept the pressure on Cam Ward. The revamped defensive front seven shut down the Titans running game. The Jets appeared to outcoach the Titans. Special teams were great. It was a complete, dominant win to start the season. Wasn’t that fun? The win brought the Jets’ record to 1-0. Now the Jets have to put the win behind them and get ready for a much more difficult challenge as they prepare for their home opener next week against the Green Bay Packers next Sunday.

title: Jets vs Titans Game Thread
summary: It’s finally here. After a long, long offseason, the New York Jets finally play a meaningful game again. All the speculation, all the hype, all the koolaid, all the doomsaying, it all comes to a head today when the actual games begin to supersede whatever your preconceived notions were about this 2026 New York Jets […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - APRIL 23: New York Jets fans cheer during Round One of the 2026 NFL Draft at Acrisure Stadium on April 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s finally here. After a long, long offseason, the New York Jets finally play a meaningful game again. All the speculation, all the hype, all the koolaid, all the doomsaying, it all comes to a head today when the actual games begin to supersede whatever your preconceived notions were about this 2026 New York Jets team. Today the Jets are on the road in a very hot Nashville, Tennessee to take on the Tennessee Titans to open the 2026 season for both teams. Last year the New York Jets cleaned house after the Aaron Rodgers Experience ran its course and predictably resulted in everybody getting fired. This year the Jets thought that was so much fun, why not fire everyone again? And so they did, with Aaron Glenn replacing nearly the entire coaching staff after the 2025 Jets were in the conversation for the worst team in the NFL. In addition to bringing in an almost entirely new coaching staff, the Jets also brought in numerous veterans in free agency. The defense has been completely revamped, with key veteran additions Minkah Fitzpatrick, Dane Belton, Demario Davis, David Onyemata, T’Vondre Sweat, Kingsley Enagbare and the injured Joseph Ossai joined by premium draft picks David Bailey and D’Angelo Ponds. On the offense the Jets added Omar Cooper Jr and Kenyon Sadiq to complement Garrett Wilson as targets for the new starting quarterback, Geno Smith. Download SB Nation’s new app for game day! Game-day discussions are so much smoother in SB Nation’s new app. Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . With all the changes, the 2026 Jets scarcely resemble the disastrous 2025 team. Will the result be a much more competitive team? We’ll begin to get the answer to that question today, against a Tennessee Titans team coached by old friend Robert Saleh. Saleh has stacked his team with double digit numbers of ex-Jets. We’ll see how that works out for him, starting today. It’s the Jets and the Titans in the opening game of a crucial year for head coach Aaron Glenn and the Jets today. Enjoy the game everyone.

title: Eagles-Commander snap counts: Dontayvion Wicks flashes as WR2
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Andy Dalton, Hollywood Brown INACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Elijah Moore, Jonathan Greenard, Micah Morris
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles scores a touchdown against Mike Sainristil #0 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Excluding garbage time situations, it’s typically a good thing when the starting quarterback and offensive line are able to play the entire game. In this case, unfortunately, Landon Dickerson did not look very playable out there. Cam Jurgens didn’t have a great game, either. DeVonta Smith is WR1 and he was only off the field for three snaps. Smitty led the Eagles in targets with six, which produced three receptions for 53 yards. His sole special teams snap came when he logged the game-sealing onside kick recovery. Not an easy play with the ball bouncing at him like it was … but he managed to make the grab! Dallas Goedert was also only off the field for three snaps. He finished second in targets with five, making four catches for 77 yards and two touchdowns. This was the most receiving yards Goedert had in a game since the Eagles’ overtime loss to the Los Angeles Chargers last year. Goedert’s 43-yard reception was the longest he’s had since his 61-yard scamper late in the New Orleans Saints game in 2024. Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles, hat tip to The Ringer’s Philly Special) is clearly WR2. He ranked tied for third (with Makai Lemon) in targets with four, which produced two catches for 73 yards and one touchdown. Saquon Barkley accounted for 15 of the Eagles’ 18 running back carries. Makai Lemon saw a good deal of playing time as WR3. The results sure weren’t great ; his five targets produced three receptions for -5 yards. Washington’s defense clearly wasn’t fooled by those designed touches for the rookie first-round pick. As expected, Johnny Mundt spent most of his time blocking inline as TE2. Of his 20 snaps, 12 were spent as a run blocker and four came in pass protection. Which means he ran a route on just four snaps. Will Shipley played more than Tank Bigsby … and saw three times as many touches (three to one). Don’t love that. The Eagles underutilized Bigsby last year and they did again in Week 1 this year. My guy Darius Cooper was a beast on special teams, logging four tackles in one game! He didn’t see a target on offense despite the fact he looks more ready to help right now than Lemon does. Cooper DeJean had two offensive snaps as the player lined up behind the offense in victory formation. The offensive safety, if you will. TE3 E.J. Jenkins mostly played on special teams. DEFENSE DeJean played eight snaps at safety in his first game as the primary option on the back end next to Andrew Mukuba in base packages. Rough game for Coop in coverage. Jihaad Campbell was not the field for three defensive snaps. Jalen Carter logging 66 snaps in Week 1 stands out. Would be ideal to see more of a rotation there but we know by now that Vic Fangio likes to lean heavily on his top defensive linemen. Would be nice if the Eagles’ offense could manage to stay on the field more often to give Carter and the rest of the defense more of a break by not having to play so many snaps. With Jonathan Greenard out, Jalyx Hunt is the Eagles’ top edge rusher in terms of playing time. No surprise but here’s the confirmation. Marcus Epps briefly missed some time after getting banged up early in the game but he returned to be the Eagles’ safety next to Mukuba in non-base packages. Moro Ojomo saw the second-most defensive tackles snaps and obviously made a game-winning play by stuffing Washington’s two-point game-tying two-point conversion attempt. With Jonathan Greenard out, Nolan Smith is the Eagles’ second edge rusher. Jordan Davis ranked third in defensive tackle snaps. Pro Football Focus had him as the Eagles’ third-highest graded defender, only behind Zack Baun and Epps. Arnold Ebiketie playing the third-most edge rusher snaps was a bit of a surprise since it seemed like A.J. Epenesa was ahead of him. But Epenesa also seemed to get banged up in this game, so, that may have been a factor. Michael Carter II is a role player for the time being. Bryon Young saw some snaps in heavier defensive line packages. SPECIAL TEAMS Kelee Ringo continues to see a lot of special teams playing time. Big reason why the Eagles kept him on the roster. Braden Mann had an active day with seven punts, already tying his most from any game last year (which he did four times in 2025). Mann was a beast in terms of both booting the ball and pinning the Commanders back deep with good directional punts. Jake Elliott made a 35-yard field goal and went 3/3 on extra points. Ty Robinson was limited to special teams duty. Zero defensive snaps despite his emergence in the preseason. Fangio clearly doesn’t trust him. Britain Covey was temporarily elevated from the practice squad to be the Eagles’ punt returner. His four returns produced 37 yards for a quality 9.7 average. Fred Johnson and Markel Bell were limited to special teams duty. It’s unclear how the Eagles will handle replacing Jordan Mailata or Lane Johnson if they go down and it would be nice not find out what the plan is there if it means the starters remain healthy. Drew Kendall and Willie Lampkin were also limited to special teams duty. Thought we might see the Eagles use Lampkin in a specialized role … but they did not. Maybe they’re saving that? Or maybe they’re not going to mess around with that knowing they might need him to actually play guard or center for them this season. Though I do believe Kendall is the top interior backup option ahead of Lampkin. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Andy Dalton, Hollywood Brown INACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Elijah Moore, Jonathan Greenard, Micah Morris The Eagles finally revealed their plan at QB2 (gasp!). It’s Dalton, which doesn’t inspire much confidence. Though I guess we’ll see if this is the case again in Week 2. With as weird as this backup quarterback battle has been, maybe there’s a non-zero chance they rotate it to where McKee is QB2 against the Tennessee Titans?! Guessing not but we’ll see. No playing time for Hollywood Brown, who did not have a very good summer. Not trusted to play on offense and not a factor on special teams … but the Eagles paid him a good chunk of change so he’s still here. Payton is QB4. Redshirt year for him, unless he manages to contribute on special teams at some point. The Eagles kept Moore on the roster only to not dress him for Week 1. You wonder why they wouldn’t just release him (he’s a vested veteran who isn’t subject to waivers) and try to get him back on the practice squad. Or, you know, they could actually play him. Based on what we saw in practice, he looks more ready to contribute right now than Lemon does. Could be nice to see more of a rotation behind the top two receivers (DeVonta and Wicks). We’ll see if Greenard is able to fully participate in practice this week or not. Week 3 might be more realistic for him. They shouldn’t need him to be able to beat the Titans. Another bonus to waiting for the Chicago Bears game is that it’s played on a Monday night, giving Greenard an extra day to get ready at that point. It’s a redshirt year for Morris as the tenth offensive lineman on the roster. Note that the Eagles still have one open roster spot after placing Eli Stowers on injured reserve .

(Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The way I’d frame the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders? I’d say it’s a performance to build on. Maybe Sean Mannion’s group can get it going against the Tennessee Titans? The Eagles are entering Week 2 as seven-point road favorites, according to FanDuel . The Jets’ top two running backs combined for 142 rushing yards and one touchdown on 32 carries (4.4 average). Until we actually see the Eagles prove they can block better, it might be hard to fully believe it. But you have to feel good about Jalen Hurts’ ability to make plays for this team after watching what he did against the Commanders. You also have to like Vic Fangio’s chances of being able to stifle the Titans’ offense, which managed a mere 195 yards yesterday. That’s 123 fewer yards than the Eagles managed to muster in Week 1. The Titans will be motivated to avoid two straight home losses to start the 2026 season but I believe in the Birds to emerge victorious. Will they definitely cover? I’ll lean yes, though I can’t say I’m 100% confident. What say you?

title: Eagles rookie report card: Need more from Makai Lemon
summary: The Eagles pieced together a divisional win over the Washington Commadners on Sunday, showing exciting flashes on both sides of the ball as they shook some rust off. While there is much to be encouraged about, the Eagles’ rookies are not among those reasons for optimism. Here are the big takeaways from Philadelphia’s 2026 NFL […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts as he walks through the tunnel against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles pieced together a divisional win over the Washington Commadners on Sunday, showing exciting flashes on both sides of the ball as they shook some rust off. While there is much to be encouraged about, the Eagles’ rookies are not among those reasons for optimism. Here are the big takeaways from Philadelphia’s 2026 NFL Draft class in Week 1. Makai Lemon: D It was to be expected that Makai Lemon would have a slow start to the season given his lack of participation in the offseason. He missed a lot of practice time due to his hamstring injury. But Sunday was still rough. Lemon was targeted four times, catching three passes and finishing the day with negative five yards. That is really tough, but it’s not all on him. Lemon’s usage was odd to say the least. Sean Mannion and company are still clearly trying to get a handle on what to do with this receiving group after DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. Two of Lemon’s catches were on doomed screens and one was a short perimeter target. Given what Lemon was good at, I think he should live in the slot and eat up short targets there to get him going. Sunday was not his day, but it’s obvious the team wants him out there given 29 receiver snaps, which was the third-most at his position. Hopefully, going forward the Eagles find different ways to get Lemon involved as he gets more comfortable with the playbook. Other Observations Eli Stowers was placed on injured reserve as the Eagles put him on the backburner. That’s a bummer and I hope he can figure it out at some point this season. The good news for the Eagles is that Dallas Goedert looks awesome. Throwback to the Eagles drafting Goedert in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft and then Zach Ertz immediately having the best season of his career. Rookie blockers Markel Bell and Micah Morris are beginning this season as depth players; the former was active while the latter was a healthy scratch. That being said, Landon Dickerson looked rough yesterday. Hopefully it is just a one-off bad day for the three-time Pro Bowler, but he really didn’t look like himself. That is worth monitoring, and luckily the Eagles have the depth to fill in if Dickerson can’t go. Cole Payton was predictably inactive as QB4. No special teams role for him.
author: Benjamin Natan

title: The Takeaway: Not much new to see in the Eagles’ escape over the Commanders
summary: By the time Lincoln Financial Field’s clock struck 0:00 late Sunday afternoon and the Eagles had survived a 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, a palpable sense of relief could be felt by the fanbase. For the sixth straight time under Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, the Eagles won their opening game. It […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs against the Washington Commanders in the fourth quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images By the time Lincoln Financial Field’s clock struck 0:00 late Sunday afternoon and the Eagles had survived a 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, a palpable sense of relief could be felt by the fanbase. For the sixth straight time under Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, the Eagles won their opening game. It is the longest active streak in the NFL and it is always better to start 1-0 than 0-1. Just ask the Dallas Cowboys. While the Eagles’ defense looked absolutely gassed by the end of it, they managed one last goal-line, two-point conversion stand, and spent the better part of the first three quarters limiting Jayden Daniels and the Washington offense for most of the afternoon. It was reminiscent of a season ago, when the defense carried an offense that had trouble maintaining consistency. Week 1 was our first opportunity to see what the new scheme was going to look like under Sean Mannion and how the passing game would function without A.J. Brown. It was also our first look at an offensive line that featured an injured-and-struggling Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson. We finally got to see if Hurts would spend more time under center, how that would affect the passing game and whether Saquon Barkley would be more productive in the new offense than he was a year ago. At the end of the day, the offense looked a whole lot like it did a season ago. And it was Jalen Hurts who saved them. There were entire quarters where the offense did nothing but go 3-and-out, but they also committed no turnovers. The short intermediate passing game over the middle was largely non existent, but there were several explosive plays and two TDs to Dallas Goedert up the seam. Saquon Barkley largely struggled again behind and offensive line that is nowhere near what it was in 2024, but broke off a long run and put up decent numbers otherwise. Baby steps, perhaps? Jalen Hurts, of course, remained the same, both in good ways and in bad. Hurts made the play of the game with his legs in the 4th quarter, converting a 3rd-and-18 with a 22-yard gain to help dig the Birds out of their offensive malaise. Jalen Hurts with a BIG gain of 22. 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/R0Fh8cdbXS — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 13, 2026 It was vintage playmaking by the still-fleet veteran, weaving his way through the defense to convert a first down when nothing was schemed open and his offensive line was leaking oil. And as in years past, it was Hurts’ deep balls and ability to play out of structure that generated most of the offensive output. There’s good news and bad news in that. The bad news is the Sean Mannion offense was supposed to create opportunities in the run and pass game for players. It’s only Week 1, and Mannion’s scheme deserves much more time to find its sea legs, but watching Dickerson and Jurgens struggle in both facets of the game was disheartening, to say the least. The run game looked a lot like it did last season and, as Tom Brady noted on the Fox telecast, there were times Hurts dropped his eyes and watched the pass rush when his first read was taken away. This is all going to take time. Patience is required, and hopefully it will all work out. In the meantime, Hurts spent much of Sunday improvising and relying on his previous strenghts — his legs and the bomb. The deep ball to DeVonta Smith along the sideline in the 3rd quarter was gorgeous, as was the toe-dragging catch by his new No. 1 receiver. Devonta Smith, First-Team All-Hands 🧤 pic.twitter.com/CJiasvVpay — TSN (@TSN_Sports) September 13, 2026 And his 64-yard deep bomb to Dontayvion Wicks in the 1st quarter was a thing of beauty. Jalen Hurts goes DEEP to Dontayvion Wicks for 64 yards! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/YWAd95NABQ — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 13, 2026 Like a season ago, the Eagles showed less play-to-play consistency, but more big splashes. It’s two different ways to score points and, on Sunday, it was enough against a Commanders team that, barring a few boneheaded mistakes, probably should have won. Defensively, Vic Fangio’s unit dominated for three quarters before the heat, humidity, and Daniels’ legs, wore them down. Zach Baun was incredible on Sunday, and the defensive line got persistent pressure on Daniels, if not sacks or turnovers. They made life uncomfortable for just about everyone. It was not Cooper DeJean’s best day, nor was it Jihaad Campbell’s. The safeties left gaps in the middle of the field. But it was enough. The big takeaway after Sunday’s 24-22 win was that it felt a whole lot like games the Eagles won last year. Never comfortable, ugly at times, finding a way to survive, overly reliant on Hurts to figure it out on his own. Happily, he did on Sunday. In Week 1, you take the win no matter how you get it, and hope things look a bit better as the schedule rolls along.
author: John Stolnis

title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts starts the season strong
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Hurts looking good was my biggest takeaway from the Eagles’ Week 1 win. The offense as a whole was … uneven … but QB1 made big plays to carry the team to victory. His run to pick up a first […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Hurts looking good was my biggest takeaway from the Eagles’ Week 1 win. The offense as a whole was … uneven … but QB1 made big plays to carry the team to victory. His run to pick up a first down on 3rd-and-18 was massive and he made some really nice precision throws (see: Dallas Goedert’s first touchdown, DeVonta Smith’s sideline catch). The offense has a lot to clean up and improve upon … but it’s always easier to feel good about your favorite team’s outlook when the QB is playing well. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Observations as Eagles hang on for Week 1 win over Commanders – NBCSP Considering the pocket was breaking down snap after snap, Hurts was terrific Sunday. On the Eagles’ third possession, he heaved a perfect 64-yard bomb down the right sideline to the 6-yard-line to newcomer Dontayvion Wicks and after Cam Jurgens’ second penalty of the quarter, threw a dart to Dallas Goedert in the end zone for a 17-yard touchdown. Two spectacular throws on his sixth and seventh passes ever in Sean Mannion’s offense. Encouraging start. Later in the second quarter a terrific nine-yard TD pass to Wicks, and with six minutes left in the fourth quarter he found Goedert open over the middle and lobbed him a short pass that the veteran tight end turned into a 43-yard touchdown, longest by an Eagles tight end since Brent Celek’s 65-yarder in the historic comeback win at the Meadowlands in 2010. Considering how little help he was getting up front, I thought Hurts was outstanding in his first game working with Mannion. He also had some terrific runs – a 14-yarder on a 1st-and-20 in the third quarter and a 22-yarder on a 3rd-and-18 on the 4th-quarter TD drive. When he ran it was out of desperation under duress not out of any kind of set play. Hurts finished 14-for-25 for 203 yards with the three TD passes and no interceptions and a 122.2 passer rating along with 48 rushing yards on five runs before a couple kneel downs. He overcame a lot. The Early Bird: Four verticals & Jalen Hurts’ old tricks helped get Eagles over the line in season-opener vs. Commanders – PHLY Eagles Jalen Hurts let out a chuckle and a smile while he contemplated what he would say, and perhaps more tellingly, what he wouldn’t. The Eagles quarterback was asked about his first touchdown pass of the new season and the fact that it looked eerily similar to the final play of the season before. Hurts found Dallas Goedert running up the seam on the same four vertical route concept that had become the lasting symbol for the group’s offensive struggles in 2025 and the limited menu some blamed the 28-year-old signal caller for during the offseason. So what was going through Hurts’ mind after he ripped the throw high enough and far enough into the back of the end zone for only Goedert to make the play and promptly turned toward the sideline, shrugging his shoulders in celebration? “It’s a great play. It’s a great play,” Hurts said with a chuckle. “Y’all will dig. Y’all will try to figure something out.” Eagles-Commanders Postgame: Goedert, Ojomo Lead Eagles To 1-0 Start, Brandon Graham Breaks It Down – PHLY Eagles Postgame Show Jalen Hurts’ first game under Sean Mannion is in the books, as the Eagles held tough against a feisty Commanders team thanks to Dallas Goedert’s two touchdowns, a big day for Tay Wicks and characteristic tough defense from Zack Baun, Nolan Smith and crew. Two-time Super Bowl champion and future Eagles Hall of Famer Brandon Graham joins the show, along with Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf, plus insight from Fran Duffy, Miles Johnston and EJ Smith, live from the LINC. NFL Week 1: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games – ESPN Did the Eagles’ new offense pass the test Week 1? There was a boom-or-bust element to it, but the explosive plays carried them to a passing grade and a win over Washington. From WR Dontayvion Wicks’ 64-yard reception (a career high) to QB Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on third-and-18 to TE Dallas Goedert’s 43-yard score moments later, there was plenty to be encouraged about from offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s debut. Some issues along the offensive front (left guard Landon Dickerson looked as if he was laboring) and long stretches of ineffectiveness brought back memories of 2025, but patience is required while Philly breaks in a new system. What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw three touchdowns, was timely with his runs and didn’t commit a turnover. The pass-and-catch between the signal-caller and new WR1 DeVonta Smith along the right sideline late in the third quarter was a thing of beauty. Hurts was at his best when attacking downfield, completing 6 of 9 such attempts for 176 yards. Hurts rushed for 46 yards and made some strong throws. His 22-yard scramble in the fourth quarter saved the game. He made sure nine different Eagles touched the ball. Hurts prides himself on finding ways to win—and it is what he did. Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Commanders game – PhillyVoice 10) The ‘Thank You’ Award 🙏: The schedule makers. If the Eagles had played a better team, maybe this would have been a loss? We’ll never know. The Eagles will get another soft opponent Week 2 to work out the kinks when they travel to Nashville to take on the Tennessee Titans, who lost decisively to the lowly Jets Week 1. Eagles Hold On For The Win – Iggles Blitz Neither team played well. The Eagles just made more winning plays and that proved to be the difference in the game. The Eagles have plenty of issues to work on. The OL was very up and down. Landon Dickerson really struggled. He allowed a sack, a TFL and was called for at least one penalty. Cam Jurgens drew a couple of flags. Jordan Mailata had one. They struggled to consistently block the WAS front on run plays. 2026 NFL season, Week 1: What We Learned from Sunday’s games – NFL.com Eagles use big plays to outlast Commanders. Much like the last several seasons, the Eagles offense wasn’t pretty, but it got the job done, eking out a two-point win over a division rival. Philly’s offense was an inconsistent mess for much of the day, with the offensive line struggling to pick up the new blocking scheme, allowing far too many free runners into the backfield. However, Nick Sirianni’s club used a trove of big plays that made the difference. Saquon Barkley had a 42-yard scamper that helped set up a second-quarter score. title: Eagles vs. Commanders: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: Let’s see this through midnight green glasses: The Eagles won. Jalen Hurts took snaps under center. He threw down the middle of the field. The Eagles just happened to be playing against two new coordinators and a Washington Commanders team that had to do more learning on the job than the Eagles did. The Eagles […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs after a catch against the Washington Commanders in the fourth quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s see this through midnight green glasses: The Eagles won. Jalen Hurts took snaps under center. He threw down the middle of the field. The Eagles just happened to be playing against two new coordinators and a Washington Commanders team that had to do more learning on the job than the Eagles did. The Eagles survived a 24-22 scare over Washington on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field to keep Eagles’ head coach Nick Sirianni a perfect 6-0 in season opening games and 35-14 overall. Under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, Hurts completed 14 of 25 for 203 yards and three touchdowns—two TDs down the middle of the field on third down. Hurts rushed for 46 yards and made some strong throws. His 22-yard scramble in the fourth quarter saved the game. He made sure nine different Eagles touched the ball. Hurts prides himself on finding ways to win—and it is what he did, going into “Jordan mode” to do it. Washington’s Jayden Daniels looked a lot like the player he was two years ago. He completed 18 of 34 for 164 yards and two touchdowns, and he made Cooper DeJean look foolish. Hurts answered the offseason criticism by winning this game. He cannot do it alone moving forward. There was a lot of good, some bad and a pile of ugly in the Eagles’ 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders. The Good Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo clamping down on Commanders’ back-up tight end John Bates , on a poorly called play, stopping the two-point conversion that would have tie the game with 1:01 to play. Hurts saving the day on a 22-yard scramble on a third-and-18 with 8:03 to play. If Hurts does not go off script and make the play, the season may have started with a highly unlikely loss. Three plays later, Hurts hit Dallas Goedert down the middle of the field for a 43-yard touchdown and a 24-16 Eagles’ lead with 6:06 to play. Tight end Dallas Goedert is still a viable option, catching a team-high four passes on five targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns—both on third down, and both down the middle of the field . The Eagles’ third quarter defense. They gave up only 48 yards and kept Daniels in check, completing three of seven for 22 yards. DeVonta Smith’s 31-yard reception on a third-and-five in the last two minutes of the third quarter. It kept alive the Eagles’ fourth drive of the second half, made possible by Smith tip-toeing the sideline on a perfect pass from Hurts to beat the Commanders’—and former Eagle—Rasul Douglas. It led to a Jake Elliott 35-yard field goal and a 17-9 Eagles’ lead with 44 seconds left in the third quarter. Smith later secured the win by securing the on-side kick. The Eagles’ second quarter. It turned over a dismal first quarter. It was a good glimpse of what this new revamped Eagles’ offense is supposed to look like under Mannion, scoring touchdowns on two of four drives, with eight different players getting touches in the first half. The Eagles churned up 102 yards of offense on 15 plays, averaging 6.8 yards a play, and converting two of four third downs. The big difference was 63 yards rushing on six carries, averaging 10.5 yards a carry—and the bulk of which came next. Saquon Barkley’s 42-yard second-quarter run, when Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen and Lane Johnson flushed the Commanders’ defensive line right , opening a massive hole for Barkley to take off down the middle. The long run set up the Eagles’ second touchdown, a nine-yard completion from Hurts to Dontayvion Wicks in the corner of the end zone for a 14-3 lead with 6:27 left in the first half. Hurts recognized the man coverage and Wicks’ cut to the corner. A.J. Who? Wicks had two catches for 73 yards and a touchdown, outperforming the player he replaced, A.J. Brown, who caught a grand total of three passes for 26 yards, before suffering a high ankle sprain in the fourth quarter of New England’s season-opening 13-10 loss to Seattle. Linebacker Zack Baun making a team-leading 12 tackles, seven solo, including several key plays, like taking down Rachaad White in the open field with an ankle tackle from behind for two yards on a third-and-six at the Washington 47 on the Commanders’ first second half drive. Baun looked like his 2024 All-Pro version, pretty all over the field breaking up passes, making open field tackles, and pressuring the quarter. He later tipped away a Daniels’ pass on a third-and-two at the Eagles’ 10 with 2:08 to play. Baun on the Commanders’ fifth drive , diving to defend a pass down the middle intended to Stefon Diggs on a first-and-20 play, and smashing through the center to come up with a seven-yard sack om Jayden Daniels with 10:15 left in the first half, forcing a third-and-27. Hurts’ 17-yard touchdown pass “down the middle of the field” to Goedert for the Eagles’ first touchdown of the season on a third-and-goal play with 14:11 left in the first half. The Commanders’ safeties sagged, Hurts saw the opening and hit Goedert in the back of the end zone for a 7-3 lead. Receiver Dontayvion Wicks making a career-best 64-yard reception on the Eagles’ third drive , Hurts dropped a perfect arc hitting Wicks on the run. It was the first big play of the season, setting up the Eagles’ score. It also tore away what had been a stagnant start for the Eagles, who had 12 total yards over their two drives. Wicks did not catch a pass in the second half in the second half. Hurts pass down the middle of the field to DeVonta Smith for 12 yards on a second-and-24 on the Eagles’ second drive. Things were so bad for the Eagles over the first quarter that punter Braden Mann was about the only thing positive going , booming his first two punts for a total of 110 yards, one inside the 20. He had a 64-yarder and hit a 62-yarder on his third punt. Two of his first three punts were inside the 20-yard line. He changed the tilt of the field. Mann punted the ball four times in the first half, putting three of the four inside the 20. The exclamation point was Mann’s 51-yard punt that was downed at the Commanders’ two with 33 seconds left in the half. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter’s blocked extra point with 1:53 left in the first half after Jacory Croskey-Merritt’s one-yard score to give Washington its first touchdown of the season. Defensive tackle Jordan Davis eating up the middle of the field, making eight tackles, three solo. Riq Woolen and Quinyon Mitchell locking down Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs for much of the game, causing Daniels to extend plays by rolling right and running for his life. Jihaad Campbell’s fourth-quarter one-yard sack, later erased one play later with a major blunder. The Bad The Eagles third quarter offense. The Eagles picked up a mere 59 yards of offense and one first down. They went three-and-out on their first three drives, and could not do anything until Smith’s 31-yard reception with two minutes left in the quarter. Left guard Landon Dickerson getting nailed for holding—the Eagles’ third holding call to that point— on a first-and-10 at the Eagles’ 40 on their fourth drive of the second half. Right tackle Lane Johnson getting beat inside by Commanders’ first-round draft pick middle linebacker Sonny Styles in taking down Barkley for a three-yard loss on a second-and-seven at the Eagles’ 44 on the Eagles’ third drive of the second half. Safety Andrew Mukuba losing the middle of the field on Daniels’ 15-yard completion to tight end Chig Okonkwo at the Eagles’ 43 on Washington’s second drive of the second half, on a second-and-12. The Eagles’ defense on the Commanders’ first drive. They allowed a third-down conversion, an 11-yard run to open the season and a 13-yard pass on a third-and-10. The Eagles special teams allowing Jaylin Lane’s 33-yard kickoff return to open the…

title: Eagles-Commanders final score: Philadelphia edges out Washington for Week 1 win
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 1-0 after narrowly beating the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday! Final score: 24 to 22. The Eagles needed to stop a two-point conversion late in the game to prevent the Commanders from potentially sending this to overtime. Vic Fangio’s defense, which was not perfect but did a lot […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the Washington Commanders prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 1-0 after narrowly beating the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday! Final score: 24 to 22. The Eagles needed to stop a two-point conversion late in the game to prevent the Commanders from potentially sending this to overtime. Vic Fangio’s defense, which was not perfect but did a lot of positive things today, came through when it counted most. Sean Mannion’s debut was … interesting. The Eagles’ offense was not exactly even. There were explosive plays, in large part led by Jalen Hurts looking good. The quarterback finished the game with the following numbers: 14/25, 203 passing yards (8.1 average), 3 TD, 0 INT, 122.2 passer rating. It felt like the Eagles’ quarterback carried the offense more than the offense functioned smoothly as a unit. That was in part because the offensive line wasn’t great; concerns with Landon Dickerson and Cam Jurgens linger. Next up for the Eagles: a road game against the 0-1 Tennessee Titans, who lost to the New York Jets. Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also check me out on the PHLY Eagles postgame show, live with Brandon Graham! FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer to put the Commanders up on offense first. Washington began at their own 36-yard line and immediately picked up a first down on the ground. Facing 3rd-and-10 on the next set of downs, Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs in a soft spot in the defense beyond the sticks with Cooper DeJean getting beat (and penalized but the flag was declined). The Commanders tried a flea flicker that resulted in a Daniels throwaway thanks to Moro Ojomo generating quick pressure up the middle. Facing 3rd-and-10 again, the Commanders went with … a coward’s draw. Is Nick Sirianni coaching Washington now? I kid. But nice of the Commanders to give up and settle for a 55-yard field goal make. EAGLES 0, COMMANDERS 3. The Eagles began at their own 35-yard line. A play-action under-center look from the jump resulted in Hurts throwing incomplete short to Saquon Barkley. An under-center Barkley run brought the Eagles to third down. Facing 3rd-and-5, Hurts stepped up against a blitz (nice pickup by Barkley) and ran for a first down. Makai Lemon logged his first career reception to bring up third down. Facing 3rd-and-8 from the shotgun, Hurts hit Dontayvion Wicks short of the sticks and old friend Rasul Douglas instantly knocked the ball out for an incompletion (hospital ball). Six plays, 13 yards, punt. Braden Mann pinned the Commanders back to their own 6-yard line with a nice coffin corner punt. Marcus Epps sniffed out a Washington run to fly into the backfield for a TFL. Facing 3rd-and-10 after a Diggs drop, Daniels overthrew a deep target while Riq Woolen had tight coverage anyway. Punt. The Eagles took over at their own 39-yard line. Cam Jurgens got called for holding. The Eagles went with a backwards pass screen to Makai Lemon, who got blown up with Wicks missing his block. Two targets for Lemon, zero for DeVonta Smith … OK, then! Hurts connected with DeVonta on the next play to set up third down. Facing 3rd-and-12, Landon Dickerson just watched Frankie Luvu go by him to sack Hurts. Yikes. The Commanders took over at their own 22-yard line after a 64-yard Mann punt. Facing 3rd-and-1, Jalen Carter and Zack Baun combined to stuff Rachaad White for no gain. Good stop to force another three-and-out. The Eagles took over at their own 24-yard line. A Barkley run to the outside picked up six yards (should’ve been more if Barkley didn’t run into DeVonta!) and then Hurts aired it out deep to Wicks for a 64-yard gain! Boom. Longest catch of Wicks’ career (previous high was just 36 yards!). The Eagles then had to take a timeout as the play clock was winding down to zero and Hurts didn’t look very happy, seemingly signaling that he wanted the play call in sooner. Jurgens got hit with another holding penalty to knock the offense back and then Barkley got tackled for a loss to continue to move the offense back in the wrong direction to end the first quarter. Tay Wicks made his first catch in Philly count! Seeshhhh pic.twitter.com/BoUVIullqB — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 13, 2026 SECOND QUARTER Facing 2nd-and-goal from the 18-yard line, the Eagles ran the ball. Too conservative! Facing 3rd-and-goal, Hurts found Dallas Goedert up the seam in the end zone for a touchdown! Great tight window throw by QB1. Good to see the aggression there! EAGLES 7, COMMANDERS 3. That first score feeling >>> pic.twitter.com/WpOA9mI0Ky — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 13, 2026 The Commanders took over at their own 32-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-9 after Riq Woolen almost came away with an interception, the Eagles’ pass rush forced Daniels to scramble for an incompletion. Pretty strong start by Vic Fangio’s defense. The Eagles took over at their own 27-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-6 after Hurts got lit up while throwing incomplete to Lemon (Barkley picked up the wrong defender in pass pro), Hurts threw incomplete to Wicks. Rasul Douglas was pretty grabby on that play … but no flag was thrown. The Commanders took over at their own 16-yard line after a 62-yard punt by Mann (he’s really booting it). Also, credit to my guy Darius Cooper, who logged his third special teams tackle of the day. A blitzing Cooper DeJean drew an offensive holding penalty to knock Washington back. Zack Baun broke up a Daniels pass over the middle. Then Baun blew up a screen play. He’s a beast. Facing 3rd-and-27, the Commanders went coward’s draw to bring up a punt. The Commanders have run 14 plays for 13 yards since their opening drive. Eagles defense dominating. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 13, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 38-yard line. The Eagles went with another backwards pass (not a fan of these, so risky!) that brought up a short third down. Facing 3rd-and-2, Barkley ripped off a 42-yard run through the Commanders’ defense. Two plays later, Hurts threw a fadeaway with pressure bearing down on him to Wicks (who cooked Mike Sainristil again) in the end zone for another touchdown! Hurts looking good. Wicks trade looking good. The broadcast showing Sean Mannion pumped up in the booth. You love to see it. EAGLES 14, COMMANDERS 3. Saquon on the loose 💨 pic.twitter.com/qW1yUWmaPq — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 13, 2026 Tay Wicks made his first catch in Philly count! Seeshhhh pic.twitter.com/BoUVIullqB — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 13, 2026 Wicks broke his ankles with a filthy route pic.twitter.com/zsyTCIISYW — Patrick (@PhillyPMC) September 13, 2026 The Commanders took over at their own 33-yard line and drove just shy of midfield. Facing 3rd-and-15, Daniels took off running out of bounds a little short of the marker. Facing 4th-and-2, the Commanders moved the chains on the ground. Facing 3rd-and-1 in the high red zone, the Commanders went with another run for a first down conversion. Daniels hit Antonio Williams just shy of the end zone to set up goal-to-go. The Commanders punched it into the end zone with a short Jacory Croskey-Merritt run. Jalen Carter blocked the extra point to at least salvage that much. 12 plays, 67 yards, TD. EAGLES 14, COMMANDERS 9. The Eagles took over at their own 29-yard line with 1:48 on the clock and two timeouts on the clock. Last year, Nick Sirianni was insanely conservative in this kind of situation. Facing 3rd-and-2 after the Eagles picked up one first down, Hurts’ third down pass was knocked down at the line of scrimmage. Facing 4th-and-2 from the minus 47, Sirianni opted to punt. I would’ve liked a go for it there but I don’t think it was egregious to punt. Mann’s…

title: EAGLES BACKUP QUARTERBACK REVEALED
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced the inactives list for their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The following Eagles players WILL NOT PLAY: Tanner McKee, Jonathan Greenard, Elijah Moore, Micah Morris, and Cole Payton. Well, the Eagles have FINALLY revealed their plan at QB2. With McKee inactive (but designated as the emergency third quarterback, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Andy Dalton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to pass against the New England Patriots during an NFL preseason football game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced the inactives list for their Week 1 game against the Washington Commanders. The following Eagles players WILL NOT PLAY: Tanner McKee, Jonathan Greenard , Elijah Moore, Micah Morris, and Cole Payton. Well, the Eagles have FINALLY revealed their plan at QB2. With McKee inactive (but designated as the emergency third quarterback, so he can come in if the two QBs ahead of him get hurt), Andy Dalton is Jalen Hurts’ primary backup. Neither Dalton nor McKee did much to inspire confidence this summer … but at least McKee has shown some promise in the past while Dalton, who turns 39 years old next month, might be physically diminished. The Eagles are really going to hope that Hurts stays healthy. Greenard was ruled out on Friday’s injury report . The veteran edge rusher returned to practice this week after missing all of training camp due to a pectoral strain … but he was only able to participate in a limited basis. We’ll see if Greenard is able to get back in Week 2. For now, the Eagles will roll with Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, A.J. Epenesa, and Arnold Ebiketie on the edge. Moore is a healthy scratch after making the Eagles’ roster as a bubble player. A little curious that they kept him on the roster (as opposed to putting him on the practice squad) only to have him not suit up. But he doesn’t have a special teams background and the Eagles are dressing six receivers on Sunday: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, and Britain Covey. No surprise that Morris is inactive. The rookie is probably going to be a healthy scratch all year, barring multiple OL injuries. The Eagles did notably keep nine offensive lineman active for this game: the five starters and then the four backups of Fred Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, and Willie Lampkin. It remains to be seen how the Eagles will handle an injury at tackle. Kendall is likely the top backup interior option. Could Lampkin be involved in a specialized role as a blocking tight end? Payton is the Eagles’ fourth-string quarterback, so, not surprising that he’s inactive. Unless McKee, he is totally ineligible to play in this game. The aforementioned Covey is active after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad . He’ll likely be the Eagles’ punt returner. Eli Stowers isn’t listed with the inactives because the Eagles put him on injured reserve . Philadelphia Eagles inactive list QB Tanner McKee* – Emergency third quarterback. EDGE Jonathan Greenard – Injury. WR Elijah Moore – Seventh wide receiver. OL Micah Morris – Tenth offensive lineman. QB Cole Payton – Fourth quarterback. summary: The 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 1 games. Go […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Jordan Davis #90 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL season is here! Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 1 games. EAGLES GAME WASHINGTON COMMANDERS at PHILADELPHIA EAGLES: We won’t see the Eagles in action until 4:25 PM Eastern on Sunday. But a win over the Washington Commanders will be well worth the wait. Go Birds. NFC EAST DALLAS COWBOYS at NEW YORK GIANTS: The Cowboys are obviously the bigger threat to the Eagles at this point in time. Root for the Giants. NFC PLAYOFF PICTURE NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at SEATTLE SEAHAWKS: This year’s NFL Kickoff Game is a rematch of Super Bowl LX. While I imagine there will be Philly fans rooting against A.J. Brown, the Pats winning here is preferable with the Seahawks being a threat to the Eagles getting a top seed in the same conference. Root for the Patriots. SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS at LOS ANGELES RAMS: This Thursday matchup between two NFC West rivals in Australia should be interesting. The Rams have the shortest odds to win the Super Bowl this season, so, they stand out as the bigger threat. Even though the Eagles have had an easier team beating LA than San Fran. Root for the 49ers. CHICAGO BEARS at CAROLINA PANTHERS: The Panthers aren’t scaring anybody. The Bears have a higher ceiling. Root for the Panthers . TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS at CINCINNATI BENGALS: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Bengals. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at DETROIT LIONS: The Lions have serious bounce-back potential this season. Best for them to lose here before they pick up a lot of wins from the league’s easiest schedule. Root for the Saints. ATLANTA FALCONS at PITTSBURGH STEELERS: AFC team over NFC team. Also, the Eagles play the Steelers later this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Steelers to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Steelers. ARIZONA CARDINALS at LOS ANGELES CHARGERS: The lowly Cardinals (with their projected win total at 3.5 games) do not pose a threat to the Eagles in the NFC. The Eagles play the Cardinals this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Cardinals to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Cardinals. GREEN BAY PACKERS at MINNESOTA VIKINGS: There’s a case to be made the Packers are the bigger threat, though these teams might be more evenly matched. Green Bay has the more favorable Super Bowl odds and I think the Eagles would rather see Kyler Murray in the playoffs than Jordan Love. Root for the Vikings. WHAT’S LEFT BUFFALO BILLS at HOUSTON TEXANS: The Eagles play the Texans this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Texans to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Texans. BALTIMORE RAVENS at INDIANAPOLIS COLTS: The Eagles play the Colts this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Colts to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Colts. CLEVELAND BROWNS at JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS: The Eagles play the Jags this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Jags to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Jaguars. NEW YORK JETS at TENNESSEE TITANS: The Eagles play the Titans this season. With the hope that the Eagles will beat them, you want the Titans to have as good of a record as possible to help boost Philly’s strength of victory tiebreaker. Root for the Titans. MIAMI DOLPHINS at LAS VEGAS RAIDERS: No Eagles impact but could be fun to cheer on Nakobe Dean. DENVER BRONCOS at KANSAS CITY CHIEFS: No Eagles impact but could be good to see the Chiefs fail to build momentum early in the season.
