title: The morning after: Aaron Rodgers needs more from his receivers
summary: Aaron Rodgers’ Week 1 box score does not do him justice in the slightest. The 42 year-old quarterback was slinging the pill all over the yard in the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 20-13 win to kickoff the season, but it was a victory that could have been much more convincing had Rodgers gotten help on some high-quality […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers throws a pass against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ Week 1 box score does not do him justice in the slightest. The 42 year-old quarterback was slinging the pill all over the yard in the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 20-13 win to kickoff the season, but it was a victory that could have been much more convincing had Rodgers gotten help on some high-quality throws from his receivers. Rodgers finished the day 24-of-40 for 221 yards and a touchdown. However, at least one other score was left off the board, and multiple big gains slipped through the hands of DK Metcalf. The potential touchdown came when Rodgers launched a deep ball to Roman Wilson. Contact was made, but the third-year receiver fought through it, jumped in the air, and had the ball in his hands. When he came do the ground, the ball popped out, erasing what would have been a 44-yard score. Metcalf had an especially forgetful day. On 10 targets, he totaled just four receptions for 40 yards. One was called back due to his second offensive pass interference of the day, erasing a 19-yard gain. Metcalf was also unable to drag his feet on a well-thrown Rodgers ball down the sideline that would have gone for 21, and he dropped Rodgers’ best throw of the day between two Falcons that would have gained 20. In totality, those plays kept 104 yards and a touchdown off the board for Rodgers and the Steelers. Had those been caught, we’d be talking about a 28-of-40, 325 yard performance from the four-time MVP and a strong 27-point outing to begin his farewell season. Rodgers himself didn’t seem too bothered, though, as he noted explosive plays were there to be had. “I think we did a lot of good things,” Rodgers told Pam Oliver after the game. “We had a chance to be really, really explosive. We had a couple drops, couple off-targets, couple non-calls that looked like penalties. So that changes the stats. We had a 40-yard PI that could have been a touchdown. We had a couple other ones that could have been big plays… it’s good to be out of here 1-0, though.” The future Hall of Famer also made sure to praise his teammates, Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt, for their outstanding performances. “T.J. played unbelievable,” Rodgers said. “He’s been on a different level this entire camp. I’m so proud of him [and] I love the way he leads. And Cam is the epitome of a Pittsburgh Steeler. To be able to share this team with them, to be able to share the leadership opportunity is really, really special in my last year and I’m just so thankful to just be back out here and play the game I love with guys I really respect and love as well.” Rodgers and the Steelers will clearly be launching the ball more in 2026, which is a refreshing development. As is the group Rodgers calls “The old guys” continuing to halt time in its tracks. It’s the morning after game day, and we have much more to dive into. Welcome back, T.J. Watt We, and everyone else in the Steelers media space, have talked extensively about Watt’s performance, but with good reason. After two down seasons, the latter of which saw the three-time sack leader notch just seven takedowns of the quarterback after getting a massive pay day, many assumed we had seen the best of Watt. But maybe we had just seen the best of Watt in a Mike Tomlin-Teryl Austin defense. The usage of the edge rushers has been a hot topic for years now. The lack of innovation and movement along the defensive line made Pittsburgh’s approach predictable. Plus, as Watt aged, his snap count stayed largely the same, naturally making him less explosive as games, and the season as a whole, went on. On Sunday, Watt played 38 snaps – the fewest of Pittsburgh’s top three edge rushers. Mike McCarthy and Patrick Graham realize the fresher Watt stays through the game, the greater the chance for explosive plays. I’d say two sacks, three tackles for loss, and his first career pick-six is all the evidence we need that this scheme change, as well as a lower snap count, will reinvigorate the former Defensive Player of the Year and see him look more like the superstar we grew used to seeing week in and week out. New Steelers defenders show up big A pair of new Steelers defensive backs left their mark in their first action wearing Steelers colors. Pittsburgh native Jaquan Brisker picked off Cooper Rush to set up an Aaron Rodgers touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and finished the day with six tackles. Jamel Dean also had a nice outing, finishing with five tackles and a forced fumble on Bijan Robinson that killed a Falcons drive and forced a punt. Dean allowed just 31 yards through the air when targeted, and Brisker picked off the only pass that came his direction. The Steelers allowed just four receptions to receivers all afternoon with only one of those receptions going for more than 20 yards. Yes, it came against Cooper Rush, but that’s how it is supposed to look when you face a bad quarterback. The secondary did its job and then some, even without Joey Porter Jr. Quick-hitters Michael Pittman had a quiet, but strong debut, catching all three passes thrown his way for 58 yards. Talked about it yesterday, but Cam Heyward is ridiculous. Three pass deflections at the line of scrimmage. He is just seven shy of the NFL record for defensive linemen. Max Iheanachor should start Week 2. Dylan Cook was bad, and the run game suffered in large part because of it. Was good to see Pat Freiermuth start off on the right foot. He was vocal at the end of last season about the frustrations he had in seeing his snap count go way down. He handled it like a good teammate does, and is now back to being a top-notch pass-catching tight end. Don’t let Alex Highsmith get lost in the shuffle. Due to Watt and Heyward’s big performances, you’d be forgiven if you forgot Highsmith had two sacks, as well. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons
summary: The Steelers have opened the Mike McCarthy era 1-0 following a one-score win over the Atlanta Falcons to start the season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. T.J. Watt looks back T.J. Watt’s performance on Sunday, with two sacks, an additional tackle for loss, four total tackles and a pick […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers have opened the Mike McCarthy era 1-0 following a one-score win over the Atlanta Falcons to start the season. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. T.J. Watt looks back T.J. Watt’s performance on Sunday, with two sacks, an additional tackle for loss, four total tackles and a pick six had me checking the clock to see if it was 2021. After an offseason full of worries about the veteran edge defender’s age and expensive contract (which was justified given his output in 2025), Watt seemed to turn back into his old self in Week 1. It was needed, too. The Steelers won by just a touchdown as a rusty Pittsburgh offense struggled to outscore the Cooper Rush-led Falcons. The defensive score proved to be key in the win. HIM 📲 Stream on NFL+: https://t.co/vqIDzYZB2x pic.twitter.com/3kIvcymaVc — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) September 13, 2026 One key stat to note is that Pittsburgh’s top three edge rushers — Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig — all played right around 40 defensive snaps each on Sunday per PFF’s charting , with Jack Sawyer recorded another 23. Keeping Watt fresh has been just as important an aspect of keeping his game impactful through his 30s as the more-talked about points such as moving him around the formation or changing up his pass-rushing arsenal. The Steelers made sure to spell Watt more on Sunday with the team’s other three competent edge rushers, and sure enough, the production followed. In a way we didn’t really see in 2025, Watt returned to game-wrecker form. Watt wasn’t the only aging defender on the Steelers to dominate against Atlanta. The 37-year-old Cam Heyward recorded two total tackles, some key pressures and a whopping three — yes, three — passes batted at the line of scrimmage. Heyward was also given more time to rest on Sunday, playing just 33 of the team’s 61 total defensive snaps Sunday after being the most played defensive lineman in the NFL last year. Cam Heyward still gets PBUs at elite corner rates pic.twitter.com/DWz3br6ogQ — Chris Ferland 🐝 (@chris_ferland) September 13, 2026 The 31-year-old Jalen Ramsey recorded a pass defensed himself, adding four more tackles as he rotated between slot corner in nickel and safety in base defense. For a team often criticized for being overreliant on a veteran defense — again, not saying it’s never justified — those aging stars sure delivered to open the season. 2. Offense is sloppy, but has pieces The Pittsburgh defense largely held up its end of the bargain against the banged-up Falcons, with Atlanta’s lone touchdown drive coming after a Jaylen Warren fumble on Pittsburgh’s own 27-yard-line. The Steelers offense, however, was the reason why this game was so close. The offensive line gave up just two sacks, with quarterback Aaron Rodgers looking more comfortable extending plays than usual against an Atlanta front down its top two edge rushers. Still, efficiency was an issue, with Rodgers completing just 24 of his 40 attempts. Plenty of the blame for the incompletions can fall on Rodgers’ receiving corps, especially wide receiver DK Metcalf, who recorded at least one clean drop and couldn’t hang onto a few other passes you’d expect a $33 million wide receiver to catch. Details…This is not much different a target than Michael Pittman’s grab but DK Metcalf’s details aren’t there. Underhand clap attack… pic.twitter.com/kx8DbLzlm6 — Matt Waldman (@MattWaldman) September 13, 2026 The good news, at least, is that Metcalf was clearly getting the best of a talented Falcons secondary, but just couldn’t always complete the catch. He’s always been an inconsistent receiver, but Sunday marked an especially low point. He should bounce back. The new big-name addition to the Steelers’ wide receiver room, Michael Pittman Jr., was targeted less but made the largest impact with a team-best 58 receiving yards on three grabs. Of a group of pass catchers that often seemed discombobulated or on a different page from Rodgers, Pittman’s savvy was immediately noticeable. Despite being known as a possession receiver primarily at this point in his career, his chemistry with Rodgers led to some of the team’s biggest gains through the air against the Falcons. The value of a veteran WR in the offense: Watch Michael Pittman (11) work to open space vs ATL’s zone as Aaron Rodgers extends this play out of the pocket. Having a smart receiver who can see coverage fluidly will be a big help for Rodgers. pic.twitter.com/byQSUZwjhv — Kevin Smith (@KTSmithFootball) September 13, 2026 Roman Wilson and Pat Freiermuth also had days worth noting. The former seems to have a firm hold on the WR3 role at the moment, and probably could’ve done more to solidify his status by holding onto a catchable contested pass right before halftime. Still, he was more involved in the offense than usual in his Steelers career thus far, and had some flashes Sunday. There’s definitely a good wide receiver to be found in Roman Wilson, but it remains to be seen if the Steelers will be able to unlock that this year. As for Freiermuth, he led the team with five catches and recorded the offense’s lone score. Freiemuth is due for a return to form of sorts as his production has plateaued in recent seasons, and Sunday was a good start. Fellow tight end Darnell Washington only logged two grabs but did manage to record a highlight-worthy stiff arm on one of them. DarnellWashingtonKilledAnotherManWithAStiffArm.GIF Paging @KyleBrandt pic.twitter.com/tdeSq92rmP https://t.co/lpH3gRuhKy — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) September 13, 2026 It’ll be interesting to see how the team involves Washington — who was recently signed to an extension — more in the offense in 2026. His impact wasn’t always felt in a run game that took until the end of the game to get going, with Warren making up for his earlier fumble by finishing the day with a solid 4.6 yards per carry (Dowdle finished with just 1.9). As the offensive line continues to improve — and if Aaron Rodgers can continue to look like he did on Sunday — there is still plenty to be excited about regarding this Steelers offense despite a disappointing opener. 3. Steelers survive Joey Porter Jr.’s absence The caveat here, of course, is that the Steelers’ passing defense looked good against a banged-up Cooper Rush as the opposing quarterback. Still, the Pittsburgh secondary looked solid despite being down its top corner in Joey Porter Jr., and a starting safety in DeShon Elliott. Free agent addition Jamel Dean looked good and even forced a fumble when playing near the line of scrimmage. And starting in lieu of Porter, Asante Samuel Jr. was strong in coverage and had few mistakes outside of an unnecessary roughness penalty for a body slam out of bounds. Honestly, it was good to see the Steelers’ secondary playing so physically even if open-field tackling was sketchy overall (and it’s worth noting most of those misses came against all-world running back Bijan Robinson in space). This is a defensive backfield willing to lay down a big hit. And it held up well in coverage, limiting Drake London to two catches for 29 yards and shutting Kyle Pitts out of the box score altogether. If and when Porter and Elliott return, the group could look even better. Brisker with the hit stick! #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/UI0bqc2S20 — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) September 13, 2026 When Pittsburgh faces more threatening quarterbacks down the road — starting next week with Drake Maye — maybe this narrative will change. The Steelers defense had plenty of hype last year but disappointed early in the season, and there was some worry the same could happen this year with how many questions there were at safety and…

title: Steelers stock report after Week 1 win over Falcons
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers escaped with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons to begin the Mike McCarthy era. After many of the Steelers’ starters sat out in the preseason, Pittsburgh looked noticeably rusty early in the contest, before settling in doing enough to get to 1-0. Let’s take a look at this week’s stock report […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates during the second quarter of a game against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers escaped with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons to begin the Mike McCarthy era. After many of the Steelers’ starters sat out in the preseason, Pittsburgh looked noticeably rusty early in the contest, before settling in doing enough to get to 1-0. Let’s take a look at this week’s stock report after the season opener. Stock Up EDGE TJ Watt After recording his lowest sack total since his rookie season in the 2025 season, the Steelers’ highest-paid player is off to a scorching start in 2026. Watt recorded three tackles for a loss, two sacks, and an interception that was returned for a touchdown. Watt jumped up and perfectly timed a Cooper Rush pass for the interception. Watt stumbled to the ground and still had enough time to gather himself and return it to the end zone. This is not the first time we have seen Watt do something like this, but it remains one of the single most impressive plays that a defender can make. The edge rusher looked noticeably more explosive compared to the end of last season after suffering a collapsed lung. It seems like Watt has found new life in the Patrick Graham defense where he isn’t asked to play every defensive snap in a rotation with Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig. TE Pat Freiermuth Freiermuth was back to being the leader in the tight end room after 2025 saw a big step back in terms of his usage. The sixth-year tight end outsnapped newly extended Darnell Washington, while posting five catches for 46 yards and a touchdown. After showing more willingness to take shots up the seam throughout training camp and preseason, we saw those reps pay off in Week 1. After recording the second lowest receiving total of his career in 2025, Freiermuth seems to have new life in the Mike McCarthy offense. DT Cam Heyward It defies all logic that Heyward is as good as he is at 37-years old. The veteran defensive tackle looks to be as good as ever after his dominant Week 1 showing. Heyward swatted three passed down at the line in the contest. The defensive stalwart is looking like he is set for another phenomenal season in the new-look defense. Stock Down WR DK Metcalf This was a terrible showing from Metcalf. The Steelers receiver was called for a pair of offensive pass interferences in this contest. Matcalf was targeted 10 times in the game, but finished with just four catches for 40 yards. The most deflating part of this performance, though, were the crucial drops. Rodgers and Metcalf seemed to be just a tick off timing wise form each other all game, resulting in a few downfield passes bouncing off the hands of Metcalf. In the third quarter, Rodgers hit Metcalf over the middle right in the hands and the receiver was not able to bring it in. The play resulted in a resounding boo from the crowd. If the Steelers offense is going to take a step up in 2026, Metcalf is going to need to step up. RB Rico Dowdle Many expected it to be a pretty even split between Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle entering the season. It was not a huge difference in terms of touches between the two, but Warren did get five more touches than Dowdle in Week 1. This is most likely because of Dowdle’s efficiency issues in the contest. The running back averaged just 1.5 yards per carry compared to his counterparts 4.6 yards per carry. Warren was the more explosive and efficient back. If Dowdle’s struggles continue, we could see more Warren going forward. Let us know what you think in the comments . OH MY T.J. WATT WITH THE PICK-6 🚨 ATLvsPIT on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9OYHvUeNTN — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 And with that interception, Watt has joined a highly exclusive NFL club. The 100 sack/10 interception club is an obscure stat, but it shows off defenders who primarily play at the line of scrimmage still finding ways to make an impact when the ball is in the air. Watt has long had a knack for intercepting passes most defenders would simply bat down. And that skill turned out to be a key aspect of a tight win to open the regular season.

title: T.J. Watt turns back clock in Steelers win over Falcons
summary: They say you can’t teach an old dog new tricks. But what happens when that old dog and his old tricks begin working again? Ask the Pittsburgh Steelers, as T.J. Watt took us back in time with a vintage performance to help lift Pittsburgh over Atlanta en route to a 20-13 WIN. In the first […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: T.J. Watt #90 and Alex Highsmith #56 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrate during the first quarter of a game against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images They say you can’t teach an old dog new tricks. But what happens when that old dog and his old tricks begin working again? Ask the Pittsburgh Steelers, as T.J. Watt took us back in time with a vintage performance to help lift Pittsburgh over Atlanta en route to a 20-13 WIN. In the first game of the year, Watt accounted for two sacks, three tackles for loss, and the play of the 1:00 window. With the Steelers leading 13-10 midway through the fourth quarter, Watt jumped a screen pass intended for Bijan Robinson and snagged it out of the air. After falling to the ground, he got up and was escorted to the end zone by Jaquan Brisker, Keeanu Benton, and Payton Wilson for his first career pick-six. And if that wasn’t enough for you, Watt is the first player with two sacks and an interception in two different season openers. Watt was far from the only defender to have a big day. Alex Highsmith finished the afternoon with a pair of sacks and Cam Heyward batted down three passes at the line of scrimmage. Jaquan Brisker made a splash in his Steelers’ debut, picking off a Cooper Rush pass to set up the Steelers’ only offensive touchdown of the day. Payton Wilson led the team with an astounding 13 tackles, two of which were for loss. Unfortunately for the Steelers, their offense wasn’t as successful. Atlanta was able to dominate the Steelers’ run offense, limiting Pittsburgh to just 58 yards on 21 carries. And while Aaron Rodgers threw the ball 40 times, he averaged just 5.5 yards per attempt. It was a particularly brutal day for DK Metcalf. The Steelers’ top wideout was called for offensive pass interference twice, one of which canceled a third-down conversion. He also dropped a perfect throw from Rodgers over the middle on another third down that prevented a potential conversion, and couldn’t get his feet in bounds on a 4th-and-3. The Steelers’ only offensive touchdown came after the aforementioned Brisker interception, where Rodgers extended the play and found Pat Freiermuth in the back of the end zone to put the Steelers up 13-7. Overall, Pittsburgh went just 3-of-13 on third downs and averaged just 4.1 yards per play. Doing so against a Falcons team who was missing its top two edge rushers is a concern. If there is a silver lining, it’s that Rodgers was dealing when it came to deep balls, he was just let down by dropped passes. Metcalf’s follies were a big stain on potential yards left out of the box score, as was a potential long touchdown that was dropped by Roman Wilson in the end zone. The accuracy and arm talent is certainly still there with Rodgers, his receivers just need to come through with receptions. Week 1 is rarely beautiful, and the Steelers will take a 1-0 start with them on the road next week to face the defending AFC champion New England Patriots, who are looking to avoid an 0-2 start. For this week only, both teams enter the matchup at 0-0; it’s a clean slate and a time to set the tone for the 2026 season. The game will be broadcast nationally […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 8: T.J. title: An All-22 review of Jadarian Price’s encouraging Seahawks debut vs. Patriots
summary: I’ve missed writing this weekly column. As a Seattle Seahawks fan and someone who loves the draft, one of the things I look forward to most is getting to study how Seattle’s rookies perform once the games actually count. Unfortunately — or perhaps fortunately, and I’ll explain why later — there isn’t much tape to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks hands the ball off to Jadarian Price #8 against the New England Patriots during the first quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve missed writing this weekly column. As a Seattle Seahawks fan and someone who loves the draft, one of the things I look forward to most is getting to study how Seattle’s rookies perform once the games actually count. Unfortunately — or perhaps fortunately, and I’ll explain why later — there isn’t much tape to work with from this season opener. We had just 24 snaps from the rookie class to analyze. So, let’s take a look at some of the key plays from the game. All data used in this article was taken from PFF . Jadarian Price, Running Back — 24 snaps Price carried the ball 10 times for 52 yards, good for a 5.2-yard average. Overall, he showed good vision, played with a strong attitude and displayed more explosiveness and straight-line speed than I expected coming into the season. At this point, it looks like the praise he received throughout Hard Knocks was legitimate. Price correctly reads LB #14 coming downhill on this Duo run and bounces outside. The issue: two cuts cost him some explosiveness. With more reps, this should become one decisive cut. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:08:14.660Z This might be the snap that gives Price the clearest indication of what he still needs to improve, although there is nothing alarming here. Seattle appears to be running a Duo concept , a gap-scheme run that uses vertical double teams at the line of scrimmage while allowing the running back to read the second level and choose his path based on the linebackers’ movement. Price reads linebacker No. 14 coming downhill toward the line of scrimmage rather than flowing laterally, so he correctly decides to bounce the run outside. The biggest area for improvement is what happens next. You can see Price make two separate cuts, and on the second one he loses a little of his speed and explosiveness. Again, this is not some glaring mistake, especially in a rookie’s first NFL game. With more experience, Price should become quicker with this read and get to the outside with one decisive cut rather than having to make two adjustments. I believe this was Price’s only pass-blocking snap. Probably smart by Seattle: he’s willing, but still inconsistent in protection. He has the tools, but this is an area where experience—and Holani—can help. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:09:14.375Z I may have missed one, but I believe this was Price’s only pass-blocking snap of the game. That’s probably a smart decision by Seattle. It’s not that Price is incapable of blocking, or unwilling to do it, but he is clearly inexperienced in pass protection and has shown both good and very poor reps in that area. He did catch two passes for six yards, but pass protection is something he’ll need to develop gradually. In the meantime, George Holani can continue to provide some of that experience in the backfield. Nothing flashy, but the little things matter. The OL creates little room, yet Price stays with the read, keeps his track and lowers his pads to squeeze out the yards.Watch Anthony Bradford’s block on No. 24—it creates just enough room to finish the run. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:10:18.050Z Nothing particularly flashy here, but the simple things are often underrated. The offensive line doesn’t create much separation, yet Price trusts the design, stays with his first read and, even with very little room to work with, lowers his pads and gets what he can. Also, keep an eye on Anthony Bradford’s block on No. 24. It helps create just enough room for Price to finish the run. Price’s discipline stands out on this outside-zone run. A gap opens between Abe Lucas and Anthony Bradford, but he doesn’t get baited inside. He stays on track, turns the corner and then hits another gear once he gets north. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:11:23.473Z One thing that stood out throughout Price’s tape is how disciplined he appears to be. He doesn’t seem overly eager to abandon the play design in search of something that isn’t there. Seattle runs another outside-zone concept here. At one point, a gap appears between Abe Lucas and Anthony Bradford, but notice where Price’s eyes are. He doesn’t get sucked inside by the opening. Instead, he stays committed to working toward the edge. Once he turns the corner and gets going north, the explosiveness shows up again. Discipline doesn’t mean lacking creativity. On this outside-zone run, Price stays on his track until he sees a better lane inside, then cuts decisively and gets north. He finishes through contact instead of dancing around defenders. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:12:10.133Z Being disciplined doesn’t mean lacking creativity. Seattle runs another outside zone here, and this time the concept works particularly well. Price sticks with the initial track until he recognizes a better opportunity. Once he sees the lane inside, he makes the cut, turns upfield and takes on the defenders rather than trying to dance around contact. He eventually gets tackled, but there is plenty to like about the way he finishes the run and fights through contact. This might be Price’s most impressive speed rep. Another outside zone, but watch how quickly he gets downhill before No. 24 can close. He slips the tackle, gets north and hits another gear.And somehow JSN avoided a block-in-the-back flag here. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T02:13:58.706Z This was one of the snaps that surprised me most in terms of Price’s speed. It’s another outside-zone run, and pay attention to how quickly Price gets moving before No. 24 can get to him. He manages to escape the tackle attempt and once again gets himself going north. The officiating crew had already made several questionable decisions throughout the game, so perhaps they were trying to avoid adding another controversial call by not flagging JSN for a block in the back here. Either way, once Price gets through it, you can see what his athleticism can bring to this offense. He appears to hit another gear once he gets north, and that acceleration is something worth watching as his role develops. Bud Clark, Defensive Back — 0 snaps Clark was one of the rookies I had the most confidence in coming into the season, so seeing him land on injured reserve was particularly disappointing . There simply isn’t any defensive tape to evaluate yet, but his absence is significant when you consider the injuries Seattle has already dealt with in the secondary. Julian Neal, Cornerback — 0 defensive snaps With Seattle’s secondary dealing with multiple injuries, Neal could have had an opportunity to work his way into the defensive rotation. Unfortunately, his injury during training camp significantly slowed his development. He saw only special-teams snaps in the opener, so there isn’t much to evaluate from a defensive standpoint yet. Beau Stephens, Guard — 0 snaps Stephens was inactive for the opener. He showed some development during the final preseason game, but the fact that he was inactive suggests he still has some ground to make up on Seattle’s offensive line. At least for now, the coaching staff appears to have others names. That’s notable considering Christian Haynes, the player Stephens was competing with in the preseason, had previously lost his starting opportunity to Sataoa Laumea — who is no longer even in the NFL. For Stephens, the first step is simply getting active on game day. Avery Smith, Cornerback — 0 defensive snaps Because Smith is a rookie, even though he was not drafted or originally signed by Seattle, he’ll be included in this weekly rookie tracker. Like Neal, Smith did not see any defensive snaps despite the injuries in Seattle’s secondary. His work came…

title: NFL Week 2 odds: Seahawks open as heavy road favorites vs. Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are comfortable favorites against their division rival Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. After opening the 2026 season with a 13-10 comeback victory over the New England Patriots, the Seahawks will hit the road for their first away game of the season when they visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 20. According to […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are comfortable favorites against their division rival Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. After opening the 2026 season with a 13-10 comeback victory over the New England Patriots , the Seahawks will hit the road for their first away game of the season when they visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sept. 20. According to the current lines at FanDuel Sportsbook , Seattle is a 5.5-point favorite (-110) . The Seahawks’ moneyline is -235 , while Arizona sits at +194 . The game total is currently set at 41.5 points . That makes Seattle a relatively significant road favorite, but the betting line comes with an important wrinkle: Drew Lock is expected to start at quarterback against Arizona with Sam Darnold sidelined by his injury. Darnold suffered the glute injury on Seattle’s opening drive against New England and did not return. Lock took over and ultimately helped the Seahawks complete the comeback, finishing the game 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown. The latest reports indicate that Darnold is expected to miss the Cardinals game, putting Lock in line for his first start of the 2026 season. That makes the -5.5 spread particularly interesting. Seattle is being asked to cover more than a field goal on the road despite making a quarterback change just one game into the season. Arizona won’t be an easy opponent, either. The Cardinals opened their season with a 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , giving them a victory on the road before returning home to Seattle. The Seahawks, meanwhile, are coming off a defensive performance in which they intercepted Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to help overturn their only 10-0 deficit and get the opening night victory. That combination helps explain why the total is relatively low at 41.5 points . FanDuel’s current market projects a game in which Seattle is favored to win, but not necessarily one expected to turn into a shootout. And, honestly, what else should we expect from a game in Glendale? There’s nothing particularly normal about playing the Cardinals in the desert, where these matchups have a habit of turning chaotic and unpredictable. Seattle should be prepared for another one of those games.

title: PFT’s Mike Florio: Seahawks’ Sam Darnold could miss 4-6 weeks
summary: While the rest of the NFL finishes off Week 1, the Seattle Seahawks have spent their weekend working through just how long they’ll be without their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold. There was apparent clarity on the injury early Sunday, with ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reporting that Darnold went down with a glute injury in the Seahawks’ […]
full_text: While the rest of the NFL finishes off Week 1, the Seattle Seahawks have spent their weekend working through just how long they’ll be without their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold. There was apparent clarity on the injury early Sunday , with ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reporting that Darnold went down with a glute injury in the Seahawks’ opener against the New England Patriots. Later on Sunday, P ro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reported that Darnold could miss up to four to six weeks with the injury, though he won’t need surgery. Florio added the Seahawks will be cautious with their starting quarterback, indicating the Seahawks feel comfortable competing with backup Drew Lock under center. It’s worth noting that the report from PFT paints a grimmer picture than what Rapoport described earlier in the day. Rapoport said it’s a for-sure thing that the Seahawks will be without Darnold for Week 2, against the Arizona Cardinals. However, Rapoport left the door open for Darnold to return as early as Week 3, describing the injury as a “we’ll see” moment. The Seahawks might be able to fend off the 1-0 Cardinals and 0-1 Washington Commanders without Darnold. But Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers starts a difficult stretch for the team that features the NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers in Week 5 and the Patrick Mahomes-led Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7. With or without Darnold, Seattle will head to Glendale for a divisional showdown with the Cardinals next Sunday at 1:25 p.m. PDT.

(Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks may be the reigning Super Bowl champions, but they entered the 2026 season as not even favorites to win the NFC West. Of course, that honor belonged to the Los Angeles Rams, whose trade for Myles Garrett put them over the top as preseason Super Bowl favorites. Well, the Rams got blown out on opening day against the San Francisco 49ers, Myles Garrett put up no stats and no pressures in his Rams debut, and he will accumulate no stats for the Rams for at least the next month. Garrett had indicated that he wasn’t feeling right with his knee, and it turns out he’s going to have arthroscopic surgery that will put him on injured reserve. Rams star Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic surgery on his ailing knee and is headed to injured reserve, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Garrett has been dealing with lower-leg pain and wasn’t himself in Thursday’s opener. The hope is he’s back in four weeks. pic.twitter.com/naTKJDV06R — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 13, 2026 Garrett will be out for games against the New York Giants, at Denver Broncos, at Philadelphia Eagles, and Buffalo Bills. Not exactly an easy stretch of opponents, let alone opposition offenses. This is the first time Garrett has missed at least four games in a season since 2019, and that was because of a suspension he served for the brawl with the Pittsburgh Steelers and his helmet-swing on quarterback Mason Rudolph. Not since his rookie season (2017) has he missed four games or more due to injury. So the Rams are supposed to get Aaron Donald on the field eventually, but any thought of him and Garrett together will need to wait a little while longer. It could certainly have a major impact on the Rams’ super season, as well as whether or not the Seahawks have a chance to gain some early separation against their great rivals.

title: Understanding Terrion Arnold’s contract with the Seahawks
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have set out on the defense of their Super Bowl title, upending the New England Patriots in a 13-10 come from behind victory to start out the 2026 season victorious. Up next for Mike Macdonald and crew is a Week 2 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals as the Hawks look for their […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 30: Detroit Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold (0) watches on the video scoreboard a replay of him being called for pass interference during the fourth quarter of an NFL Monday Night Football regular season football game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Detroit Lions on September 30, 2024 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have set out on the defense of their Super Bowl title, upending the New England Patriots in a 13-10 come from behind victory to start out the 2026 season victorious. Up next for Mike Macdonald and crew is a Week 2 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals as the Hawks look for their first road win of the year. Of course, when the Seahawks and Cardinals face off, one of the more recognizable names added to the Seattle roster during the offseason, Terrion Arnold, will not be in action as he remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List pending the outcome of the legal case in which he faces a total of eight felony charges. While Arnold will not be on the field for the ‘Hawks until the situation is resolved, player’s placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List earn their full salary, and we now know how much Arnold is being paid by the Seahawks this season and that amount is: $1,075,000 (base salary) And that’s it, just league minimum base salary for a player with two credited seasons. No incentives, no bonuses, no signing bonus and no guaranteed money at all. Of course, the big question mark when it comes to Arnold is his availability because it’s entirely possible he might not be able to play this season, but that may be less of a concern than the simple fact of having Arnold under contract. That is the case for a number of reasons, but what it boils down to is that even though he was a 2024 first round pick who has already played two seasons in the NFL, Arnold is still just 23 years old. Realistically, that means he likely have several years of good football in front of him prior to reaching his prime, and even though his contract is for league minimum, unless they opt to release him, the Seahawks own his rights going forward. In addition, the calculation for accrued seasons as laid out in Article 8, Section 1 of the CBA is as follows, with the relevant portion bolded for emphasis: Section 1. Accrued Seasons Calculation: (a) For the purposes of calculating Accrued Seasons under this Agreement, a player shall receive one Accrued Season for each season during which he was on, or should have been on, full pay status for a total of six or more regular season games (which shall include any games encompassed in any injury settlement, injury grievance settlement or injury grievance award), but which, irrespective of the player’s pay status, shall not include games for which the player was on: (i) the Exempt Commissioner Permission List , (ii) the Reserve PUP List as a result of a nonfootball injury, or (iii) a Club’s Practice Squad. What this means specifically is that as long as Arnold remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, he gets paid but does not earn accrued seasons towards being a free agent. That means that even if his legal situation drags on until the offseason and he never sets foot on the field for the Hawks this year, he would be an exclusive rights free agent in the offseason, and that would allow the Seahawks to bring him back on a league minimum salary for $1,120,000 in 2027. Alternatively, if Arnold is cleared and comes off the Commissioner’s Exempt List and plays enough this season to earn an accrued season, it would render him a restricted free agent in the offseason. That would afford John Schneider and Mike Macdonald the option to retain his services for 2027 on a restricted free agent tender, and means that even though the contract Arnold signed is a one year deal, it is effectively a two-year deal, with the second year being at the amount of the RFA tender.

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 2: Fred Warner #54, Jason Pinnock #25, Deommodore Lenoir #2 and Upton Stout #20 of the San Francisco 49ers make a tackle during the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 2, 2025 in Inglewood, California. The 49ers defeated the Rams 26-23. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you outclass your opponent in the way that the San Francisco 49ers did to the Los Angeles Rams, it’s difficult to come up with multiple “losers.” The Niners won by 20, but it felt like the margin was greater. Brock Purdy’s QBR was 50 points higher than the other starter. The running game averaged 1.6 yards per carry more than the Rams. The vaunted defense we heard about all offseason was wearing the wrong jersey. Sprinkle in a couple of special teams plays, and it was a butt-kicking, through and through. Here are the winners and losers from Week 1. Winners The offensive line Sumer Sports tracks impact plays for offensive linemen, and the Niners had three players in the top 45 in Week 1: (6th) Connor Colby – 5 (13th) Jake Brendel – 4 (36th) Trent Williams – 3 Impact plays are defined as “highlight plays where a player demonstrates exceptional execution relative to their role and alignment.” During Colby’s five, he displaced the defender he was blocking by multiple yards. Four linemen — Brendel, Williams, Dominick Puni, and Colton McKivitz — allowed one pressure each on 36 pass-blocking snaps. Colby allowed two pressures. As a unit, they combined for four total blown blocks — two against the run and two against the pass. The 49ers led all teams in rushing success rate at 56.7%, five percentage points better than second place. Brock Purdy faced the second-lowest pressure rate, while the running backs benefited from the fourth-most yards before contact of the week and only 7.1% of their carries resulting in a stuff —good for the third-best mark of Week 1. According to Sports Info Solutions, all five starters earned multiple points in Week 1, with Colby and Puni leading the way with 3 points earned. For reference, Colby earned six total points in 425 snaps as a rookie. There’s no denying the scheme, like a heavy dose of screens or different motions, played a significant role in the play of the line, but that shouldn’t take away from how effective they were Raheem Morris Against an offense everyone projects to be tops in the league, Morris allowed the 3rd-lowest EPA per play and passing success rate. Despite losing his starting defensive tackle the week of the game, Morris devised a scheme that held one of the most dangerous rushing attacks to the sixth-worst EPA per rush mark of the week. Morris gave Sean McVay a swirlie and stuffed Matthew Stafford in a locker. The Rams don’t go four quarters without reaching double digits. Stafford usually has a few touchdowns a game and is somewhere around 275 yards. Puka Nacua has made a habit of terrorizing NFC West opponents. Outside of a long Nacua reception, the Rams rode the struggle bus for much of the game. Morris designed blitzes that got home, mixed in coverages that led to turnovers, and was two steps ahead of McVay all game. Osa Odighizuwa Odighizuwa managed four pressures in 18 pass-rush snaps. He’s precisely the kind of pesky interior pass rusher the Niners have been craving for years. That 22.2% pressure rate is good for the fifth-best among all defensive tackles in Week 1. Unlike some pressures, there was no fluke or fluff here. Odighizuwa hit the quarterback on four separate occasions, which made up for half the number of times the Niners defense as a whole hit Stafford. He is just what the doctor ordered for Morris. Fred Warner Only five players had more run stops than Warner in Week 1. Every one of those players played at least five more snaps than Fred, with some playing as many as 24 more snaps. Warner had multiple plays where he defended Nacua 1-on-1. He broke up a pass on one of those plays. Warner and his 11 tackles all came at timely moments. The Rams had an opportunity to make it a game again in the third quarter, but Warner and Jaden Dugger halted their plans in the backfield on a goal-to-go situation. The most telling Warner stat was how seldom Stafford threw it over the middle. You can’t quantify this in Warner’s favor, but it’s a sign of respect from a veteran quarterback who knows better than to test a future Hall of Famer: Warner takes away the part of the field where today’s offenses want to target the most. Nick Bosa We’ll do our best to leave Warner and Bosa off these lists throughout the year, as they’re expected to perform great. But it’s been nearly a full year since we’ve seen Bosa. The assumption was that he’d take some time get his feet underneath him. Well, not this guy. Bosa hit Stafford on the first play from scrimmage. It was the quickest pressure of the defense, checking in at two seconds flat. He tied Colby for a team-high five impact plays. Three of those came in the first quarter. It’s refreshing to be reminded that your edge defenders can be run stoppers. Bosa had a tackle for loss early and added another in the third quarter. He joined Warner with another stop two plays later. Best of all, Bosa humiliated a tight end whenever the Rams blocked him with one. Mike Evans Evans caught six of his seven targets for 49 yards. When he was targeted is why he’s on the list. Over half of his targets came on late downs. Evans added at least a point in EPA on three different routes. It would have been four, had he not dropped his final target. Evans was 3-for-3 against man coverage and was also perfect out of the slot. Brock Purdy, knowing he has Evans as a fallback option on third downs, is quite the luxury to have. Evans caught five of his six targets on third down, and both red zone targets. Upton Stout One of the few bright spots on defense toward the end of the season last year was Stout. He was third on the team in impact plays with four. Stout’s IQ was on full display. He had a quarterback hit, a run stop where he recognized what was coming before the ball was snapped, and only allowed three yards in coverage on three targets. Raheem Morris manipulates the protection to get exactly what he wants. The top DCs will always attack the back. He uses Bosa's gravity to his advantage here. Warner walks up to occupy the center. The line slanting basically makes it a 1-on-1 drill for Stout vs. the RB. No chance pic.twitter.com/DMbTeV63xJ — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) September 11, 2026 Stout picked up where he left off last season. Honorable mentions: We could list another 10 players if we wanted to, but Keion White, Jack Jones, Renardo Green, and Deebo Samuel were all close to making the list.
author: Kyle Posey

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers in first place after Week 1; the Rams are not
summary: Welcome to the weekly NFC West recap. For those of you new to the program, we’ll do a rundown of how the San Francisco 49ers are faring against their other NFC West rivals and any news from those games that might be noteworthy. And we begin things with who is in the lead. First, all […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the weekly NFC West recap. For those of you new to the program, we’ll do a rundown of how the San Francisco 49ers are faring against their other NFC West rivals and any news from those games that might be noteworthy. And we begin things with who is in the lead. First, all the NFC West teams won this weekend—except the Los Angeles Rams. Of those three, the 49ers are in first place after Week 1. Divisional games are considered a “game and a half” in terms of value, and since that was the only NFC West game this weekend, the 49ers start out on top. Don’t get too excited; it is Week 1 after all. Last year the 49ers beat the Seahawks in Seattle, and then the season happened. Regardless, starting the season with not just a win, but a divisional win can only help in January tiebreakers. Everyone else? Whatever. San Francisco 49ers (1-0)/Los Angeles Rams (0-1) Oh, you know what time it is. It’s time to RAM IT . I don’t know about you, but I really, really enjoyed that 27-7 thumping the 49ers handed the Rams on Thursday. Obviously, just because it’s the Rams, it’s already enjoyable, but seeing the 49ers look so crisp and efficient while the Rams look the opposite (especially after all the offseason hype) brings a lot of optimism about what the 49ers could do. Just stay healthy. Please, 49ers? Speaking of health, the 49ers got nailed by the injury bug twice. Tight end Jake Tonges went down with what was later said to be MCL-related and “not good.” A bit less severe was wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, who went down with what is speculated to be a grade 2 deltoid sprain . This is the first time I learned the ankle has a “deltoid,” but leave it to the 49ers to teach me about every ligament in the human body you can sprain or tear. Stribling is expected to be out for at least a month, and surgery is on the table. Given that this is his rookie season and the 49ers are already dealing with the absence of Ricky Pearsall, we can all hope Stribling gets healthy sooner rather than later. Things could have been worse; when you see a player carted off the field (which happened to Stribling), it usually indicates something devastating. Making any declarations from Week 1 is a terrible idea, and I’m sure the 49ers might have some challenges in Week 2, even against the Miami Dolphins, but if they can stay healthy, I don’t see why someone can’t see them as a threat to the NFC (not just the West). As for the Rams, again, it’s Week 1. When they play the 49ers in Week 14, they will have Aaron Donald (and whether he’s still got it or not is left to be determined), and Myles Garrett will probably be a much different player than the one who laid a goose egg on the stat sheet Thursday. That is, of course, if the Rams have Garrett back by then. It came out Sunday that the defensive lineman will undergo knee surgery and head to injured reserve. The minimum is four games, but there’s no timeline on when Garrett will be back on the roster. Not good, especially when the Rams have some tough games coming up. Outside of the defense, some might think Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford might be on the “decline” after one game. Just because they brought in the backup to protect Stafford from getting blasted in garbage time doesn’t mean anything. We’ve also seen Stafford play bad games before, so Week 1 in Australia doesn’t indicate anything. Should Stafford be a bit less efficient this year, the Rams have plenty of talent on offense around him to prevent that side of the ball from taking a nosedive. Seattle Seahawks (1-0) The defending Super Bowl champs began their season against the New England Patriots. The first points weren’t scored until six minutes into the second quarter. And things imploded in the fourth quarter, when Drake Maye threw three straight interceptions that led to points and a 13-10 win for the Seahawks. It wasn’t all roses for the Seahawks, however. Quarterback Sam Darnold left with an injury to his hip five plays into the game, leaving Drew Lock to fill in. Darnold is expected to miss some time. It’s not a fracture, so at the moment it’s not thought to be season-ending, but he will miss some time. Lock went 16-of-22, 187 yards for one touchdown. Simply having zero interceptions means he was far more efficient than Maye. The Seahawks don’t have a favorable schedule the next few weeks, with the Arizona Cardinals, Washington Commanders, and Los Angeles Chargers coming up, so if Darnold is going to be resting up, Seahawks fans will be hoping Lock doesn’t tip things over. Arizona Cardinals (1-0) Sure, the 49ers win over the Rams was a surprise, but there was no bigger surprise than the Cardinals beating the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers were favored by 9.5 points. Or were the Cardinals favored? I really don’t know because the final score was 26-14, Cardinals. Looks like those points wouldn’t be needed. The game was relatively close until the fourth quarter. That was when stuff like this happened: Cardinals block the punt and will take over near the goal line! AZvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AKdFclsKgP — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 The Cardinals have Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, but the Chargers have Justin Herbert. And for a team like the Cardinals, you’d think Herbert would do better than going 17 for 27 and handing the game away with a costly interception. Then again, Herbert’s offensive line was not helping him at all as the Cardinals’ pass rush was in the backfield on the regular. The stat sheet says Herbert was sacked three times, but it sure felt like a lot more. The win puts the Cardinals into a tiebreaker with Seattle—one we aren’t going to break down in Week 1. Are the Cardinals better than we thought? Again, it’s Week 1. We’ll see how they do next week in their first NFC West matchup. Onto Week 2 If the 49ers are going to deal with any jet lag in their return from Australia, it at least will be against the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium. The Dolphins didn’t have a great Sunday, losing to the Las Vegas Raiders 27-13. That’s the start of what many think will be a bad season. The Seahawks and Cardinals will be giving us our second NFC West matchup of the season. I want to say the Seahawks won’t have trouble with this, but after Sunday’s upset—and Seattle’s issues with their quarterback—who knows. The game is in Arizona, so take what you will from that. The Rams will host the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. While we shouldn’t hold our breath, a Giants victory here would open the floodgates for chaos next Tuesday with the Rams, an anointed “super team” in the offseason, starting 0-2. The Giants didn’t have many issues against the Dallas Cowboys, but the Rams are a massive difficulty spike over the Cowboys. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next vs. Miami Dolphins TIE – 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: at Arizona Cardinals TIE-2nd: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Seattle Seahawks 4th: Los Angeles Rams; Next: vs. New York Giants (Monday Night Football)
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 49ers open up as nearly 2-touchdown favorites against the Dolphins
summary: The San Francisco 49ers were underdogs in Week 1. After the beatdown they put on the Rams, it might be months until they’re not favored to win. According to the Week 2 odds on FanDuel Sportsbook, the Niners are favored to beat the Miami Dolphins by 13.5 points, with the total on the game listed […]
full_text: (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers were underdogs in Week 1. After the beatdown they put on the Rams, it might be months until they’re not favored to win. According to the Week 2 odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , the Niners are favored to beat the Miami Dolphins by 13.5 points, with the total on the game listed at 45.5. Generally, large spreads with low totals are a sportsbook’s way of telling you a blowout is coming. The 49ers allowed one touchdown against the Rams. The Dolphins’ lone touchdown against the Raiders came when they were gifted the ball at midfield to begin the third quarter after a Kirk Cousins interception. Cousins threw two interceptions, and the Raiders went 5-for-13 on third down, yet they still scored 27 points, scored a touchdown on three of their four red zone trips, and lived in Dolphins territory. Ashton Jeanty had a field day. He went over 100 yards, while rookie Mike Washington averaged nearly six yards per carry on seven attempts. That’s impressive when you factor in Cousins only completed one pass beyond 10 yards. Going from the Rams to the Dolphins is the definition of stepping down in class. One team was the Super Bowl favorite heading into 2026. The other was penciled in for a top-three pick. A big reason is its inexperience and lack of offensive threats. Malik Willis had a QBR of 29.4, thanks to taking five sacks. He was also Miami’s leading rusher, with 39 yards. The Dolphins receiver with the most targets was Malik Washington, a 6th-rounder from the ’24 NFL Draft. Rookie Caleb Douglas was the second-leading receiver in targets. He’s a unique challenge at 6’4″. But this will be the second game of his professional career. It’s the home opener, so the 49ers shouldn’t be lethargic. A letdown after a win over a divisional rival is always a worry, but it’s Week 2. That should not be an issue for San Francisco. This is a spot where they need to handle business and get out of this contest healthy.

summary: The San Francisco 49ers played well on Thursday in their 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams. So good, the Rams’ recently acquired defensive lineman, Myles Garrett, didn’t show up on the stat sheet. Well, we may have an answer as to why: reports say Garrett will undergo arthroscopic knee surgery and be placed on injured reserve. The minimum […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers played well on Thursday in their 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams. So good, the Rams’ recently acquired defensive lineman, Myles Garrett, didn’t show up on the stat sheet. Well, we may have an answer as to why: reports say Garrett will undergo arthroscopic knee surgery and be placed on injured reserve. The minimum amount of time for a player to be on IR is four games, so Garrett will be out at least that long. This didn’t begin during the game; Garrett was reportedly dealing with lower-leg and knee issues during Rams training camp, and those probably carried into the regular season. Something was obviously up during the game. The broadcast often cut to the sideline to show Garrett standing and watching the defense on the field, which, given the Rams’ predicament, would be strange. Normally we wouldn’t be talking about Rams players and their injuries, but it’s Myles Garrett, and the 49ers just got done playing their rivals. The Rams acquired Garrett in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in the 2026 offseason in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round pick. That’s a lot of draft capital for a player going to IR after one game, and 49ers fans know this all too well. The Rams also brought Aaron Donald out of retirement. The thought was that Donald and Garrett together on the field would make an unstoppable pass rush. At this point, we’ve seen a limited sample size of Garrett, and Donald hasn’t suited up yet. The 49ers don’t see the Rams again until Week 14. The Rams host the New York Giants for Week 2, and a Garrett injury may level the playing field.

title: 49ers’ rookie De’Zhaun Stribling to miss ‘at least a month’ with deltoid sprain in ankle
summary: When San Francisco 49ers rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling suffered an injury in Week 1 against the Rams, it seemed like we were headed for the dreaded worst-case scenario, as it was a non-contact injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that Stribling’s Achilles was still intact, which was great news. After Stribling needed further testing, […]
full_text: (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images When San Francisco 49ers rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling suffered an injury in Week 1 against the Rams, it seemed like we were headed for the dreaded worst-case scenario, as it was a non-contact injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that Stribling’s Achilles was still intact, which was great news. After Stribling needed further testing , Ian Rapoport tweeted that he is out at least a month with a deltoid sprain in his ankle. According to Rapoport, Stribling is still seeking additional opinions. There is no current plan for surgery, but it’s not ruled out. San Francisco will be cautious with Stribling. Here’s more information about the deltoid ligament from a clinic : The deltoid or medial ligament is an important part of your ankle’s structure. It connects and holds together several bones in your foot and ankle. This ligament helps prevent you from over-rotating your foot or rolling your ankle inward. It acts as a counterbalance to the lateral ligaments on the outside of your ankle. It’s known as an uncommon type of sprain: Deltoid ligament sprains are an uncommon type of ankle sprain. A strain or tear of the deltoid ligament results from rolling your ankle inward (pronation). The medial ligament is stronger than the lateral ligaments. This strength makes it less likely to strain or tear. Deltoid or medial ligament sprains account for only about 15% of ankle sprains. Most injuries to the deltoid ligament result from a direct impact to your ankle. An ankle fracture (broken bone) on the outside of your ankle is the most common cause of a deltoid ligament sprain. Like any injury, the time missed depends on whether it’s a Grade 1, 2, or 3. A Grade 1 is a mild sprain that’ll sideline athletes for 1 to 3 weeks. A Grade 2 generally results in a walking boot or brace for a few weeks, and you cannot begin running until 6 to 8 weeks. If there’s a complete rupture, that’s when surgery is needed because there is associated bone damage, and you’ll be out for three months or longer. That’s considered a Grade 3 . The 49ers are probably bracing for a Grade 2 injury. Stribling played the most snaps of any wide receiver on the roster before he left early with his injury. He was and still will be a big part of the 49ers’ offense. Hopefully, Stribling can return soon enough and make an impact for the Niners as a rookie. Here are a couple of doctors from Twitter: Re: De’Zhaun Stribling for #49ers fans. Isolated deltoid ligament injuries are quite rare. Most injuries occur when there is an ankle fracture. Many of these injuries can respond to rehab (even grade 3 injuries). As pain and swelling go down, the ankle can be introduced to… — Dr. Nirav Pandya, M.D. (@DrNiravPandya) September 13, 2026 De’Zhaun Stribling Sounds like close to a Grade 3 deltoid ligament sprain. Recovery from surgery could be 5-6 months so at this stage it makes sense to rehab first to see if it improves. Plenty of time to get surgery later & be ready by May/June 2027 worst case scenario. He’ll… https://t.co/7fBBxg2VFy pic.twitter.com/mBNULrgB5D — Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT (@jmthrivept) September 13, 2026

title: Brock Purdy makes history after Rams win
summary: We’ve been talking about both the suffocating defense and Brock Purdy’s effectiveness in the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Rams. Here, we’re going to do a bit more on the former, because there’s a nice Brock Purdy stat to bring up here, if you don’t mind. With his 25-for-34 passing […]
full_text: Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’ve been talking about both the suffocating defense and Brock Purdy’s effectiveness in the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Rams. Here, we’re going to do a bit more on the former, because there’s a nice Brock Purdy stat to bring up here, if you don’t mind. With his 25-for-34 passing (73 percent completions), Brock Purdy now has the highest completion percentage of any NFL quarterback in their first 50 starts. In his 50 starts, he has 68.1 percent completions, putting him at first . I managed to dig up a chart of who he’s in front of: Brock Purdy now has the highest Completion % of any QB in their first 50 games. Truly unheard of from a 7th round pick. pic.twitter.com/pogi3S3NS2 — Cam (@42Cyc) September 11, 2026 I agree with this guy; that’s unheard of from a 7th-round pick. Now, one-tenth of a percentage point isn’t that much of a lead, but the guy he’s over, Joe Burrow, should say something about the company he’s keeping. Is this really record-breaking history? Well, when you see who else is on it- namely Jimmy Garoppolo and Tua Tagovailoa it’s not exactly a list of Hall of Famers. Having the likes of Kurt Warner is. It’s probably also fair to note that while Purdy is one-tenth of a percentage point ahead of Burrow, his yards and touchdowns are less, but his interceptions are slightly more. This isn’t so much a knock on Purdy; it’s more that when you see Tagovailoa and Garoppolo on the same list, you know this is a characteristic of the Kyle Shanahan offense. There are a lot of short passes, and we all know how good Jimmy Garoppolo was on a certain kind of throw. In fact, that’s proven even more when you see how few yards Garoppolo has compared to everyone else. Regardless, completion percentage is completion percentage, and in his first 50 games, Brock Purdy has shown he is one of the most accurate quarterbacks in the league. He also did this in 50 games when he was sometimes without his all-star cast of pass-catchers. In the Rams win, Purdy threw a single interception, a throw into quadruple coverage to tight end George Kittle. A throw Kittle appreciated nevertheless: George Kittle was asked what he saw from Brock Purdy: “Besides the one pass that he threw into quadruple coverage to me, which I appreciate, Brock, keep throwing those, besides that, he was on all day.” 💀 Great interview 🔥 pic.twitter.com/xfehcT3NcV — Coach Yac 🗣 (@Coach_Yac) September 12, 2026 Purdy also has this dime to Demarcus Robinson, which turns out to be his longest completion by air yards of his career. #49ers Brock Purdy's longest completion by AIR YARDS of his career was an absolute missile 🚀 pic.twitter.com/UNXl02Dvjz — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) September 11, 2026 All of this is more evidence that Brock Purdy is that good. With or without loaded talent around them, being that accurate isn’t very common. Add all the other stats he’s leading, and one has to wonder why people keep moving the goalposts.

title: Buccaneers Week 1 Top Performers at Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The Buccaneers came into 2026 looking to distance themselves from their disaster 2025 campaign…and proceeded to showcase many of the same issues that plagued them last year. Baker Mayfield playing recklessly, the defense allowing way too many freebies, and general communication issues plagued the Bucs from start to finish as they floundered to a 33-27 […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 13: Josiah Trotter #45 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs with the ball against the Cincinnati Bengals during the second half of the game at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buccaneers came into 2026 looking to distance themselves from their disaster 2025 campaign…and proceeded to showcase many of the same issues that plagued them last year. Baker Mayfield playing recklessly, the defense allowing way too many freebies, and general communication issues plagued the Bucs from start to finish as they floundered to a 33-27 defeat in Cincinnati. Four turnovers (all fumbles, three from Mayfield) led to 24 of Cincinnati’s 33 points. There were some bright spots across the roster, but there needs to be massive amounts of cleanup when the Bucs stage their home-opener next week against the Cleveland Browns. Offensive Top Performer: RB Bucky Irving The biggest sigh of relief on the offensive side might’ve been how good Bucky Irving looked — minus an early lost fumble. After suffering through serious knee and shoulder injuries last season, Irving looked explosive and decisive in new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson’s new wide zone-based scheme. Irving commanded the snap load, out-touching newcomer Kenny Gainwell 15 to 6. Irving rushed 8 times for 45 yards and a touchdown and added 7 catches for 48 yards. If he can remain the dangerous dual-threat weapon he established himself as in 2024, the entire offensive process should stabilize. Bucky Irving runs in for 6️⃣ TBvsCIN on FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/h0gNZUlkjZ — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 When Mayfield was functioning properly in the dropback passing game, Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka both created some moments. Godwin looked like he wanted to hunt defensive backs, leaning into contact and even administering a vicious stiff arm at one point en route to 4 catches for 40 yards. Egbuka broke a few chunk receptions, snagging 5 catches for 63 yards. Overall, Robinson called a good game that got sabotaged by turnovers. The process needs tweaking but yards and scores were there to be had. DAMN: THIS STIFF ARM BY CHRIS GODWIN WAS LETHAL. A text book stiff arm 💀 pic.twitter.com/B41SeNGXaE — MLFootball (@MLFootball) September 13, 2026 Defensive Top Performer: LB Josiah Trotter The temptation to give a Week 1 “nobody” here was strong through nearly 3 quarters, but luckily a positive development brewed in the form rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. Trotter, who’s only 21, went through some characteristic debut ups and downs in the first half, exasperated by his running mate Alex Anzalone’s inability to do literally anything at a competent level. The second half told a much different tale, as Trotter looked more confident and trusting of his instincts, which paid off in a big way in the form of a sack (Tampa’s only one of the game) and a 38-yard pick-six. The list of NFL players who have gotten a sack and a pick-six in their debut: Josiah Trotter. Per FOX research, Bucs rookie LB Josiah Trotter is the first player in NFL history with a pick-six and a sack in his NFL debut. — Greg Auman (@gregauman) September 13, 2026 It’s only Week 1, but the Bucs, who were already very high on Trotter, will be feeling good about him after Sunday. There’s not much else to comment on here. The defense still hemorrhaged yards in the middle of the field, it still suffered from miscommunications, and there were still issues with missed tackles. Basically nothing changed, and that is extremely concerning. If they make whatever schmuck the Browns trot out next week look competent, the seat is going to be red hot for Todd Bowles early. JOSIAH TROTTER WITH THE PICK-6 🔥 THE ROOKIE IS HAVING A DAY TBvsCIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/v71cdd3uyp — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Special Teams Top Performer: K Chase McLaughlin Chase McLaughlin needs his extension, as he remains one of the league’s elite kickers. He nailed both his field goal attempts to keep the Bucs somewhat in it, one being from 51 yards out. On an overall note, the coverage and return units looked solid. After how awful last season was, that will be a welcome relief. The Bucs allowed a long kick return of just 26 yards. That said, both teams punted a grand total of once, so we didn’t see the punt side of things get put to work.

title: Week 1 Game Recap: Buccaneers look… Like the Bucs, lose in turnover-laden slop
summary: With a new season comes new hope. The optimism of a new year on the horizon. A chance to place a new feather the cap. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, a freshly minted star quarterback Baker Mayfield, highly touted first round pick Rueben Bain Jr. How would the Buccaneers bounce back from flagrantly disappointing 2025? […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - SEPTEMBER 13: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) fumbles the football during the game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With a new season comes new hope. The optimism of a new year on the horizon. A chance to place a new feather the cap. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, a freshly minted star quarterback Baker Mayfield, highly touted first round pick Rueben Bain Jr. How would the Buccaneers bounce back from flagrantly disappointing 2025? Presenting the 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. First Quarter: The Buccaneers kicked off their season, by receiving the ball. Tampa’s opening drive was a well executed mix of run and pass featuring mainly Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving. The Bucs took the opening lead of the game 3-0 and then they were hit by a self-inflicted turnover avalanche. The Bucs actually forced a three-and-out on Cincinnati’s opening drive, however, that only led to a horrendous Baker Mayfield fumble on Tampa’s next drive. Trying to extend a play, Mayfield’s ball security was nonexistent as he was stripped from the backside for a Demetrius Knight Jr. scoop and score. 7-3, Bengals and some foreshadowing underway. Awfully timed fumbles came in like oceanside waves as Bucky Irving capped off Tampa’s next drive with one of his own. Two first quarter giveaways, two Cincinnati touchdowns, and 3-0 quickly became 14-3. Second Quarter: At the start of quarter number two, the Bucs’ offense looked like they were still playing in the first. Yet another positive drive all the way inside of the Bengals’ 10-yard line— Yet another Baker Mayfield fumble, the second potentially more unforgivable than the first. If ever there were ever a time for the Baker Mayfield detractors to scream their loudest this would be the day megaphones were in their Amazon order history. The quarterback’s second turnover was a setup for a clean cruise down the field, effortless in nature. 21-3, Bengals. With just over five minutes remaining in the half, Chris Godwin tallied his second hook to the jaw of a Cincinnati defender with stiff arms Derrick Henry would be proud of. Tampa Bay, in a game they were arguably dominating while simultaneously losing, finally struck gold as Bucky Irving crossed into the end zone and gave Tampa their first touchdown of the season 21-10, Bengals. Unfortunately, for Tampa Bay fans the good feeling was short-lived. In a classic ‘too much time on the clock’ situation Joe Burrow took the near two minutes left on the clock, walked back onto the field and dog-walked Todd Bowles’ defense for another three points. Third Quarter: Cincinnati began the third quarter with the ball and heaping pile of momentum. Leading 24-10, Joe Burrow’s Bengals found Tee Higgins for a lengthy catch-and-run which, even though the drive stalled out shortly after, did set the group up for three more points. 27-10, Cincinnati. Zac Robinsons’ offense matched Cincinnati’s— three for three with a long Chase McLaughlin field goal. 27-13, Bengals. It was Josiah Trotter’s pass rush, via a third-down sack, on Cincy’s previous drive that halted the drive and forced a kick. It would be his pass coverage that daggered Cincinnati’s next. In the shotgun, (A consistently discussed talking point in Sunday’s broadcast) Joe Burrow audibled to a pass to beat Todd Bowles’ defense, but Tampa’s scheme reigned superior as Josiah Trotter undercut a short pass underneath and returned it all the way to the end zone for the score. The Cherry on top highlight of a phenomenal debut for the rookie. 27-20, Cincy. Fourth Quarter: The fourth quarter of Sunday’s contest opened with a Cincinnati field goal. Trailing by 10, Baker Mayfield would take his first fourth quarter possession— It would not go as well. One more fumble for Mayfield would bring the team’s total four and his personal total to three. More good field position for the Bengals and more good offense. Evan McPherson added to an impressive game (1st kicker in franchise history with multiple 55+ yard kicks in a game) with three more points. 33-20, Bengals. In a helter skelter frantic drive that should be earmarked as the Ted Hurst III drive (Three straight throws to Hurst III for what would be his only three catches of the day) Baker Mayfield and Tampa Bay’s offense woke up accelerating down the field for a spark of energy. They jolted into the end zone like they hit smelling salts on the sideline, however, Baker Mayfield’s score was the embodiment of too little too late. 33-27, Cincinnati. Given the ball back with a chance to ice the game Joe Burrow did exactly that. Todd Bowles on the flip side, was iced— A story all too familiar for Buccaneers’ fans during the Todd Bowles era.

summary: The Washington Commanders traveled to Philadelphia for a late afternoon start to open the 2026 season.
