There are a lot of good things […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders traveled to Philadelphia for a late afternoon start to open the 2026 season. It was a mixed bag, as Washington’s defense was better than expected while the offense left a lot to be desired. Ultimately, Washington fell 24-22 in what was a very competitive game. There are a lot of good things fans can take away from this game, however, there are no moral victories and a loss is a loss — especially within the division. Quinn and company will have a week to clean some things up before traveling to Dallas to take on a Cowboys squad who lost to the Giants Sunday evening. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs: WR Antonio Williams : The rookie led all Washington pass catchers with 64 receiving yards and tied Stefon Diggs with a team-leading four receptions and a touchdown. It was a hell of a debut for Williams. Ball touches the ground (which is allowed) but ball never moves and Williams maintains control!!! TOUCHDOWN! pic.twitter.com/tlhPTb25i5 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Williams is the best Washington receiver on the day so far pic.twitter.com/NPy6yONjVv — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Huge 3rd and 14 conversion from JD to Williams pic.twitter.com/7DolzbvsQa — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 LB Sonny Styles : Styles had a really nice debut. He seemed to get into the flow of the game later on and just let his athleticism take over. He had a blitz where he absolutely destroyed Saquon Barkley on the way to his first NFL sack. He had four tackles (two of which were for a loss), three being solo, a sack and two pressures. Sonny Styles plays this about as well as you can pic.twitter.com/9eLCNZZGNw — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Styles TFL on Barkley💪🏻 pic.twitter.com/NtMSyHNF4V — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Sonny Styles with his first NFL sack! – and it’s a good one! pic.twitter.com/IQgo6SG9qe — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 S Nick Cross : Cross led all Washington defenders with eight total tackles, five of them solo, with two going for a loss. He was all around the football and was as advertised! Great play by Nick Cross here down in the box pic.twitter.com/tI5BtjOZSO — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Hell of a play here by Cross fighting through this block and getting the tackle on Barkley pic.twitter.com/XuiQlX1hbR — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 EDGE Odafe Oweh : Oweh played good, disciplined football all afternoon. He got his first sack on the season and also had two tackles for a loss, multiple pressures and a quarterback hit. Oweh and Kinlaw combine for sack pic.twitter.com/lFJGC9Xo47 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 DB Tyler Owens – It’s not often I give out special teams studs, but Owens earned it! This special teams play on punt coverage was amazing from the get-go! Get this man more snaps with Washington’s defense!!! Tyler Owens could not be stopped 😳 WASvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d4Tyw1MnqS — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Duds: C Nick Allegretti – Washington’s new center did not fare very well against a stout Eagles’ front. He allowed multiple pressures on the afternoon and whiffed on the 2-point conversion what could have tied the game late in the fourth quarter. But don’t worry folks, Peters and Quinn believe in him… This is absolutely PATHETIC by Allegretti😡 Thankfully a penalty against Philly saved the play pic.twitter.com/01eLF6ma0l — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Allegretti can’t handles Carter. Forced Jayden off his spot. pic.twitter.com/wbUpN7zf07 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Allegretti loses his block on the 2pt conversion pic.twitter.com/ILHmVfw8Fw — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 CB Mike Sainristil : Overall, the defense played well, but Sainristil was not one of the guys who can stake that claim. In fact, he was the worst player on our defense giving up chunk plays, allowing an easy touchdown and missing tackles by taking poor angles to the ball. It was a DISASTROUS start to the 2026 season on what was supposed to be a defense that played to his strengths. Wicks broke in Sainristil’s house, sat down at his kitchen table, and ate the family’s food right in front of Mikey — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 This is ABSOLUTELY PATHETIC by Mike Sainristil!!! He’s in man coverage! What the HELL is he doing😡 pic.twitter.com/76vmK3jJbD — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Did Sainristil think he had deep safety help, or did he just lose Wicks? pic.twitter.com/zJ9NcWJWqE — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 OC David Blough: This may seem a bit harsh to give a first-time play caller Dud status for his first NFL game, but I don’t think Blough called a very good game for the majority of three-and-a-half quarters. All the talk during the offseason was about getting McLaurin 10-plus touches per game and that certainly didn’t happen. There were too many times when Washington had just two guys in the route tree and the Eagles EASILY identified and shut those players down. Jayden looked uncomfortable with the early play calling and never got into a rhythm. Better days for this offense will be on the way, but this was an offensive game to forget. Offense is REALLY struggling. Jayden looks really out of sync. Thought they’d get things going out of the half and after a nice defensive series… but nope! — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Game Notes: QB Jayden Daniels never looked comfortable. Maybe that was Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio getting him rattled. Maybe that was having a new center he barely worked with throughout the summer and maybe that was a new coordinator who didn’t do him any favors in play calling. Whatever the case, he looked flustered and a bit indecisive. He did have some big throws and runs later in the game, and I think things between him and Blough will eventually click. Jayden with a 16yd 🎯 to Antonio Williams who gets down to the 1yd line💪🏻 pic.twitter.com/HvclkssyPW — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Jayden is a human joystick pic.twitter.com/eUuX1TWIxR — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 WR Stefon Diggs had a very up-and-down game. He had two big drops before finally finding his groove on offense. His “humping” of the goalpost after his touchdown was immature and cost the team a shot at a 2-point conversion – which turned out to be costly. I contemplated giving him Dud status for the game, but decided to be kind. Diggs is not having a great game today. Here is his 2nd drop of the game pic.twitter.com/Vw5DQbmLPm — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Daniels hits Diggs for the TD!!! pic.twitter.com/feZAxxS7wr — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 CB Amik Robertson played very well, so much that I thought about including him as a Stud. He was second on the team with six total tackles and showed well in coverage. Lost in all the bad play from Sainristil talk, is how well Amik Robertson played. This defense is tailor-made for him — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 14, 2026 I thought RT Josh Conerly played a pretty good game. He held his own and I saw a few really good anchors. I will be watching All-22 to get a better look of his individual performance, but from what I saw during the broadcast, he more than held his own. The “great” PFF rated LT Brandon Coleman’s play as pretty poor, but I did not see the same. Overall, I though he held his own. He did allow a sack and got called for a false start (which I did not agree with), but he blocked pretty well in the run game and pushed his defender outside the pocket more often than not in pass protection. It wasn’t a perfect game, but it was nowhere near as bad…

title: Commanders News: A lot of good, a lot of bad in Week 1 loss to Eagles
summary: The Daily Slop – 15 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 15 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) Commanders’ loss to Eagles revealed a new-look defense with an edge Facing Philadelphia’s vaunted offensive line and its multiple playmakers, Washington held the Eagles to only 10 first downs, half as many as the Commanders’ offense. That was the lowest total in the league through the first 15 games of Week 1. The physicality coach Dan Quinn has preached since he arrived in Washington two seasons ago was evident throughout, with 13 total “havoc” plays — takeaways, tackles for loss, sacks and pass breakups — the Commanders’ fourth-most in a game since the start of the ’24 season. View Link Rookie linebacker Sonny Styles, who wore the green dot in the second half when Frankie Luvu was sidelined with a groin injury, showed his mettle in the third quarter when he trucked Eagles running back Saquon Barkley on the way to his first career sack. On the next drive, he stuffed Barkley for a three-yard loss on a run. Just as promising as the production was much of Washington’s process: It sent five-man pressures on 12 of the Eagles’ 33 dropbacks and generated pressure on two-thirds of them. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Eagles outlast Commanders, but lots of issues for both teams’ new-look offenses Washington, in its first game with 31-year-old David Blough as offensive coordinator, struggled to generate consistent offense until its final two possessions. Meanwhile, Philadelphia had issues of its own sustaining drives in the second half under 34-year-old first-time coordinator Sean Mannion. Leading 14-9 at halftime, Philadelphia went three-and-out on each of its first three drives in the second half — setting the stage for Washington’s near comeback. Eagles fans will not be happy after having to sit through yet another system going mostly stale in the second half. Mannion’s offense stagnated after entering the second half with a 14-9 lead. The Eagles went three-and-out on their first three drives. They opened each drive under center while fielding two tight ends. Barkley was stuffed on the first run for a 1-yard loss. On the third drive, the Eagles fielded the same look on second-and-7, and Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles shot through a gap on a blitz to bring Barkley down for a 3-yard loss. Hurts was sacked on the subsequent third-and-10, and the Eagles punted again. The style of play mirrored that of the 2025 season. Former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo oversaw an offense that too often leaned on the strength of the Eagles’ defense. The 2025 Eagles had a minus-30 point differential while playing with a lead in the second half. They had a minus-3 point differential in the second half against the Commanders. Commanders fans should put their heads on their pillows believing their defense isn’t going to be the utter disaster it has been for two seasons. Rookie linebacker Sonny Styles recorded the first sack of his career and absolutely blew up Barkley in the process. Safety Nick Cross, linebacker Frankie Luvu, cornerback Rasul Douglas and others delivered heavy hits. And the Commanders sacked Hurts three times — from Styles, Luvu and new $100-million man Odafe Oweh. View Link But even with the flashes, there is plenty to clean up — most notably, the absolute gash plays that killed the Commanders all day. At halftime, the Eagles had 182 yards of offense — 64 on a Hurts-to-Wicks completion and 42 on a Barkley run. That’s 58 percent of their output on two plays, and that doesn’t count the 17-yard touchdown pass on third-and-goal to Goedert. That continued in the second half. On third-and-18, Hurts was allowed to scamper for 22 yards. And the play that ended up being the difference in the game: Goedert’s 43-yard touchdown — on which he got wide open. That’s 171 of the Eagles’ 318 total yards on just four plays. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) If only the Commanders had another shot at two Jayden Daniels, hemmed in much of the game by one of the league’s top defenses and hampered by pre-snap penalties, threw touchdown passes to Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. On Washington’s final 12-play, 63-yard drive, Williams snatched Daniels’ throw a nanosecond before it hit the ground for a 1-yard touchdown with one minute remaining. Momentum, Washington. Now came the chance to tie the game. The two-point play call from first-time offensive coordinator David Blough had Daniels attempting a shovel pass to tight end John Bates. Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn liked the call from the Eagles’ 2-yard line. But as the play began, Quinn’s eyes told him danger lurked. For more from Ben Standig, click here Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . ESPN NFL Week 1: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games Commanders Did quarterback Jayden Daniels show enough to inspire a bounce-back season? Daniels looked sharp this summer in new coordinator David Blough’s offense. But for most of Sunday’s game — his first since Week 14 last season — the offense struggled against one of the NFL’s best defenses. Daniels hesitated too many times because he didn’t have an open target or wasn’t confident in what he saw. That’s concerning, as one of his best traits is being decisive. In the first half, he completed 6 of 16 passes for 43 yards. Daniels still finished strong, leading two scoring drives to nearly tie the score. But if Washington is going to avoid a bad start, Blough and Daniels need to find a better rhythm early. Most surprising performance: Wide receiver Terry McLaurin did not catch a pass until less than five minutes remained in the contest. He finished with just two catches and four targets. It’s not what Blough had in mind when he took over, saying he wanted to get McLaurin 10 targets per game. But the Eagles often doubled him, rolled coverage his way or simply blanketed him. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Mistakes doomed the Commanders — but Jayden Daniels finished standing upright For most of the first three quarters, the Commanders offense, and Blough, its first-year offensive coordinator , got very little done, wasting multiple opportunities given to it by Washington’s defense, which stacked three-and-outs much of the night and forced seven Eagles punts. (To be sure: The defense gave up a handful of killer big plays, too.) Washington’s offense produced a field goal on its first possession, then didn’t move the ball again until its next-to-last possession of the first half. Eagles linebacker Zack Baun was just … everywhere. They have to be better. But. Sunday marked the first time Daniels started and finished a game for Washington since Oct. 13, against the Chicago Bears. Think of that: It’s almost been a year since Jayden Daniels actually played four full quarters for the Commanders. That is a significant hurdle for him to overcome, after his disastrous 2025, which included separate hamstring, knee and elbow injuries that limited him to seven games. He is the North Star for owner Josh Harris’ team, capable of doing great things when on the field. With Daniels, Washington has a chance. View Link Daniels, in his third season, looked like a quarterback who understood his importance. He didn’t take off at the first sign of pressure. title: Podcast: The Commanders Left a Win on the Table Against the Eagles
summary: The Washington Commanders season opener came down to a 2-point conversion against the Philadelphia Eagles. What’s most frustrating about the loss in Philadelphia is seeing how a lack of execution in key moments throughout the game ultimately cost Washington points. Washington has no one to blame but themselves. The Commanders’ offense didn’t come alive until […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders signals for a two point conversion attempt while a touchdown is under review against the Philadelphia Eagles in the fourth quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders season opener came down to a 2-point conversion against the Philadelphia Eagles. What’s most frustrating about the loss in Philadelphia is seeing how a lack of execution in key moments throughout the game ultimately cost Washington points. Washington has no one to blame but themselves. The Commanders’ offense didn’t come alive until the fourth quarter, but for the first three quarters against the Eagles, the unit couldn’t get favorable second and third downs to stay ahead of the chains. Jayden Daniels completed nine passes on 23 attempts for 64 yards through the first three quarters; the only chance that the Commanders had at success offensively was with running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Bill finished the game with 63 yards on 16 attempts, but was the catalyst behind the run game, wearing down the Eagles’ defense as the game went on. Between the pressure Jayden Daniels faced on his dropbacks and the wide receivers not getting open quickly enough for him (and drops), Washington has to find an immediate fix for its pass-game issues. On the Trap or Dive post-game recap, Dre and I dissect the Commanders mistakes that led to their 24-22 loss to the Eagles. The defense undoubtedly kept Washington in the game by containing Saquon Barkley and consistently getting home on Jalen Hurts, preventing him from attacking the secondary. Between Washington’s two first-time coordinators, Daronte Jones had the most impressive debut, and his scheme highlighted the front seven’s potential to take over games. However, even with a strong debut, Washington lost the explosive-play battle, couldn’t create a turnover, and the Eagles scored three touchdowns by capitalizing on just a handful of defensive mistakes. title: Commanders report card: Team grades in NFL Week 1 loss to Eagles
summary: The Commanders are 0-1. That’s a simple fact following Sunday’s 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.   While NFL football’s a zero-sum game, there was some nuance to the season-opener worth noting, with some standout performances and (let’s be honest) unacceptable blunders that played a huge role in the outcome.   […]
full_text: The Commanders are 0-1. That’s a simple fact following Sunday’s 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. While NFL football’s a zero-sum game, there was some nuance to the season-opener worth noting, with some standout performances and (let’s be honest) unacceptable blunders that played a huge role in the outcome. There was a reason why the Commanders struggled at the outset and found a way to come storming back, only to be felled by a failed 2-point conversion attempt , and a few explosive plays allowed defensively leading up to that. We learned a ton about this new-look Commanders team with still so much more to glean. Let’s grade out how Washington looked in each phase of Sunday’s game following that disappointing Week 1 result in Philadelphia: Rushing offense The Commanders ground game produced 132 yards on 32 carries , just squeaking above four yards per rush thanks to some Jayden Daniels moves straight out of Madden. The Commanders weren’t terribly efficient outside of that, besides a few bright spots. It’s hard to blame run blocking or the backs without film study, but coordinator David Blough’s offense is predicated on rushing efficiency. So much is available to scheme if you achieve that. The Commanders were committed to the ground game — get used to that – but must be better at it. Grade: C-minus Passing offense Terry McLaurin spent most of this game without a catch, a rarity of the highest order. Stefon Diggs had four catches and a touchdown, but on nine targets. Antonio Williams was, well, awesome, with four receptions for a team-high 64 yards and had an excellent late-game touchdown. Daniels wasn’t efficient in completing 18-of-34 passes for 164 yards and two touchdowns – it’s probably safe to say the Eagles secondary beat the Commanders receivers on Sunday – but he was smart with the football and largely avoided big hits. We’ll need to see more from Daniels and the passing game and we will. There should be confidence in that. The passing scheme is good. The execution must be better. Yet, somehow, Daniels found a way to get revved and make a valiant comeback attempt. Grade: C-plus Rushing defense Take away Saquon Barkley’s 42-yard explosion and Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on third-and-long(!!) and it’s a respectable rushing day at 72 yards on 23 carries (3.13 ypc). Problem is, you can’t do that. The run defense overall, looked pretty good. As you’ll read in the next item, those explosive plays simply must be eliminated. Barkley’s gonna get a big one every now and then. That Hurts run was inexcusable. Watching it live, I thought the linebackers and safeties played well against the run overall, and the defensive line looks much improved. Grade: B-minus Passing defense The Commanders limited Hurts to 203 yards. Sounds like a good day. Largely it was, save two bad plays by Mikey Sainristil against Dontayvion Wicks and a 43-yard Dallas Goedert TD at the worst possible time — wasn’t that a false start ?? — and it gets rough. Commanders simply must limit explosive plays. It’s that simple. They gave up some big ones at the worst possible time. Overall, though, the pass rush was strong, with three sacks and five quarterback hits. Sonny Styles looks like that dude. So does Odafe Oweh. Grade: B Special teams Tyler Owens gets an A-plus all on his own. But the high Tyler Ott snap that led to a missed extra point and a 54-yard field goal Drew Stevens sailed very wide right was not. Special teams should be a strength. Hard to say it unequivocally was on this day. Grade: C Coaching You’ll come to find that I gave A’s or F’s for coaching. Did the staff win Washington this game or lose it? It’s that simple. But maybe not this time. Again, more tape review is required, but my initial thought was that Daronte Jones’ game plan was aces. Really good, and I love the style of play. David Blough’s night felt more uneven, though execution was lacking and that Eagles defense is pretty good. And, on that 2-point conversion, I find a way to target McLaurin or Diggs and let those dudes make a play, maybe on a roll out where Daniels can run if he wants. I liked that Dan Quinn wasn’t finding moral victories after the loss, but his impact on the game was negligible. Grade: C How would you grade Commanders after that loss to Philly? Let us know in the comments below.
author: Scott Bair

title: Inside failed Commanders 2-point conversion that secured loss to Eagles
summary: There was a break in the action as officials reviewed Antonio Williams’ touchdown catch, left the Commanders two points from tying the Eagles with roughly a minute left.   Offensive coordinator David Blough and head coach Dan Quinn discussed 2-point conversion options while the touchdown was being confirmed.   Blough suggested the play call that was […]
full_text: There was a break in the action as officials reviewed Antonio Williams’ touchdown catch , left the Commanders two points from tying the Eagles with roughly a minute left. Offensive coordinator David Blough and head coach Dan Quinn discussed 2-point conversion options while the touchdown was being confirmed. Blough suggested the play call that was eventually run. Quinn gave the green light. The Commanders ran it well during the practice week. It was in the game plan. There was high confidence it would work “On that particular one, he said, ‘what do you think?’” Quinn said, “And I said, ‘let’s go for it.’” The Commanders in fact went for it and came up short. A failed onside kick and a few kneel-downs later and the Eagles secured a 24-22 victory on Sunday night at Lincoln Financial Field. “I knew the play,” Quinn told reporters in a postgame press conference. “I thought it was a good one. When it doesn’t execute, it sucks.” Commanders fans won’t like it. Not one bit. The play was a shovel pass to tight end John Bates that got blown up by Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo, who spun around center Nick Allegretti and shut the play down. You’ve certainly seen it before, either once or a thousand times, but here it is. Allegretti loses his block on the 2pt conversion pic.twitter.com/ILHmVfw8Fw — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 You can see running back Rachaad White open in the flat, but a widening defensive end lent itself to this inside play to Bates. “It was an option, but I’ve got to do my job, too,” Daniel told reporters in his postgame presser . “The defensive end played up the field. We had the look that we wanted. We just didn’t execute.” Daniels had to make a quick judgement call in the moment, and he followed his rules on that play by choosing to shovel the ball inside. Quinn and Daniels stood by the call, which will be negatively viewed because of the result. “The 2-point play, we just didn’t execute,” Daniels said. “It was the right call. Anything Blough calls, I’m with him. Regardless of who everyone else might view it, I’m with Blough 100%.” This film will be broken down a ton in detail, including by our HH analysts. Here’s a night-of takeaway from Mark Bullock: I know you all will hate this play-call. I don’t really like it either. But a trick play in a key spot looks incredible if it works and incredibly stupid if it doesn’t. Tackle was made by a DT who spun out of a down block on the back side of a run. Hell of a play by the DT,… https://t.co/nX7nBfJwAD — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) September 13, 2026

title: Key takeaways from Washington Commanders loss vs. Philadelphia Eagles
summary: BOX SCORE We’ve been talking and talking and talking about how the Washington Commanders would look in the 2026 regular-season opener (and beyond). All spring and summer. Ever since the NFL draft, if we’re being honest.   Week 1 finally arrived on Sunday afternoon, with the Commanders facing the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles. It […]
full_text: BOX SCORE We’ve been talking and talking and talking about how the Washington Commanders would look in the 2026 regular-season opener (and beyond). All spring and summer. Ever since the NFL draft, if we’re being honest. Week 1 finally arrived on Sunday afternoon, with the Commanders facing the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles. It was the first time we’d see new offensive coordinator David Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones run their respective shows. So many free-agent additions were making Commanders debuts as well, adding anticipation to a contest that’s always must-see. We learned a ton about how Washington will operate, including an aggressive-as-heck defense and an intriguing offense that has some work to do. This one remained close into the fourth quarter and was decided late. A valiant comeback effort came up just short, with Washington losing a 24-22 decision to the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. The Commanders showed resilience in this game, but ultimately ended up with a loss. Washington had too many costly mistakes, with each phase shouldering some of the blame. Here are some quick Commanders takeaways after watching the game live: Commanders offense finds stride late The Commanders offense spent most of Sunday’s game trying to find a flow. Quarterback Jayden Daniels had a tough time working the ball downfield to his best receivers, and while the run game had some nice moments, it didn’t help sustain drives that too often stopped short. It wasn’t always pretty, with Philadelphia’s talented secondary limiting options in the passing game. The offensive line looked okay watching it live but had some tough times, with Daniels scrambling to find productive space. The Commanders kept fighting despite all that, and found a way to keep things very close down the stretch. Daniels converted a third-and-14 with a 33-yard connection with Antonio Williams early in the fourth quarter to sustain a scoring drive. Then Daniels found Stefon Diggs for a touchdown. With that and the extra point – Diggs’ unsportsmanlike penalty took away the opportunity for a 2-point conversion — the Commanders cut it to 17-16. first as a Commander 🤩 📺 #WASvsPHI FOX pic.twitter.com/BFX7I2XBpb — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 13, 2026 Could the offense find a way to win, as Daniels had so many times before? They’d have an uphill battle, with the Commanders down eight points with roughly six minutes left. Washington pushed deep into Eagles territory, and earned a goal-to-go situation with a fourth-down conversion to Terry McLaurin. Daniels then hit Williams for a touchdown with 1:01 left. Antonio Williams scores his first NFL TD! pic.twitter.com/D0vWt4e98d — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) September 13, 2026 The subsequent 2-point conversion was stopped, which sustained the Eagles lead and ultimately proved decisive. Blough may have gotten cute there, with a shovel pass to tight end John Bates that got shut down and ultimately prevented a Commanders comeback. Did not love this play call on the failed 2-pt conversion pic.twitter.com/Pd6XVs3Pp3 — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) September 13, 2026 This offense clearly has some work ahead to find consistency, but could prove dangerous if it can do so. That Eagles defense is tough, but Washington wore that unit down over time. There were still too many mistakes, however, to overcome quality opposition. There were pluses and minus to the effort, but the offense (and its coordinator) must be better. Daronte Jones is aggressive Daronte Jones spent his last three seasons working under Brian Flores in Minnesota, so it was assumed Washington’s new defensive coordinator would bring pressure from all over the place and create confusion with exotic looks. That was confirmed on Sunday, when Jones sent pressure on the regular, testing the Eagles on almost every play. We won’t see advanced metrics until later – again, this is being written live – but the pressure numbers will be high. Rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was attacking a ton, with a highlight play you can see right here on his first NFL sack, where he blitzed and also blew Saquon Barkley the heck up: first sack for our first-rounder ✅ 📺 #WASvsPHI FOX pic.twitter.com/a6Z2QpBHmf — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 13, 2026 Washington was often impactful, but the Commanders gave up some costly explosive plays. That included two from cornerback Mike Sainristil, and one where he apparently lost track of the ball: Tay Wicks made his first catch in Philly count! Seeshhhh pic.twitter.com/BoUVIullqB — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 13, 2026 That got Washington in trouble early, but they revved up in the third quarter. Odafe Oweh’s first sack as a Commander on a five-man pressure forced a punt. Odafe Oweh leads the pack to take down Jalen Hurts! pic.twitter.com/akNedbo5tg — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) September 13, 2026 The defense conceded a late touchdown to Dallas Goedert at just the wrong time, putting the Eagles up eight points. Dallas Goedert runs into the end zone for his second TD of the game 🗣️ WASvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QJFypWhLGb — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 That play proved costly, with the points tallied that proved to be the difference despite a late Daniels comeback attempt. Overall, it’s clear aggressiveness, and the appearance of it, will rank high among of Washington’s core values under Jones. That should make for a fun defense to watch over the course of the season, one that should be impactful creating takeaways and stops. Special teams giveth (and taketh away) Washington’s Tyler Owens – I mean, my goodness. He was incredible on special teams, battling through double teams to make one big hit in coverage after another. His relentlessness is a marvel, as are his statement hits seemingly designed to both cut returns short and energize his sideline. Owens was that good, in the first half especially. And this effort might be one of the best I’ve ever seen on special teams. This is an ALL-TIME rep by Commanders S Tyler Owens 🤯 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/AW47P6Hq1q — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) September 13, 2026 He unfortunately ended up getting hurt in the second half. The Commanders announced he had an ankle injury. Washington surely hopes he can return soon, considering his impact in the kicking game While special teams put for some great plays, a blocked extra point (the snap was high) and a Drew Stevens field-goal attempt missed wide right. What are your immediate takeaways from Washginton’s season opener? Let us know in the article comments below.

title: Touchdowns galore, awards market moves and a great Sunday for NFL bettors
summary: A high-scoring Week 1 with a variety of players scoring TDs made for a bettor-friendly Sunday.
full_text:
The Bears ' 59-37 victory over the Carolina Panthers in Sunday's early slate kept the momentum of Chicago's offseason hype train going and was representative of a great first Sunday of NFL action for bettors. 

 For starters, the Bears were one of the most popular teams to win and cover the spread (-3) on Sunday, which they did with ease in the second half. DraftKings classified the Bears as the second-most-backed team by bets and handle going into Sunday's action, while BetMGM said Chicago minus-3 was the most-bet spread of the early slate by tickets, with the sportsbook's senior trading manager Christian Cipollini classifying it as "a good outcome for bettors."

 

 Then there was the avalanche of touchdowns. Five Bears got in the end zone on Sunday, with QB Caleb Williams and RB D'Andre Swift each getting in multiple times. With the Panthers contributing plenty of scoring on their own, the game flew over its total of 47.5 with 2:35 left in the second quarter. The final score's 96 total points were the most for a Week 1 game in NFL history.

 The game set the pace for an explosive opening Sunday that saw six teams score 24 or more points in the first half of their games -- also the most in Week 1 in NFL history, according to ESPN research. With players such as  Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown , Derrick Henry , Jonathan Taylor and Josh Allen finding the end zone multiple times, that made for a tremendous day for a betting public that makes a habit of rooting for scoring from superstars.

 "The first NFL Sunday of the season was a champagne-popping day for bettors, while the book was left cleaning up the corks," Caesars Sportsbook football lead Joey Feazel told ESPN. "Seven of the eight morning favorites won outright, six games flew over the total -- many reaching that mark by halftime -- and eight of the top 10 most popular touchdown scorers found the end zone. 

 "Favorites, overs and touchdown scorers combined to create a bettor-friendly trifecta on opening Sunday."

 Chicago's big win built on the goodwill the team had accrued with bettors throughout the offseason via the futures market -- both for the team as a whole and its star quarterback.

 The Bears were a hot commodity in a variety of futures markets before the season, chief among them being the Super Bowl. Just before the campaign kicking off, DraftKings reported 7.5% of its Super Bowl handle backing Chicago -- the third most behind the Los Angeles Rams (20.2%) and Buffalo Bills (9.8%) -- while BetMGM said the Bears had garnered the most NFC championship tickets at 14.4%. Feazel called Chicago "a moderate position" in the Super Bowl market Sunday. 

 

 "Chicago's offense looks great," Circa Sports NFL oddsmaker Jamey Pileggi told ESPN. "Bad defense is going to hold them back from being real contenders."

 At DraftKings, Chicago made only a small move from 24-1 to 21-1 to win the title, but the big odds move came for Williams in the MVP market, where he went from 12-1 to +700, tying him for second with Lamar Jackson behind Allen in the lead at +500. 

 Several sportsbooks considered Williams a liability in the awards market coming into the season, and he accumulated around 10% of the tickets at both BetMGM and Caesars. Joe Burrow (+950) has been the public's favorite throughout the offseason, but if Williams can continue to put up performances like Sunday's, he could continue to gain traction with bettors.

 "Given his Week 1 performance and the amount of early support we've already seen, we would expect Caleb Williams to remain one of the more heavily backed players in the MVP market moving forward," Feazel said.

 Odds & Ends 

 
 The Arizona Cardinals closed as 8.5-point underdogs to the Los Angeles Chargers before upsetting them outright on the road. It was the largest Week 1 upset since 2018 ( Tampa Bay Buccaneers +10 over the New Orleans Saints ). 
 The Chargers were the most-picked team in ESPN Survivor contests (21.4%), the second-most in Circa Survivor (30.3%) and the second-most in Splash Sports' $1,000 entry survivor contest (21.5%). 
 The Cardinals are the first team with a preseason win total of 3.5 or lower to win their Week 1 game since at least 1990, according to ESPN Research. 
 After losing and failing to cover plus-3.5 on Sunday, the Buccaneers are now 0-10 against the spread in their past 10 games, tying the longest ATS losing streak in the Super Bowl era. 
 On the flip side, the Jacksonville Jaguars have covered nine consecutive regular-season games, the longest ATS winning streak since the Green Bay Packers in 2021 and the longest in Jaguars history.  
 
 ESPN's David Purdum contributed to this report.

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces seven active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald , who un-retired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7 all-time. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach top-five all-time territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks were 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research, heading into the seaosn. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the all-time list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all of the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: NFL Week 1: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 1.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season  is already off to an exciting start.

 In the early window Sunday, the Bears and Panthers combined for 96 points, the most in a season opener in NFL history, per ESPN Research. The host Jaguars easily handled the Browns in quarterback  Deshaun Watson 's first regular-season game since October 2024. The Bills looked sharp offensively in Joe Brady's head coaching debut against the Texans, and the Lions needed overtime to get past the Saints.

 In the late window, the Cardinals and Raiders won in the respective debuts of first-year coaches Mike LaFleur and Klint Kubiak. The Commanders fell despite a comeback against division foe Philadelphia. And after losing quarterback Kyler Murray to a concussion early, the Vikings scored 29 unanswered to defeat the Packers. The Giants finished things off by beating the Cowboys on Sunday night, marking the first time since 2009 both New York teams opened with a victory.

 Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

 
 Jump to: 
 DAL-NYG |  GB-MIN |  WSH-PHI 
 MIA-LV  |  ARI-LAC  |  CHI-CAR 
 BUF-HOU  |  NO-DET  |  BAL-IND 
 ATL-PIT  |  NYJ-TEN  |  TB-CIN 
 CLE-JAX 

 Catch up on weekday games: 
 SF-LAR | NE-SEA 

 
 

 

 N.Y. Giants 28, Dallas 20 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Giants 
 Should the Giants be taken seriously in the NFC East? This was a statement game for the John Harbaugh Giants. They looked like the better team in beating a Cowboys squad that had prevailed in 16 of its previous 18 meetings with the Giants. New York's offense looked dangerous with a power running game (165 yards) led by Cam Skattebo  (18 carries, 81 yards), and quarterback Jaxson Dart was in command throughout. The defense also looked greatly improved. With neither the Eagles nor Commanders looking dominant in Week1, the Giants could be a real threat in the NFC East. For the first time in years, it's not an outlandish thought.

 What to make of the QB performance: Brilliant. Dart was in control throughout, running and throwing with precision. He finished 23-of-29 for 230 passing yards with three touchdown and added 54 rushing yards. The chemistry that Dart showed all summer with new tight end Isaiah Likely translated to the opener. Likely caught eight passes on eight targets for 78 yards with two touchdowns and helped ice the game late with two big third-down receptions. -- Jordan Raanan 

 Next game: at Rams (Monday, Sept. 21, 8:15 p.m. ET)

 
 

 Cowboys 
 Will this serve as a wake-up call for the Cowboys? After a drama-free offseason, the return of a top-tier offense and a revamped defense, expectations were high. Though there are 16 more games to go, the loss to the Giants showed the Cowboys have a lot of work to do. An ill-timed Dak Prescott interception at the end of the first half led to a Giants' TD. There were far too many penalties in the first half (seven, tied for the most in an opener since 2008) and a costly one in the fourth quarter, as Javonte Williams ' taunting penalty led to a missed extra point attempt in a one-score game. The Giants were able to control the line of scrimmage and the clock in the second half to win a game that went according to the Giants' desired script.

 Most surprising performance: Things were supposed to be different for this Cowboys defense. Not necessarily a massive move to the top of the league, but they were disappointing throughout Christian Parker's first game as playcaller. The end-of-half work that saw New York go ahead 14-7 was filled with coverage breakdowns. The second half opened with the Cowboys needing to call timeout because they had only 10 defenders on the field, and they could not come up with any stops in the final two quarters. With eight new starters from last season's opener and another handful of new key contributors, it's clear it will take time for it to come together. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs. Commanders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 
 Fantasy football takeaway:  Likely paced the Giants with eight catches -- the most by any Giants tight end in nearly three years -- with two going for touchdowns. His 27.8 fantasy points led the position, and are an indicator he'll be involved enough to be a weekly TE1.  -- Cockcroft 

 

 

 Minnesota 39, Green Bay 22 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Vikings 
 What now at quarterback? For the second consecutive season, and for the third campaign in the past four, the Vikings are dealing with an injury to their quarterback. This time, new starter Kyler Murray made it only 11 plays -- and they were 11 shaky plays, at that -- before suffering a concussion at the end of a first-quarter scramble. Backup Carson Wentz , named the No. 2 quarterback last week after he was a bystander in the competition between Murray and J.J. McCarthy this summer, was understandably rusty at the outset but hung in to throw three touchdown passes and avoid a turnover. Wentz will be the starter until Murray is cleared to return.

 Trend to watch: The Vikings blitzed Packers quarterback Jordan Love on nearly every first-half snap (15-of-18, or 83%), and Love burned them repeatedly en route to putting up 19 points. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores adjusted with more variety in the second half, taking down the blitz rate to 63%. It wasn't the only reason the Packers struggled to score thereafter, but it made the blitzes the Vikings did execute more effective. -- Kevin Seifert 

 Next game: at Bears (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 

 
 

 

 Packers 
 Did the Packers learn nothing from last year? So much for all that offseason talk about finishing. Week 1 followed the same script from late last season: Grab the lead, make major mistakes in the second half and let the opponent back in the game. The blunders were many in this matchup: a special teams miscue (allowing a 69-yard kickoff return); a blown coverage (leaving tight end T.J. Hockenson wide open for a touchdown); bad penalties (three of them on the Vikings' go-ahead drive that wiped out a pair of would-have-been third-down stops and nullified an interception); shoddy offensive line play; and a poor coaching decision (opting to take a field goal off the board on a penalty then failing on the ensuing QB sneak).

 What to make of the QB performance:  Love, despite a 387-yard passing game, barely had a chance, especially down the stretch, thanks to a disastrous performance by his offensive line. Being without starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) wasn't the reason the Vikings recorded 15 QB hits on Love; it was because the Packers couldn't handle the myriad of blitzes. When the Packers needed a fourth-quarter drive to regain the lead, Love was sacked on back-to-back plays, losing a fumble on the second one that was returned to Green Bay's 1-yard line. -- Rob Demovsky 

 Next game: at Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 Fantasy football takeaway:   Christian Watson 's 32.7 fantasy points were the second most among wide receivers in Week 1 through the late window. He caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns for the Pack. With an expanding route tree and big-play speed, Watson can be safely played as a lower-tier WR2 for Week 2. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Philadelphia 24, Washington 22 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Eagles 
 Did the Eagles' new offense pass the test Week 1? There was a boom-or-bust element to it, but the explosive plays carried them to a passing grade and a win over Washington. From WR Dontayvion Wicks ' 64-yard reception (a career high) to QB Jalen Hurts ' 22-yard scramble on third-and-18 to TE Dallas Goedert 's 43-yard score moments later, there was plenty to be encouraged about from offensive coordinator Sean Mannion's debut. title: Giants' jab at Cowboys following SNF victory tops NFL Week 1 trolls
summary: Early season rust didn't apply to teams around the NFL trolling their opponents after a victory.
full_text:
It's just Week 1 of the NFL season, but that doesn't mean the trolls are starting out slow.

 

 The New York Giants defeated the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 on "Sunday Night Football." New York enjoyed a wire-to-wire win behind a stellar performance from quarterback Jaxson Dart .

 He had 230 passing yards and three passing touchdowns, plus 54 yards rushing. Dart is the third quarterback in Giants history with three passing touchdowns and 50 rushing yards in a game, according to ESPN Research. New York's defense had a say in the victory, too, holding Dallas to just 244 total yards of offense -- the fewest for the Cowboys versus the Giants since 2008. In his debut with the team, Giants tight end Isaiah Likely had eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns. 

 New York's win didn't come without a petty post on social media aimed at its rivals. The Giants shared a video of "SpongeBob SquarePants" character Sandy Cheeks, who is from Texas, playing "Sandy's Texas Song." The track ends with Sandy going down into her tree dome while singing the lyrics: "I want to go home."

 In this case, it's presumably the Cowboys who want to go home. 

 

 Here are more of the top trolls from Week 1 of the NFL season.

 

 Buffalo Bills 36, Houston Texans 31 
 In an early-season matchup between two AFC favorites, the Buffalo Bills defeated the Houston Texans  on Sunday. The high-scoring affair came to an end when Buffalo linebacker Greg Rousseau had a sack fumble on Houston quarterback  C.J. Stroud  with 16 seconds left in the game.

 Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen had 334 passing yards and four total touchdowns -- two on the ground and two in the air. Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid led the team with 130 receiving yards, while wide receiver DJ Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two scores.

 The big victory came with simple trolls from Buffalo. First, it posted an image of someone doing a horns down motion to the Texans' mascot, Toro. Then, the Bills put a spin on the city of Houston's famous blue tiles, creating their own sign that read: "Bills Win," with the Houston skyline in the background.

 

 
 Pittsburgh Steelers 20, Atlanta Falcons 13 
 The first game of the Mike McCarthy era in Pittsburgh began with a W as the Steelers defeated the Falcons at home.

 Pittsburgh's defense showed out with two forced turnovers, including a pick-six by linebacker T.J. Watt , and four sacks. Watt had two of those sacks, becoming the first Steelers player with at least two sacks and an interception return for a touchdown in a game since LaMarr Woodley in 2010, according to ESPN Research.

 The victory came with a postgame jab aimed at the Falcons' namesake. Pittsburgh posted a viral TikTok audio and meme with a bird hopping up and down when exiting a cage with the caption: "Feather in our cap."

 

 
 San Francisco 49ers 27, Los Angeles Rams 7 
 Even from down under, the trolls hit the same. San Francisco made sure to poke fun at its division rival after a dominant win in Australia.

 The 49ers' statement victory against the Rams on Thursday night included 24 unanswered points to close it out. Los Angeles had just 290 offensive yards plus two turnovers, while San Francisco hummed all game. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy threw for 205 passing yards and three touchdowns to three different players -- wide receivers Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel Sr.  and Demarcus Robinson .

 While in Australia, San Francisco seemingly picked up on trends of the Oceanic country. One of them became the theme of its troll: Vegemite, a thick Australian spread made from brewer's yeast . It has a strong, salty and meaty-rich flavor, according to Food Network . The 49ers spread it out on a piece of bread to spell out "W," presumably served up for the Rams.

 

 
 Seattle Seahawks 13, New England Patriots 10 
 Seattle's championship-defending season began with a victory against New England last Wednesday.

 The Seahawks lost quarterback Sam Darnold on the first drive due to a hip injury. Drew Lock stepped up under center and threw for 187 yards and a touchdown. However, Seattle's defense made the plays of the game, picking off Patriots quarterback Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to help secure the win.

 No different from last season, a Seahawks victory came with a comic trolling of the other team, this time the Patriots.

title: NFL Week 1's best arrivals, led by Dak Prescott and Cam Skattebo

The first NFL Sunday of the year has arrived, and with it comes fresh fits around the league.

 

 In recent years, NFL players' arrival outfits have become more sophisticated and diverse. Sometimes, they are suited and booted. Other times it's simply trendy streetwear.

 "It's like I put on a costume," Dallas Cowboys linebacker Von Miller told ESPN. "It gives me a different energy, a different spark."

 Miller isn't the only player who believes a great fit can set the tone before a game.

 The first two games of the season, on Wednesday and Thursday, gave us a glimpse of what we could see during players' arrivals this year. Now, as the Week 1 action continues, even more players must battle the September heat for their best pregame looks. So if they make this list, you know they brought the smoke.

title: Lamar Jackson looks like old self in Ravens' new offense
summary: In his first season with new OC Declan Doyle, Jackson has embraced changes to how he played football for most of his life.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- It was third-and-16 in the first quarter Sunday when Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson dropped back and saw two Indianapolis Colts pass rushers quickly closing in. 
 
 For many quarterbacks, it would have been a sack, the loss of 11 yards and the end of the drive. For Jackson, it was an opportunity to show he can create plays that make you question what exactly you just saw. 
 
 Ducking under linebacker Arden Key and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , Jackson made an unlikely escape and scrambled 16 yards for a first down. In Baltimore's 41-23 season-opening win, Jackson proved he can be his old self in the Ravens' new offense. 
 
 "It was just like, 'What just happened? How did he get it in there and get the first down?'" Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell said. "It is like, 'How many people can actually do that?' Not many -- not many. He might be one of the only ones." 
 
 
 
 It was a play that had everyone shaking their heads except for Jackson himself. 
 
 "I believe I did it a few times throughout my career, but [I'm] just playing football," Jackson said. "I am trying to get out of the situation. [The] offensive line [is] doing a great job at protecting me, [and] sometimes I have to have their back." 
 
 In his first season with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, Jackson has embraced changes to how he played football for most of his life. 
 
 Instead of primarily working out of the pistol formation, Jackson was under center 53% of the time (34 of 64 snaps), which was the highest percentage of his nine-year NFL career. He also altered his footwork, switching to a left foot-forward stance because Doyle believed it would help the timing of the passing game. 
 
 The result was a throwback game for the two-time MVP. This was Jackson's sixth game where he threw over 300 yards and ran for at least 40 yards -- but it was his first such performance since October 2024. 
 
 
 
 "The best player in the league," Ravens running back Derrick Henry said. "He's been one of the best players in the league for a long time. That's never [been a] doubt in my mind. I know what Lamar's about. You all have seen it. He just keeps showing you." 
 
 One of the buzzwords with Doyle all offseason has been explosiveness, which soon became a theme for the opener. 
 
 On the first play called by Doyle, Jackson rolled left off play-action and connected with wide receiver Zay Flowers for 49 yards to set up Baltimore's first touchdown. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Jackson threw a 53-yard pass to wide receiver Chris Moore to set up the Ravens' fifth and final touchdown of the day. 
 
 Jackson finished 17-of-25 passing (68%) for 324 yards and one touchdown. 
 
 "You can see he is just comfortable back there," Ravens wide receiver  Chris Moore  said. "He is reading his keys. He is going through his progressions, and he is finding the open guy. We already know Lamar has an incredible playmaking ability, so that just happens naturally. But for him to be able to just have that poise in the pocket now, you can see it shine." 
 
 
 Jackson will face an increased challenge throwing the ball downfield. Two of Baltimore's top three wide receivers -- Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) -- were injured Sunday and didn't play in the second half. 
 
 If Flowers is forced to miss some games, it would be a major loss because he is Jackson's most reliable receiver. On passes where Jackson threw the ball 10 yards or longer Sunday, he was 4-of-5 for 96 yards when targeting Flowers and 2-of-5 for 70 yards when targeting others, according to ESPN Research. 
 
 The Ravens' only healthy wide receivers are Rashod Bateman , the No. 2 wide receiver who didn't record a catch Sunday; Moore, who was elevated from the practice squad; LaJohntay Wester , who's primarily a punt returner; and Elijah Sarratt , a rookie fourth-round pick who was a healthy scratch. 
 
 "I have all the confidence in my guys who stepped in," Jackson said. "You never know when the next guy [is] going to be up, so just dial in [and] stay locked in."

title: Ben Johnson, Ravens DBs lead top NFL quotes from NFL Week 1
summary: Sometimes the highlights come from the postgame pressers. Here's a look at the top quips and comments from around the league in Week 1.
full_text:
The NFL season has just begun, but players and even coaches have been in midseason form after their opening games, providing plenty of interesting moments during postgame speeches in the locker room, interviews at the podium and on social media.

 Ahead of the first "Monday Night Football" matchup of the year between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos , we rounded up the best quotes from around the league on Sunday.

 

 "He had 124 [yards] on the ground, three touchdowns and a brand-new f---ing contract." -- Chicago Bears  coach Ben Johnson 
 The Bears coach was fired up for his team in the locker room after beating the Carolina Panthers in a 59-37 shootout.

 While handing out game balls to his players, Johnson made sure to mention star running back D'Andre Swift 's recent massive payday. It was reported two days ago that Swift and Chicago had agreed to a three-year, $33.75 million extension .

 

 

 "I'm Malaki Starks, and I'm a dawg." -- Baltimore Ravens DB Malaki Starks 

 During his usual postgame stream on social media with teammates following a victory, defensive back Marlon Humphrey caught up with Starks. The Ravens throttled the Indianapolis Colts 41-23 , posting over 500 total yards of offense.

 While Starks was giving an honest breakdown of his team's performance on Sunday afternoon, Humphrey was having none of that. Instead, Humphrey told the sophomore safety to let the world know just how talented he is.

 

 

 "Plain and simple, we got our ass whupped." -- Colts DT DeForest Buckner 
 While it was all smiles and laughs for the Ravens on Sunday, their opponent's locker room was anything but. Indianapolis allowed 506 total yards and gave up 41 points, its second-most points allowed in a season opener in the past 10 seasons, according to ESPN Research.

 When asked about his team's performance in its home opener, Buckner didn't hold back.

 

 "I guess I've got to get 200 [touchdown passes] now. I'll keep that one." -- Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence 

 Lawrence threw for four touchdowns in Sunday's 34-10  win over the Cleveland Browns , but one of them was more special than the rest. His second TD toss to rookie receiver Josh Cameron was the 100th of his career. However, it was also Cameron's first career NFL catch.

 Knowing this was a special moment for the rookie pass catcher, Lawrence graciously let Cameron keep the ball. But he won't be so generous with the one from his 200th touchdown pass.

 

 "Waited a long time to be a head coach in this league, man. It's freaking awesome. And we're not where we want to be, and they better get us now." -- Cleveland Browns  coach Todd Monken 
 The first-year head coach expressed his disappointment following a defeat to the Jaguars. However, Monken offered some optimism for the future, too.

 He focused on his young group improving, while pinpointing that they just "didn't play well today." Monken spent 10 seasons as an assistant coach in the NFL before getting his first head coaching job. Therefore, the blowout loss presumably won't get him too shook up, as he added: "You're not going to get me down."

 

 

 "There's a time and place for everything." -- Washington Commanders QB Jayden Daniels 
 Washington suffered a narrow two-point defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles following a failed 2-point conversation late. One play that might have had an impact on the outcome happened early in the fourth quarter.

 Daniels connected with wide receiver Stefon Diggs for a 10-yard touchdown to make it a one-point game. However, Diggs celebrated by leaping on the goalpost and received a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty. It pushed the Commanders' PAT back, though the kick was good anyway. After the game, coach Dan Quinn said the team would have gone for two if Diggs wasn't penalized. 

 Washington's quarterback reflected on Diggs' penalty postgame.

title: NFL Week 1 offense explosion: Bears, Ravens, Bills, Jaguars
summary: Chicago (59), Baltimore (41), Buffalo (36) and Jacksonville (34) were among 10 teams that scored 30-plus points Sunday. What happened, and can it continue?
full_text:
There are few joys in sports like the first Sunday of the NFL season . After an entire offseason without professional football, we finally get a flood of Week 1 games all at once. NFL RedZone springs to life for the first time since January. Some years, the anticipation can be more exciting than the actual action, with offenses playing in the regular season together for the first time struggling to find a rhythm. This year, though, offensive struggles were few and far between.

 Nine different teams scored 30 or more points in the early window on Sunday, just the second time that has ever happened. And with the Vikings unexpectedly making it to 39 points in their comeback win over the Packers , 10 teams scored 30 or more points in all on Sunday. That's the first time that has happened since 2002 and just the third time it has happened on the opening Sunday of the NFL season since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970 (1986 being the other).

 Some of those big scores were a product of uncommon circumstances. The Lions and Saints went to overtime , when they each scored a touchdown. The Vikings scored four consecutive touchdowns in the second half to come back against Green Bay, with three of those drives starting deep in Packers territory after a big kickoff return and two defensive turnovers, making life easier for a Carson Wentz -led offense to rack up points. A Bengals defense that forced and recovered four fumbles against the Buccaneers took one to the house for a defensive score and set up the offense with two short fields.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 Others attempted to keep up in shootouts but fell short. The Texans managed 31 points against a conservative Bills defense in C.J. Stroud 's first start since his playoff meltdown. But after driving into the red zone in the last minute of the game, Stroud was sacked twice on the final three plays, including on a three-man rush that produced a game-ending strip sack. And while the Panthers scored 37 points on a day when  Bryce Young threw for 361 yards, well, the Bears scored more points on offense than any team has since the Dolphins went for 70 in September 2023.

 Today, I'm going to focus on the four other teams that hit 30-plus points and how their offenses got off to blistering-hot starts. The Bears, Bills, Jaguars and Ravens all had high hopes for their offenses heading into Week 1, but they scored a combined 170 points in their season-opening victories. How did they pull that off? Were the defenses more to blame? Or should we be projecting these offenses to lead the league in scoring the rest of the way?

 I'll run through all four, starting in Chicago, where the Bears heard Ben Johnson say that he wanted to field the highest-scoring offense in NFL history and proceeded to tie the 2019 Ravens in scoring the most points on offense of any team in NFL history in a season-opening performance.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Bears | Bills | Jaguars | Ravens 

 
 

 

 Bears 59, Panthers 37 
 While there will still be concerns about the Bears' defense after it allowed Bryce Young & Co. to score 37 points, defense isn't going to matter if you're approaching 60. In their season opener, the Bears' offense scored more points than they have in any other game in the 105-year history of the franchise. They somehow scored 59 points on offense without a single catch from tight end  Colston Loveland , the sort of combination that would seem impossible if it hadn't just played out Sunday afternoon in Charlotte.

 To get there, the Bears produced something that we didn't see from them on offense in 2025: big plays on the ground. For all the things the Bears did well during Ben Johnson's first year at the helm, creating big rushes wasn't one of them. They had just four runs of 25 or more yards last season, tied with the Saints for 25th in the NFL.

 

 It took the 2026 Bears all of one game to match their seasonlong total from a year ago. Johnson's offense produced four 25-plus-yard gains on the ground against the Panthers, including touchdown runs of 28 yards (by  D'Andre Swift ), 29 yards ( Caleb Williams ) and 61 yards ( Kyle Monangai ). Swift added a 32-yarder early in the game to make it four. The Bears finished with 291 rushing yards on 39 attempts, averaging 7.5 yards per carry.

 The Panthers don't have a great run defense, given that they ranked 24th in DVOA on the ground in 2025. And defensive issues certainly made life easier for the Bears. Carolina inadvertently doubled Rome Odunze over the middle of the field instead of passing him off from one defender to the next as Williams scrambled just before halftime, leaving a free path for the young quarterback to escape a four-man rush and scamper up the sideline for a 29-yard score. The Panthers also didn't get anybody into the A-gap on Swift's 32-yard run in the first quarter, then missed multiple tackle attempts on the newly extended back before he changed fields to pick up extra yardage.

 On the whole, though, the Bears were dominant running the ball because they simply overwhelmed the Panthers. Tight end  Cole Kmet had one of those games where you can't wait to get back into the building for film review; in addition to making a great catch on a leak concept for a 22-yard touchdown, Kmet made big blocks on Swift and Monangai touchdown runs, driving defenders out of the play to create run lanes. The right side of Chicago's O-line -- highly paid guard Jonah Jackson and budding star  Darnell Wright  -- had an excellent game. And both Swift and Monangai got more than what was blocked, which wasn't always the case a year ago. The Bears were average on rush yards over expectation per attempt on designed runs last season (NFL Next Gen Stats), but they were comfortably tops in the league in Week 1.

 Williams made a number of plays with his legs, but he was also just as spectacular as a passer. The 2024 first overall pick has deservedly lived in the dreams of Bears fans all offseason for the memorable moments he had down the stretch and into the postseason in 2025, creating magic in the fourth quarter for the Bears as they led late comebacks. We know Williams still has that capacity to extend plays and deliver passes that few other quarterbacks on the planet can make, and we saw a little bit of that Sunday.

 The touchdown pass to Kmet was inch-perfect. Williams also extended a play, scrambled, then threw against the grain on a deep out to Kalif Raymond  for 28 yards. (Raymond surprisingly led the team in targets, catches and receiving yards.) If there had been any need for late-game heroics, Williams was playing like they would have come.

 

 What was really striking, though, was just how in-control Williams looked as a passer, something that wasn't the case on a regular basis last season. The Panthers didn't offer much of a pass rush, as their 16.1% pressure rate was the worst of any team in Week 1, but Williams didn't give them much time to generate one, either. He was really effective early in the game at getting to the end of his drop and getting the ball out quickly. And when Williams did extend plays, they usually produced positive results.

 With the ball coming out when it was supposed to within the context of the offense and little pressure from Carolina, Williams was also a more accurate passer. His off-target rate was a league-worst 20.2% a year ago, but it improved to 13.8% in Week 1. That was almost exactly league-average. Williams' minus-6.7% completion percentage over expectation (CPOE) was the worst in football among regular starters in 2025, per NFL Next Gen Stats. His plus-11.4% CPOE on Sunday was the third-best mark of Week 1 and the best mark he has posted in a single game under Johnson.

 Are there elements that probably won't stick? Yes. The Bears went 4-for-4 in the red zone and 10-of-14 on third down, rates even the best offenses in football would struggle to hit for any stretch of time. They started three possessions in Carolina…

title: Inside Patrick Mahomes' remarkable return from knee injury
summary: Exactly 274 days ago, Mahomes, after suffering the most significant injury of his career, vowed to be back for Week 1. Here's how he did it.
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Positioned next to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes , at the start of what would be a nine-month odyssey, was the MRI machine. The results of the scans that Dec. 14 day revealed the most significant injury of Mahomes' nine-year career: a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.

 As the minutes passed, more people entered the room inside the Chiefs' training facility, located a few hundred feet from Arrowhead Stadium -- team head trainer Rick Burkholder; Mahomes' agent, Chris Cabott; Mahomes' wife, Brittany; coach Andy Reid; general manager Brett Veach; and club owner Clark Hunt. Together -- less than an hour after Mahomes had crumpled to the turf, grabbed his knee and screamed in pain -- the group began contemplating next steps.

 At one point, someone looked at the calendar. The first Sunday of the 2026 NFL season was scheduled for Sept. 13, 273 days away. While exploring surgical options, a phone call was made to Dr. Dan Cooper, the renowned Dallas Cowboys  head team physician who specializes in knee and shoulder injuries. Cooper presented a proposition to Mahomes: If he wanted to return to the field as soon as possible, giving himself a chance to be back in uniform for the start of the Chiefs' 2026 campaign, he would need to fly from Kansas City to Dallas the next morning to have surgery.

 

 "I'm willing," Mahomes responded, "to do whatever it takes."

 Throughout his rehab and recovery, Mahomes has said that same sentence many times. And his exhaustive, day-after-day actions have led to him achieving his mission -- one that began next to the MRI machine 274 days ago.

 When the Chiefs open their season Monday against the Denver Broncos (8:15 p.m. ET on ABC/ESPN), Mahomes, 30, will be available and is expected to be the starting quarterback.

 "It's incredible," Veach said. "That's a guy that defines what leadership and what the face of a franchise should look like. He gave up an entire summer. He just attacked [the rehab]. Everybody in the building sees it. The level of sacrifice is something that has been an example throughout the entire organization."

 Mahomes' injury punctuated Kansas City's disappointing 2025 season. Following the two-minute warning in the team's Week 15 game against the Los Angeles Chargers , Mahomes tried to rally the Chiefs to a game-winning drive. He scrambled out of the pocket, rolling to his right. With defensive end Da'Shawn Hand chasing him from behind, Mahomes threw the ball away. But a few steps later, Mahomes planted his left foot, which stuck into the turf, and hyperextended his knee, the knee bowing to the outside of his leg, which damaged his LCL.

 

 The Chiefs' 16-13 loss to the Chargers eliminated Kansas City from the playoffs, the team's first time missing the postseason since 2014.

 "I wasn't playing my best at the end of last year before I got hurt," said Mahomes, who rushed for a career-high 422 yards and five touchdowns last season. "I think I ran a little bit too much."

 One reason Mahomes and the Chiefs selected Cooper is his experience repairing two of the four main stabilizing knee ligaments 24 hours after injury, including reattaching the LCL.

 Aaron Borgmann, the founder of Borgmann Rehab Solutions and a former physical therapist and athletic trainer with the Chiefs, said most players wait a week or sometimes longer before having the surgery because of how much their knee has swelled. By having an expedited procedure, Mahomes avoided that wait. Also in his favor: He did not have any artery, nerve, joint surface or meniscal damage, according to Burkholder.

 "For [most people], it's 10 days for an MRI, it's another doctor's visit and then another week to schedule surgery and so on," said Borgmann, describing general practices involving a torn ACL. "But we're not professional football players. I stand on this: NFL players of today have the best medical care in the world due to our healthcare system and our availability of imaging.

 "We have more doctors associated with NFL teams than any other professional sport in the United States. It is the best medical care you can find in the world."

 Even before his surgery, Mahomes wrote on his social media accounts, vowing to not fail his expectations.

 "I [will] be back stronger than ever."

 

 

 AWAITING MAHOMES ON Day 1 of 274 was Julie Frymyer, one of the Chiefs' top assistant athletic trainers. In his first rehab session, less than 24 hours after the surgery, Mahomes gritted his teeth and grimaced in pain while Frymyer assessed his muscles and worked to make sure the knee didn't swell up.

 Mahomes and Frymyer had been through such a scene many times before for three other injuries over the quarterback's career.

 Since Mahomes became the Chiefs' starter in 2018, Frymyer has been one of the team's most sought-out trainers. Mahomes on numerous occasions has credited much of his success in recovering from injuries faster than the average player to Frymyer -- and not to the fan theory that he possesses healing powers similar to Marvel character Wolverine. Also helping him, according to Frymyer and various others in the Chiefs organization, is Mahomes' remarkable ability to tolerate pain, whether during a game or in the team's training room.

 

 Frymyer's first major assignment with Mahomes occurred Oct. 17, 2019, when Mahomes dislocated his right kneecap while attempting a quarterback sneak.

 "I remember going into that halftime and he's trying to talk me into [him] going back out and playing," Reid said of Mahomes. "That [mindset] is huge for that position. You've got a lot of eyes on you. Guys are going to watch how you go about your business."

 With Frymyer's help, Mahomes surprised the Chiefs by missing just two games, returning to the field 24 days later. Before his 2025 knee injury, that was the longest absence of his career. A few months later, Mahomes led the Chiefs to their first Super Bowl victory in 50 years. The following year, during the postseason, Mahomes returned seven days after sustaining a painful turf toe in his left foot -- while also having a concussion from the previous week. Back on the field, he excelled, leading the Chiefs to Super Bowl LV, where they were beaten by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 Frymyer became well-known among Chiefs fans and trainers in the NFL after the 2022 postseason, when she administered almost around-the-clock treatment and therapy for eight consecutive days after Mahomes experienced a painful high sprain of his right ankle in a win against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the divisional round. Despite his limited mobility, Mahomes once again carried the Chiefs back to the Super Bowl, defeating the Philadelphia Eagles for the franchise's third championship.

 "I trust her so much," Mahomes said of Frymyer, who last year starred in a State Farm commercial alongside the quarterback and pop singer Meghan Trainor. "There's days you come in [and] you're tired. I mean, you're sore. But she makes sure I finish the entire workout -- and I'm going to do it the right way. She knows when to pull back on some days.

 "It lets me go out there and work and not have to think about if I'm doing too much [or] am I doing not enough."

 

 Unlike those previous, brief rehabs, Frymyer this time had to find the correct balance of when to motivate and when to encourage Mahomes through a monthslong process.

 The most grueling days were in late December, when he couldn't walk. While wearing a protective brace, Mahomes couldn't sleep with much comfort. Christmas Day was not ideal, either. Instead of playing with his teammates, Mahomes watched the Chiefs lose to the Broncos from a suite inside Arrowhead Stadium, his crutches nearby.

 "The toughest part was the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around," Mahomes said. "I remember sitting at the [training] table and watching us play those last few [road] games and how much it hurt me."
