title: How to bet Broncos-Chiefs on MNF: Mahomes back, KC a field goal fave
summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Broncos-Chiefs on "Monday Night Football."
full_text:
Week 1 wraps up with Patrick Mahomes making his return to action when the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos  on "Monday Night Football" ( 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC ).

 I love Week 1 games with divisional opponents because it gives us a road map of what to look for based on previous head-to-head matchups, which includes personnel usage, scheme and more. And we get that here with Denver and K.C. on Monday night.

 

 Yes, there is an unknown in this game with Mahomes after the season-ending knee injury in 2025. He's a natural mover and creator. Let's keep an eye on his mobility in this one. Now, going back to the Week 11 Broncos-Chiefs game last season (when Mahomes was on the field), Denver lowered their blitz rate slightly to 28.6% (down from their season average of 31.3%). And what do you get from the Denver secondary? A lot of single-high looks and man coverage.

 Mahomes attempted 45 passes in that game, threw for 267 yards and was sacked three times. My take for Monday? Coach Andy Reid will use the run game -- and free agent addition Kenneth Walker III -- to control tempo out of multiple tight end sets. You don't want Mahomes dropping back 40-plus times versus this Denver pass rush.

 On the offensive side for the Broncos, Davis Webb takes over as the new playcaller, though I expect to see coach Sean Payton's influence in the game plan, which includes the quicks and shot plays deigned for offseason addition  Jaylen Waddle . Waddle fits the Denver route tree and the throwing traits of Bo Nix . The key here is Nix's ability to reads the heavy post-snap movement from Chiefs defense. In the backfield, we should look for a committee approach with  J.K. Dobbins , RJ Harvey  and rookie Jonah Coleman versus a top-10 Kansas City run front.

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 Do we feel that Mahomes is back to a point where he can take over critical moments of the game by extending plays outside of structure? Or does Reid have to craft a game plan that leans on running the ball and throwing quick from the pocket to counter a Denver pass rush that had an NFL-best 68 sacks last season?

 

 I think it's a little of both, even if Mahomes is somewhat limited as a runner. Playing in Arrowhead helps here for Kansas City. That's the toughest road environment I ever experienced as a player (though Philly is close). The spread dipping under the three-point mark works, too. And when I look at Week 1 games, the value of coaching really jumps. We saw that in the 49ers-Rams game, right? And Reid has had an entire offseason to study a very multiple (and pressure-heavy) Denver defense. If Steve Spagnulo's defense can limit the after-the-catch production versus Denver (gotta tackle), while creating a few takeaways, this sets up a physical, low-scoring Chiefs' winner. 

 The bets: Chiefs -2.5 (-105), Walker receiving yards OVER 17.5 (-116) 

 Notable player props, bets 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 

 Bo Nix rushing yards OVER 16.5 (-108) 

 Eric Moody: Nix has averaged 23.1 rushing yards per game in his career. With the Chiefs allowing the 10th-fewest passing yards per game last season, Nix could rely more on his legs in this matchup. He cleared this line in 10 of 18 games last season, and even though he's returning from a broken ankle that kept him out of the AFC championship, there's a strong chance he clears this line on Monday night.

 

 Travis Kelce receiving yards OVER 41.5 (-112) 

 Liz Loza:  Kelce registered 42 or more receiving yards in 13 of 18 regular-season contests last season. Moreover, he has managed 43 or more receiving yards in five of his last six meetings against Denver. The Broncos' defense allowed an average of nearly 60 receiving yards per game to tight ends in 2025 (ninth most). With Mahomes working his way back into game shape, Kelce figures to serve as a reliable safety valve on primetime.

title: Broncos using the same formula as the 2015 Super Bowl team?
summary: The 2015 Broncos used a united front office, shutdown defense and clutch play to win Super Bowl 50. And the 2026 Broncos have a similar makeup -- and goal.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- When Aqib Talib looks at the current version of the Denver Broncos , he sees a reflection of his football past.

 "They're us," the former Pro Bowl cornerback said when comparing the current Broncos to the franchise's Super Bowl 50 championship team. "They all love ball, talk to each other, hold each other to it. It's clear as day when you see it."

 Talib is not the only player from the Broncos' most recent Super Bowl-winning team to see history potentially repeating itself. Dallas Cowboys edge rusher Von Miller  -- who was the MVP of the Broncos' Super Bowl win over the Carolina Panthers at the end of the 2015 season -- feels a similar vibe with the 2026 Broncos.

 "Oh yeah, I see it," Miller said earlier this summer. "They do it the way we did it. ... You can tell they keep it straight with each other."

 This is turn-back-the-clock stuff for Talib, Miller and those who lived it in 2015. They see similarities between how their championship team was set up and how the current Broncos, who were 14-3 last season and went to the AFC Championship Game , function. The two teams share parallels on and off the field, including institutional support, reliance on an elite-level defense and a penchant for thriving in close games. And these Broncos now hope that the culture created from this formula gets them a Super Bowl win, just like the 2015 team. Denver begins its quest for its fourth title when it plays at the Kansas City Chiefs on "Monday Night Football" ( 8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN/ABC ).

 

 "Real winning is in what you might not even see until it's right," Talib said. "It's that attitude, that giving and sharing. You give everything you have, and you don't ever lower that bar on anything, and you hold each other to it every day. And you get guys who can take that accountability. They have it, we had it."

 When Broncos coach Sean Payton is asked a question about winning, his responses start with words like program, grit and culture. He believes this roster has those things, which is why 45 of the players who were on the 53-man roster for last season's opener still remain with the franchise.

 That rate of retention is almost unheard of in the NFL and is risky in its own way. But Payton believed this group was good enough to be in the Super Bowl hunt last season because of how it was assembled -- and believes it is good enough again.

 "Culture is one of those things, we all talk about it, it's like a go-to word sometimes, but to really have it ... it's rare I think," Broncos defensive tackle Zach Allen said. "Some places just say they have it and it's really nowhere to be found. ... If you need to be pushed, or reminded to work, or, like be told to get to work, you're not going to be around here."

 
 'Finding the right people' 
 Payton has often said that the number of NFL teams that can actually win a Super Bowl is fewer than most think because "a lot of them have trouble getting out of their own way."

 When Payton, who coached the New Orleans Saints from 2006 to 2021, looked to return to coaching in 2023, he searched for franchises that had a "triangle" for success. That involves ownership that provides and understands the resources and infrastructure it takes to win; a personnel department capable of finding the right players; and a coaching staff with the game-day chops and developmental skills to make the most of that talent. And all three of those sides of the triangle must be connected, with a clear vision.

 "It's still finding the right people, ownership like we have in Greg and Carrie [Penner] and our group, like [general manager] George [Paton] and our relationship," Payton said. "... So when you get that triangle, and you get the ownership triangle ... you have a chance to then do the right things, a chance to acquire the right people."

 Gary Kubiak, who coached the Super Bowl 50 winner and spent more than two decades with the Broncos as a player, assistant coach and head coach, had a similar mindset to Payton. He described the 2015 dynamic, when he and then-executive vice president of football operations John Elway worked together to form the roster, as a "talent puzzle."

 They agreed that not all players will fit together, no matter their talent level, if there is not a clear mission about which players are acquired and retained. Talib calls it the process of finding players with "good ego" and avoiding those with "bad ego."

 

 "Good ego is you know what you can do ... and we hold up each other to the standard, don't pull down, pull up, no grudges, just real talk," he said. "But you get bad ego, and talent don't mean s---."

 Many players on both 2015 and 2026 versions of the Broncos say it's that mix that separates them. That the character and accountability have to hold up under stress and the inevitable tests of a season.

 Kubiak said the current Broncos show the mission he saw in the 2015 team.

 "It's always about the players,'' Kubiak said. "But the 53 most talented guys just put into the meeting room probably won't win if they don't go together. They have to demand of each other to prepare right, demand of each other to be smart, if that's something you're getting from your group, not coaches, the group, that's special."

 Payton calls it the "debrief," when the game that has just been played is put through the grinder. He has often said the debrief might be more important than the game itself. No matter the result, Broncos players know what's coming.

 "Honest talk," Broncos cornerback Jahdae Barron said. "Look at it, assess it, fix it. And that's everybody."

 Talib, Chris Harris Jr . and T.J. Ward -- members of the 2015 secondary -- said weekly players-only film sessions by the defensive backs were a constant exercise in accountability 11 years back.

 "All those cliches and s---, it's true; you don't have that 'everyone is accountable' mentality, you ain't going to get the ultimate prize," Kubiak said. "You've got to have it from the top down in the building, at every locker in your locker room."

 
 'Just play badass defense' 
 The 2015 Broncos had one of the best defensive postseason runs in the Super Bowl era. Denver's defense surrendered only one total touchdown pass in three playoff games combined against Ben Roethlisberger, Tom Brady and Cam Newton, that season's MVP. The Broncos had 14 sacks and 32 quarterback hits in the playoffs, and Miller capped off that run as the ninth (and most recent) defensive player to be named Super Bowl MVP.

 It was the continuation of a regular season in which the Broncos led the league in defensive EPA (by a whopping 17 points), sacks, total defense and pass defense. Denver was also No. 4 in scoring defense. The rugged, make-things-happen group allowed the 2015 team to stay afloat despite injuries and inconsistency from quarterback Peyton Manning. Manning missed seven games with a foot injury and completed a league-low 59.8% of his passes with 17 interceptions (second most in the NFL).

 "We just felt, and I think as a coach you take it with you into every game, that our defense was going to keep us in it," Kubiak said. "... Even after Peyton was injured and Brock [Osweiler] was playing, we could put things together week-to-week knowing we could play tight games ... and feel good about winning them."

 The current Broncos have also been led by their defense. Denver's defense led the league in sacks in each of the past two years, setting franchise records in each of those seasons. Edge rusher Nik Bonitto has turned into an All-Pro (14 sacks in 2025), finishing second to Micah Parsons last season in pressure rate among rushers with at least 300 rush attempts. Allen led all players in quarterback hits a year ago, while All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II (the 2024 Defensive Player of the Year) leads a deep and schematically flexible secondary.

 

 Over the past two seasons combined, the Broncos have allowed the fewest points per game in the NFL (18.3) and have given…

title: Why Baker Mayfield's contract means the QB market could burst
summary: Baker Mayfield just got $55 million per year in new money -- which is telling about where the QB market is headed. That's great news for 11 other passers ready for big deals.
full_text:
Fifty-five million dollars per year for Baker Mayfield ? Seriously?! 

 Well, yes and no. Mayfield got his new deal from the Buccaneers on Tuesday, and it was a doozy. But it was also one of those win-win NFL contract outcomes where the player and agent get to brag about one number while the team gets to say, "Yeah, but ..."

 Mayfield was already making $27 million in 2026. He now makes $37 million in 2026, $50 million in 2027, $50 million in 2028 and $55 million in 2029. That's four years and $192 million, which works out to $48 million per year over four years. But the "new money" in the deal -- money he didn't already have coming to him -- totals $165 million, and the Bucs added three years to his existing deal. Over three years, the average of $165 million is $55 million per year.

 That's why both sides can claim victory and call it a win-win.

 But you know who else comes out of this looking like winners? Every other quarterback who is or could be coming up for a contract extension within the next year.

 Mayfield is a really good player. His career looked destined for an early end just a few years after he was the No. 1 pick in the 2018 draft, but he has found a home in Tampa, and it agrees with him. He has averaged 32 touchdown passes and 4,079 yards per season, and he won two NFC South division titles in three years with the Bucs. He has been good for them -- and they've been good for him.

 

 But $55 million per year puts him in a tie with five other guys for third-highest average salary in the league. Dak Prescott makes $60 million per year. Patrick Mahomes ' new-money average in his most recent deal was $64 million. Mahomes is the only quarterback who has even threatened -- let alone passed -- Prescott's salary in the two years since his deal was completed. Mahomes is also the only one with two MVP trophies, three Super Bowl titles and a 17-4 career playoff record. Mahomes is his own category.

 The five who are tied with Mayfield at $55 million? Matthew Stafford (has won a Super Bowl and an MVP award), Joe Burrow (has been to a Super Bowl), Josh Allen (has won MVP), Jordan Love and Trevor Lawrence (uhh ... have excellent timing).

 In eight NFL seasons, Mayfield has made two Pro Bowls, and his highest finish in MVP voting is 11th. His place is among the last two names in that previous paragraph, not the first three. But his presence there is what should finally make it a crossable threshold for the next group. Unlike Love and Lawrence, Mayfield wasn't benefiting from a red-hot extension market at the time he signed. This was a quiet year for top-of-the-market quarterback deals.

 Mayfield had some leverage -- his contract was set to void three days after the Super Bowl and trigger an immovable $30 million dead-money cap charge for 2027 -- but the Bucs could have let him walk and trusted in their ability to find a good, affordable solution. You know, the way they did when Tom Brady retired and they signed Mayfield in the first place. The Buccaneers appear to have done this deal because Mayfield has been a really good quarterback for them, and this is what really good quarterbacks' contracts cost now.

 This is fantastic news for anyone who considers himself a really good NFL quarterback and is (or will be) looking for a contract extension between now and next summer. And there are a lot of people in this category. The 2027 quarterback extension market could be the busiest we've seen in a while. And that is why 2027 should be the year when one or (likely) more quarterbacks try to join Prescott and Mahomes in the $60 million club. Many of them should, at least, get past the $55 million that we will now, for the purpose of this exercise, call the "Baker Line."

 Here's a look at the quarterbacks in those conversations.

 

 

 Lamar Jackson , Baltimore Ravens 
 Jackson enters this season with two years left on his contract. He is making $52 million this year and is scheduled to make $52 million next year. The team approached him about an extension this past offseason, but nothing got done .

 

 Jackson has tremendous leverage because his deal includes a clause that prohibits the Ravens from using the franchise or transition tags on him when he (hypothetically) becomes a free agent in 2028; it also has a no-trade clause. So, even if the Ravens couldn't get an extension done by next offseason and decided to trade Jackson rather than let him play out his contract year, he could pick his destination and veto any trade he didn't like.

 Is he over the Baker Line? He is, by two MVP awards if nothing else. Jackson is the one guy in this group who already has a strong case to surpass Prescott's average annual salary of $60 million. It would be shocking and foolish at this point for him to agree to anything less. Imagine if Jackson were to stay healthy for two more years, play lights-out in both of them and become an unrestricted free agent in spring 2028 with no franchise tag to limit his earnings potential? What would he get ... $70 million per year? $80 million?

 
 

 Drake Maye , New England Patriots 
 Entering his third year in the NFL, Maye will be eligible for a contract extension whenever the Patriots' season ends. Having finished second in MVP voting and led the team to the Super Bowl in his second season, Maye would have had a case to be over the Baker Line if he had been allowed to negotiate an extension this offseason. (CBA rules say you have to wait until after the player's third year.) The Patriots have a fifth-year option for 2028, which would buy them time next spring to work on this.

 Is he over the Baker Line? Right now, probably. Mayfield has never been to the Super Bowl or placed second in MVP voting. If Maye were to suffer a significant injury or experience dramatic regression from his 2025 performance, he might be in a situation similar to the one C.J. Stroud is in right now, with the team picking up the option and waiting to see more before committing. But ( Wednesday night 's fourth-quarter meltdown aside) that feels unlikely.

 
 

 Caleb Williams , Chicago Bears 
 

 Jayden Daniels , Washington Commanders 
 

 Bo Nix , Denver Broncos 
 I'm grouping these three together because they're in very similar situations. Maye's 2024 first-round classmates have yet to reach the Super Bowl (which is why he got his own entry here), but each has shown plenty of the promise that led their teams to draft them where they did.

 

 Daniels won Offensive Rookie of the Year and took the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game in his rookie season, then injuries derailed his second year. Nix helped the Broncos reach the AFC Championship Game last season, though he couldn't play in it because he broke his ankle during one of the final plays of Denver's overtime playoff victory over the Bills the week before. Williams struggled in his first year but really took off last season once the Bears hired Ben Johnson as their head coach. Williams didn't get to the NFC Championship Game, but the Bears took the Rams to overtime the week before in the divisional round.

 All three of these guys can likely count on their teams picking up their fifth-year options next spring for 2028 if they can't get deals done before then. The other 2024 first-rounders were Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr . and Minnesota's  J.J. McCarthy , who don't yet merit much mention in a conversation like this.

 Are they over the Baker Line? It depends. But given their credentials and accomplishments so far, each should get there as long as they show improvement rather than regression in Year 3.

 
 

 C.J. Stroud , Houston Texans 
 The second pick in the 2023 draft had his fifth-year option for 2027 picked up in May, but he still hasn't secured an extension from the Texans, a team that is as proactive and generous as any in the league when it comes to veteran contract extensions. He was Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2023 and has reached the second round of the playoffs every…

title: Joey Porter Jr. trade fits: Which NFL teams could target CB?
summary: Joey Porter Jr. is open to a trade. We look at five teams that could trade for the star Steelers CB.
full_text:
The Joey Porter Jr . situation in Pittsburgh has reached a tipping point.

 Porter is open to a trade and the Steelers are willing to deal him . This has been brewing for a while, with Porter long considering his options after the team's hardline stance on a contract despite paying several teammates from his 2023 draft class.

 He is a good young player at a premium position on a prominent team known for developing -- and paying -- its own draft picks. That's why this situation is so surprising.

 Porter will have a trade market. It's important to note that contract demands have scared some teams away from giving up significant draft capital for certain players. They would rather trade for players on rookie deals or team-friendly contracts. The cornerback market features six players making at least $30 million.

 But Porter is on the short list of cornerbacks who can cover elite receivers in space, and that's worth a lot.

 It's also worth noting that the Steelers can decide to hold on to Porter.

 Here are a few teams that qualify as trade fits.

 

 

 Dallas Cowboys 
 Dallas has been looking for cornerback help, though more so in the bargain bin to this point.

 The franchise has trade-market rapport with Pittsburgh GM Omar Khan. The sides have reached deals in back-to-back offseasons, as Dallas traded for wide receiver George Pickens in May 2025 and offensive tackle Broderick Jones on Aug. 29.

 

 Dallas did not discuss Porter with Pittsburgh at the time of the Jones trade. But that would be an easy call for the Cowboys to make if interested.

 The problem: Dallas has given up some of its draft capital. The team has seven selections in 2027, but four of those are in the sixth and seventh rounds. Porter would likely cost at least a second-round pick, possibly a first. The Cowboys owe the better of theirs or Green Bay's first-round pick to the New York Jets , and their third-round selection to the Steelers.

 

 Detroit Lions 
 The Lions were looking for corner help even before they released Terrion Arnold in June. Detroit can spend the early weeks of the season evaluating how D.J. Reed , Keith Abney II , Roger McCreary and others play together.

 Detroit has ample salary cap space -- around $38 million as of Sunday, according to OverTheCap.com -- but has committed more than $1 billion in extensions for star players, which could lead to a cap crunch very soon. Detroit also could decide to pay 2027 free agents Sam LaPorta (tight end) and Brian Branch (safety).

 Detroit likes man-coverage corners, and Porter definitely qualifies.

 

 New Orleans Saints 
 New Orleans is rolling with young corners Quincy Riley and Kool-Aid McKinstry , but if the team wants reinforcements, Pittsburgh is the sensible call.

 The Saints have around $8 million in cap space and has six total draft picks in April.

 With quarterback Tyler Shough in the second year of his rookie deal, the timing might be right to take a swing on a young difference-maker who will soon be expensive.

 

 New York Jets 
 The Jets' roster has improved from a year ago but is still thin at corner. Coach Aaron Glenn, who had 41 interceptions as a player, can appreciate a good man-coverage player.

 

 No team is better positioned in the 2027 draft than the Jets, who have 10 picks, including three first-rounders. Getting the quarterback of the future will be the Jets' priority. But exploring other avenues to improve the roster is an option, too.

 

 San Francisco 49ers 
 The 49ers' cornerback rotation looked stout Thursday against the Los Angeles Rams , but seasons are long and Porter would help the defense immensely.

 San Francisco has eight draft picks in 2027 and around $45 million in cap space.

 Porter opposite Deommodore Lenoir would form a stout 1-2 cornerback combo.

title: Is Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence's hot start sustainable?
summary: Jacksonville's QB looked dominant vs. the Browns in Week 1. Can he shake his career September woes as tough matchups loom?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. --  Trevor Lawrence has not been his best in September. Statistically, anyway.

 The Jacksonville Jaguars ' quarterback has won only 33% of games, completed only 60% of his passes, and posted a Total QBR of 47 in September -- all the worst marks of any month of his career.

 But on Sunday, he had one of the best days of his career in a 34-10 rout of the Cleveland Browns at EverBank Stadium. He looked a lot like the quarterback who got on a roll in the second half of 2025, when he led the Jaguars to the playoffs and earned MVP consideration. That version of Lawrence will need to continue if the Jaguars are going to successfully manage a five-game stretch that includes four 2025 playoff teams.

 "When he is playing to the best of his ability like we know he can, the offense starts clicking and he makes some big plays downfield with some great throws, and we feed off of that," running back Bhayshul Tuten said. "We love him."

 The sixth-year QB was on a roll against the Browns. He completed 78.3% of his passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns with a 93.4 Total QBR. It was just the third time in his career that he has thrown four or more TD passes. On passes of 10-plus air yards, Lawrence completed 10 of 11 attempts for 179 yards and a career-high three touchdowns, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

 

 Spreading the ball worked really well for the offense. Lawrence completed passes to nine players, and each TD pass went to a different player. 

 "I thought he spread the ball around, trusted the guys that were in to make plays," head coach Liam Coen said. "I thought we protected him really well, thought we mixed it up from the run game and some different things to keep them off-balance to allow Trevor to continue to do what he does. He did some really good stuff off-schedule again today, especially the touchdown to Jakobi [Meyers] , I thought was a phenomenal throw and play in the back of the end zone.

 "So was definitely pleased with the way that Trevor ran the offense today."

 It was the sixth time in the past nine regular-season games (all victories) that the Jaguars have scored 30-plus points. Lawrence has 23 touchdown passes -- more than any other quarterback -- and only five interceptions in those nine games.

 But the Jaguars will need him to continue that pace for the next five weeks if they are going to establish themselves as legitimate AFC contenders. That starts with Sunday's game at the Denver Broncos , followed by a home game against the New England Patriots , a road game versus the Cincinnati Bengals and then back-to-back games in London against the Philadelphia Eagles and Houston Texans .

 

 "I feel really comfortable, really confident in what we're doing," Lawrence said. "I think last year at this time, I knew what we were doing, but it was still -- you're still getting used to the game plan and the moving parts of the offense, which was a lot, which is a big change for me. I think there was that dynamic of still trying to get completely comfortable in it.

 "It was awesome to get a win in Week 1 but excited now. We have a big challenge next week and got to turn the page and go put together another great game plan."

 Lawrence's best game of 2025 came against the Broncos in Denver. He withstood a strong pass rush -- five sacks and 14 QB hits -- and threw for 279 yards and three touchdowns with no turnovers in a 34-20 victory. The Jaguars didn't start that game fast but pulled away with two third-quarter touchdowns. Lawrence would like the Jaguars to repeat what they did against the Browns, scoring two first-quarter touchdowns and leading 24-0 at the half.

 "You want to start the game fast and play well in that first possession so you can settle in as soon as possible and not give the ball back to the other team," he said. "I think that's always something you want to do, but I think it comes down to preparation. Also, every game is different. You don't know exactly what the defense is going to do first series, and so there's a lot of moving parts.

 "For us to start fast today like we did, that's the goal moving forward, obviously, and going to continue to build on that."

 Which could make this Lawrence's best September.

title: Judging the biggest overreactions to NFL Week 1 games
summary: Is Jackson going to reset the market? What's up in L.A.? And which class of 2023 QB will be extended first? We sized up potential Week 1 overreactions.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Week 1 overreactions are the absolute best. I make this point every season, but I can't contain my excitement. When you do a weekly overreactions column during the season, along with a few in the offseason around the draft, free agency, etc., there are times when you're reaching for overreactions. But not in Week 1. No way.

 Almost everything is an overreaction in Week 1. If you had a specific concern about your team in the offseason -- such as C.J. Stroud turnovers, to pick a random example -- and that concern is the reason that team lost its opener , you overreact.

 See?!?! I TOLD you this was going to happen!!! 

 If you were looking forward to something about your team -- such as the Bears possibly having the best offense of all time -- and it scores 59 points in Week 1, well, you're inclined to believe you were right about that, too.

 Week 1 is the best ! I could write 100 overreactions off what has happened this week, but that's a lot of work and you guys have other stuff to read, too. So let's sort through five potential Week 1 takeaways and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational overreactions -- and we also hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Bears' offense will be forced to set scoring record? 
 Jackson to be first $70 million player? 
 Young will get long-term deal before Stroud? 
 Chargers were the offseason's most overhyped team? 
 Rams' "superteam" will miss playoffs? 
 Fantasy overreactions 

 
 

 

 The Bears are going to have to set the scoring record with the state of their defense 
 Second-year Bears head coach Ben Johnson made headlines this offseason when he said that his goal was to set the single-season team scoring record . He knows the record is 606 points -- 37.9 points per game -- by Peyton Manning and the 2013 Denver Broncos . The Bears scored 59 points against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday and are on pace to score 1,003 points. I'll save you having to open your calculator app -- that's more than 606.

 Chicago had 552 yards Sunday on 70 plays. The Bears converted 10 of 14 third downs. Quarterback Caleb Williams had 269 passing yards and two touchdowns, along with 65 rushing yards and two more touchdowns. Two Bears running backs reached 100 rushing yards, with D'Andre Swift having 134 and three touchdowns.

 

 But the Bears also gave up 37 points and 478 yards to the Panthers and couldn't seal the win until the fourth quarter despite punting only twice.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 The concerns about Chicago's defense entering the season were legitimate. The Bears are light in the secondary and the pass rush. They signed safety Coby Bryant in free agency , but he suffered a knee injury in camp and will miss significant time . Xavier Woods , who was signed in part to help make up for the Bryant loss, was inactive Sunday because of a groin injury. The Bears are very much piecing things together in the secondary, and they're having to do it with fewer pieces than they planned.

 

 Bryce Young and the Panthers are better offensively than given credit for, but the Bears will face tougher offenses than Carolina's this season. Johnson's offense should hum all season, but there will be weeks when Dennis Allen might have to manufacture a miracle or two on defense for the Bears to remain on playoff pace.

 

 

 Lamar Jackson could get $70 million per year on his next contract 
 One of the big questions entering this season is what the Ravens' offense would look like under new coordinator Declan Doyle and new head coach Jesse Minter. Week 1 provided a very encouraging answer. The Ravens scored 41 points in Sunday's victory over the Colts. Jackson was 17-for-25 for 324 passing yards and a touchdown and added 40 rushing yards and another touchdown.

 Running back Derrick Henry added 144 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Wide receiver Zay Flowers had 150 receiving yards and didn't play in the second half. Flowers and rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane  left early due  to injuries in this game, and it didn't matter. The Ravens' offense did basically whatever it wanted to do. Jackson looks healthy and energized, and he often becomes the MVP when that happens.

 Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION 

 Here's the deal: Jackson has two years left on his contract. It includes a no-trade clause and a clause that prohibits the Ravens from using the franchise or transition tag on him at the end of it. His 2027 cap number is currently projected to be $74.81 million unless the Ravens extend his contract next spring. They approached him about an extension this offseason and could not get one done .

 Jackson has incredible leverage. If -- I say if because I do not know his mindset -- he wants to play out the deal and become a free agent in 2028 at age 31, he can do that. If he doesn't want to sign an extension with the Ravens, he doesn't have to. Jackson holds the cards. So, if he does have a huge year and the Ravens do end up extending him, they shouldn't be expecting a hometown discount. If you're going to do your team a favor, you do your deal the way Patrick Mahomes does his. Not the way Jackson seems to be doing his.

 

 Whether he gets his new deal from the Ravens this season, next spring or he plays out the contract and hits the market in 2028, Jackson should eclipse Mahomes' $64 million per year average in his next deal. If Jackson wins another MVP award, he should clear that by a lot.

 

 

 The Panthers will extend Bryce Young before the Texans extend C.J. Stroud 
 Young was pretty good in that ridiculous loss to the Bears. He had 361 passing yards and a touchdown while adding 10 rushing yards and another score. It's a promising start after he helped lead the Panthers to a division title and the postseason in 2025. Young has shown consistent improvement since being benched for Andy Dalton early in the 2024 season. Though the Panthers didn't make a move to do an extension this offseason, it's not out of the question for them to do one eventually. They like Young and still think he can be their franchise QB.

 Stroud played well in the Texans' tough season-opening loss to Buffalo. He threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns and had the Texans marching toward a possible winning score in the final minute. Unfortunately, he took two bad sacks on that possession, with the second ending in a fumble that the Bills recovered to seal their 36-31 victory. Stroud also lost a fumble on Houston's first possession of the game. After his turnover-riddled postseason last January, turning the ball over twice in Week 1 wasn't what he needed to do to change the discourse.

 

 Verdict: OVERREACTION 

 Yeah, it has been only one week. The Texans still like Stroud and would be happy to sign him to an extension. One of the reasons they haven't yet is because Stroud wanted to bet on himself and see if he could get a top-of-market deal next  spring after what he hopes will be a successful season with a better ending than last year's. That is still within the range of realistic outcomes.

 

 There is a long way to go before Stroud and Young are talking to their respective teams about new deals next spring. If you -- based on one week of the 2026 season -- think you know how things will go when the time arises ... well, you're overreacting.

 
 

 The Chargers were the most overhyped team of the offseason 
 Remember how awesome the Mike McDaniel / Justin Herbert combination was supposed to be? Well, nobody told the Arizona Cardinals , who thumped the offseason darlings 26-14 to salvage the day for the LaFleur family. Herbert was sacked three times, threw one interception and managed only 209 passing yards. The offense didn't offer much variety or creativity. It basically looked as if Herbert was locked onto Ladd McConkey and no one else. And once McConkey left the game because of an injury, Herbert had nowhere to go.

 Anybody's entitled to a tough Week 1. The Patriots and Seahawks lost in Week 1 last…

title: NFL betting buzz: Circa Survivor kicks off with Jaguars taking the most Week 1 picks
summary: With a total of $25 million on the line, the Jaguars are the most popular Week 1 pick for Circa Survivor.
full_text:
Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry. 

 Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season.  

 Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds |  Sports betting home  |  DraftKings   

 

 Sept. 13: Circa Survivor kicks off with $25 million grand prize, Jaguars lead Week 1 picks 

 By Doug Greenberg 

 The Circa Sports pro football contests are locked in for the 2026 season with a total of $38.7 million on the line. 

 Circa Survivor will begin the season with a record 25,017 entries, making a winner-take-all $25,017,000 prize pool. The contest exceeded its guarantee of $20 million with four days remaining before registration closed.

 Grandissimo, Circa's $100,000-per-entry survivor contest, also easily met its $4 million guarantee and ended up with a record 77 entries vying for a $7.7 million prize pool. The casino's traditional $100,000-per-entry handicapping contest, Circa Million, did not meet its $6 million guarantee and ended up with 5,790 entries, creating an overlay of $210,000.

 Circa Survivor is the largest legal pro football contest in the country. Contestants pick one NFL team to win outright each week, with the caveat that they cannot use that team again the rest of the season. The entries must survive all 18 weeks of the regular season, plus two "mini weeks" for the Thanksgiving and Christmas slates.

 The Jacksonville Jaguars are the most popular pick in the contest for Week 1, with 8,121 entries (32.5% of the pool) selecting them to defeat the Cleveland Browns . The Los Angeles Chargers come in next at 7,585 entries (30.3%) and the Pittsburgh Steelers round out the top three at 4,013 entries (16.1%). 

 Some entries opted to pick from the first two games of the season, with 174 (0.7%) getting through with the Seattle Seahawks and 10 (~0.0%) surviving with the San Francisco 49ers . On the flip side, 49 entries (0.2%) backed the Los Angeles Rams and 25 (0.1%) were on the New England Patriots , leading to their immediate elimination.

 There were also 18 (0.1%) immediate eliminations via the dreaded No Pick designation.

 

 Sept. 11: Rams suffer worst opening loss by preseason Super Bowl favorite in 50 years 
 

 by David Purdum 

 Preseason Super Bowl favorites have lost before, just not as badly as the Los Angeles Rams did Thursday in Melbourne, Australia.

 The Rams lost 27-7 to the San Francisco 49ers , becoming the first preseason Super Bowl favorite to lose its opener by 20 or more in the past 50 seasons, according to SportsOddHistory.com. The 1993 Dallas Cowboys lost by 19, and the 2017 New England Patriots and 1987 New York Giants each lost by 15 in their season openers. Both the Cowboys and Patriots would play in the Super Bowl in those seasons, with the Cowboys winning and the Patriots losing, but the Giants failed to make the playoffs.

 Los Angeles closed as a 3.5-point favorite over the 49ers and attracted the bulk of the bets and money from bettors. BetMGM reported that 60% of the money bet on the point spread was on the Rams.

 The Rams have attracted more than twice as many bets to win the Super Bowl as any other team at DraftKings Sportsbook. They remain the favorites to win the Super Bowl, NFC and NFC West, but their odds dipped from 5-1 to 6-1 after Thursday's loss, and their odds to win the NFC West shifted from -105 to +164.

 The 49ers, in turn, improved from +300 to +180 to win the division. The defending-champion Seattle Seahawks moved from +215 to +184 in the tightly contested NFC West. San Francisco improved from 19-1 to 14-1 to win the Super Bowl at DraftKings.
